## Introduction to Accounts Receivable
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 13*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Introduction to Accounts Receivable 

This book describes how to use the Accounts Receivable application to manage the full A/R cycle. 

This chapter describes the Accounts Receivable application, its Home page, and the tasks that you can perform in 

Accounts Receivable. 

In This Chapter

C H A P T E R 1 

---



### Accounts Receivable Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 14*

Introduction to Accounts Receivable 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Accounts Receivable Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All`


Before you first use A/R, you or your system administrator must subscribe to and configure this 

application for your company. Configuring this application involves selecting the features you 

want to appear in the A/R menus and pages and assigning permissions to those who need to 

access those features. 

For step-by-step instructions on how to configure A/R for your company, see Configuring the 

Accounts Receivable Application in online help or download (on page 604) the RealPage 

Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide. 

With the Accounts Receivable application, you can: 

• 
Convert from your existing system to RealPage Accounting by importing lists of customers, 

invoices and adjustments from spreadsheet files. 

• 
Invoice customers on a recurring basis. 

• 
Set penalties for past due accounts. 

• 
Receive payments by check, cash, charge card, or funds transfer. You can receive advance 

payments any time and apply them when an invoice is created. 

• 
Make deposits as you normally do. As you receive payments, you probably accumulate 

them for later deposit, so the system places the funds into an undeposited funds account 

until you make the deposit. Alternatively, you can make a manual deposit that is attributed 

to the customer account but not to a specific invoice. You can also receive non-invoiced 

payments, such as counter sales, which are not attributed to customers that you track. 

• 
Deliver invoices and statements by printing them or emailing them. 

• 
Retain transaction detail forever, providing quick access customer history. And you can close 

accounts receivable but keep the G/L open. 

• 
Create custom terms. In addition to the default Accounts Receivable terms and aging 

periods, you can create custom terms as you need them. 

• 
Use manual check entry to write invoices manually - a quick way to enter several invoices 

per page. You cannot delete or edit invoices once they are paid, which allows for a high 

degree of accounting control. 

• 
Close Accounts Receivable periods while keeping the General Ledger open; financial data is 

retained indefinitely. 

• 
Create and print reports.  

The application generates a wide variety of customizable aging and receivables reports and 

graphs. Reports include the customer list, A/R ledger, customer aging reports and graphs 

and the sales register. Sales can be analyzed by many criteria, including by territory. The 

system also supplies report data you can use to calculate commissions.

Customers Overview 

Use the Customers list to add a record for any company to which you sell goods or services. 

Other RealPage applications use much of the customer information, not only for record-keeping 

purposes but also for printing the names and addresses on forms, such as invoices, and for 

determining the location of the Ship To contact so that the sales tax can be computed. 

For multi-entity shared companies: Customers are a master object. Master objects can either 
be common (that is, accessible) to all entities or exclusive (private) to a specific entity. 

The Customers record has multiple tabs that contain basic information about the customer, such 

as company name, address, and phone numbers. 

• 
Customer: Use this tab to add company and contact information. 

• 
Additional information: Use this tab to add accounting details. 

• 
Contact list: Use this tab to add categories and contacts associated with the company. 

• 
Restrictions: Use this tab to control who can see this customer record.

#### Guidelines for Updating Customer Records
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 30*

Customers 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Guidelines for Updating Customer Records 

The most important thing to remember when updating customer records through CSV import is 

that changes you make in the spreadsheet will affect your customer records.  

• 
If you update spreadsheet data for a customer, the information you specify will overwrite 

the data in the existing customer record.  

• 
If you remove data from the spreadsheet, the corresponding information will be removed 

from the customer record.  

Don’t overwrite existing data with blank data unless you intend to remove that data from your 
Customers list. For example, if you export the Email Address field and then clear the data in the 
Email Address column of your spreadsheet, existing customer email addresses will be deleted 
when you import the file. 

Recommended Precautions 

• 
Make a backup of your customer information before you make changes. Save a copy of the 

CSV for Import spreadsheet so that you have a record of the Customers list before the 

update process.  

• 
Before making large-scale changes, test the update process. Try creating a few test 

customers and then update just those customer records.  

Additional Tips 

• 
When you export the CSV for Import file, be sure to include the Customer ID column. This 

identifies the customer record that you are updating.  

• 
Column order isn’t important; for example, the Customer ID doesn’t need to be first. The 

header row identifies the contents of each column.  

• 
When you’re updating the CSV for Import file, keep in mind that different types of fields 

require different information.  

• 
For check box options, enter TRUE to select the option and enter FALSE to deselect 

the option 

Required Fields for New Customers 

When you’re adding new customers, you must include at least the following columns:  

• 
Customer ID: Be sure to enter a unique customer ID that hasn’t already been used in the 

system.  

• 
Customer Name: Enter the customer’s name.  

• 
Print as: Enter the customer’s name as it should appear on payments and reports.  

• 
Required custom fields: If you’ve created any custom fields that are required, you must also 

include these columns.

Customers List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 28) topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Use the Customers list to view and manage customer records. From this list, you can: 

• 
Add new customers. 

• 
Edit or view existing customer details. 

• 
Import customer records. 

• 
Export the list of customers. 

• 
Open a customer’s A/R ledger. 

• 
View the total amount that a customer owes to an entity. 

By default, the Customers list uses icons and indentation to show how parent and child customers 

are related. This hierarchical view is helpful when you have customers that belong to the same 

parent customer, such as when you are doing business with subsidiaries or divisions of the same 

company and need to separately track their contact and billing information. 

The list also provides access to related information, including: 

a) Customer’s A/R ledger: Click the customer’s name to open the customer’s A/R ledger. 

b) Customer totals box: Click the amount in the Total due column to open the Customer 

totals box and view the individual amounts due from the customer.  

If you are working in a multi-entity, multi-currency company, then a View due link appears in 
place of an amount in the Total due column. Click this link to open the Customer totals box 
to see the total amount due for each entity.

#### Adding Customers
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 33*

Chapter 2: Customers

Adding Customers 

See the How to Get Here (on page 28) topic for a list of ways to access the Customers list. 

The Customer information page has multiple tabs that contain basic information about the 

customer, such as company name, address, and phone numbers. 

To add a customer: 

1. 
From the top level, click the Applications menu, and then select Accounts Receivable. 

2. 
Select 
 Add next to Customers. 

Filling In the Customer Section 

To fill in the customer’s company and contact information. 

1. 
In the ID field, type a unique identifier for the customer. 

After creating and saving a customer record, you can only change the Customer ID with the 
Customer Utility Tool. Most users do not have access to the Customer Utility tool. 
Contact your system administrator if you need to change a Customer ID. 

2. 
In the Name field, type the name of the company as it should appear in lists and menus. 

3. 
Select the One-time use check box to designate the customer as a one-time or occasional 

use customer that you don’t want to include in your standard customer lists. 

These customers won’t appear in the Customers list unless you select the Include 

one-time check box at the top of the list. 

4. 
Select the Status of the customer record, either Active or Inactive. Inactive customers do not 

appear in any system lists or drop-down lists. 

Filling In the Tax Information Section 

The Tax information section appears when you use the international version of the RealPage 
Financial Suite.  

1. 
Select the country where the customer files taxes in the Country drop-down list. 

2. 
In the VAT reg no field, type the customer’s VAT registration number so that you can track 

VAT taxes. 

Filling In the Primary Contact Section 

1. 
Type the name, address, and contact information for the person who is your primary contact 

associated with the company. 

2. 
In the Print as field, type the name of the company as it will appear on payments and 

notices. 

---


<!-- Page 34 -->
Customers 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

When you create a new customer, the system automatically creates a related contact record 

for you. The Print as field is used in coordination with the Customer ID to create the 

suggested contact name, which is the unique contact ID used throughout the system that 

can’t be edited after creation. This is also the name that appears in all lists and drop-down 

lists. See Contacts (on page 591) for more detailed information. 

Duplicate information is shared between the Customer tab and the Contact list tab. 

Therefore, if you change the data in the Customer tab, the changes are reflected in the 

Contact list tab and vice versa (provided you have not selected the Exclude from the 

company contact list check box). 

3. 
Open the Additional information tab. 

Filling In the Additional Information Tab 

Enter accounting details for this customer: 

1. 
Select the customer’s type in the Type ID drop-down list. 

2. 
In the Sales rep drop-down list, select the user who is responsible for this customer’s 

account. 

3. 
If this customer account is a subsidiary of another customer, click the Parent drop down list, 

and then select the name of the parent company. 

4. 
To use a G/L group other than the default, select it in G/L group drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Territory ID drop-down list, select the sales territory to which you assigned the 

customer. You can also add a territory by clicking the Add link in the drop-down list. 

6. 
In the Attachments drop-down list, add an attachment to associate with the customer 

record. See Adding attachments to a record. Learn more about who can add attachments in 

Permissions for attachments. If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your 

file in the Attachments (on page 549) box to attach the file to this record. 

Filling In the Invoicing Details Section 

1. 
In the Term drop-down list, select the credit terms to extend to the customer. The selected 

term becomes the default term whenever you perform transactions related to the customer. 

You can also add a new term by clicking the Add link and filling in the A/R Terms 

Information box. 

2. 
In the Default revenue account drop-down list, select the G/L account that you want the 

system to use for revenue transactions. When you select an account, the system completes 

the G/L account field with the selected account in revenue transactions, but you can change 

it. 

If your system is an international system, the A/R account drop-down list appears instead.

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

To use an alternative A/R account to override the default G/L A/R account, select it in the 

A/R account drop-down list. The system populates the A/R override account you select 
here to every invoice or adjustment transaction that includes this customer. See 
Overriding the G/L account in A/R transactions (on page 522 ) for more information.  
In Accounts Receivable, this feature applies to invoices and adjustments only. It doesn ’t

3.

Viewing Customer Credit Limits and On Hold Status 

If you have implemented credit limits for your customers, you can run a Customer List report to 

see which customers have exceeded their credit limits and which are currently placed on credit 

hold. 

To run a report showing which customers have exceeded their credit limits and/or are currently 

placed on credit hold: 

1. 
Click the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click Customer listing. 

3. 
To show results for a specific customer type, click the Customer Type drop-down box, and 

then click the vendor type you want the report to include. 

Consultants and distributors are two examples of vendor types. 

4. 
To show results for a specific vendor or range of customer, use the From Customer and To 

Customer drop-down boxes. 

5. 
Select the Show Only Customers Exceeding Credit Limit check box if you want the report 

to display only those customers who are exceeding their credit limit. 

6. 
Select the Show Only Customers on Hold check box if you want the report to display only 

those customers whose accounts are on hold. 

7. 
Select the check box for each category of data to display in your report. 

8. 
Click View. 

Why view customers who have exceeded their credit limits? 

• 
You have recently implemented the credit limit feature and want to see if any of your 

customers exceed their new limits. 

• 
To enforce credit limits, you have chosen to allow transactions that exceed the credit limit 

and display only a warning message. In that case, you may have customers who exceed their 

credit limits as time goes by, and you can use this report to monitor that. 

Similarly, you might want to show only those customers that you have explicitly placed on credit 

hold.

Restrictions Tab 

In a multi-entity shared company, you can use the Restrictions tab to select which entities should 

be able to view each customer. You can choose from the following options: 

• 
Unrestricted customer: Visible to all entities at all levels. 

• 
Restricted to top-level only: Visible only to the top-level entity. 

• 
Restricted customer: Activates Location/Location group and Department/department 

group selection boxes.  

Selected locations or departments will be able to view this customer. See Using the 

multi-select box (on page 596) for help on selecting locations and departments. 

When setting up location groups or department groups, keep in mind that restrictions can 
be based on groups that contain specific locations or departments, but can ’t be based on 
groups that filter dynamically based on the value of certain fields (such as locations where 
the status equals “Active ”). Location groups and department groups that contain dynamic 
filtering won’t appear on the Restrictions tab for you to select. 

For field-level help, see Field-by-field descriptions (on page 52). 

Setting Up Customers in a Multi-Entity Shared Company 

In a multi-entity, shared company, the customers that you see in the Customers list will depend 

on whether you are at the top level or one of the entities. In this type of company structure, 

customers can be shared among all entities, restricted to the top level, or restricted to particular 

entities. 

Set Up Customers at the Top Level  

In many cases, it is simplest to set up a shared customer list at the top level and then specify 

which entity or entities can view each customer using the visibility feature. See Customer Visibility 

List (on page 89). 

You can no longer create customers directly at the entity level. When you display the Customers 

list from the top level, you’ll see customers that were created at the top level and at the entity 

level. Customers were previously allowed to be created at the entity level, and customer records 

may still be associated only with an entity. To hide items created at the entity level, clear the 

Include Private check box. 

Include Private Does Not Appear on Your Page 

The most common reason that you don’t see this feature is because you’re using a custom view. 

When you select a custom view, some options are hidden. Depending on the page you’re on, the 

Include inactive, Include one-time, Include private, and Display hierarchy options aren’t visible. 

For example, if you’re viewing from a custom view, the Financial Reports list won’t provide the 

Include inactive option.

#### Viewing and Organizing Related Customers in a Hierarchical View
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 49*

Chapter 2: Customers 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Viewing and Organizing Related Customers in a Hierarchical View 

Some lists, such as customers, vendors, and projects, can display a hierarchical structure of 

parent-child relationships using icons and indentations. For example, you might want to view a list 

that displays customers as subsidiaries of the same parent company. Also, you might purchase 

goods or services from subsidiaries or divisions of the same company and need to separately 

track their contact and payment information. Also, you might want to see an inventory item, 

including all its subcomponents, at a glance. 

Parent items can have up to five levels of child items, allowing you to view and act on the items as 

needed. You can still sort and search for items as you would in any view. 

If the parent isn’t visible because of permission restrictions, or if you filtered the list in a way that 

the parent isn’t visible, the system still shows that the child as indented and colored to indicate 

that it is a child in a relationship. 

To toggle between a flat and hierarchical view of a list 

When a list has hierarchical items, the default view is hierarchical. 

• 
To switch to a flat view, clear the Display hierarchy check box on the white bar above the 

list. Clearing the check box causes all items to be displayed by their unique ID, whether or 

not they have relationships to other items. 

• 
To return to the hierarchical view, select the Display hierarchy check box. 

When Display Hierarchy Is Not on Your Page 

The most common reason that you don’t see this feature is because you’re using a custom view.  

When you select a custom view, some options are hidden. Depending on the page you’re on, the 

Include inactive, Include one-time, Include private, and Display hierarchy options aren’t visible. 

For example, if you’re viewing from a custom view, the Financial Reports list won’t provide the 

Include inactive option.  

To see the options again, switch back to View All. See Custom list views (on page 574) for more.

Attachments 
An attachment is a bundle of one or more supporting files. It can include

or delete an attachment or continue to add or delete files in an

Fill in the Customer Group Details 

1.

When displayed elsewhere in the system, the customer group will be listed with the ID and 

name together (ID--Name), as in NAOPS--North America Operations. IDs can’t be changed 

once you’ve saved the group, but you can edit the name at a later time.  

2. 
(Optional) Enter any description that will remind you of what this group includes or how it’s 

used.  

3. 
From the Group type drop-down menu, select the type of group you want to create and 

then define the group.  

• 
Select Specific members if you want to hand pick the customers to include in the 

group. 

• 
Select All members if you want to filter based on criteria of your choice. For example, 

you might define a Direct Customers group which includes all members but then 

filters the results to include only customers where the Customer Type field is equal to 

Direct.  

To include all active members of a group, select All members as the group type. Then, in the 
Filters section, select Status as the Field, equals as the Operator, and Active as the Value. 

Learn more about determining what’s in a group (on page 68). 

4. 
(Optional) Specify how dimension members should be sorted when displayed in reports. 

The display order for members is controlled by how you define the group. 

If the group type is All Members, then members are sorted in ascending order based on ID 

by default, but you can change the sort order. For example, you might want to sort a 

customer group in Ascending order based on the Last Name field.  

If the group type is Specific members, then to define the sort order, set the Sort order to 

Ascending or Descending, and then choose the field to use for sorting. Members display in 

the order they appear in the Members list. Learn how to add customers to a customer group 

(on page 74).  

5. 
Select the Dimension structure option to automatically create a dimension structure that 

enables the group to be used on the rows or columns of financial reports. You can later find 


> **Navigation Path:** `your dimension structures by going to Reports > Setup > Dimensions and then the name`


of the dimension. If you don’t create a dimension structure for the group, you will be able to 

use the group only for filtering.  

6. 
Set up the customer group’s filters if desired. Group filters can determine which customers 

are included in the group. For information, see Filtering Groups (on page 65). 

7. 
Click the Save button.

#### Filtering Groups
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 65*

Chapter 2: Customers 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Filtering Groups 

Use filters on dimension groups to affect what appears in reports. This page describes a few 

examples of how you can apply filters to dimension groups. You can: 

• 
Filter with field values. 

• 
Filter for employees, locations, or departments managed by the current user. 

• 
Combine multiple filters. 

• 
Create dimension groups that contain both active and inactive members (on page 67). 

Filtering with Field Values 

You can add filters that select dimension members based on the value of certain fields. For 

example, you might want to select customers of a certain type or vendors that have a payment 

priority of urgent. 

1. 
Select the field you want to filter on. 

2. 
Choose the operation and value you want to filter for. 

The options you’ll see depend on the field you choose. 

By default, if you add more than one filter, members are included only if they match all 

criteria. However, you can change this behavior using the options in the Filter conditions 

section. 

Filtering for Employees, Locations, or Departments Managed by the Current User 

Dimension groups can automatically show managers only the information that’s relevant to them. 

For example, you can set up an Employee dimension group called My employees, which 

dynamically filters for employees managed by the current user. Similarly, groups can be used to 

filter for departments or locations managed by the current user. 

The current user is the user who is currently logged into the system. 

When you set the filter to current user, you limit the user to see only the group—such as 

employees or locations—that is associated with the user. For example, if you set a filter where the 

field is Manager and the operator is current user, when the manager runs the report, he or she will 

only see his or her own employees. To create a group that filters for the current user: 

1. 
Create a new group of type Department or Location. 

2. 
Define the group by giving it a name that users will recognize. 

For example — My department. 

3. 
In the Filters section, select a field that is connected to an employee who is a user in the 

system. For Department or Location dimension groups, you can select the Manager field. 

Not all contact fields are connected to a user. For this reason, filtering for the current 
user is restricted to the Manager field. 

---


<!-- Page 66 -->
Customers 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

4. 
Set the Operator to is current user. 

Combining Multiple Filters 

If you have multiple filters, the default behavior is to match only members that meet all of the 

criteria. However, you can change how this works using the Filter conditions section. 

Filter Conditions 

All (AND) 
Include members that match all criteria (the default). 

Any (OR) 
Include members that match any criteria. 

Expression 
Uses an expression that you define to apply the filters. 

For example, the following expression matches members that either meet criteria 1 

and 2, or that meet criteria 3. 

(1 AND 2) OR 3 

If you want to select one of something, such as departments where the manager is either Jim, 
Sue, or Terri, create several filters and use the Any (OR) filter condition. 

---

*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 67*

Creating a Dimension Group Filter for Both Active and Inactive Members 

If you want to include inactive dimensions in reports, you can create a dimension group that 

filters for both active and inactive members. To do this: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the Dimension groups section, select the dimension type to filter (for example, 

departments or locations.) 

3. 
Select the dimension group to filter, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
In the Filters section, create two filters: 

• 
Status equals active  

• 
Status equals inactive 

Make sure the filter conditions are set to All (AND). 

5. 
Save your changes. 

You can use this group when you want the system to include both active and inactive 

members in a report.

criteria. If the group is based on a manual selection of customers, you can add another customer 

to the group using this method.

Click the Applications menu, and then select Reports. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab. 

3. 
In the Dimension groups section, click Customer.

Locate the customer group to which you want to add a member.  

5. 
Click the Edit link next to the customer group. 

6. 
In the Members section, in the Members column, click the last row. The drop-down list 

appears. 

7. 
Click the drop-down list and select the customer you want to add to the group. 

If you don’t see the customer in the list, click the Find option to open the Select customer 

list and search for the customer. If you still don’t find it, click Cancel to close the box.  

You can add a new customer record from here. Re-open the drop-down list and click Add to 

add a new Customer record. 

8. 
Click the Save button to save the changes to the customer group.

### Customer Types List
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 79*



#### Before You Begin

Chapter 2: Customers

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Customer Types List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Types`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Customer Management > Types`


Use the Customer types list to add and manage customer types. 

Customer types allow you to group customers into categories, such as reseller and end user. With 

customer types, you can quickly manage and report customer information. For example, you can 

sort lists based on customer type or suppress unused types from appearing in lists and in reports. 

By setting up customer types with parent types, you can create a hierarchy that reflects how you 

like your customers organized. The Standard Industrial Classification code is an example of an 

official standard for classifying vendors (suppliers); however, you can create a hierarchy that 

reflects the unique characteristics of your business.  

For multi-entity shared companies 
Customer types are a master object. Master objects can either be common (that is, accessible) 
to all entities or exclusive (private) to a specific entity. In multi -entity shared companies with 
multiple base currencies, we recommend that you create customer types at the top level to be 
shared across all the entities. Creating customer types in an entity restricts them to that 
entity. If you do create them in an entity, use a naming convention to differentiate them from 
the top level customer types. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with customer type records: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Accounts Receivable 
Customer types 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 584) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions.

Customers in a Multi-Entity Shared Company 

In a multi-entity, shared company, the customers that you see in the Customers list will depend 

on whether you are at the top level or one of the entities. In this type of company structure, 

customers can be shared among all entities, restricted to the top level, or restricted to particular 

entities.  

Set Up Customers and Then Restrict Where Necessary 

In many cases, it is simplest to set up a shared customer list at the top level and then specify 

which entity or entities can view each customer using the visibility feature. See Customer Visibility 

List (on page 89). 

You can no longer create customers directly at the entity level. When you display the Customers 

list from the top level, you’ll see customers that were created at the top level and at the entity 

level. Customers were previously allowed to be created at the entity level, and customer records 

may still be associated only with an entity. To hide customer records created at the entity level, 

clear the Include Private check box. 

When you edit a record that was created in an entity, your changes apply to that entity. After you 

save your changes, you are returned to the top level. 

Customer Visibility 

The Customer visibility page enables you to view, edit, mass update, and manage multi-entity 

restrictions for customers. 

Make sure to enable customer restrictions in the Multi Entity Console configuration. This first 
step is required when you want to use restrictions. For information, see Enabling customer 
restrictions (on page 87 ). 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with customer type records: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts Receivable 
Customer types 
List, View 

Add and Edit permissions are required only for 

importing customer restriction records.

Creating the List View that Includes the Data You Want to Export 

To control what gets exported, you can create a custom view of the Customer visibility list that 

includes just the data you want to see.  

To customize a view before exporting: 

1. 
Locate the Manage views drop-down menu at the top of the Customer visibility list, and 

then choose Create New View.  

2. 
On Step 1 of the Create New View wizard, select the columns of data you want to include.  

You can choose from standard customer fields (such as name and ID) and any custom fields 

that you’ve created for your company.  

3. 
Make other changes as needed.  

Using the wizard, you can:  

• 
Choose the order in which columns appear.  

• 
Filter the list of customer restrictions, such as filtering for customers who are 

unrestricted, or customers who can be viewed by top level only.  

• 
Choose the sort order for columns, for example, sorting customers by ID or Visibility.

Required Fields for New Customer Restrictions 

When you’re adding new customers, the following columns are required:  

• 
Customer ID: The identifier field for all other values  

• 
Visibility: The type of restriction: Unrestricted, Root Only, or Restricted  

• 
Required custom fields: If you’ve created any custom fields that are required, you must also 

include these columns.  

Guidelines for Updating Customer Restrictions 

The most important thing to remember when updating customer restriction records through CSV 

import is that changes you make in the spreadsheet will affect your customer restriction records.  

• 
If you update spreadsheet data for a customer restriction, the information you specify will 

overwrite the data in the existing customer restriction record.  

• 
If you remove data from the spreadsheet, the corresponding information will be removed 

from the customer restriction record.  

Don’t overwrite existing data with blank data unless you intend to remove that data from 
your Customer visibility list. For example, if you export a number of customer restrictions 
that include a location, and then clear the data in the associated location column of your 
spreadsheet, those existing location restrictions will be deleted when you import the file.  

Recommended precautions:  

• 
Make a backup of your customer restriction information before you make changes. Save a 

copy of the CSV for Import spreadsheet so that you have a record of the Customer visibility 

list before you update it.  

• 
Before making large-scale changes, test the update process. Try changing a few test 

customer restrictions and then update just those customer records.  

Additional tips:  

• 
When you export the CSV for Import file, be sure to include the Customer ID column. This 

identifies the customer record that you are updating.  

• 
Column order isn’t important; for example, the Customer ID field doesn’t need to be first. 

The header row identifies the contents of each column.  

• 
When you’re updating the CSV for Import file, keep in mind that different types of fields 

require different information. For check box options, enter TRUE to select the option and 

enter FALSE to deselect the option.

Printing Customer Visibility Details 

To display the Customer visibility list:

Printing a record creates an electronic PDF file that you can view on your computer, send 
as an email attachment, and so on. Use your PDF reader program to print a hard copy of 
the document if desired.  

Updating Multiple Customer Visibility Records 

RealPage Accounting allows you to update multiple customer visibility records as a group. 

By exporting the existing customer visibility list to a CSV file, you can quickly update all 

customer’s restrictions in your favorite spreadsheet application. After updating the data, just save 

the file in CSV format again, and import the file right from the Customer visibility list.  

By default, visibility is set to Unrestricted. To restrict customer visibility, you will need a list of 

locations and departments that are allowed to see the customer records you want to restrict.  

The following procedures walk you through each step of the process in detail.

Saving a Transaction as a Draft 

When you are not ready to post that A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or adjustment, you can save the 

transaction as a draft without affecting the G/L or any subledger. With the ability to save 

transactions in draft state, you can save your progress so far. Later on, you or another user can 

come back and post the transaction.  

The system validates transactions only when they are posted. For example, required departments 

or locations are not validated until posting.  

Prerequisites: Your ability to add a transaction in draft state or post a transaction depends on 

your permissions:  

Add permission enables you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as a draft.  

Add, Edit, and Post permissions enable you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as draft, 

and edit and post the transaction when you’re ready.  

To save a transaction in draft format:  

1. 
Add an A/R invoice, A/P invoice, or adjustment to your company.  

2. 
Save the transaction as a draft by clicking the Draft button.  

3. 
Select: 

• 
Draft & Continue to save the transaction and continue working on it. 

• 
Draft to save your progress on the transaction without posting it to the system.  

• 
Draft & New to save the transaction and create a new transaction of the same type. 

The system saves your progress on the transaction without posting it. 

Saving a transaction as a draft allows you or another user to review and post the transaction 

later.

#### Editing an A/R Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 108*

Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Editing an A/R Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > A/R Invoices > Edit`


The most important elements of the A/R invoice appear at the top of the page, such as the 

invoice date, due date, number of days that the payment is overdue, invoice total, amount paid, 

and amount due.  

You can edit most aspects of an invoice or only partially edit it based on its state: 

• 
Full edit: If the state is Drafted or No Value and the period is open, then you can change 

most aspects, including the associated account. 

If the state is Posted, then other factors affect whether you can edit the invoice and what 

you can edit, such the application in which the invoice originates, and whether the period is 

open or closed. In some cases, if the invoice originated in another application, then the 

invoice can be edited, but what you can change is limited. In other cases, you cannot edit 

the invoice. In such cases, you would have to delete or reverse the invoice and start over. 

• 
Partial edit: For other states, you can only change aspects that don’t affect the G/L, such as 

the invoice number, term, or memo. However, if the invoice has been partially paid or fully 

paid, you might be able to click Reclassify to change the G/L account label, the department, 

or the location. (You see the Reclassify button only if your company has opted to add the 

reclassification feature, and you have permission to reclassify this type of transaction.) 

When you can’t edit a posted invoice  

You can’t edit a posted invoice under any of the following conditions: 

• 
The period is closed. 

• 
You don’t have the relevant permissions. 

• 
The posted invoice was created at the top level, and you’re working at the entity level. 

When you can edit a posted invoice 

You can make limited changes to a posted invoice under any of the following conditions: 

• 
Payment and allocations. If cash or an allocation has been applied to a posted invoice, then 

you can only edit the following fields in the invoice: 

• 
Reference number 

• 
Description 

• 
Term 

• 
Due date - Changing the due date of a paid A/R invoice does not affect late fees.  

• 
Attachments 

• 
Memo 

You can also edit a paid A/R invoice to reclassify segments.

#### Deleting or Reversing Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 113*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Deleting or Reversing Invoices 

On occasion, you may need to remove an invoice. Perhaps it was mistakenly entered, or you 

cannot edit or reclassify the invoice to your satisfaction and need to remove the invoice and 

recreate it. To remove an invoice, you either:  

• 
Delete the invoice: Completely removes the record of the invoice from the system. Deleting 

completely removes the record of the invoice. You can delete invoices with a Draft or Posted 

state.  

• 
Reverse the invoice: Creates a record in the system that allows you to track changes and 

maintain an audit trail. 

The action you take depends on the state of the invoice and whether your A/R configuration is 

enabled for the reversal of unpaid invoices. When reversal is enabled, you can reverse all invoices 

except those in Draft state. 

Summary: When to Delete and When to Reverse 

Whether you delete or reverse an invoice depends on your A/R configuration and the state of the 

invoice. After a transaction is cleared, after reconciliation, you can no longer delete or reverse the 

transaction.  

From the A/R invoices list, you can only delete or reverse invoices that were directly entered in 
Accounts Receivable.

Viewing an Invoice’s State 

To view the invoice state: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select A/R Invoices. The system opens the list of invoices. 

3. 
On the Invoices page, check the State column for the appropriate invoice.  

From the A/R invoices list, you can only delete or reverse invoices that were directly entered in 
Accounts Receivable.  

Configuring Invoices for Reversal 

To track changes and maintain an audit trail, you can reverse unpaid invoices instead of deleting 

them. Your company can be configured to enable reversal of unpaid invoices, which means that a 

transaction can only be reversed, not deleted, unless it is in Draft or Posted state.  

The reversal process uses the A/R account and the revenue account. The A/R and revenue 

accounts are defined on Accounts Receivable Configuration page.  

Example of a Reversal Entry 

When you reverse an invoice, the system automatically creates the required adjustment to the A/R 

account targeted in the transaction. If you want to target a different A/R account, you can leave 

the transaction as is and create a manual adjustment. For example, if you create an invoice and 

then learn that you’re never going to receive payment on it, you might want to create a manual 

adjustment that targets a bad-debt A/R Account.  

To enable reversal:  

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab. 

3. 
Select Configuration. 

4. 
In the Enable functionality section, select Enable reversal of unpaid invoices.  

5. 
Click the Save button.

When this check box is enabled, you cannot delete invoices.

Clearing a Negative Invoice 

1. Apply the Credit to an Open Invoice 

If the customer has another invoice due: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select A/R Invoices. 

3. 
Find the desired invoice. 

4. 
Click Apply Payment. 

5. 
Select the negative invoice (credit) to apply. 

6. 
Confirm the change. 

7. 
Save the invoice.  

This reduces the balance of the open invoice using the credit. 

2. Issue a Refund (if no open invoice exists) 

If the customer has no outstanding invoices: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select A/P Invoices. 

3. 
Create a negative invoice to represent the refund. 

4. 
Post the invoice and process the payment to the customer.

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

This clears the credit from A/R and reflects the refund in your cash accounts. 

3. Reverse a Payment or Invoice (if entered incorrectly) 

If the negative invoice was created due to a mistake: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu. 

2. 
Click Payments. 

3. 
Find the desired payment, and then click Reverse. 

4. 
Choose the reversal date to match the original transaction. 

This creates a negative payment to offset the incorrect entry. 

If needed, you can also reverse the invoice itself: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select A/R Invoices. 

3. 
Find the invoice in the list, and then click Reverse. 

4. 
Select the reversal date and recreate the correct invoice. 

Reversing an Invoice 

Reversing an invoice allows you to track your changes and maintain an audit trail. The system 

retains the original invoice transaction and creates a new transaction that essentially zeros out the 

invoice. You can reverse invoices with the following states:  

• 
Posted, if the reversal of unpaid invoices is enabled (if your A/R configuration is not enabled 

for the reversal of unpaid invoices, you see a Delete check box instead)  

• 
Partially paid  

• 
Paid  

• 
No value  

The steps to reverse an invoice depend on whether the invoice is unpaid or paid.  

After you reverse an invoice, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can create another invoice 

to replace it.  

An invoice with a state of Posted or No value is unpaid. It doesn’t have an associated payment.

#### Reversing a Paid Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 120*

Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reversing a Paid Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Payments`


An invoice with a state of Partially paid or Paid has an associated payment. To reverse a paid 

invoice, locate and reverse the payment, and then reverse the invoice. This method works for a 

payment regardless of type, whether it is a cash payment, credit card payment, Paymode-X 

payment, RealPage payment, ACH/EFT/BACS payment, Third Party payment, payment with a 

printed check, payment with a manual check, or a Petty cash reimbursement. 

Alternatively, you can also reverse the invoice during the process of reversing the payment. Learn 

more about reversing a posted payment (on page 295).  

To reverse a paid invoice requires two steps.  

1. 
Reverse the payment on the invoice. 

2. 
Reverse the invoice. 

Step 1: Reverse the payment on the invoice 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select Payments. The system opens the list of posted payments. 

3. 
In the list of Posted Payments, click Reverse beside the appropriate row. The Transaction 

Reversal Date box opens.  

4. 
Review the reversal date and memo, making any changes you might need.  

• 
Reverse the transaction on date: Select the date for reversing the transaction. This is 

usually the original transaction date or a later date.  

• 
Memo: We recommend that you enter the reason for the reversal.  

5. 
Click Submit.  

The system retains the original payment transaction and creates a new transaction that 

essentially zeros out the payment, which provides an audit trail. Now the invoice has no 

payment associated with it. You can reverse it.

#### Using Transaction Allocations
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 125*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Using Transaction Allocations 

Create a transaction allocation if one does not already exist. The new transaction allocation 

appears in your list of allocations, and you can select it when you allocate an A/R invoice, an A/P 

invoice, or a journal entry. The system automatically applies the distribution you specified when 

you created this transaction allocation. For more information, see Defining transaction allocations 

(on page 234). 

1. 
Select the line item and select the transaction allocation to use.  

After you’ve selected a transaction allocation, the system removes any dimension values 

selected for the line item. Instead, it populates the dimension values from the transaction 

allocation directly. 

2. 
To change the dimensions for the line item, click the Show details tab, and click Customize 

allocation. 

Even when a transaction allocation with a predetermined distribution of amounts is assigned to 
a line item, you can still override these amounts. You can also override aspects of the allocation 
at the line item level of the relevant transaction page (A/R invoices, A/P invoices, or journal 
entries). 

Transaction allocations enable you to automatically distribute transaction amounts across multiple 

dimensions such as departments or locations. 

For example, you might apply an allocation to an insurance A/P invoice in order to distribute costs 

across several sales offices. The amounts of that A/P invoice are then automatically distributed 

across the appropriate locations. 

This topic assumes that the allocations you want to apply have been previously created. If you’re 
new to allocations, review the allocations overview and learn how to define allocations (on page 
234 ). 

To use the allocation on the transaction: 

1. 
Select the allocation on the line item.  

After you’ve selected the allocation, the system removes any dimension values selected for 

the line item. Instead, it populates the dimension values from the allocation directly.  

To change the dimensions for the line item: 

1. 
Click the Show details tab. 

2. 
Click Customize allocation.  

Even when an allocation with a predetermined distribution of amounts is assigned to a line 

item, you can still override these amounts. You can also override aspects of the allocation at 

the line item level of the relevant transaction page (A/P invoices, A/R invoices, or journal 

entries).

#### Editing an Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 136*

Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide

Editing an Invoice 

The most frequently edited elements of the invoice appear at the top of the page, such as the 

customer balance, invoice date, due date, invoice total, amount paid, and amount due.  

You can navigate into payment details for partially or fully paid invoices. 

You can also delete or reverse an invoice to clear it. 

To edit an invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select AR Invoices. The system opens the list of invoices. 

3. 
On the Invoices list, locate the invoice you want to edit, and click Edit. The system displays 

the Invoice page with information about the invoice. 

4. 
Add, modify, or delete information as needed. For details, go to Field-by-field descriptions. 

(on page 126) 

You can edit all aspects of an invoice or only partially edit it based on its state: 

• 
Full edit: If the state is Drafted, Posted or No Value and the period is open, you can change 

any aspect including the associated account. 

• 
Partial edit: For other states, you can only change aspects that don’t affect the G/L, for 

example, the invoice number, term, or memo. However, if the invoice has been partially paid 

or fully paid, you might be able to click Reclassify to change the G/L Account Label, the 

department, or the location. (You see the Reclassify button only if your company has opted 

to add the reclassification feature, and you have permission to reclassify this type of 

transaction.) 

If you can’t edit or reclassify the invoice (on page 139) to your satisfaction, you might have to 

delete or reverse the invoice and start over.

#### Reclassifying Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 139*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Reclassifying Invoices 

Reclassification typically happens when an invoice was coded to a valid but incorrect G/L account 

— meaning the expense or revenue was recorded in the wrong category. The goal is to move it to 

the right account without changing the total amount or vendor record. 

Typical examples of reclassification include: 

• 
Reclassify a Utilities Expense to Repairs & Maintenance when the charge was for equipment 

servicing rather than usage. 

• 
Reclassify Rental income to Other income for non-rent charges such as late fees. 

• 
Reclassify Security Deposits Payable to Tenant Refunds Payable when the deposit was 

returned. 

What You Can Reclassify 

You can reclassify A/R and A/P invoices and adjustments. 

• 
Reclassifying an A/R invoice enables you to change how revenues are assigned for an 

invoice that was paid or partially paid.  

• 
Reclassifying an A/P invoice enables you to change how expenses are assigned for an A/P 

invoice that was paid or partially paid.  

For example, when you reclassify an A/P invoice, you could assign line items to different G/L 

accounts, or change the department, location, or other dimensions..  

When to Reclassify 

Consider reclassifying a transaction:  

• 
When the transaction is initially recorded in the wrong account. 

• 
When there’s a change in the accounting period. 

• 
When adjustments are needed to reflect the proper allocation of revenue or expenses. This 

ensures that financial statements accurately represent the company’s financial position and 

comply with accounting standards.  

Who Can Reclassify 

Only users who have special permission can reclassify invoices. They can edit accounting 

information on both partially and fully paid invoices. You can update almost anything on the A/P 

invoice except for the amount and the payment date. For example, if the A/P invoice was assigned 

to the wrong department, you can choose a different department from the drop-down menu. 

Accessing the Reclassify Function 

In the Financial Suite, you can reclassify a single invoice or adjustment, or you can reclassify 

several invoices or adjustments at the same time 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 140*

You can reclassify a single invoice or adjustment from the A/R Invoices or A/P invoices lists. Edit 

the invoice that you want to reclassify and click the Reclassify button. See Reclassifying an Invoice 

(on page 143). 

You can reclassify multiple transactions at the same time using the Invoice Reclassification menu 

option. See Reclassifying Multiple Invoices. 

Things to Keep in Mind When Reclassifying Transactions 

• 
Do not change the transaction total or vendor. 

• 
Always add a memo that explains why you reclassified the transaction. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

How to Get Here

Open the Accounts Receivable menu.

Select the A/R invoices option.

1.

Why You Can’t Find the Reclassify Option 

There are a couple of reasons why you might not see the option to reclassify invoices. Contact 

your system administrator for help with resolving the issue. 

Check Your Accounts Receivable Configuration 

Accounts receivable may not have been configured to allow reclassification of invoices. 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Accounts receivable. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab. 

3. 
Select Configuration. 

4. 
In the Enable functionality section, select the Enable reclassification for invoices and 

adjustments check box. 

5. 
Click the Save button. 

Check Your Accounts Payable Configuration 

Accounts payable may not have been configured to allow reclassification of invoices. 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Accounts payable. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab. 

3. 
Select Configuration. 

4. 
In the Enable functionality section, select the Enable reclassification for invoices and 

adjustments check box. 

5. 
Click the Save button.

#### Multi-entity or Multi-currency Restrictions
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 142*

Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Check Your Permissions 

You might not have permissions to reclassify invoices. If you do not have access to your user 

record, ask your system administrator to check your permissions. 

1. 
Locate your user record. 

2. 
Edit your subscriptions. 

3. 
Open Accounts receivable permissions. 

4. 
Make sure that you have permissions to edit and reclassify invoices in Accounts receivable. 

5. 
Open Accounts payable permissions. 

6. 
Make sure that you have permissions to edit and reclassify invoices in Accounts payable. 

7. 
Save your changes. 

Multi-entity or Multi-currency Restrictions 

There are a few limitations on reclassifying invoices in multi-entity or multi-currency companies. If 

you aren’t able to make the change that you need by reclassifying, you can reverse the invoice (on 

page 117).

Reclassifying One Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Edit > Reclassify`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > A/R Invoices > Edit > Reclassify`


You can reclassify both A/R and A/P invoices to update almost anything except for the amount 

and the payment date. An exception is reclassifying an A/R invoice when the payment has been 

deposited. The only fields that you can reclassify on a paid A/R invoice include: 

• 
Account 

• 
Segments 

• 
Any standard dimension (location, department, customer, employee, vendor) 

Reclassification Examples 

• 
If the invoice was assigned to the wrong department, you can choose a different 

department from the drop-down menu. 

• 
In Accounts Receivable, you can reclassify the A/R invoice and change the location to a 

different city. Only the location listed on the A/R invoice changes to the different city. The 

location listed on the originating sales invoice in the purchase order does not change. The 

original location listing is permanent. You cannot open the original sales invoice and change 

the location manually. 

Reclassifying an A/P invoice that was generated in Spend Management does not affect the 
original purchase order.  

To reclassify an invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable or Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select A/R invoices or A/P invoices. 

3. 
Click Edit next to a Paid or Partially paid invoice that you want to reclassify. 

To reclassify an A/P invoice, its status must be Paid or Partially paid. 

4. 
Click Reclassify. 

5. 
Update the invoice details as needed. 

You can also add a Segment type and Segment value at this time. 

When you reclassify a transaction, you can’t split lines or add new lines. 

When You Can’t Change a 1099 Option 
Make sure that Enable override of the 1099 flag on an A/P line item is selected in A/P 
configuration. For other reclassification issues, see Troubleshooting Reclassification (on page 
144 ).

#### Creating a Recurring Transaction from an Existing Transaction
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 149*

Duplicating an Invoice 

Sometimes it is easier and faster to add a record by duplicating an existing one, and editing the 

duplicate than creating a new record from scratch. You can view and access a list of invoices from 

the Invoices list. 

To duplicate an invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section of the menu, select A/R Invoices. The list of invoices opens. 

3. 
On the A/R Invoices list, find the invoice that you want to copy, and click Edit. The system 

opens the A/R Invoice page. 

4. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system opens a copy of the invoice. 

5. 
Change the data in the invoice as needed to differentiate it from the original invoice. 

6. 
Save the invoice as a draft or post it.  

Creating a Recurring Transaction from an Existing Transaction 

You can create a recurring transaction that is based on an existing transaction. 

To create a recurring transaction: 

1. 
Find the transaction that you want to make a recurring transaction. 

2. 
Click the Edit link next to the transaction. 

3. 
Click the More actions button, and then select Create recurring transaction. 

4. 
Change any information as needed. 

5. 
Click the Schedule tab. 

6. 
In Start Date, click the Calendar, and then select the first date on which you want this 

invoice to be generated. 

7. 
In Repeats, select the frequency in which the transaction is to recur: 

• 
To have the invoice occur only once, select None. You may want to select none if you 

are setting up an invoice for an item that might be recurring such as a 30-day trial for 

a new service. Later you can choose to change the schedule if the service becomes an 

ongoing expense. 

• 
To have the invoice occur at regular intervals, select Days, Weeks, End of month, 

Months, or Years, and then type the number of intervals in the adjacent text box. 

For instance, if an invoice only occurs every other month, select Months and type 2. If 

you select a time period but do not type a number, the system will default to 1. 

---

For weeks, months, and years, the invoice will recur at the next interval on the same 

day as the start date. For instance, if you set an invoice to start on the 15th of the 

month and recur monthly, the system generates the invoice each month on the 15th.  

• 
To make an invoice with a month’s interval generate at the end of the month, select 

End of Month. 

8. 
Click Save.

Finding Draft or Posted Transactions 

There are two easy ways to locate and view items in the draft and posted state.  

Filter for Draft or Posted Transactions on the Fly 

In the appropriate transaction list view, enter either Draft or Posted in the State column, then 

press Enter. The list displays only those items you filtered for.  

Create a Permanent Custom View that Filters for Draft or Posted Transactions 

Create a view, and then set the filter to State = Draft or State = Posted. The custom view is 

available for use whenever you go to the list.  

Quick Editing 

The most important elements of the invoice appear at the top of the page: 

• 
customer balance 

• 
invoice date 

• 
due date 

• 
invoice total 

• 
amount paid 

• 
amount due 

You can drill down to payment details for partially or fully paid invoices.  

Applying Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > A/R Invoices > Apply Payment`


If you have an invoice for which you’d like to quickly apply a payment, you can start the process 

directly from the Invoices list page or from the Invoice page itself. The system automatically filters 

for just that invoice and auto-populates it to the Select invoices for payment page.  

If you have multiple invoices or debit memos for which you want to apply payment, such as for 

the same customer, use the normal select-invoices-for-payment process.  

To apply a payment to an invoice from the Invoices list 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select A/R Invoices. The system opens the list of invoices.  

Invoices that are eligible for payments display an Apply payment link near the end of the 
row. 

3. 
Click Apply payment. The Select Invoices for Payment page opens with the invoice 

information completed by the system. 

4. 
Type the amount to apply, and then select or edit other options as required.

To receive a subsidy payment:

Open the Accounts Receivable menu.

3. 
Select the payment method. 

4.

5.

you selected. These are the fields that appear when the payment method was Check.

Receipt date

Check amount

Check #

4030.00--Rent from Subsidy / Third Party. 

7.

does not cover the full rent, enter the partial amount in the Amount received field.

Billing a Customer for an A/P Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All`


To forward an A/P invoice for a customer (tenant) to pay: 

1. 
Create a new A/R invoice (on page 100). 

2. 
Add the A/P invoice number to the Reference number field. 

3. 
Attach the A/P invoice to the A/R invoice. 

4.

### Packaging Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 160*

Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Packaging Invoices 

This section describes how to create a package of invoices. You can create a package of A/P or 

A/R invoices. 

Use this feature when you need to provide a set of invoices to another party. Many customers use 

this feature to create a package of invoices for stakeholders. Customers who do not own the Job 

Cost and Reserves application can use the packaging feature to collect a set of invoices for the 

draw request document bundle, which they then submit to the lender as a request to release 

funds. 

When you generate the package, you can specify the components that you want to include in the 

package: 

• 
Cover page: Include a cover page and either use the system default cover page or import a 

custom cover page. 

• 
Summary: This is a list of the invoices in the package. 

• 
Attachments: Include the attachments of the invoices in the package. 

• 
Printed invoice: For A/R invoice packages, you can include the A/R invoices in printable 

format. 

• 
Printed AP invoice: For A/P invoice packages, you can include the A/P invoices in printable 

format. 

• 
Payment information: For A/P invoice packages, you can include additional payment 

information. 

• 
Proof of payment: For A/P invoice packages, you can include the proof of payment 

information when it is available. 

• 
Include separator pages: You can choose to include or exclude pages between the invoices. 

The separator page contains this text “The following invoices are included in this package:”  

and it lists the invoices in the package with these details: vendor name, invoice number, 

invoice date, amount of the payment, payment method, payment number, and the number 

of documents associated with the invoice.  

Packaging the invoices does not change the status of the invoices or their presence in the 
invoices list. 

If you are packaging A/P invoices, you have the choice of saving the package of invoices in a ZIP 

file or a printable PDF file.  

A/R invoice packages are saved as PDF files and open in Adobe Acrobat after the system creates 

the package.  

Regardless of file format, the system saves the package in your browser’s default download 

location.  

---



#### Creating A/R Invoice Packages
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 161*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Creating A/R Invoice Packages 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Search & Find > A/R Invoices > Package 
Invoices`


Use the Package invoices button when you want to bundle a set of invoices. 

To select the invoices that you want to include in the A/R invoice package: 

1. 
Open the A/R Invoices list. 

2. 
Click the Package invoices button. 

3. 
Filter the list so that the invoices that you want to package are displayed in the list. 

4. 
Select the invoices to include in the package. 

After you have selected an invoice, three buttons appear: 

• 
Click the Show Only Selected Invoices button to remove any unselected invoices so 

that you see only the invoices that will be included in the package. This action cannot 

be undone. If you accidentally exclude an A/R invoice, you must cancel the package 

and then start over. 

• 
Click the Generate Package button to build the package. See Generating the A/R 

Invoice Package. 

• 
open the box where you can select the elements include in the package in addition to 

the invoices, including a cover page, summary, attachments, and a printed invoice. 

• 
Click the Cancel Package button to discard this package and return to the A/R 

invoices list. 

You can also click the Add button to begin creating A/R invoices. If approvals are enabled, 

then the A/R invoice must go through the approval process before being included in the 

package. 

To generate the package of selected A/R invoices: 

1. 
From the Package A/R invoices list, click the Generate Package button. The Generate 

invoice package box opens. 

2. 
In the Package name field, type a name that describes the package. 

• 
Select the Cover page check box if you want to include a cover page in the package. 

Click the Browse button to find and load a custom cover page. 

• 
Select the Summary check box to include a summary list of invoices in the package. 

• 
Select the Attachments check box to include any attachments on the invoice records 

in the package. 

• 
Select the Printed invoice check box to include printable versions of the A/R invoices 

in the package.

#### Moving In and Out of Packaging Invoices Mode
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 162*

Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide

• 
Select the Include separator page check box if you want the system to include a page 

between each invoice. The separator page contains this text “The document(s) that 

follow are for:” and then lists the details about the invoice that follows, including: 

Customer ID, Customer Name, Invoice Number, Invoice Date, and Invoice Amount.  

3. 
Click the Build Package button.  

The system saves the package to RealPage Document Director, and then downloads the 

package as a PDF in your browser’s default download location.  

You can open and print the PDF file or send the pdf in an email for further distribution. 

See Troubleshooting PDFs for information in the event that you have trouble opening the 
PDF file. 

Moving In and Out of Packaging Invoices Mode 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Package Invoices`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > A/R Invoices > Package Invoices`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > A/P Invoices > Package 
Invoices`


When you click the Package Invoices button, you enter into Packaging mode. If you choose 

another option from the menu and then return to invoices, the system displays the Package 

Invoices list, not the Invoices list. In other words, the invoices list will still be in Packaging mode. 

To return to the invoices list from the Package Invoices list, you can either generate the package 

or cancel the package. 

• 
When you generate a package, the system builds the package and saves it where your 

browser saves downloaded files, and then returns to the Invoices list. 

• 
You can cancel the current package, which leaves Packaging mode and returns to the 

invoice.

Multiple Invoices: Quick Invoice Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Quick A/R Invoice Entry`


You must be at an entity level to use this feature.  

Select the desired entity from the Top level menu. 

Quick A/R invoice entry enables you to create invoices after the fact. For example, you might have 

entered a large group of invoices through another system, and now want to get them quickly into 

the accounting system. 

When you enter invoices this way, the system automatically creates a summary based on your 

company preferences. 

What’s Next? 

• 
Creating Multiple Invoices (on page 173) 

• 
Selecting invoices for payment (on page 272) 

Before You Begin 

You must be at an entity level to use this feature.  

Select the desired entity from the Top level menu. 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have limited or full Administrator privileges to use the quick invoice entry page. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to use the quick invoice entry page: 

Application 
Activities/Lists Permissions 

Accounts Receivable 
Summaries 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete, Open, Close 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 584) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions.

transaction.

 Click to display the Select attachments box. This box allows you to filter and sort

 Click to attach a document that is not yet stored in the system.

 Roll over this button to view a quick summary of selected attachment’s details or 

click the button to view the full attachment details in a new window. 

• 
Select a document from the drop-down list and then click 
 Attachment to view it. 

When no document is selected, click 
 Attachment to display the Attachments for 

list. From this list you can view, open, and save a document that is stored in the 

system. 

7. 
Select the View the list in a separate window check box to display a new window for the list 

of invoices for fast entry pages.

Click Continue. The Quick A/R Invoice Entry page opens.

#### Creating Multiple Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 173*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Enter Invoices > Quick Invoice Entry > 
Continue`


Use the Quick invoice entry page to create several invoices quickly. 

Creating Multiple Invoices 

Use this method of creating invoices when you want to create multiple invoices from one entity 

quickly. You enter multiple invoices in the Quick Invoice Entry Preferences page.  

1. 
From the Level menu, select the desired entity. 

2. 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu. 

3. 
In the Daily tasks section, select Quick A/R invoice entry. The Quick A/R invoice entry 

preferences page opens.  

4. 
Click Continue. The Quick invoice entry page opens. 

Filling In the Header and Line Item Information 

For each invoice, enter header and line item information as follows: 

• 
Customer Name: Select the customer for the invoice. 

• 
Invoice date: The default date for the invoice is the current date. To change it, type a new 

date. 

• 
G/L posting date: Type the date that you want the invoice to be posted. 

• 
Amount: Enter the total amount of the invoice before entering line items. This is the total 

amount of the invoice. This can be a good check against the sum of the line item amounts. 

• 
Term: Select or enter the payment terms if terms apply to this invoice. 

• 
Due date: Type the date the invoice comes due. 

• 
Invoice number: Type the number the vendor assigned to the invoice to record an invoice 

number with the invoice record. The system can use the invoice number to prevent 

duplicate invoice entry. The system also prints the invoice number on the check remittance 

stub. 

• 
Reference number: Type a number to add a reference number by which the invoice can be 

filtered or searched. This can be a PO number, an associated project number, or anything 

that you may want to use to track this invoice. 

---


<!-- Page 174 -->
Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Description: Type a description for this group of charges. The system fills in the line items’ 

Memo fields with this text. You can change the line item memo text as needed. 

Filling In the Line Items 

Complete the line items for each line item of this invoice. 

1. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location or property where the cost was incurred. 

2. 
In the G/L Account drop-down list, select the account to categorize the charge. 

3. 
In Amount, type the cost of the item. 

4. 
To apply the charge to a specific department, click Department, and then select the 

department to which you want to attribute the charge. 

5. 
In the Memo field, you can either leave the text that the system automatically inserted from 

the Description field, or you can change the text as needed. 

If you have more than two charges to include on this invoice, you can add more rows. Type 
the number of rows that you need in the More rows field, and then click More rows. The 
rows you already entered, plus the number of blank rows that you requested open in a new 
window. For more information, see Adding multiple line items (on page 179 ). 

6. 
Click the Enter button. The summary of the invoice appears below the line items. 

If you selected View the list in a separate window in the Quick invoice entry preferences, 
the summary of invoices appears in a separate window instead of below the invoice entry 
form. 

As you add more invoices, they appear in the invoices list at the bottom of the page (or in 

the separate window if selected): 

While entering quick invoices, you can edit or delete any of the previously entered invoices. 

After posting the invoices, you can view, edit and reverse them as you would any other 

invoice. Go to Accounts receivable > All > Search & find > Invoices. 

You can only delete the invoices before you post them.  

7. 
After entering all invoices for the summary, double-check your manual calculations against 

the status bar values.

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to use recurring A/R invoices. 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Accounts Receivable 
Recurring Invoices 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 584) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

Adding a New A/R Recurring Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Recurring A/R Invoices > Add`


You can add a recurring AR invoice by clicking 
 Add next to the Recurring A/R Invoices option 

or by opening the Recurring A/R invoice list and then clicking the Add button. 

If the 
 Add does not appear, or if the Recurring invoices option does not appear on the menu 

at all, it may be because you are working in a multi-entity shared company.  

If your system is configured this way, open the Level menu and select the entity for which you 

want to create a recurring invoice. The system opens a new tab allowing you to work within the 

selected entity. Look for the 
 Recurring invoices option. If the option still does not appear, 

check your permissions or contact your system administrator. 

To add a recurring A/R invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Month end section, click Recurring A/R invoices.  

3. 
Click the Add button. The Recurring invoice page opens. The page has multiple tabs that 

contain different types of information about the invoice.  

Filling In the Invoice Tab 

1. 
In the Customer drop-down list, select an existing customer, or click Add to create a new 

customer record. The system fills in the Bill to Contact and Ship to Contact areas based on 

the information it finds in the Customer record, but you can change them here. To select a 

---


<!-- Page 187 -->
