RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

different value for either Bill-to or Ship-to contact, click the drop-down list, and then select 

the preferred contact. 

2. 
In the Customer message drop-down list, select a message that you want to appear on the 

invoice if needed. You can also click Add in the drop-down list and then add a new message 

that you want to use. 

3. 
In Reference number, type the customer’s purchase order number or another reference 

number, and description as needed.  

You can use the reference number to search, sort, and report on invoices.  

4. 
In Description, type a description of this transaction that will be helpful in the future. 

5. 
To include an invoice number, click Invoice Sequence Number, and then select an existing 

sequence type, or click Add to create a new sequence number.  

You can use invoice numbers to search, sort, and report on invoices.  

6. 
In Contract ID, if this recurring invoice is part of an ongoing contract, type the identification 

number for the contract here.  

7. 
In Contract description, type a brief description of the contract.  

Filling In the Transaction Details 

1. 
Click the Payment Terms drop-down list, and then either select an existing payment term or 

click Add to create a new A/R term.  

2. 
To permanently and safely store a digital version of a supporting document, in the 

drop-down next to Attachments, select an attachment, or click Add, then upload your 

attachment. Learn more about who can add attachments in Permissions for attachments.  

If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file in the 
Attachments (on page 

549) box to attach the file to this record.  

3. 
To deactivate a recurring invoice without deleting it, click Status, and then click Inactive.  

To reactivate a recurring invoice, click Status, and then click Active.  

4. 
To assign an allocations template to the recurring invoice, click Allocation, and then click 

the appropriate template.  

For information about allocations, see Using Allocations (on page 238). 

For information about overriding allocations, see Overriding an Allocation (on page 239). 

5. 
In the Source entity drop-down list, select the entity that pays this A/R invoice. 

6. 
In the Bank account drop-down list, select the bank account into which the funds are 

deposited.

<!-- Page 188 -->
Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

7. 
In the Bank G/L account drop-down list, select the Bank G/L account to associate with this 

recurring A/R invoice. 

For Companies Using Multiple Currencies  

1. 
Click Transaction currency, and then select the currency being used for this invoice.  

2. 
If the transaction currency is not your company’s base currency, click Exchange Rate Type, 

and then select an exchange rate type such as RealPage Daily Rate. 

If you know what the exchange rate should be for this A/P invoice or have contracted a set 

rate with the customer, you can type it into Exchange Rate. Otherwise, the exchange rate is 

generated by the system at the time the occurrence of the invoice is generated.  

Filling In the Entries Section 

 In the Entries section, enter information for each line item in the invoice:  

1. 
If you are assigning the charge to a location, click the Location drop-down list, and then 

select the location to which you want to assign the charge. 

2. 
In the G/L Account column (or Account Label if you have enabled account labels), click the 

drop-down list, and then select an account to receive the invoice.  

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 

find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

3. 
If you are assigning the charge to a department, click the Department drop-down list, and 

then select the department to which you want to assign the charge. 

4. 
If you are assigning the charge to a unit, click the Unit drop-down list, and then select the 

unit to which you want to assign the charge. 

5. 
If you want to track this charge by a segment, in Segment Type 1, select a segment type, 

and then select a segment value from the Segment value 1 drop-down list.  

6. 
To track the line item with a second segment, select the segment type in Segment type 2, 

and then select its value in Segment value 2. 

Segment type and Segment value columns appear only if your company enabled the 
Segments feature (on page 513 ). You can define up to four segment types and values in 
total. Learn about Segments. 

7. 
In the Amount field, type the item amount of the item.  

For companies using multiple currencies, the field is called Transaction amount. This is the 
amount in the transaction currency. The system then calculates the Base amount in your 
company’s base currency according to the exchange rate.  

8. 
In Allocation, if your company has created allocations for assigning portions of the invoice, 

click the Allocation drop-down list, and choose the type of allocation.

9. 
In Memo, type a note for line items that might require explanations at some future date.  

10. 
Optionally, click the Show details tab and then fill in any dimensions that you want to 

associate with the recurring A.R invoice. You can also assign custom allocations here. Click 

the Hide Details tab when completed. 

Filling In the Payment Tab 

1. 
Select the Payment tab. 

2. 
Click the Payment method drop-down list and select one of the options: 

• 
Check 

• 
Record transfer 

• 
Cash 

• 
Third party payment 

• 
RealPage debit card 

• 
Petty cash reimbursement 

• 
None 

If you select Check, Record Transfer, Cash, Third Party Payment, or RealPage Debit Card, or Petty 

Cash Reimbursement 

1. 
Select the Account type, Bank or Undeposited funds account. 

2. 
If you selected Bank, then select the bank account. 

3. 
If you selected Undeposited funds account, then select the account. 

4. 
Select the Pay in full check box.  

• 
The system automatically posts payment for the full invoice amount, excluding term 

discounts.  

• 
The system does not apply available credits.  

• 
When the system generates the invoice, it also attempts to post full payment.  

• 
If the payment attempt is successful, the system changes the invoice payment status 

to Paid. 

5. 
If you are not selecting Pay in full, then enter the amount to pay in the Payment amount 

field. Type a number greater than zero but less than the invoice amount in Payment 

amount. Partial payments have the following effects:  

• 
The system does not apply term discounts for partial payments. 

• 
The system does not apply available credits.  

• 
When the system generates the invoice, it also attempts to run the partial payment.  

• 
If the payment attempt is successful, the system changes the invoice payment status 

to Partially Paid.

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

If you selected Charge card, see Setting Up Online Payments for a Recurring Invoice (on page 

191). To set up offline payments, see Setting Up Offline Payments for an Invoice (on page 192). In 

this case, the system will generate invoices and you will receive payments from customers 

manually. 

Filling In the Schedule Tab 

To set up the recurrence: 

1. 
Select the Schedule tab. 

2. 
On Start Date, click 
 Calendar, and select the first date on which you want this invoice to 

be generated.  

3. 
For Repeats, select the frequency in which the invoice is to recur:  

• 
To have the invoice occur only once, select None. You may want to select none if you 

are setting up an invoice for an item that might be recurring such as a 30-day trial for 

a new service. Later you can choose to change the schedule if the service becomes an 

ongoing expense.  

• 
To have the invoice occur at regular intervals, select Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, 

and then type the number of intervals in the adjacent text box.  

For example, if an invoice only occurs every other month, select Months and type 2. If 

you select a time period but do not type a number, the system will default to 1.  

For weeks, months, and years, the invoice will recur at the next interval on the same 

day as the start date. For instance, if you set an invoice to start on the 15th of the 

month and recur monthly, the system generates the invoice each month on the 15th. 

To make an invoice with a Month’s interval generate at the end of the month, select 

End of Month.  

4. 
For Ends, select the appropriate termination point for this invoice:  

• 
Select Never to keep the invoice perpetually running. This is common for invoices like 

ongoing services that have a set price.  

• 
Select After to have the invoice run for a limited number of times, and then, in the 

adjacent text box, type the number of times you want the invoice to recur. This setting 

is often used for debts that are being paid over time. Setting the number of 

occurrences eliminates the possibility of making payments after the debt is paid off.  

To have the invoice recur until a specific date, select On, and then type or select the 

last date on which the invoice is to recur.  

Completing the Invoice 

When you finish entering or editing invoice information, you have two options:  

• 
To save the invoice and then display the list of invoices, click Save.  

• 
To save the invoice and open a new invoice page, click Save & New.

#### Setting Up Online Payments for a Recurring Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 191*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Setting Up Online Payments for a Recurring Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Recurring A/R Invoices > Edit > Payment`


When the customer prefers to pay the invoice with a charge card on file, you can set up online 

payments. 

To set up online payments for this recurring invoice: 

1. 
Click the Payment tab of the Recurring A/R invoice record. 

2. 
Click the Payment method drop-down list and select Charge card. The system displays 

additional fields to specify how you want to account for the payment.  

3. 
If the payment amount fills the invoice amount, select the Pay in full check box. Otherwise 

clear the check box.  

Paying in Full 

Selecting the Pay in full check box produces the following effects:  

• 
The system automatically posts payment for the full invoice amount, excluding term 

discounts.  

• 
The system does not apply available credits.  

• 
When the system generates the invoice, it also attempts to post full payment.  

• 
If the payment attempt is successful, the system changes the invoice payment status to Paid. 

Paying a Partial Amount 

When you clear the Pay in full check box, the system displays the Payment amount field.  

Type a number greater than zero but less than the invoice amount in Payment amount. Partial 

payments have the following effects:  

• 
The system does not apply term discounts for partial payments. 

• 
The system does not apply available credits.  

• 
When the system generates the invoice, it also attempts to run the partial payment.  

• 
If the payment attempt is successful, the system changes the invoice payment status 

to Partially Paid. 

Filling In the Rest of the Charge Card Settings 

1. 
Click the Card type drop-down list and select one of the listed credit cards. This list varies 

depending on your company’s configuration. 

2. 
Click the Charge card/Customer bank account drop-down list, and then click the customer 

payment item to be used in this transaction.  

3. 
In the Account type drop-down list, select where you want the system to post the payment, 

to the bank or into an undeposited funds account.

Deleting a Recurring Invoice 

If there’s no chance you’ll use a recurring invoice any more, you can delete it instead of turning 

off the recurring schedule. For example, if you’ve permanently canceled a contract with a 

customer, you can delete the recurring invoice that was set up for that customer. The system 

removes the recurring invoice from the Recurring Invoices list and creates no more invoices. 

To delete a record: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Month end section of the menu, click Recurring A/R Invoices. 

3. 
On the Recurring A/R Invoices list, find the record you want to remove, select the check box 

at the end of the row, and then click Delete.  

A delete confirmation box appears. 

4. 
Click OK. 

Turning a Recurring Schedule On or Off 

You can activate or deactivate a recurring invoice schedule as needed. For example, if a contract is 

temporarily put on hold, you can turn off a schedule to stop the system from automatically 

creating invoices. When you are ready to restart the recurring schedule, you can turn the schedule 

back on. 

To activate or deactivate a schedule: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Month end section, click Recurring A/R Invoices. 

3. 
On the Recurring A/R Invoices list, find the row associated with the schedule, and click: 

• 
Turn on to activate the schedule. 

• 
Turn off to deactivate the schedule. 

When you turn off a schedule and then turn it on again at a later date, the system resumes the 
recurrence schedule from the turn-off point. If periods were closed in the meantime, the system 
generates an error message as it tries to create recurrences in each of those closed periods. As 
soon as it reaches an open period, the system generates those recurrences to the turn -on date.  
If you want to turn on the schedule and have the system generate recurrences from a later date, 
first edit the Next Execution Date in the recurring schedule.

Payment Tab 

Use the Payment tab of a recurring invoice record to set how the system processes payments 

from the customer. You can set the payment method to automatically process payments.  

The system automatically fills in the Customer and Term fields for your reference.  

Leaving the Payment Method set to None allows the system to process the invoice through your 
normal accounts receivable collection cycle. You can set the Payment Method to automatically 
process payments. 

To set the payment method for a recurring invoice:  

1. 
In Payment method, select the payment method that the customer used to make the 

payment. Depending on your company’s configuration, options are: 

• 
None: This option allows the system to process the invoice through your normal 

accounts receivable collection cycle.  

• 
Charge Card  

• 
Check 

• 
Record transfer 

• 
Cash 

2. 
If you selected Charge card, select the type of credit card used for the payment. 

3. 
Select the Pay in full check box when the payment amount equals the invoice amount. 

When you select Pay in full: 

• 
The system does not apply term discounts or available credits. 

• 
The system automatically posts full payment when it generates the invoice. If the 

payment attempt is successful, the system changes the payment status to “Paid.” 

4. 
If Pay in full is not selected, the Payment amount field appears. Enter a value for the partial 

payment amount (a number that is greater than zero but less than the full invoice amount). 

When you enter a partial payment amount: 

• 
The system does not apply term discounts or available credits. 

• 
The system posts partial payment when it generates the invoice. If the payment 

attempt is successful, the system changes the invoice payment status to Partially Paid.

Schedule Tab 

Use the Schedule tab to enter information to establish the recurrence schedule. 

To schedule the recurring invoice: 

1. 
In Start Date, click 
 Calendar and select the first date on which you want this invoice to 

be generated. Or type the desired date. 

2. 
In the Next execution date field, type the date that you want the system to create the next 

invoice.  

This field is available only when you are editing the record.  

3. 
In the Repeats section, select the frequency in which the invoice is to recur: 

• 
To have the invoice occur only once, select None. You may want to select none if you 

are setting up an invoice for an item that might be recurring such as a 30-day trial for 

a new service. Later you can choose to change the schedule if the service becomes an 

ongoing expense. 

• 
To have the invoice occur at regular intervals, select Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, 

then type the number of intervals in the adjacent text box. 

For example, if an invoice only occurs every other month, select Months and type 2. If 

you select a time period but do not type a number, the system will default to 1. 

For weeks, months, and years, the invoice will recur at the next interval on the same 

day as the start date. For example, if you set an invoice to start on the 15th of the 

month and recur monthly, the system generates the invoice each month on the 15th.  

• 
To make an invoice generate at the end of the month, select Months, specify the 

interval, and then select the End of Month check box. 

Customer and Term on the Additional Information, Payment, and Schedule tabs are 
for reference only. You can edit them only from the Invoice tab. 

4. 
In the Ends section, select the appropriate termination point for this invoice: 

• 
To keep the invoice perpetually running, select Never. This is common for invoices like 

ongoing services that have a set price. 

• 
To have the invoice run for a limited number of times, select After ___ occurrences, 

and then in adjacent text box, type the number of times you want the invoice to recur.

#### Saving an Invoice as a Draft
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 215*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Saving an Invoice as a Draft 

When you are not ready to post the A/P or A/R invoice or adjustment, you can save it as a draft 

without affecting the G/L or any subledger. With the ability to save invoices and adjustments in 

draft state, you can save your progress so far. Later on, you or another user can come back and 

post the transaction. 

The system validates transactions only when they are posted. For example, required 
departments or locations are not validated until posting. 

Your ability to add a transaction in draft state or post a transaction depends on your permissions: 

• 
Add permission enables you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as a draft. 

• 
Add, Edit, and Post permissions enable you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as 

draft, and edit and post the transaction when you’re ready. 

To save a transaction in draft format: 

1. 
Add an A/R invoice, A/P invoice, or adjustment to your company. 

2. 
Save the transaction as a draft by clicking Draft & New or selecting Draft, or Draft & 

Continue from the button drop-down list. The system saves the entry but doesn’t post it. 

Finding Draft or Posted Transactions 

There are two ways to locate and view items in the draft and posted state. 

• 
Filter for draft or posted transactions on the fly: In the appropriate transaction list view, 

enter either Draft or Posted in the State column, and then press ENTER. The system filters 

the list to include only those items you filtered for. 

• 
Create a permanent custom view that filters for draft or posted transactions: Create a 

view and set the filter to State = Draft or State = Posted. The custom view is available for 

use whenever you go to the list.

### Penalties
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 225*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 225*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Penalties 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Account Maintenance > Penalties`


When you apply a late fee to a customer invoice, the system automatically creates and posts an 

AR adjustment, which you can then view, print to PDF, and email to the customer as needed. 

Applying penalties requires two steps to accomplish: 

1. 
Select penalty calculation options and filtering for invoices that are eligible for penalties. 

2. 
Select invoices to penalize from the resulting filtered list.  

After applying the penalties, you can see the resulting penalties in the A/R Adjustments list. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have limited or full Administrator privileges to apply penalties. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to apply penalties: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Accounts Receivable 
Apply penalties 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 584) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

---


<!-- Page 226 -->
Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Required Configuration 

Select an account for penalties in the Configure accounts receivable page. You must do this from 

the top level. See Configuring Accounting Settings (on page 517). 

To apply penalties, create an A/R account label that refers to the same account if your system 

uses account labels. See Adding A/R Account Labels. 

---


<!-- Page 227 -->
Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Conditions 

You must also have the following conditions in place: 

• 
At least one term with a penalty. See Adding an A/R Term (on page 505). 

• 
At least one past-due invoice for which the term includes a penalty. 

• 
The penalty cannot already be applied for the current past-due term. 

For example, suppose the term is net 30, the penalty is 1.5 per cent per month, the invoice is 

past due by six weeks, and you have already applied the penalty for the first month. The 

system makes sure you cannot inadvertently apply another penalty until the invoice is past 

due a total of two months.

### Apply Penalties Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 228*



#### Applying Invoice Penalties
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 228*

Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Apply Penalties Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Penalties`


Use this page to determine how the system calculates the penalty and to set up filters to retrieve 

a list of invoices to penalize. After you click the View button, the list of invoices displays, allowing 

you to select the specific invoices and then apply the penalty. 

This page has four sections: 

• 
Penalty options: Set the name of the penalties batch file, and then select the calculation 

method. 

• 
Filters: Set up filters to get a list of the invoices you want to penalize. 

• 
Additional filters: Set up advanced filters to target the list of invoices to select from. 

• 
Format: Select how you want the list to be sorted. 

Applying Invoice Penalties 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Account Maintenance > Penalties`


To apply penalties: 

1. 
If you are at the top level, select the desired entity from the Level menu.  

2. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

3. 
In the Account maintenance section, select Penalties. The Apply Penalties page opens. 

Setting Penalty Options 

1. 
Type a description for the penalty document. This text will appear on the adjustment record 

for the penalty. 

When you penalize invoices, the system creates an adjustment within a summary named 

PENALTIES. The adjustment documents have a Description field. The system uses the text 

you enter here for the Description field in the adjustment. The default description is Penalty, 

but you can change that description to describe the penalty more closely, for example “Late 

Fee.” The description also appears on the printed adjustment. 

2. 
In the Calculate penalty by section, choose whether to calculate the amount of the penalty 

based on the amount of the invoice or the due amount.  

• 
Select Invoice amount to penalize the entire invoice amount.  

• 
Select Due amount to penalize just the remaining amount due when the customer has 

partially paid the invoice. For example, suppose you have an invoice of $100, and the 

customer has paid $75 leaving an amount due of $25. You can penalize the entire 

invoice of 100 or only the amount due of $25. 

Next, see Setting and Applying the Filters (on page 229). 

---

Setting and Applying the Filters 

Setting filter options enables you to narrow the focus to only those invoices you want to penalize. 

The resulting filtered list appears in the Select Invoices to Penalize list, which appears after you 

click View. 

You can set as many filter options as you want. You can also choose not to set up any filters to 
get a complete list of invoices eligible for penalties. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

You can filter for a range of customer invoices in From Customer and To Customer. Select a 

beginning and ending customer respectively to identify a range of customers. The drop-down 

lists customers in order by ID number. 

Filling In the Additional Filters Section 

Use the additional filters to target specific eligible invoices.  

• 
These filters are optional. 

• 
Use up to four filters to target specific eligible invoices.  

• 
Set up the filters in the order which you want them filtered and sorted.  

For each filter you use, select an operator such as equals or greater than, and type the value you 

want to filter by in the text box. Customer, Customer ID, Invoice Amount, and Total Due are all 

derived from the invoice. 

To apply additional filters: 

1. 
Starting with the top drop-down list in this section, select the most important information to 

filter on: Customer, Customer ID, Invoice amount, or Total due. 

2. 
Select an operator and enter the value to filter on.  

3. 
For each additional filter, select an operator such as equals or greater than, and type the 

value you want to filter by in the text box.

#### Select Invoices to Penalize List
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 231*



#### Selecting Invoices to Penalize
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 231*

Chapter 3: Billing

Select Invoices to Penalize List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Penalties > View`


When you click the View button on the Apply Penalties page, the system applies the filters and 

then lists the invoices that are eligible for penalties on a new browser tab.  

Use this list to: 

• 
Select the invoices to penalize 

• 
View a full invoice  

• 
Apply the penalties 

After selecting invoices and clicking the Save button, you can close the browser tab. 

Selecting Invoices to Penalize 

To select invoices: 

1. 
Select the check boxes of one or more invoices to penalize. 

If you have doubts about an invoice, you can click the Invoice link to open and review it. 

2. 
Click Save to save your selections. The system bases the calculation on your selection and 

on the invoice’s payment terms and creates a summary adjustment to account for the 

penalty. You can access the summary adjustment on the A/R adjustments page. (Accounts 

Receivable > Account Maintenance > Adjustments). 

To view, edit, or print the adjustment: 

1. 
On the All tab of the Accounts receivable menu, select Adjustments. A list of A/R 

adjustments opens.  

2. 
Locate the row with the appropriate adjustment. Penalty adjustments are easy to locate in 

the list because they have a summary title PENALTIES - <timestamp> (where time stamp is a 

combination of the date and time the penalty was applied), for example, PENALTIES - 

09/28/15 16:32:42. 

To send a copy of the adjustment to the customer, click Print. The system creates a PDF of 
the adjustment, which you can then save, and then attach to a customer email.

### Transaction Allocations
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 234*



#### Defining Transaction Allocations
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 234*

Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Transaction Allocations 

You can use allocations in A/R invoices, A/P invoices, and journal entries to distribute an amount 

across two or more dimensions, such as locations or departments. Allocations can be either a set 

amount or a percentage. If you choose to allocate a percentage, then the allocation must add up 

to 100 percent. 

Some configuration is required before you can use transaction allocations. After configuration, 

you can apply allocations as you enter transactions.  

For example, you can create a transaction allocation that distributes costs such as occupancy 

across several departments. By selecting that allocation when you enter the expense line, the 

amount of that expense is then automatically distributed across the appropriate departments: 

Defining Transaction Allocations 

To use transaction allocations, you must first enable the feature in the desired application, then 

create an allocation template that determines how to allocate the amount. After completing this 

configuration, you can apply the allocation to a transaction’s line item. 

Enabling the Transaction Allocation Feature 

You can use transaction allocations in Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and the General 

Ledger. Before you can use transaction allocations in any application, you must enable the 

transaction allocation feature in each application’s Configuration page. Enable transaction 

allocations in the Configuration area in the application where you need to use them. This example 

shows where to enable transaction allocation in the Accounts Payable application. 

---

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality > Enable Allocation in`


Invoice Entry 

Creating the Allocation Template 

You create a template that defines how you want to allocate the transaction, and then apply the 

allocation template to the desired transaction.  

For example, you can create a transaction allocation template so that it allocates the cost of a 

single line item across multiple locations. Whenever you want to apply this allocation to a line 

item, you select the allocation in a transaction’s line item row. 

Applying the Allocation 

When you enter an A/R invoice, A/P invoice, or journal entry and apply a transaction allocation to 

any line, the system automatically splits the amount based on the transaction allocation template.  

For example, if a company distributes an expense such as janitorial services across five business 

units, the transaction allocation can be set up to reflect the percentages of occupancy per 

business unit. When you apply this transaction allocation to a line item, the system will 

automatically divide the amount across the business units according to the percentages saved in 

the transaction allocation template. 

To see how a transaction allocation is divided in a transaction, open the A/P invoice, A/R invoice, 

or journal entry, and then click the line in the Entries section, and then click Show details. The 

allocation is displayed in the Allocation Splits section of the Details page. You can further 

customize the allocation

#### Restrictions on Applying Allocations
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 241*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Restrictions on Applying Allocations 

Although each transaction allocation you create is available anywhere transaction allocations are 

an option, the system prevents you from applying allocations that violate certain transaction rules: 

• 
The dimension used by the transaction allocation must be turned on for the corresponding 

application.  

For example, the Project dimension must be turned on in A/P if you want to allocate an A/P 

invoice across projects. 

• 
The transaction allocation must make sense for the type of transaction.  

For example, you can’t allocate an invoice to more than one customer. 

• 
If you use revenue recognition, you can’t allocate line items for which you are deferring 

revenue. 

In addition, for multi-entity organizations: 

• 
You can use transaction allocations across entities only if they have the same base currency. 

• 
You can use transaction allocations to allocate an A/R invoice or A/P invoice across entities 

only if all of the entities have access to the related customer or vendor. For example, you 

can’t allocate an A/P invoice to the Chicago and New York locations if the vendor is 

restricted to only the New York location.

### Intercompany Billing
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 243*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Intercompany Billing 

 You must be at the top level to use this feature. 

Intercompany Billing is a tool for creating billing between entities. An Intercompany Billing 

process generates A/P invoices and A/R invoices that can be settled through your company’s 

standard settlement process. 

The primary purpose of this feature is to distribute supplier costs for the paying entity. You can 

also use the ICB process to distribute the cost of management fees, common area maintenance 

(CAM) fees, staff working at another entity, or corporate fees such as software or training that 

entities pay a parent entity.  

Use the ICB tool when one entity pays an A/P invoice on behalf of other entities. You can also 

create a chain of bill-to entities as needed. You begin by creating an ICB invoice. When you post 

the ICB, the process simultaneously creates an A/R invoice and an A/P invoice for repayment. 

---


<!-- Page 244 -->
Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Examples of Supported Billing Scenarios 

• 
When accounting services are paid at the corporate level, the company can use this feature 

to distribute the costs among its locations.  

• 
When a vendor invoices more than one entity, resulting in a chain of bill-to parties. 

ICB Transaction Process 

• 
The parent entity pays an A/P invoice (full or partial).  

• 
The parent entity, in turn, invoices the lower entity/locations (child locations).  

This process can also function with more than one intermediate bill-to party, resulting in a chain 

of bill-to parties. 

Segments and Intercompany Billing 

You can select up to four segments on A/P and A/R invoices. RealPage Commercial Property 

Management completes the ICB segment based on the billing entity that you select.  

To see the value of the ICB segment, run the Segment Activity report.

### Inter-company Bill-Back
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 262*

Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Inter-company Bill-Back 

The inter-company bill back feature enables you to handle situations in which one entity provides 

goods or services to another entity and expects to be paid back. 

After you configure the bill back feature, when you create a bill back invoice, the system creates a 

corresponding A/P invoice on the second entity’s books.  

Invoicing must happen at the top level. 

---



### What Does Inter-company Bill Back Do?
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 263*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

What Does Inter-company Bill Back Do? 

You can have one bill back-associated customer and one bill back-associated vendor for each 

entity. The bill back customer and the bill back vendor are not mapped to each other, only to the 

entity. After association, if you create an invoice at the top level for the bill back customer, the 

customer information automatically appears on the invoice. 

When you choose a bill back template for the bill back customer invoice, the information from 

that template is included on the invoice and the template bill back vendor serves as the billing 

entity. 

When inter-company bill back is enabled, creating the invoice automatically creates the bill in the 

Accounts Payable of the customer-associated entity. 

Inter-company Bill Back Example 

Suppose that you have a property management company. The corporate office is set up as one 

entity with separate entities for satellite offices that manage individual properties. Each satellite 

office pays the corporate office the rent every month. Instead of manually creating and sending 

an invoice each time, creating an inter-company bill back customer for each entity allows you to 

automatically generate a bill in the Accounts Payable of the satellite office each time an invoice 

for the rent is created from the corporate office, using the bill back template created with the 

corporate entity information and rent line item. 

After enabling the Inter-company bill back feature, you can set up, and then use the feature. 

---



### Bill Back Feature Configuration Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 264*

Billing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Bill Back Feature Configuration Workflow 

Inter-company bill back requires configuration changes and additional setup. 

1. 
Enable the bill back feature. 

2. 
Grant bill back template permissions. 

3. 
Create Inter-entity receivable and Inter-entity payable accounts to use for inter-entity 

transactions if you don’t have them already. 

4. 
Create a vendor record and a customer record for each entity. 

5. 
Associate the customer record and the vendor record with its entity. Do this for each entity. 

6. 
Create bill back templates. 

The system uses these templates to complete the vendor-related information and invoice 

entries in the line item section.  

Bill back templates require an invoice G/L account and a bill G/L account. For example, you 

could create a revenue (invoice) account that a bill back template uses for a Corporate 

G/L account to bill to a Western Regional office. 

This might require you to create General Ledger accounts for the specific bill back setup. 

---



### Using the Inter-company Bill Back Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 265*

Chapter 3: Billing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Using the Inter-company Bill Back Workflow 

When the feature is enabled and configured, create an invoice, choosing an entity’s customer. 

Two controls associated with a bill back invoice appears: 

• 
The Bill back template drop-down list. 

Best practice: Create a bill back template for each set of line items you plan to bill back. All 
line items on the bill back template appear on the invoice, and thus, on the bill.

• 
The Generate matching bill for invoice check box. By default, the check box is selected, and 

bills are generated automatically. 

Leaving this check box selected causes the system to create the bill automatically after the 

invoice is saved. Clear the check box if you don’t want the system to create the bill 

automatically. 

Best practice: Automate bill creation by selecting Generate matching bill to avoid the need 
for manually creating a bill in the second entity.

Managing Inter-company Bill Back Invoices 

Setting up the bill back feature enables you to handle situations in which one entity provides 

goods or services to another entity and expects to be paid back. When an A/R invoice is created 

at the top level for the service or goods-providing entity, a corresponding A/P bill is automatically 

created in the second entity, the consuming entity.  

This functionality works for multi-currency companies. 

• 
Creating a bill back A/R invoice 

• 
View an A/P invoice created with the bill back feature 

Before You Begin 

Requirements 

Inter-company bill back has specific requirements. You can use bill back if your company: 

• 
Is multi-entity shared. 

• 
Is single-currency. 

• 
Does not use account labels. 

• 
Uses A/R-A/P-focused invoicing and billing. 

• 
Has the necessary permissions to push A/P invoices directly to the second entity. 

Permissions 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

You must have Administrator privileges to configure bill back templates. 

These permissions are required to create and manage inter-company bill back templates: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Accounts Receivable 
Bill back templates 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 584) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

Inter-Company Bill Back Configuration Workflow 

Inter-company bill back requires configuration changes and additional setup. 

• 
Enable inter-company bill back 

• 
Associate vendors and customers with entities

Enable bill back template permissions 

For information, see Configuring inter-company bill back (on page 524). 

Creating a Bill Back Invoice 

After you’ve set up inter-company bill back, a Generate matching bill for invoice check box and a 

Bill back template drop-down menu appear on the Invoice page.  

Before you begin, you need to know what the customer record of the consuming entity is. To 

identify the consuming entity’s customer record, open the entity and select the Additional 

information tab. 

To create a bill back invoice: 

1. 
Go to the top level. 

2. 
Click the Applications menu, select Accounts receivable, and then select the All tab. 

3. 
Select 
 Add next to A/R Invoices. 

4. 
Select the customer record of the consuming entity. If you have selected the right customer 

record, the two bill back options appear in the Term section. 

The system adds the customer information to the invoice. 

5. 
Fill in the top section of the invoice as you normally would. 

6. 
Verify that Generate matching bill for invoice check box is selected.  

7. 
In the Bill back template field, select a bill back template that includes the line items that 

you want to charge the entity. 

When selected, the line items appear in the Entries list below. The information, including 

line items and G/L accounts, appears on the invoice. All line items in the bill back template 

appear on the invoice.

Viewing an A/P Invoice Created with the Bill Back Feature 

To view an A/P invoice created by the bill back feature: 

1. 
From the Top level menu, select the entity. 

2. 
From the Applications menu, select Accounts payable. 

3. 
Select A/P Invoices.  

You can see the A/P invoice and identify it as a bill back invoice because the status is Not 

Owned, indicating that the A/P invoice was not created by this entity. 

4. 
Click the View link to open the A/P invoice.  

You cannot edit a bill back invoice. 

Disabling Inter-company Bill Back Transactions 

This feature is controlled by a global setting. That means, when you change the setting, the 

change applies to all entities within your company. 

To disable intercompany bill back transactions for all entities in your company: 

• 
Clear the Enable inter-company bill back option on the Configure Accounts Receivable 

page.  

To disable the feature for a single transaction: 

• 
When you create the invoice, clear the Create A/P Invoice check box.

Question: How should I enter an uncashed check that carried over at property takeover?

### Select Invoices for Payment Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 272*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Select Invoices for Payment Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Receive a Payment`


Use this page to receive and record a payment from a customer and apply the money to invoices 

or debit memos. 

The system lists only invoices on which you can take some action. Invoices that are fully paid are 

not displayed; you can view them at Accounts Receivable > All > A/R Invoices.  

After accepting a payment, you can: 

• 
Apply the payment to one or more invoices or debit memos 

• 
Apply existing credit to one or more invoices 

• 
Apply a term discount to an invoice 

• 
Assign an overpayment to a department or location 

• 
Assign an advance payment to an invoice or debit memo. 

This page is divided into the following sections.  

• 
Payment options: This section collects information about the payment method, location, 

customer, and shows the customer’s total balance.  

• 
Payment Information: This section collects details about the payment date and amount, 

and details about the payment method. The section’s options change based on the payment 

method. 

• 
Available overpayments and advances: This section lists any overpayments and advances 

that are available to work with. 

• 
Available credits: This section lists any credit memos, negative invoices, and inline credits 

that are available to apply against the customer’s invoices and debit memos. 

• 
Available invoices and debit memos: This section lists the invoices and debit memos of the 

customer.  

The sections that appear below the Payment information section are determined by whether the 

customer has any outstanding invoices or debit memos, credit memos, overpayments, or advance 

payments. 

---

Receiving a Payment

Payment`


When you enter a check amount, the system automatically populates some or all of the fields in 

the Available invoices and debit memos list, depending on the setting of the Turn off automatic 

payment suggestions option. If the preference is disabled, which is the default, the system 

proposes which invoices to pay and the amount to pay for each.  

If you usually overwrite the amounts proposed by the system and no longer want the system to 

propose those amounts, enable the Turn off automatic payment suggestions preference. 


> **Navigation Path:** `(Accounts receivable > Setup > Configuration)`


To select invoices against which to apply payments:

In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, click Receive a payment. The Select invoices for 

payment page opens. When this page appears, at first you see only the Payment options 

section. 

Filling In the Payment Options Section 

These settings apply to all of the invoices for which you want to apply payment at this time:  

1. 
In the Payment method drop-down list, select the method of payment, Check, Credit card, 

Record transfer, Cash, or Third Party Payment. The payment method that your system 

offers may vary. 

2. 
In the Account type section, select whether to deposit the payment in a bank account or in 

an undeposited funds account.  

3. 
In the Account drop-down list, choose the account into which to deposit the payment, 

depending on the account type.  

• 
If you selected Bank account, then select the bank account in the Account drop-down 

list, and then choose the Bank G/L account to record the payment. 

• 
If you selected Undeposited funds account, select the G/L account in the Account 

drop-down list.

This section appears when the customer has invoices or debit memos. In the list of Available

overpaid box will remain as a credit or overpayment.

A customer has one outstanding invoice for $500.00, has a credit for $100.00, and sent a

Entering an Overpayment 

If you receive a payment for more than what the customer owes on all invoices, enter the amount 

of the payment. The system tracks the excess as an overpayment, which can be applied to future 

invoices. For information, see Receiving a Payment (on page 273). 

If the customer would rather have the excess money returned, refund the overpayment. For 

information, see Refunding an Overpayment (on page 277). 

Refunding an Overpayment 

A customer may have a negative balance as the result of overpaying an invoice, paying an 

advance that was never used, or receiving a credit that was never used. If you don’t plan on 

invoicing the customer again or the customer would like the money back without delay, you can 

issue a refund check:  

1. 
Create an A/R adjustment (debit memo) that adjusts the customer balance to zero. Learn 

about Creating a Debit Adjustment (on page 361). 

2. 
Receive the payment: 

• 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Accounts receivable. 

• 
Click Receive a payment. The Select invoices for payment page opens.  

• 
Apply the adjustment.  

• 
Unless you apply the debit memo, open transactions and the adjustment will continue 

to display on your aging report.  

• 
Create the customer as a one-time vendor. Learn about creating vendors. 

• 
Create a manual payment to refund the money owed to the customer, making the 

vendor you created the payee.  

If you get stuck, learn how to find help or contact support (on page 603).

invoice is $5,500.00.

Amount 

The system displays one of these two fields if your company uses

Rate. For example, maybe you want to use a monthly rate that fluctuates

The Base Amount is the effective amount that ends up in your bank 

account. You get this number from the bank. Your customer remittance 

information tells you how much of their liability this check represents. 

For example, say your invoices to the customer are in foreign currency, 

but your customer pays in base currency. Alternatively, your invoice is in 

base currency and the customer pays in foreign currency. Because you 

deposit the transfer into your bank, the bank uses its own exchange rate. 

Consequently, you must get the exact amount from the bank. This is also 

the amount that the system uses to calculate gain/loss. In addition, if the 

invoice was in USD, but the customer pays $100 CAD, the customer’s 

remittance information tells you that this represents payment for a $120 

USD invoice.

amounts that add up to more than the credit available.) Advances are

To take some or all of the credits and/or advances, enter an amount in

The system applies credits in the following order: advances, 

overpayments, negative invoices, and then adjustments.  

In other words, say you received an advance of $1,000 and also issued a 

credit memo for $500. You will have a total credit available of $1,500. 

Let’s say you then enter $1,200 in the Credits to apply field. The system 

first uses the entire $1,000 advance, and then uses $200 of the credit 

memo, leaving $300 on that credit memo.  

The amount of credit that you apply is automatically subtracted by the 

system when you click Save. If an invoice is fully paid by the application 

of credit, the system removes it from the list when you save.  

In addition, the amount of credits/advances that you applied to the first 

invoice is no longer available to apply to other invoices. For example, say 

you had $132 in credits for that customer, but you only apply $100. The 

system remembers that you have an additional $32 that you can take 

later. However, if you reverse the resulting transaction, the amount of 

the credits/advances is returned to the full original amount.

#### Receiving Other Payments
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 290*



#### Applying a Payment to an Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 290*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Receiving Other Payments 

The system offers two additional ways for receiving payments:  

• 
Manual Deposit: This method enables you to receive a customer payment without applying 

it to a specific invoice. Instead, it deposits the receipt directly into a bank account. See 

Manual deposits (on page 322) for more details.  

• 
Other Receipts: This method enables you to receive payments from customers that do not 

have an account in A/R. The system either deposits the payment into an undeposited funds 

account or directly into a bank account. See Other receipts for more details.  

When you save with any payment method except Online Charge Card, the system immediately 

updates the accounts receivable ledger, general ledger, sales register, statements, customer aging 

records and so forth.  

Partial receipts are reflected in the customer’s invoice, showing the reduction and balance due. 

Full receipts show that there is a zero balance due on the invoice. (If you chose Balance Forward 

as the customer type for this customer, the payment is not applied to a specific invoice, but is 

applied to the total balance due for that customer with oldest balances being cleared first. You 

make that choice in the Configure accounts receivable page under Customer Type).  

Applying a Payment to an Invoice 

Certain company configurations, such as multi-currency companies, don’t support recording a 
payment directly from this page. In this case, you won’t see the Apply Payment link or button. 
Instead, select Accounts Receivable > Receive a Payment. See Receiving a Payment (on page 
273 ). 
Look for this feature in an upcoming release. 

If you have an invoice for which you’d like to quickly apply a payment, you can start the process 

directly from the Invoices list page. The system automatically filters for just that invoice and 

auto-populates it to the Select Invoices for Payment page. 

If you have multiple invoices for which you want to apply payment, for example, for the same 
customer, we recommend that you use the normal select-invoices-to pay process which is faster 
for more than one invoice. 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select A/R Invoices. 

Invoices that are eligible for payment show an Apply Payment link at the end of the row. 

3. 
Click Apply Payment for the A/P invoice of choice. The Select Invoices for Payment page 

appears with the invoice information auto-populated. 

4. 
Enter the amount to apply, and then select or edit other options as required.

#### Turning Off Auto Payment Suggestions
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 291*

Chapter 4: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

5. 
Click Save. 

Turning Off Auto Payment Suggestions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality > 
Turn Off Automatic Payment Suggestions`



> **Navigation Path:** `You set preferences in the Configure Accounts Receivable page (Accounts Receivable > Setup`


tab > Configuration). If you usually overwrite the amounts proposed by the system, and no longer 

want the system to propose those amounts, select the Turn off automatic payment suggestions 

check box to disable this feature. 

When this feature is enabled, the system applies the payment to the invoices starting with the 

oldest invoice. If the amount of the payment is sufficient to fully pay that invoice, the system 

automatically selects the Receive Full check box for that invoice, and then applies the remainder 

to the next invoice, and so on until the entire payment amount is used. If any amount is left over 

because the payment amount is greater than the total of the invoices, the overpayment amount 

appears in the Amount Overpaid field. 

Simultaneously, the system also applies any available discounts. In doing so, the system subtracts 

them from the amount received and places that adjusted number in the Amount Received field.  

Example 

You receive a check from a customer for $200 against two invoices, each for $100. The second 

invoice has a discount of $10. The system marks both invoices as Received Full. An amount of 

$100 is placed in the Amount Received field for the first invoice, but only $90 appears for the 

second because the system has subtracted the $10 discount. This leaves an overpayment of $10. If 

you wish, you can override the discount that the system applied by entering $100 into the 

Amount Received field for that invoice. 

To turn off automatic payment suggestions: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select Configuration. 

4. 
In the Enable functionality section, select the Turn off automatic payment suggestions 

check box. 

5. 
Click the Save button.

Viewing a List of Posted Payments 

Posted payments include all check payments, and any off-line transactions that are fully approved 

(credit card, electronic funds transfer, cash, or online credit card).  

To view the posted payments list: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Search and find section, select Payments. 

The items you can see on this page vary slightly depending on whether your company is an 

enterprise or a multi-entity shared company.  

If your company is a multi-entity shared company at the top level, you initially see all items, 

regardless of where they were created.  

To hide items created in the entities, clear the Include private check box. Also, when you 

edit an item that was created in an entity, your changes apply to that entity. After you save 

your changes, you are returned to the top level.  

Viewing Posted Payments 

You access posted payment details through the Posted Payments list.  

To view a list of posted payments: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select Payments. The Posted Payments list opens.  

3. 
Click View to see details about a posted payment. The Posted payment page opens, 

showing the details of the payment. 

Reversing Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Payments`


Reversing posted payments is useful in cases where you apply a payment to the wrong customer, 

or perhaps you apply it on the wrong date.  

After you reverse a posted payment, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can create 
another payment to replace it.  

When you reverse a payment, the system retains the original payment transaction, and creates 

anew transaction that essentially zeros out the payment, which provides an audit trail. For 

example, if you apply a charge for $10 that you then reverse, the system displays the original $10 

charge, but also a charge for -$10, resulting in a net of zero.  

Best practice: Reverse the payment on the same date as you applied it so that you get the 

immediate net effect of zero for that transaction.

#### How to Access the Invoice Again to Apply the Correct Payment
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 296*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To remove the invoices that were paid by this check, select the check boxes in the Reverse 

column.  

5. 
In the Transaction reversal date box, click Submit.  

The system returns you to the Posted Payments list, and you can see two line items for this 

transaction. (The transaction is not zeroed out so there is an audit trail.)  

• 
One line item is the original transaction, where the Reverse link now is labeled 

Reversed.  

• 
The other line item added by the system is the reverse of that transaction, which 

produces a net effect of zero for that transaction. This transaction is labeled Reversal.  

If you selected one or more invoices, a negative invoice is also created, resulting in a net of zero 

for those transactions as well.  

Reversing a Payment from the Receipts Register Report 

Before you begin, run the Receipts register report. 

1. 
Locate the entry you want to reverse in the receipts register, and then click Reverse at the 

end of the entry. The Transaction Reversal Date page opens. 

2. 
Select the date for reversing the transaction. This is usually the original transaction date or a 

later date. 

3. 
Click Submit.  

The Receipts Register page removes the Reverse link and tags the entry as Reversed. The 

system adds an additional balancing entry, which it tags as Reversal. 

How to Access the Invoice Again to Apply the Correct Payment 

After you reverse a payment against an invoice, that payment is no longer available to apply. 

Except for the record of its reversal, the payment is gone from the system. The invoice amount 

reverts to the original amount owed. If you want to apply the correct payment to the same 

invoice, you receive and apply the payment (on page 273). 

For example, if you receive and apply a $100 payment to Invoice INV_001, which had a balance of 

$200, and then reverse it because you applied the wrong amount, the invoice still carries a 

balance of $200 owed. Now you can receive and apply the correct amount to INV_001.

### Deposits
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 307*

Chapter 4: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Deposits 

When you deposit multiple payments, it’s normal to group the payments and submit them to 

your bank with one deposit slip. When you deposit payments and later receive your bank 

reconciliation statement, all you see is one entry with the total deposit amount. The Deposits 

page enables you to record all of the individual payments that constitute a deposit. 

Deposits automatically post to the General Ledger and appropriate subledgers. 

When you record a deposit, the payment must already be received against your undeposited 
funds account. 

Use the manual deposit feature to record a customer payment that isn’t made against a specific 

invoice, for example, an over-the-counter cash sale. 

Deposits, Automatic Deposits, and Manual Deposits 

Deposits in the RealPage Accounting system are different from automatic deposits and manual 

deposits. 

Method 
Description 

Deposits 
When you receive payment for A/R invoices, A/R advances, or Cash 

Management other receipts into an undeposited funds account, create a 

deposit as the next step in the workflow. This type of deposit enables 

you to record payments from multiple customers into one deposit. 

When you deposit multiple payments in a single deposit, you see only 

one entry for the total deposit amount when you receive your bank 

statement. The Deposits page enables you to record all of the individual 

payments that constitute the deposit. 

Automatic deposits 
When you receive payment for A/R invoices, A/R advances, or Cash 

Management other receipts directly to a bank account and not into an 

undeposited funds account, the system automatically posts the deposit 

to the G/L and appropriate subledgers. You do not have to take any 

further action. 

Manual deposits 
When you receive a payment and don’t have an A/R invoice to apply the 

payment to–for example, an over-the-counter cash sale–you can create 

a manual deposit. The system automatically records the payment and 

creates the matching invoice at the same time. 

You can view all these methods of deposit in the Bank Register report. You can view only 

undeposited funds for which you create a deposit on the Deposits page. 

---

Deposits Workflow 

The following diagram illustrates the deposits workflow and the posting activity in the General 

Ledger and subledgers. Remember, you can add a deposit only after you receive payments into 

an undeposited funds account. 

When you receive a payment into an undeposited funds account, the system: 

• 
Posts the payment amount to the General Ledger. 

• 
Credits the appropriate account, depending on what the payment is for and how your 

accounts are set up, and debits the undeposited funds account. 

• 
Adds the payment to the list of payments that can be deposited on the Create deposit slip 

page.

### Undeposited Funds Accounts
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 311*

Chapter 4: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Undeposited Funds Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration`


You use an undeposited funds account to hold checks and cash payments that you are collecting 

for a future deposit. As you collect checks and cash, you can enter these payments even if you do 

not know when you will make the deposit, or to which bank you will make the deposit. 

Example 

You make your deposits on Fridays. You collect payments throughout the week and record 

them. The payments are correctly accounted for in the undeposited funds account. 

However, the deposit is not actually in the bank account until you complete the Create 

deposit slip page. At that point, the funds are transferred from the undeposited funds 

account to the bank account. 

Thus, if you received a particularly large check, but were not yet sure where you want to 

deposit it, you could record it when you receive it so that the payment is on the books and 

preserve your options with regard to which financial institution you want to deposit it. 

When you select an account for undeposited funds, you cannot select a General Ledger account 

that is associated with a bank account, even though that might seem natural. Rather, you should 

specify an account that can be used as a transfer account so that you can deposit them later. (If 

you were to choose a bank account, the funds would already be posted to that bank, even though 

you have not yet deposited them. That would defeat the whole purpose of having an undeposited 

funds feature.) Typically, you create an account such as 1500 Undeposited Funds. However, you 

can have a more granular structure of multiple undeposited funds accounts. 

You can set up a standard undeposited funds account and an undeposited funds account for 

intercompany billing. Both are configured on the Configure Accounts Receivable page. 

To set up undeposited funds accounts: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Click Configuration. 

Setting up a standard undeposited funds account: 

1. 
Find the Defaults section of the Payments section. 

2. 
In the Offline payment account drop-down list, select Undeposited funds account. The 

Undeposit account drop-down list opens. 

3. 
Select the desired account for funds from standard transactions.  

4. 
Click Save. 

---

Reversing Deposits 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Enter Payments > Deposits > 
Reverse`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Deposits > Reverse`


To maintain an audit trail of cash activity, you cannot edit a deposit. However, you can reverse the 

deposit and then re-create it to make changes. For example, if you entered a deposit that is 

missing an A/R payment, you can re-create the deposit to include the payment. 

When you reverse a deposit, a new transaction appears in the Deposits list labeled “Voided 

Deposit Slip.” The reversal is a mirror image of the original deposit, but the debits and credits are 

reversed so the journal entries cancel each other out. 

You can reverse a deposit when: 

• 
You have permission to reverse. 

• 
The deposit has not been reconciled. 

• 
No items in the deposit—A/R payments or Cash Management other receipts—have been 

reversed. You can, however, reverse any of the other items in the deposit. 

---



#### Reversing a Deposit
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 316*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

After you reverse the deposit, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can record another 

deposit to replace it. 

Reversing a Deposit 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Enter Payments > Deposits > 
Reverse`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Deposits > Reverse`


To reverse a deposit: 

1. 
In the Deposits list, click the Reverse link next to the deposit slip you want to reverse. 

The Transaction reversal date box opens. 

2. 
In the Reverse the transaction on date field, type or select the date to reverse the deposit. 

This is usually the original transaction date or a later date. You can even select a date in a 

prior closed period so that your financial statements are correct. 

3. 
In the Memo field, type a description that applies to this deposit. This text is for your 

information only. 

4. 
Click the Submit button. 

The Deposits list now displays two line items for the deposit: 

• 
The first line item, the original deposit, is now labeled Reversed. 

• 
The second line item, labeled Reversal, is the reversed deposit. 

Example 

You have a deposit for $500. After reversing, you still have the original $500 deposit, but also a 

voided deposit for -$500, resulting in a net of zero. 

The resulting journal entry debits undeposited funds and credits the bank account. A/R payments 

and other receipts that were in the original deposit are not reversed and are available to be 

redeposited. 

---



#### Reversing a Payment in a Deposit
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 317*

Chapter 4: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Reversing a Payment in a Deposit 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Enter Payments > Deposits > 
View`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Deposits > View`


A deposit includes payments for A/R invoices, A/R advances, and other receipts that are received 

into an undeposited funds account. The deposit generates the journal entry to record the transfer 

of funds from undeposited funds to the bank (debits the bank account and credits undeposited 

funds). 

After you make a deposit, even if it has been reconciled, you can reverse a payment in the 

deposit. For example, you might need to reverse a payment to correct a payment date or handle a 

bounced check. 

Reversing a payment creates a new reversing payment to offset the original. The combination of 

the original payment and the negative reversal produces a net effect of zero and serves as an 

audit trail. 

The new reversing payment has its own G/L date so that you can optionally use a different date 

for the reversing payment than the date on the original payment. The resulting journal entry 

debits Accounts receivable (or some other account if another receipt was reversed) and credits 

the bank account. 

After a payment in a deposit has been reversed, the deposit can’t be reversed. You can, however, 
reverse as many payments in the deposit as you like. Reversing all of the payments effectively 
voids the deposit. 

To reverse a payment in a deposit: 

1. 
In the Deposits list, click the View link to view details about the payments in the deposit. 

You can drill down further into each payment. 

2. 
Reverse the payment according to your payment type: 

• 
A/R invoice: Reverse the payment from either the Posted payments list or the Receipts 

Register report in Accounts Receivable. 

• 
A/R advance: Reverse the payment from either the Posted advances list or the 

Receipts Register report in Accounts Receivable. 

• 
Other receipt: Reverse the payment (deposited into undeposited funds) from the 

Other receipts list in Cash Management.

Manual Deposits 

Use the manual deposit feature to record a customer payment that isn’t made against a specific 

invoice (for example, an over-the-counter cash sale). 

Add a Manual Deposit record to the Deposits list when:  

• 
You have received one or more customer payments that were not made against a specific 

invoice, such as an over-the-counter payment.  

• 
You have already made the deposit, and you are recording the details after the fact. 

When a customer payment is made against an invoice, record the deposit using the Receive a 

payment command.  

Accounts Receivable > All > Payments > Receive a payment 

Deposits automatically post to the General ledger and appropriate subledgers.  

Manual deposits can be viewed but not edited or deleted. 

When you want to refund a customer against their invoice, refund a credit to the customer (on 

page 389).

linked to another record. 

• 
 In this example, the Customer ID text is linked to the customer record. Clicking the link 

opens the customer record in view mode. Once open, you can click the Edit button to make 

changes to the record, if needed (and if you have appropriate permissions).

email address you clicked.  

You may need to give the system permission to open your email client the first time you 
click an email address.

Duplicating a Manual Deposit 

You can add a record by duplicating an existing one and editing the duplicate. You can view and 

access a list of manual deposits on the Manual deposits list. 

To duplicate an existing manual deposit record: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Manual deposits. 

3. 
Locate the manual deposit record that you want to duplicate. 

4. 
Click View. The system displays the Manual deposit page. 

5. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system creates a new record that is identical to the original. 

6. 
Change the required fields, such as the Date, Bank, and Invoice number. 

7. 
Fill in the page’s other fields with new values as needed. 

8. 
Click the Save button. Click the Save & new button to save the manual deposit and record 

another manual deposit.

### Advances

#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 334*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide

Advances 

When you receive a prepayment or retainer from a customer, you can record it as an advance that 

can later be applied to an invoice. 

The Receive Advances page enables you to record an advance. Later, when you create the 

invoice, any advances that you create for a customer account are shown as credits that you can 

apply to one or more invoices, adjusting the customer account. This process is similar to that of 

applying an overpayment.  

In shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies, you can receive and record 

advances only at the entity level where they are recorded in the entity’s base currency. (From the 

top-level of the company, the Advances list only displays a list of all the advances in your 

company hierarchy.)  

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to receive and record advances: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts receivable 
Receive Advances 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 584) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions.

To add information to an advance record: 

1. 
On the Receive Advances page, select the Payment method by which the customer paid

2. 
Decide where you want to record the advance: 

•

Bank 

If you selected Bank, then the Bank field appears. Select the bank account where you want 

to record the advance. 

Payment Summary 

If you selected payment summary, then depending on your system configuration, you can 

select a Payment summary, or have the system automatically use a default summary. 

• 
If your system is configured for user-specified payment summary frequency, then 

select the user-specified Payment Summary.  

The Payment Summary groups payments together that are being deposited into 

the same account or into Undeposited Funds. The summary names in the 

drop-down list are the same ones that you see when you click Accounts 

Receivable > All > Subledger > Payment summaries.  

If you haven’t already created a Payment Summary, go to Accounts Receivable > 

All > Payment Summaries and add one. When creating the payment summary, 

select the bank account into which the payment will be deposited or select 

Undeposited Funds for payments (such as cash and checks) that will be deposited 

at a later time.  

• 
If you don’t see the Payment summary field here, your system is configured for a 

default payment summary frequency, such as daily or monthly. In this case, the 

system automatically creates that summary.

If your company uses multiple currencies, note that a specific bank currency is

currency as the summary. That is, if you select an EUR summary, you see only EUR

Posted Advances List

The Posted Advances list contains advance payments that you received from a customer before 

sending an invoice.  

Use this list to: 

• 
View posted advance details (on page 347) 

•

• 
Export the list (on page 579) 

For example, if a customer sends you a retainer, the retainer payment should appear in the 

Posted advances list. When the invoice comes due, you can apply the advance amount to the 

total amount before sending the invoice to the customer. If, for some reason, you need to reverse 

an advance, you can do it here. 

After you reverse an advance, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can create another 

advance to replace it.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.
