© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reversing an Advance 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Advances > Reverse`


You can reverse advances that you misapplied and need to correct. 

To reverse a posted advance: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, click Advances. The Posted advances list opens.  

3. 
Find the advance that you want to reverse, and then click Reverse. The Transaction reversal 

date box opens. 

4. 
In the Transaction reversal date box, enter the following: 

• 
In Reverse the transaction on date, select the date for reversing the advance. This can 

be the payment summary date or a later date. You can even include a date from a 

prior closed period, so that your financial statements are correct. 

• 
In Memo, type a description that applies to this line item of the check. This text is for 

your information only. 

5. 
Click Submit. The Posted advances list appears, and you can see two line items for this 

transaction. (The transaction is not zeroed out so that there is an audit trail.) 

• 
One line item is the original transaction, where the Reverse link now is labeled 

Reversed. 

• 
The other line item added by the system is the reverse transaction, which produces a 

net effect of zero. This transaction is labeled Reversal. 

For example, you have a charge for $10. After reversing, you still have the original $10 charge, but 

also a charge for -$10, resulting in a net of zero. 

If you selected one or more invoices, a negative invoice is also created, resulting in a net of zero 

for those transactions as well.

Posted Advance Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Advances`


Use this page to view the details of a posted advance. When the information is complex, the 

system categorizes the information into two tabs: Advance information and Invoices. 

The Advance information tab has two sections: 

• 
The top section lists the details of the advance transaction. 

• 
The bottom section lists the line items.  

• 
Click the blue Customer ID to view the customer’s record. 

The Invoices tab lists the invoices that the advance paid for.  

• 
Click a blue invoice number to open the invoice. 

• 
Click the blue Customer ID to view the customer’s record. 

From the Posted advance details page, you can also: 

• 
Click the Print to button to print the posted advance’s detail. 

• 
Click the View audit trail button to view the audit trail. 

Printing Posted Advance Details 

You can save information about a posted payment to either a PDF or an XML file. From the 

Posted advance page, click the Print to button to print the posted advance’s detail. 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, click Advances. 

3. 
Find the advance that you want to print, and then click the View link. 

4. 
Click Print to and select the format in which you want to save the exported data. 

• 
XML: Select for round trip importing and exporting or if you want to use this data in 

an external application. 

• 
PDF: Select PDF for a printable format. 

If you select PDF, the system opens the exported file in Adobe Reader or in the application 

associated with PDF file extensions on your computer. Save the file on your computer. 

5. 
If you select XML, the system displays the XML formatted data on the page. Select and copy 

the data, and then paste it into a text editor. Save the file with an .xml extension.

### Adjustments
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 353*

Chapter 4: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Adjustments 

Managing accounts receivable adjustments involves adding, editing, exporting, and deleting 

adjustments made to customer accounts. You can use the Accounts Receivable Adjustment list to 

see all of the adjustments made to your customer accounts. You can then examine each 

adjustment transaction individually. 

Using Adjustments to Increase or Decrease the Amount a Customer Owes 

It is a better accounting practice to make an adjustment than to edit an invoice, so there is an 

audit trail of the history. Use adjustments in the event that there is a balance due you or the 

customer after an invoice is paid. For example, if the customer received damaged goods, you can 

make an appropriate adjustment to show the difference you owe the customer. When the 

customer applies the adjustment to a future payment, the balance will then be zero. 

In addition, you can designate adjustments as a credit memo (to decrease the amount the 

customer owes you) or a debit memo (to increase the amount the customer owes you). You 

would issue a credit memo if, for example, a customer inadvertently sends you a check for greater 

than the amount due or paid an invoice in full and then later returned the goods. 

In Multi-Entity, Multi-Currency Companies 

If your company is a multi-entity, multi-currency company, you can make adjustments at the top 

level or in the entities. When creating a top-level adjustment, you must select the base currency 

and location. However, when you make adjustments at the entity level, the system already knows 

the location and the base currency. In either case, you must select a transaction currency if you 

are entering a foreign currency adjustment. 

What Is the Difference Between an A/R Debit and Credit Memo? 

• 
Debit memo: increases the amount a customer owes you. For example, the customer might 

owe a late charge for failing to pay on time. 

• 
Credit memo: decreases the amount a customer owes you. For example, you might credit a 

customer for a product return, or reparation on bad service, or for shipping fees that were 

charged incorrectly.

Adding an A/R Adjustment

This section provides the fast track to getting an adjustment entered. For a description of every 

field, see field-by-field descriptions (on page 379). 

You are adjusting the overall customer account, not a particular invoice. Adjusting the account 
enables the customer to decide where and when to apply the adjustment. 

Credit Adjustments 

When you provide a credit to a customer, to record a simple decrease in the amount the 

customer owes, such as a credit for shipping costs, a return, or poor quality or service, you can 

enter the credited amount to show a decrease in your customer’s overall debt to you. You can 

then apply the decrease to one or more invoices at your convenience. 

This article describes how to create a credit adjustment for recording a simple decrease and 

answers questions about recording decreases when there are additional considerations, such as 

an associated project. 

A credit adjustment decreases the overall amount the customer owes you. For instance, if a 

customer makes a return, you create a credit adjustment for that customer to decrease the 

amount the customer owes you. 

Debit Adjustments 

A debit memo increases the overall amount the customer owes you. For instance, if you forgot to 

charge the customer for shipping or some other service, you can create an adjustment rather than 

a whole new invoice. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Before you start creating a credit memo, have the following key information on hand: 

• 
Supporting documents within or external to the system, such as an invoice. If you haven’t 

already done so, scan any hard-copy supporting documents onto your local drive for easy 

upload to the system. 

• 
The amount of the decrease. 

• 
The general ledger accounts to be affected, such as shipping or expense. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a

Exchange rate date if you’re a multi-currency company). You can change either date as 

needed, for example, if you want to create the adjustment today, but post it on a different 

date. 

4.

required.

decreases the overall amount the customer owes you.

—New— indicates that the system will complete the adjustment number when you save 
the draft or post the adjustment. 

6. 
Enter a Reference invoice number and Description as needed. The Reference invoice 

number can be used to search, sort, and report on invoices. 

7. 
To permanently and safely store a digital version of a supporting document, in the 

drop-down list next to Attachments, select an attachment from the list, or click Add and

to a record. Learn more about who can add attachments in Permissions for attachments.

Multi-Entity, Multi-Currency Companies 

If your company is a multi-entity, multi-currency company, you can make adjustments at the top 

level or in the entities. When creating a top-level adjustment, you must select the base currency 

and location. However, when you make adjustments at the entity level, the system already knows 

the location and the base currency. In either case, you must select a transaction currency if you 

are entering a foreign currency adjustment. 

If you’re a multi-currency company, enter the currency details in the Currency section: 

1. 
In the Transaction currency drop-down list, select the currency that was used in the 

transaction. If the currency is not your company’s base currency, continue with the next two 

steps. 

2. 
In the Base currency drop-down list, select the currency used by your entity. 

3. 
Click Exchange rate type, and then select RealPage Daily Rate which is the system-supplied 

default exchange rate type, unless you’ve defined a different one. 

If you know what the exchange rate for this transaction is or have contracted with the 

customer on a set exchange rate, you can type it in Exchange rate to override system 

calculations. 

4. 
In Exchange rate date, type or select a date. The default value is the current date, but you 

can override this. For example, you may want to change it to the date the transaction was 

issued or the date you intend to pay the transaction. (If you override the Date, the exchange 

rate date updates automatically.) 

Filling In the Line Items in the Entries Section 

Set Up Default Values for All Line Items (Optional) 

In the Entries section, you can add values directly to each line item where needed or click the 

Show defaults link to set up default values that the system will use to complete each line item. 

To set up a value as a default for each existing and new line item: 

1. 
Click Show defaults. 

2. 
In each drop-down list that you want the system to complete, choose a value.  

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button to save the selections.  

Keep in mind that you can override any default value on any line item.  

Learn more about setting up default line-item values (on page 558 ). See Line-Item Entry Tips in 
the online help or download the RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide for more tips.  

Entering Line Items Manually 

The minimum information required to post the adjustment is the account (or account label) and 
an amount for each line item.

Depending on your company, you may be required to enter other information, such as the 

department or location. Also, depending on how your company is set up, you can drill down to 

the detail level in line items to enter additional information. 

Enter line item information for each line item in this adjustment: 

1. 
Select the Location to associate with the adjustment. 

2. 
In the Account column, select the account to associate with the credit adjustment. 

 If your company has enabled account labels, this column is called Account label. Select the 

account label to associate with the credit adjustment. 

3. 
In the Amount column, type the item amount of the item. 

For companies using multiple currencies, this column is called Transaction amount. The 

Transaction amount is the amount expressed in the transaction currency. After you enter 

the transaction amount, the system calculates the amount using the exchange rate that you 

provided in the Currency section, and then completes the Base amount column. 

The system expects the Amount or Transaction amount column to be populated, even if 
the amount is zero (0). 

4. 
If you use departments, you can assign the adjustment to the desired department. Click the 

Department drop-down list, and then select the department that you want to associate with 

the credit adjustment. 

5. 
In the Memo field, type a note for any line item that might require explanation at some 

future date. 

6. 
To assign the adjustment to a unit, select the unit from the Unit drop-down list. 

7. 
To track the line item for reporting purposes, select the segment type in the Segment type 1 

drop-down list, and then select a value in the Segment value 1 drop-down list. Learn more 

about Segments. 

If the Segment type and Segment value fields do not appear, then your system may not 
have the segments feature enabled (on page 513 ). 

When you clicked in the line item’s row, the Show details tab appears. 

8. 
Click the Show details tab. The Details section opens. From this section, you can select 

additional segment types and their values.  

9. 
The A/R Account drop-down list appears in the Details section if you’ve enabled the default 

G/L account to be overridden as needed. You can select a G/L alternative account here to 

override the default G/L account for all line items, or you can override the designated 

account individually per line item. When you select an A/R account, the system populates

the override account list from the General Ledger alternative account information, or from 

the vendor or customer G/L account, if defined. 

Finishing the Adjustment 

When you finish entering the adjustment, save it as a draft or post it.  

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the transaction. The system saves the 

entry, but doesn’t post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the transaction. The system validates the transaction and 

posts it to the General Ledger. 

Which to Choose: Draft or Post? 

Draft: You can save a transaction as a draft without affecting the G/L or any subledger. With the 
ability to save A/P invoices, A/R invoices, and adjustments in draft state, you can save your 
progress. Later on, you or another user can come back and post the transaction. 

Post: The system validates transactions when they are posted. For example, required 
departments or locations are not validated until posting. 

If you are writing off an unpaid invoice, go to Apply credit to an invoice (on page 385).

To track the line item for reporting purposes, select the segment type in the Segment type 1 

drop-down list and then select a value in the Segment value 1 drop-down list. Learn more 

about Segments. 

When you click in the line item’s row, the Show details tab appears. 

If the Segment type and Segment value fields do not appear, then your system may not 
have the segments feature enabled (on page 513 ).

8. 
Click the Show details tab. The Details section opens. 

From this section, you can select additional segment types and values.

G/L account to be overridden as needed.  

9. 
You can select a G/L alternative account here to override the default G/L account for all line 

items, or you can override the designated account individually per line item. When you 

select an A/R account, the system populates the override account list from the General 

Ledger alternative account information, or from the vendor or customer G/L account, if 

defined. 

Finishing the Adjustment 

When you finish entering the adjustment, save it as a draft or post it.  

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the transaction. The system saves the 

entry, but doesn’t post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the transaction. The system validates the transaction and 

posts it to the General Ledger. 

Which to Choose: Draft or Post? 

Draft: You can save a transaction as a draft without affecting the G/L or any subledger. With the 
ability to save A/P invoices, A/R invoices, and adjustments in draft state, you can save your 
progress. Later on, you or another user can come back and post the transaction. 

Post: The system validates transactions when they are posted. For example, required 
departments or locations are not validated until posting. 

For help in finding the transaction later, see Finding Draft or Posted Transactions (on page 373).

#### Clearing an A/R Credit Adjustment
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 369*



#### Deleting Adjustments
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 369*

Chapter 4: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Clearing an A/R Credit Adjustment 

You can create a credit memo to record a credit against a customer, such as a credit for shipping 

costs, or a return of product. After you create a credit memo, if you need to clear it from the 

system, you can either reverse or delete it depending on where the adjustment stands in the work 

flow: 

• 
If you haven’t applied the adjustment to a customer invoice, you can delete the credit 

memo (on page 369). 

• 
If you’ve applied the adjustment to a customer invoice, then you can reverse the credit 

memo (on page 370). 

This topic describes how to clear a credit memo and answers questions about clearing credit 

memos when there are additional considerations, such as adjusting for monies owed by a 

customer that won’t be paid. 

After you delete or reverse an adjustment, you can’t undo the action. However, you can create 
another adjustment to replace it. 

Deleting Adjustments 

You can delete an adjustment only if it has not yet been applied to an invoice. After applying an 

adjustment to an invoice, you may be able to reverse it.  

The deletion is reflected in the month that you entered the adjustment.  

To delete an adjustment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Adjustments. The A/R Adjustments list opens. 

3. 
Select the Delete check box of the credit memo that you want to delete, and then click the 

Delete button. 

4. 
Confirm that you want to delete the credit memo. The system clears the credit memo from 

the list and from the system. 

---



#### Reversing Adjustments
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 370*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reversing Adjustments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Adjustments > Reverse > 
Submit`


You can’t delete a credit memo if you’ve applied a portion, or all, of the available adjustment to 

one or more invoices, but you can reverse it to clear the adjustment as follows: 

• 
If you’ve applied no payment on the adjustment against the customer, such as a check or 

ACH, you can reverse the credit memo. 

• 
If you’ve applied a payment on the adjustment, such as a transfer of funds to the customer 

bank account, you have to void the entire applied payment, and then reverse the 

adjustment. 

To reverse a credit memo that has no associated customer payment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Adjustments. The A/R Adjustment list opens to show a list 

of credit memos. 

3. 
Click Reverse by the desired credit memo. 

If you see a Delete link instead of a Reverse link, the credit memo hasn’t been applied to one 
or more invoices, and you can delete it. When deleted, the credit memo is cleared from the 
system. 

The Transaction reversal date page opens. 

4. 
Select the date for reversing the transaction. This is usually the original transaction date or a 

later date. 

5. 
To reverse the adjustment, click Submit. 

The credit memo is cleared from the system. The A/R Adjustment list displays the reversal 

on two rows to show the balancing transactions for removing the credit memo from the 

system. 

6. 
Optional. If you want to reverse one or more invoices associated with the adjustment, under 

Reverse, select the check box for each invoice, and click Submit. 

Both the credit memo and the selected invoices are cleared from the system. The A/R 

Adjustments list and the invoices list display the reversal on two rows to show the balancing 

transactions for removing the credit memo and the unpaid invoices from the system. 

To reverse a credit memo that has an associated customer payment: 

If you’ve recorded a customer payment associated with a credit memo, such as a transfer of funds 

to your bank account, you can reverse the payment in a couple of ways. You can reverse the 

payment from either the Posted payments page, or from the Receipts register. 

---


<!-- Page 371 -->
Chapter 4: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

To reverse a payment from the Posted Payments list: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select Payments. 

3. 
Locate the desired payment, and then click Reverse. The Transaction reversal date page 

opens with a default of today’s date, which you can change as needed. 

4. 
To reverse the payment, click Submit. The payment is cleared from the system. The Posted 

payments list displays the reversal on two rows to show the balancing transactions for 

removing the payment from the system. 

5. 
Now that there is no associated payment, you can reverse the credit memo. 

To reverse a payment from Receipts Register: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Receipts & Reports section, select Receipts. 

3. 
Select the Customer, and then click View to see the list of payments made by the customer. 

4. 
Click Reverse beside the payment associated with the customer credit. The Transaction 

reversal date page opens with a default of today’s date. 

5. 
To reverse the entry in the register, click Submit. 

The payment is cleared from the system. The Register payments list displays the reversal on 

two rows to show the balancing transactions for removing the payment from the system. 

Now that there is no associated payment, you can reverse the credit memo.

#### Other Ways to Reverse a Transaction
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 372*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Other Ways to Reverse a Transaction 

You can reverse a transaction from several places in RealPage Accounting, including: 

• 
Check register: Select Void to void the payment. The system reverses the A/P invoice. 

• 
Receipt register: Reverse the receipt of payment. 

• 
Bank register: Reverse a receipt of payment, or void payment to automatically reverse an 

A/P invoice. 

• 
A/R Adjustments List 

If the transaction was created in a closed period, you can: 

• 
Open the closed period to reverse the transaction with the original date. 

• 
Reverse the transaction in the current open period. 

The transaction must be partially or fully paid, unless you specifically configured your application 

for reversal of unpaid transactions, such as A/P invoices, A/R invoices, expenses, or adjustments. 

If the transaction state is Selected, remove the transaction from the selected state, and then 
reverse the transaction. 

If the transaction state is Partially paid or Paid, reverse the payment first, and then reverse the 
transaction.

Finding Draft or Posted Transactions 

Lists of transactions let you view and access all transactions of a specific type, such as invoices or 

adjustments. 

There are two ways to locate and view items in the draft and posted state. 

• 
Filter for Draft or Posted Transactions on the Fly

The system filters the list, displaying only those items with a state matching the text that you 

typed. 

• 
Create a Permanent Custom View That Filters for Draft or Posted Transactions 

Create a view (on page 576).  

In the view, set the filter to the desired state (Draft, Posted, Submitted, Selected, Partially 

Paid).

Saving an A/R Transaction as a Draft 

When you are not ready to post that A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or adjustment, you can save it as a 

draft without affecting the G/L or any subledger. With the ability to save A/P invoices, A/R 

invoices, and adjustments in Draft state, you can save your progress so far. Later on, you or 

another user can come back and post the transaction. 

The system validates transactions only when they are posted. For example, required 
departments or locations are not validated until posting. 

Prerequisites: Your ability to add a transaction in draft state or post a transaction depends on 

your permissions: 

• 
Add permission enables you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as a draft. 

• 
Add, Edit, and Post permissions enable you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as 

draft, and edit and post the transaction when you’re ready. 

To save a transaction in draft format: 

1. 
Add an A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or adjustment to your company. 

2. 
Save the transaction as a draft by clicking Draft & new or selecting Draft, or Draft & 

continue from the button drop-down list.  

The system saves the transaction entry, but doesn’t post it. 

To retrieve a draft transaction, open the transaction type ’s list. For example, if you created a 
draft A/R invoice, open the A/R invoices list. To find draft transactions in a list, type the word 
“Draft ” in the State column, and then press ENTER.  

Posting an A/R Adjustment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Adjustments > Edit/View > 
Post/Post & New`


To post an adjustment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, select Adjustments. The adjustments list opens. 

3. 
Find the adjustment you want to post, and then click Edit or View. 

4. 
When the adjustment is ready to post, click Post and select one of the following: 

• 
Post to post the transaction. 

• 
Post & New to post the transaction and create a new transaction of the same type.

#### Printing a Transaction
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 379*



##### Fields
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 379*

Chapter 4: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Printing a Transaction 

After you create a transaction, you can print a copy of it. You can print from the transaction page 

itself, such as from the A/P invoice or A/R invoice pages, or from the transaction list page. 

To print a transaction: 

• 
From a transaction list: Locate the appropriate transaction and, at the end of the row, click 

Print. 

• 
From a transaction page: Click the Print button at the top of the page. 

The system generates a PDF of the transaction, which you can view, print, or save to add as an 

email attachment as needed. 

After you apply a credit adjustment to an invoice, the invoice is updated to show that the 
amount due is reduced by the amount of the credit. However, if you send the customer an 
updated invoice, the invoice does not show why the amount due was reduced. You can send the 
customer an A/R statement to show which adjustments were applied to which invoices. Learn 
more about printing or emailing A/R statements (on page 461 ). 

Fields 

Adjustments List Columns 

Customer name 
This is the customer who is the target of the adjustment. 

Adjustment number 
This is the record number assigned to the adjustment.  

Date 
This is the transaction date. 

Transaction currency This is the currency used in the transaction. 

This column appears only when your company has enabled the 

multi-currency feature. 

Transaction amount 
If you’ve enabled multi-currency, the system displays Base Amount and 

Transaction Amount in place of Amount. 

Transaction amount is the amount of the adjustment in the currency you 

set for the transaction. 

For example, if your base currency is USD and you create a 100.00 Euro 

adjustment, for the adjustment line item, you see the adjustment with 

100.00 Euro as the transaction amount and 110.00 USD as the base 

amount (assuming a 1.1 exchange rate from Euro to USD). 

---


<!-- Page 380 -->
Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Amount 

or 

Base amount 

If you’ve enabled multi-currency, the system displays Base Amount and 

Transaction Amount in place of Amount. 

Base Amount is the amount of the adjustment in the base currency of 

your company. 

State 
This is the current part of the processing cycle for the adjustment: 

Draft: The adjustment is created, but not posted. It can be changed 

without consequence. 

Posted: The adjustment was posted to the G/L 

Paid: Customer payment was applied. 

Partially Paid: Only partial payment was applied. There is a remaining 

amount to be applied. 

Finding transactions in a specific state  

List views of transactions provide a one-stop shop for viewing and 

accessing all transactions of a specific type, for example, A/P invoices or 

A/R invoices.  

There are two ways to locate transactions in a specific state: 

• 
Filter for the transaction state on the fly: In the transaction list 

view, enter the state in the State column, then click Go. The list 

displays only those transactions in that state.  

• 
Create a permanent custom view that filters for the transaction 

state: Create the view, and set the filter to State = <state>, 

where <state> equals the state that you are seeking, such as 

Draft, Posted, Paid, Reversed, and so forth. This custom view is 

always available from the transaction list. 

Summary title 
This is the name of the summary that contains this adjustment. 

---


<!-- Page 381 -->
Chapter 4: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

The following table describes each item on the A/R Adjustment page. 

A/R Adjustments 

Date 
The date defaults to the current date. You can choose to enter a 

different date. Editing a date in an A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or 

adjustment associated with a project requires you to:  

1. Edit the transaction to remove the project, and then post it. 

2. Edit the transaction to change the date, and then post it. 

3. Edit the transaction to add the project back in, and then post it. 

G/L posting date 
Displays only if enabled in the Configure Accounts Receivable page. This 

is the date on which the transaction actually posts to the general ledger. 

Unless you change it, this date defaults to the transaction date. 

Customer 
The customer who is the target of the adjustment. You can either select 

a customer from the drop-down list or enter the name of the customer 

for the adjustment. For customers you use repeatedly, it’s best to enter 

them into the system. 

Bill to  
This field determines the customer contact to invoice for this sale. The 

system automatically defaults this field from the Bill to contact field in 

the customer record. You can override the default as required, for 

example, if the customer has multiple offices and requests that you send 

the invoice to an office other than the one on record. 

Ship to 
This field determines the customer contact for shipping. The system

#### Applying Credit to an Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 385*

Chapter 4: Payments

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

How to Refund a Credit Memo 

If a customer has a credit and prefers to have the money refunded instead of waiting to apply the 

credit to a future invoice, see Refunding credit to a customer (on page 389). 

How to Get Here 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Receive a Payment`


1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily tasks section, select Receive a payment. 

Applying Credit to an Invoice 

After you’ve entered one or more credits to decrease the amount of money a customer owes you, 

you can then apply that credit to an entire invoice, or multiple invoices. 

After you apply credit, you can view the posting details from the adjustment record. Go to the 
adjustment record and select View details in the summary header. 

In a multi-entity company, RealPage Accounting applies credit to the owning entity first, and then 

applies credit from the oldest to the newest invoices. If you enable your company to limit credits 

to the owning entity, then credits are applied to the invoices of the owning entity and no other. 

Any remaining credit is reserved for other invoices owned by that entity. 

You can apply credits to invoices for the same customer. You cannot apply credits from one 
customer to the invoices of another customer, even if they are in a parent-child relationship. 

To apply credit to an invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select the Receive a payment option. 

3. 
Select the customer. The customer’s available credits and invoices appear below. 

• 
To receive a payment in addition to applying credits, select the payment method, and 

then type the payment amount. 

• 
To apply credits without recording a payment receipt, set the payment method to 

Cash and then verify that the payment amount is 0.00. 

4. 
In the Available Credits section, select the credits that you want to use for the invoices to 

pay. If you select the Receive full check box, the system applies the full amount of the credit 

to the selected invoices. Otherwise, you can enter a partial amount of the credit in the 

Credits to apply field. 

---



#### Selecting Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 386*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The total amount that you can use to pay invoices appears in the Amount available to 

apply field at the top of the Available invoices and debit memos 
section. This includes the 
credit amount, the payment that you are receiving if any, and any overpayments or 
advances that you have selected.  

5. 
In the invoices or memos that you want to apply credit to, either click the Receive full check 

box or type the amount to apply to the invoice in the Amount received field.  

As you apply the credit amount against invoices, the Amount available to apply number 
reduces to reflect your actions.  

6. 
Click Save. 

After you apply credit, you can view the payment details in the Posted Payments list. Open 

the payment record and select the Invoices tab.  

Selecting Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Receive a Payment`


You can quickly filter for customer invoices for the purpose of applying credit. 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Receive a payment.  

3. 
In the Customer drop-down list, select the customer. The system completes the Select 

invoices for payment page with a list of all available credits, invoices, and debit memos for 

the selected customer. 

For a more detailed description of options for selecting invoices, see Pay A/P Invoices page.

#### Applying Credits Without Recording a Payment Receipt
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 387*

Applying Credits Without Recording a Payment Receipt 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Enter Payments > Receive a Payment`


You can apply one or more credit memos to any outstanding invoice or debit memo solely on its 

own. 

To apply credit without recording a payment receipt: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Enter payments section, select Receive a Payment. The Select invoices for payment 

page opens. 

3. 
In the Available Credits section, do one or both of the following: 

• 
Select the Receive Full check box next to one or more credits. 

• 
Type a partial amount in Credits to Apply for any credit that you won’t use fully. 

The total credit amount appears in the Amount available to apply field at the bottom of the 

page. 

4. 
In the Available Invoices and Debit Memos section, do one of the following: 

• 
Type the amount of the credit in the Amount Received field of any available 

transaction, and then click Save. The system applies the credit to the selected 

transaction. 

• 
Leave the fields in the Amount received column empty, and then click Save.

#### Applying Credits Along with Recording a Payment Receipt
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 388*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Applying Credits Along with Recording a Payment Receipt 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Receive a Payment`


You can combine receiving a payment with applying credits as needed. 

To record a payment receipt and select and apply credits: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Receive a Payment. The Select invoices for payment page 

opens. 

3. 
Enter the payment amount in the appropriate field, depending on the type of payment. For 

example, if the payment is a check, enter the amount in the Check amount field. 

4. 
In the Available Credits section, do one or both of the following: 

• 
Select Full beside one or more credits. 

• 
Enter a partial amount in Credits to apply for any credit that you won’t use fully. 

The total credit amount appears in the Amount available to apply field at the bottom of the 

page. 

5. 
In the Available invoices and debit memos section, do one of the following: 

• 
Select Receive full beside one or more transactions to which you want the payment 

applied. The system records payment in full for the selected transactions and 

distributes the credit across them. 

• 
Enter a partial amount in Amount received for one or more transactions. The system 

records the payment of partial amounts for the selected transactions and distributes 

the credit across them. 

Example 

If you receive a check for $5,000.00 and apply a credit of $500.00, the Amount Received for an 

invoice is $5,500.00. 

The Invoice and Debit Memo Subtotals is $5,500.00. 

The Amount Applied is equal to the actual check amount of $5,000.00. 

The Amount Overpaid is equal to 0.00.

#### Refunding a Customer
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 389*



#### Changing the Amount Credited After Applying It
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 389*

Chapter 4: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Refunding a Customer 

A customer may have a negative balance as the result of overpaying an invoice, paying an 

advance that was never used, or receiving a credit that was never used. If you don’t plan on 

invoicing the customer again or the customer would like the money back without delay, you can 

issue a refund check. 

To refund a credit to a customer: 

1. 
Add an A/R adjustment (on page 356) (debit memo) that adjusts the customer balance to 

zero. 

2. 
Open the Accounts receivable application, and then select Receive a payment.  

3. 
Select apply the adjustment (on page 385). Unless you apply the debit memo, open 

transactions and the adjustment will continue to display in your aging report. 

4. 
Create the customer as a one-time vendor. Learn more about Adding vendors. 

5. 
Add a manual payment to refund the money owed to the customer, making the vendor you 

created the payee. 

If you get stuck, find out how to find help or contact support. (on page 603 ) 

Changing the Amount Credited After Applying It 

You can’t change the credited amount after you apply and save it, but you can reverse the credit 

under the following conditions: 

• 
If you recorded a payment and applied an A/R credit, then you can reverse the payment, 

which also reverses the credit and makes it available again. 

• 
If you applied an A/R credit, then you can reverse the credit, which makes it unavailable. 

---

### Subledgers
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 392*

Subledgers 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Subledgers 

Summaries are collections of the same type of transactions, grouped together for processing. 

Until you or the system creates a new summary, no line items appear in the Summaries list. 

Summaries can be either opened or closed. When summaries are open in Accounts receivable, 

you can add invoices, adjustments, and deposits.  

In designing an accounts receivable process, the system administrator can give access to the 
pages involved with managing invoices, but not opening or closing summaries. 

A subledger includes all transactions of a certain type. In RealPage Accounting, the Accounts 

receivable application has two subledgers. 

Summaries List 

The A/R Summaries list includes all types of Accounts receivable transactions. 

• 
Invoices 

• 
Imported invoices 

• 
Reversed invoices 

• 
Penalties 

• 
Intercompany billing invoices 

• 
Adjustments 

• 
Reversed adjustments 

• 
Quick deposits (Manual deposits) 

Payment Summaries List 

The Payment summaries list includes all incoming payment transactions, including: 

• 
The A/P invoice and adjustment summaries that users can directly access. 

• 
The invisible transactions that involve payments. 

Subledger Status 

Summaries can be either opened or closed. When summaries are open in Accounts receivable, 

you can add invoices, adjustments, and deposits.  

When you first create a summary, the summary is open. While it is open, you can add transactions 

to it. You close a summary so that no one can change the transactions in the summary.

About A/R Summaries 

Summaries are collections of the same type of transactions, grouped together for processing. 

Until you or the system creates a new summary, no line items appear in the Summaries list.  

Summaries can be either open or closed. When summaries are open in Accounts receivable, you 

can add invoices, adjustments, and deposits. In designing an accounts receivable process, the 

system administrator can give access to the pages involved with managing invoices, but not 

opening or closing summaries. 

Summaries for invoice, adjustment, and quick deposits are created in two ways. 

• 
You can create payment summaries manually. 

• 
You can have the system automatically generate summaries at intervals.  

Manually Created Summaries 

A manual summary is useful when you need a special summary that includes specific invoices. You 

might need a manual payment summary for receiving payments. In these cases, you can create a 

special summary by creating and naming the summary for the special situation. 

To make a payment manually, go to Accounts Receivable > All > Receive a Payment. For details, 

see Receiving a payment (on page 273). 

Automatically Created Summaries 

The system can automatically create summaries so that a summary always exists for invoices and 

other transactions as they are entered throughout the day. Automatic summaries are created 

according to preselected time intervals. See Creating Automatic Summaries (on page 411). 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have Administrator privileges to work with summaries. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with summaries: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts receivable 
Summaries 
List View, Add, Edit, Delete, Open, Close 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 584) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions.

Opening and Closing Summaries 

Closing procedures and policies vary from company to company. Consequently, RealPage 

Accounting offers flexibility so the system can adapt to your business practices. 

Before you finally close the books for a period, you can close individual transaction summaries in: 

• 
Accounts Payable (AP) 

• 
Accounts Receivable (AR) 

You can also close periods in Cash Management. 

This section includes: 

• 
Closing books

### Closing A/R Summaries
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 396*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 396*

Subledgers 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Closing A/R Summaries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Periodic Tasks > Month End > Close 
Subledger`


Closing the books for a period also closes all the summaries and Cash Management periods. 

When you close the books for a period, the system closes all open transaction summaries and the 

Cash Management period.  

If you need to make a change to a particular summary in A/P, A/R, TE, and CE, or a period, you do 

not need to re-open all the books for that period. You can re-open only the application subledger 

that you need.  

By subledger, we mean all transactions in a given application. For example, in Accounts Payable, 
this includes not only the A/P invoice and adjustment summaries users can directly access, but 
invisible transactions that involve payments or even inter-entity transfers.  

If you have different staff for A/P and A/R, you need to: 

1. 
Stop writing checks as you approach your monthly closing of the books. 

2. 
Close down the A/P clerks’ books while leaving the A/R clerks free to continue entering 

invoices and payments.  

• 
Close all books. 

• 
Re-open only the A/R books.  

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to close A/R summaries: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Accounts receivable 
Summaries 
List, Close 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 584) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions.

### Close A/R Subledger Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 397*

Chapter 5: Subledgers 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Close A/R Subledger Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Periodic Tasks > Month End > Close 
Subledger`


Use the Close A/R Subledger page to close a summary.  

The purpose of closing a summary is to prevent everyone from posting transactions to the wrong 

period. After closing a summary, no one can add transactions to it, or delete transactions from it. 

Closed summaries can later be reopened.  

The list shows the entities and the dates that the A/R subledgers are closed through. To generate 

a report of entities and their closed through dates, click the Export to Excel button.  

RealPage Accounting uses the summary ’s date as the posting date for almost all transactions.

Closing Summaries in a Multi-Entity Company 

You can close a summary based on an entity and a starting period that you select, or you can 

close a single summary.  

From the Close A/R Subledger page, you can close previously open summaries either by period 

or by summary name.  

After you’ve closed a summary, you can no longer add transactions to it or delete transactions 

from it. If you open a summary to post only one transaction, remember to close it immediately so 

no one can inadvertently post transactions to it. 

Users in the top-level company may close summaries for all entities or a single entity. Users at 
the entity level may close summaries only for the entity they are currently in.

Finding Which Periods Are Closed 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Books > Close`


If you need to determine which months or periods are closed, go to the General ledger and look 

at the Close books page. 

Because closing one period closes all of the prior periods, there can’t be any unclosed books 

before the last closed date. The Close company books from field shows you the date that the 

company books were last closed. 

For multi-entity companies, select the entity of interest to see the last closed date.

#### Reopening the A/R Books
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 405*

Chapter 5: Subledgers 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Reopening the A/R Books 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Month End > Books > Open`


To reopen A/R books: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic Tasks section, under Month end, click Books, and then select Open. 

3. 
In the Open Books page, select the Open accounts receivable check box.  

4. 
Click the Open Books button. 

Because the permissions check boxes for the Close/Open Books pages in G/L, Close/Open 

Subledger in AP/A/R, and Close/Open Periods in Cash Management are separate, you can 

assign different staff to different tasks. For example, an A/P supervisor might have 

permissions to close and open A/P summaries, but only the Accounting Manager has 

permission to Close books and Open books in the G/L. While this is useful in a stand-alone 

company, it is even more useful in a shared structure of multiple companies. Users in the 

top-level company have control over the entities directly from the top level, and do not 

need to slide into the entities to close books or open them. More specifically, they can open 

the books for all entities or a single entity, and open specific subledgers in the selected 

entities. In other words, the top-level user can open one subledger in one entity to make a 

change without exposing other subledgers in that entity or any subledgers in any other 

entities.

#### Adding a Summary
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 409*

Chapter 5: Subledgers

Adding a Summary 

See the How to Get Here (on page 407) topic for a list of ways to access the Summaries list. 

This procedure refers to adding the summary itself, not adding items to the summary. 

We recommend that you set up automatic summaries (daily or monthly) by going to Company > 

Subscriptions and clicking Accounts Receivable, and then clicking Configure. The summary date is 
the date the General Ledger uses to post all transactions within that summary. Therefore, it is 
important that you do not combine transactions from different time periods in the same 
summary. Also, note that a summary is posted automatically to the G/L after all transactions in 
the summary are saved. 

To add a summary: 

1. 
Open the Summaries list (on page 407). 

2. 
Click Add.  

3. 
In the Summary title field, type a name for the summary. The system uses this name to 

identify the summary throughout the application. 

4. 
In the G/L Posting date field, type or select the date you want the items in this summary to 

post to the general ledger.  

The system fills in the field with the current date, but you can change it. 

5. 
To deactivate (or close) the summary, click Status, and then click Inactive. Otherwise, leave 

Status set to Active. 

6. 
In the Summary Type section, select the type of items that you want this summary to 

contain: 

• 
Invoice 

• 
Adjustment 

• 
Quick deposit (Manual deposit) 

7. 
Click Save.  

The summary you created is a manual summary even if the auto-summary feature is on.

Deleting Summaries 

See the How to Get Here (on page 407) topic for a list of ways to access the Summaries list. 

You can delete a summary in the Summaries list. Before you can delete a summary, make sure its 

status is open, and that it does not contain any transactions. If the summary is closed, open it. If it 

contains transactions, first delete the transactions, and then delete the summary. 

To delete a summary: 

1. 
Open the Summaries list (on page 407). 

2. 
In the Summaries list, find the summary you want to delete. 

3. 
At the end of the row, click the check box in the Delete column.  

4. 
Click the Delete button. The system opens the delete confirmation page. 

5. 
Click OK. 

Deactivating or Closing a Summary 

To deactivate (or close) a summary: 

1. 
Open the Summaries list. 

2. 
Find the summary that you want to deactivate (or close) and click the Edit link. 

3. 
In Status, select Inactive. 

4. 
Click the Save button. 

Creating Automatic Summaries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration`


We recommend that you set up automatic summaries. The system offers four types of automatic 

summaries: 

• 
Invoices 

• 
Adjustments 

• 
Quick deposits 

• 
Payments 

The system posts summaries automatically to the G/L after the transactions in the summaries are 

saved. 

 You must be at the top level to use this feature. 

You must have administrator-level permissions to set up automatic summaries. 

---


<!-- Page 412 -->
Subledgers 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

RealPage standardizes the date format for all automatically created summaries on the 
internationally accepted format of YYYY -MM-DD24:MI:SS. Standardizing the date format in 
the summary title ensures that transactions are always grouped or matched to the appropriate 
summary, and eliminates the risk of posting errors due to a date format mismatch.  
The date that the system creates a summary is the date the General Ledger uses to post all 
transactions in that summary. Therefore, it is important that you do not combine transactions 
from different time periods in the same summary.  

To create automatic summaries: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

3. 
In the Accounting settings section, locate the Summary frequency section. 

4. 
Select how often that you want the system to create summaries. 

5. 
Select the Per payment method check box if you want the system to run a separate 

payment summary for each method of payment. 

6. 
Click the Save button.

#### Importing Transactions into a Summary
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 422*

Subledgers 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide

Importing Transactions into a Summary 

(Summary Title) > Import 

See the How to Get Here (on page 407) topic for a list of ways to access the Summaries list. 

You can import transactions into a summary in Accounting and Commercial Property 

Management.  

You can choose whether to post the imported transactions to the G/L or to mark them as 

historical. The system does not post historical transactions to the G/L. 

Transactions that you import and post to the general ledger must follow these guidelines: 

• 
The CSV file can include a maximum of 5,000 transactions per file. 

• 
Import open transactions only. Do not include paid or partially paid transactions. 

• 
The file you import must be in CSV format. If your csv file contains dates, you can set the 

date format to match the format in the CSV file. 

To import transactions: 

1. 
Open the Summaries list. 

2. 
Find the summary into which you want to import transactions, and then click the link in the 

Summary title column. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Import company information page opens. 

4. 
Click the Browse button and click the file with the transaction data to import. 

5. 
Click the Open button to choose the file. 

6. 
In File encoding, you can allow the system to auto detect the type of CSV file that you are 

uploading, or you can select a specific CSV file format, such as Mac OSx, Windows-1252, 

and more. 

7. 
In Post to, select the mode for importing: 

• 
Historical: imported transactions have no effect on the general ledger. 

• 
General ledger: imported transactions are posted live to the general ledger. 

When importing to the General ledger, the system processes the import offline and posts 

the transactions using daily batching. 

Errors cause the system to roll back the import immediately. 

8. 
If you select Historical, you can choose to process the import offline. This is useful if your 

import file is large.

Transaction currency  This column contains the currency used in the transaction.

Transaction amount  This column contains the amount of the transaction in the currency used

This column only displays when multi-currency is enabled. 

Base amount 
This column contains the amount of the transaction in the base currency 

of your company. 

This column only displays when multi-currency is enabled. 

State 
This column contains the current location of the transaction in the 

processing cycle: 

• 
Draft: the invoice is created, but not posted. It can be changed 

without consequence. 

• 
Posted: The invoice was posted to the G/L. 

• 
Paid: The customer payment was made. 

• 
Partially Paid: Only partial payment was made. There is a 

remaining amount to be paid. 

• 
Reversed: The invoice was reversed by a second transaction, 

which essentially zeroed out the balance in the G/L. Your 

company retains a record of the reversed invoice and the 

reversal transaction for audit trail purposes. 

• 
Reversal: This transaction is created when you reverse a 

transaction, which causes the balance to zero out. 

• 
No value: This transaction is posted but has not affected the 

G/L. 

Summary title 
This column contains the title given to the summary when you or the 

system created it.

### Payment Summaries List
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 426*

Subledgers 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Payment Summaries List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 427) topic for a list of ways to access the Payment summaries 

list. 

Use the Payment summaries list to view a list of summaries of payment transactions. Payment 

summaries include: 

• 
Payment receipts 

• 
Reversed receipts 

• 
Manual deposits 

The list includes both manually created and system-created payment summaries. 

• 
Manually created payment summaries are summaries that you create when you are paying a 

batch of invoices and you want to add the invoices you are paying to a group. 

• 
System-created payment summaries are created by the system when your system is 

configured to create automatic summaries (on page 411). 

We recommend that you set up automatic summaries (daily or monthly) by going to Company > 

Subscriptions > Accounts Receivable > Configuration. 

The Summary date is the date the General ledger uses to post all transactions in that summary. 

Therefore, it is important that you do not combine transactions from different time periods in the 

same summary. Also, note that summaries are posted automatically to the G/L after transactions 

in those summaries are saved. 

From this list, you can: 

• 
Add a new payment summary manually 

• 
Edit a payment summary’s details 

• 
Deactivate or close a summary 

• 
Delete a payment summary 

• 
Export the payment summary list 

• 
Sort and filter this list to see just the payment summaries you want. 

• 
View the list of transactions in a payment summary 

• 
Display transactions that are related to customers, tenants, or owners (depending on the 

application that you are using). 

List Tools 

For information about filters, sorts, and views, see Managing lists using filtering, sorting, and 

views (on page 560). For information about field-level controls, see Using controls in drop-down 

lists.

#### Creating Automatic Payment Summaries Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 428*



#### Creating Automatic Summaries
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 428*

Subledgers 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Creating Automatic Payment Summaries Workflow 

The system can automatically create payment summaries so that a summary always exists as they 

are entered throughout the day. Automatic summaries are created according to preselected time 

intervals. You set the frequency of automatic summary creation in the Configure Accounts 

Receivable page.  

Workflow 

1. 
Set the payment summary frequency (on page 411).  

2. 
Create payment transactions during the period. 

At the designated interval, the system automatically creates payment summaries. 

Creating Automatic Summaries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration`


We recommend that you set up automatic summaries. The system offers four types of automatic 

summaries: 

• 
Invoices 

• 
Adjustments 

• 
Quick deposits 

• 
Payments 

The system posts summaries automatically to the G/L after the transactions in the summaries are 

saved. 

 You must be at the top level to use this feature. 

You must have administrator-level permissions to set up automatic summaries. 

RealPage standardizes the date format for all automatically created summaries on the 
internationally accepted format of YYYY -MM-DD24:MI:SS. Standardizing the date format in 
the summary title ensures that transactions are always grouped or matched to the appropriate 
summary, and eliminates the risk of posting errors due to a date format mismatch.  
The date that the system creates a summary is the date the General Ledger uses to post all 
transactions in that summary. Therefore, it is important that you do not combine transactions 
from different time periods in the same summary.  

---

Chapter 5: Subledgers 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

To create automatic summaries: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

3. 
In the Accounting settings section, locate the Summary frequency section. 

4. 
Select how often that you want the system to create summaries. 

5. 
Select the Per payment method check box if you want the system to run a separate 

payment summary for each method of payment. 

6. 
Click the Save button.

#### Creating a Payment Summary Manually
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 430*

Subledgers 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Creating a Payment Summary Manually 

Payment Summaries > Add 

See the How to Get Here (on page 427) topic for a list of ways to access the Payment Summaries 

list. 

To create a payment summary manually: 

1. 
Open the Payment summaries list. 

2. 
Click the Add button. The Payment summary information page opens. 

3. 
In the Summary title field, type a name for the summary. The system uses this name to 

identify the summary. 

4. 
In the G/L posting date field, type or select the date you want the items in this summary to 

post to the general ledger. The system fills in the current date, but you can change it. 

5. 
Select the account to use for cash and check deposits: 

• 
If you select Bank account, then select the account where the deposits were made. 

• 
If you select Undeposited funds account, select the account to use as a transfer 

account so that you can deposit the payments later. You can also use the field-level 

options Add to add a new G/L account or Find to find a G/L account’s record. To add 

or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

RealPage recommends using this feature when applying payments so that the deposit 
shows as a single amount on the bank reconciliation. 

6. 
Set the Status to Active.  

7. 
Click the Save button. The Payment summaries list opens. 

The summary you create is a manual summary even when the auto-summary feature is 

enabled. 

8. 
Find the payment summary that you just created, and then click the Payments link. The new 

payment summary opens as a blank list.  

9. 
Click the Add button. The Receive payments list opens. 

10. 
Find the invoices that you want to include in the payment summary and click the Select 

invoices link. The Select invoices for payment page is displayed. 

11. 
Select the invoices to add to the payment summary. 

12. 
Click the Save button.

Editing Payment Summaries

#### Adding Transactions to a Payment Summary
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 435*

Chapter 5: Subledgers 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Adding Transactions to a Payment Summary 

Payment Summaries > Add > Payments > Select Invoices 

See the How to Get Here (on page 427) topic for a list of ways to access the Payment summaries 

list. 

A payment summary is a batch of deposited money. Typically, someone deposits multiple 

payments at one time, resulting in a billing batch. Each batch of payments is given a name so that 

you can refer to the payment by the name of the batch it is in, and make the association with the 

original invoice.  

You can add payments to any payment summary except for a manual deposit summary, which 

can’t be edited. 

To add a transaction to a payment summary: 

1. 
Select Payment summaries. 

2. 
Find the desired summary to which you want to add a payment receipt, and click Payments. 

The system displays the Payments list. 

3. 
Click Add. The Receive payments page opens. 

4. 
Click the Select invoices link of the customer, tenant, or owner whose payment you are 

receiving. The Select Invoices for Payment page opens. 

5. 
Select and process the invoice that you want to include in the payment summary.  

The total of the invoice that you select must match the payment that you received. 

6. 
Select the Receive full check boxes of all invoices against which you want to apply the 

payment. You can also type a partial amount in the Amount received field. 

7. 
Click Save. The system adds the payment to the summary and the Receive Payments list 

opens. 

8. 
On the Receive Payment page, click Done to close the list. You can also: 

• 
Select another Select invoices link to continue selecting invoices for payment. 

• 
Click the Export button to save this list of owners and their Totals due in a file. The 

Payments page of the selected summary now reflects the payments that you received.

#### Applying an Overpayment an Invoice in a Summary
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 437*

Chapter 5: Subledgers 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Applying an Overpayment an Invoice in a Summary 

Payment Summaries > Payments > Apply More 

See the How to Get Here (on page 427) topic for a list of ways to access payment summaries. 

When you receive a payment for more than is owed on all invoices, you can use the overpayment 

amount to either pay future invoices or refund the amount to the payer. The system tracks the 

amount left over as an overpayment. 

This procedure describes how to apply an overpayment credit using the Apply More feature.  

To use the Apply More option, the summary must be open, and the summary status must be 

active. 

To apply an overpayment to an invoice: 

1. 
Open the Payment summaries list. 

2. 
Click the Payments link to display the list of payments in the summary.  

3. 
In the list, find an invoice that needs to be paid. The column next to Left to Apply shows the 

payment status. Look for a transaction that shows Apply more in the column, and then click 

the link. The Select Invoices for Payment page opens so that you can apply the 

overpayment to the charge.  

At the top level of a multi-entity shared environment, the overpayment location must be 
the same as the bank you’re using to receive the payment, or the location of the invoice you 
are paying. If you’re applying payment to a multiple line item invoice belonging to a different 
entity, then the bank location is designated as the overpayment location by default. 
At the entity level, you can use the invoice entity and sub-location as the overpayment 
location. 

4. 
Process the payment as usual.  

You can select the Receive full check box for a charge in the Available invoices and debit 

memos section that can be paid by using the amount shown in the Amount available to 

apply field. 

5. 
Click Save.

#### Applying Invoice Penalties
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 445*

Chapter 6: Account Maintenance 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Penalties 

Use the Penalties menu option to apply penalties to one or more customers. 

Apply Penalties Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Penalties`


Use this page to determine how the system calculates the penalty and to set up filters to retrieve 

a list of invoices to penalize. After you click the View button, the list of invoices displays, allowing 

you to select the specific invoices and then apply the penalty. 

This page has four sections: 

• 
Penalty options: Set the name of the penalties batch file, and then select the calculation 

method. 

• 
Filters: Set up filters to get a list of the invoices you want to penalize. 

• 
Additional filters: Set up advanced filters to target the list of invoices to select from. 

• 
Format: Select how you want the list to be sorted. 

Applying Invoice Penalties 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Account Maintenance > Penalties`


To apply penalties: 

1. 
If you are at the top level, select the desired entity from the Level menu.  

2. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

3. 
In the Account maintenance section, select Penalties. The Apply Penalties page opens. 

Setting Penalty Options 

1. 
Type a description for the penalty document. This text will appear on the adjustment record 

for the penalty. 

When you penalize invoices, the system creates an adjustment within a summary named 

PENALTIES. The adjustment documents have a Description field. The system uses the text 

you enter here for the Description field in the adjustment. The default description is Penalty, 

but you can change that description to describe the penalty more closely, for example “Late 

Fee.” The description also appears on the printed adjustment. 

2. 
In the Calculate penalty by section, choose whether to calculate the amount of the penalty 

based on the amount of the invoice or the due amount.  

• 
Select Invoice amount to penalize the entire invoice amount.  

---



#### Setting and Applying the Filters
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 446*

Account Maintenance 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Select Due amount to penalize just the remaining amount due when the customer has 

partially paid the invoice. For example, suppose you have an invoice of $100, and the 

customer has paid $75 leaving an amount due of $25. You can penalize the entire 

invoice of 100 or only the amount due of $25. 

Next, see Setting and Applying the Filters (on page 229). 

Setting and Applying the Filters 

Setting filter options enables you to narrow the focus to only those invoices you want to penalize. 

The resulting filtered list appears in the Select Invoices to Penalize list, which appears after you 

click View. 

You can set as many filter options as you want. You can also choose not to set up any filters to 
get a complete list of invoices eligible for penalties. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

You can filter for a range of customer invoices in From Customer and To Customer. Select a 

beginning and ending customer respectively to identify a range of customers. The drop-down 

lists customers in order by ID number. 

Filling In the Additional Filters Section 

Use the additional filters to target specific eligible invoices.  

• 
These filters are optional. 

• 
Use up to four filters to target specific eligible invoices.  

• 
Set up the filters in the order which you want them filtered and sorted.  

For each filter you use, select an operator such as equals or greater than, and type the value you 

want to filter by in the text box. Customer, Customer ID, Invoice Amount, and Total Due are all 

derived from the invoice. 

To apply additional filters: 

1. 
Starting with the top drop-down list in this section, select the most important information to 

filter on: Customer, Customer ID, Invoice amount, or Total due. 

2. 
Select an operator and enter the value to filter on.  

3. 
For each additional filter, select an operator such as equals or greater than, and type the 

value you want to filter by in the text box. 

Example: 

---

This example narrows the list of customers to those with names starting with U that have an 

invoice amount of $1,269.00.

Print or Email A/R Invoices 

RealPage Accounting offers several places where you can print and email A/R invoices. This 

section describes how to use the Print or email A/R invoices menu option. Use this option when 

you want to print or email multiple invoices at the same time. 

You can also print or email invoices from the A/R invoices list (on page 137).  

Printing or Emailing A/R Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Periodic Tasks > Account Maintenance > 
Print or Email A/R Invoices`


To print or email A/R invoices: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic Tasks section of the menu, under Account Maintenance, click Print or email, 

and then select A/R invoices. 

The system displays the Print/Email Invoices page, where you can set delivery options and filters 

on the range of invoices to print or email. This page is similar to a report’s setup page. You’re 

using standard reporting filters to limit the range of invoices to print or email. 

Don’t worry about being too precise on the options page. On the next page, you can specifically 
select (or deselect) invoices to print or email. 

Setting Up Delivery Options 

In the Delivery options section, the system automatically sets Sender Email, Sender name, and 

Sender phone based on the main contact listed for your company (Company > All > Company).  

1. 
You can change the sender information. For instance, you may want to change the Sender 

Phone so that return calls to go to a customer service line. 

2. 
In the Marketing text field, you can add custom messaging to the invoice. The text that you 

enter appears toward the top of the page, above the date line. The default for this text is set 

via the Company information page. However, you can temporarily override it here. 

3. 
In the Message text field, you can add custom messaging to the invoice. The text that you 

enter appears toward the bottom of the footer line. The default for this text is set via the 

Company information page. However, you can temporarily override it here. 

4. 
To deliver invoices to a company contact’s main and alternate email addresses, select the 

Deliver to all available email addresses check box. Otherwise, the email is sent only to the 

contact’s main email address.

invoices.

drop-down list, such as Current month. Select the Prompt on run check box to enter the

Child customers: Selects the customers in the range, plus their child customers.

### Statements
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 454*

Account Maintenance 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Statements 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Periodic Tasks > Account Maintenance > 
Print or Email Statements`


You must be at an entity level to use this feature.  

Select the desired entity from the Top level menu. 

If the Print or Email Statements option does not appear, it may be because you are working in a 
multi-entity shared company. If so, from the Top level menu, select the entity for which you want 
to print or email a statement. If the option still does not appear, check your permissions. Finally, 
contact your system administrator. 

A statement, or Statement of Account, is essentially a report. It’s a snapshot that includes all open 

and unapplied transactions at the time the snapshot was taken—usually at the end of a period. 

Statements are generally sent directly to customers or, at the customer’s request, to others such 

as auditors or accountants. The system generates the statement when you request one to be 

printed or emailed. 

Statements are based on A/R transactions that affect A/R that you have already entered. 

Individual balances are listed so that you can scan the list of charges by date, item, amount due 

and amount paid, and the total due and total payments received. 

Statements also include aging information. 

Workflow 

To print and email statements: 

1. 
Click the Print or email statements menu option. 

2. 
Create (on page 455) the statements, filtering for the correct account, date, and activity. 

3. 
Select (on page 457) statements to print or email. 

4. 
Email (on page 459) and print (on page 458) the statements.

#### When to Print Statements
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 458*



#### Printing Statements
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 458*

Account Maintenance 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide

When to Print Statements 

Printing a statement depends on several factors, such as your agreements with the customer or 

your corporate practices. 

Statements aren’t invoices. They are reminders of open transactions, or list the transactions for 

the period with the ending balance. This allows customers to make sure they received everything 

and contact you if there are any concerns or if they need copies of the invoice sent. 

Charges are sent out as invoices. Generally, you send out invoices or adjustments at the time 

they’re created. Statements can be sent any time for any period, or not sent at all if there is no 

need to send them. 

Printing Statements 

After you select the documents that you want to print and click the Print/Email button, the 

document opens in the Adobe application (Reader, Viewer, or Acrobat) and you can print it. 

The customers’ addresses must be valid before you can print statements. 

To print Acrobat Viewer documents: 

1. 
In the Adobe application, click 
 Print in the upper left. 

2. 
In the Print dialog box that appears, select the printer from the Name drop-down list, and 

then click OK. 

Troubleshooting Printing 

I don’t see a PDF of my statements. 

The PDF documents open in an Adobe application, but they are not saved to your local computer 

unless you save them manually. You may choose to save the statement as needed. Click the File 

menu and choose Save as. 

Where does my browser save my downloaded documents? 

I don’t see a PDF of my statements. 

Select the internet browser that you are using for PDFs: 

Chrome (on page 599) 

Microsoft Edge (on page 597) 

Firefox (on page 597) 

Safari (on page 597) 

Fix a Problem with the Billing Address 

1. 
On the Accounts receivable menu, click Customers.

PEX Import 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide
