Importing PEX Transactions 

The PEX import menu option allows you to import transactions from PEX.  

The transactions imported from PEX can be invoices, payments, and cash transactions. After 

importing the transactions, the system saves the transactions as journal entries in the RealPage 

Financial Suite. The system also creates journal entries for value added taxes. 

• 
When the system imports a payment that is not associated with an invoice, the system 

creates a journal entry for it.  

• 
The system considers allocation only on payments and charges for refunds.  

You can run multiple PEX imports a day. 

The PEX Invoices list does not retain filters. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 584) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions.

Overview of Importing Data into RealPage Accounting 

The two most common imports into Accounts Receivable application are customer records and 

A/R invoice records. Consult the appendices for the data structure of customer and A/R invoice 

records.  

Regardless of the type of data that you are importing, the process contains the same basic steps: 

• 
Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page (on page 477). 

• 
Filling in the template with data that matches the template types (on page 478). 

• 
Save the file in CSV format. 

• 
Import the CSV file (on page 485). 

In addition, there are some nuances between handling invoice and customer data. For these, 

please refer to the individual import sections: 

• 
Importing accounts receivable invoices 

• 
Importing and exporting customer records (on page 491) 

This section includes best practices about the processing of imports. 

• 
Best practices for preparing data for import (on page 476) 

• 
Order of CSV imports (on page 485) 

• 
Importing Offline (on page 486) 

• 
Automating Imports (on page 486) 

This section also includes information that can help you resolve problems when importing:

##### Best Practices for Preparing Data for Import
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 476*

Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Best Practices for Preparing Data for Import 

Follow these best practices to prepare your data. 

• 
Download a template from the Import data page. 

Always use the latest template, especially following a product release. 

Use the correct template for the data object that you want to import. 

• 
Use the column descriptions as a guide to enter information. 

Do not change the titles in the header row. 

The header titles correlate to fields in the system. Incorrect header titles may cause an 

upload error. When you download a template from the Import data page, the correct 

headers are in the template. 

Read the header descriptions in the template. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains the type of 

information to include in each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, or with 

an incorrect accepted value, it may cause an error in your import. 

Enter required information. 

Read the description field to determine which information is required. If you do not enter 

the required information, your import may fail. 

• 
Save the data as a comma-separated value, or CSV, file. When saving from Excel, choose the 

comma delimited file (.csv) type. 

The file has the file extension .csv after you save it. 

• 
Leave the file open until your import is successful. Excel can sometimes reformat the file if 

you close it before the import is successful. 

---



##### Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 477*

Chapter 8: Importing Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of RealPage 

Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
Find the type of data that you want to import.  

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

A prompt opens at the bottom of the web page, asking if you want to Open, Save, or 

Cancel. 

• 
Open: Opens the file in Excel. 

• 
Save: Saves the file to your browser’s default download folder. 

• 
Save as: Saves the file under a new name and in a different location. 

• 
Save and Open: Saves the file to your local computer, and then opens the file in Excel. 

5. 
Click Save. 

Save the template to your computer, and then continue downloading templates as needed until 

you have downloaded all of the templates for data that you want to import. 

If you have a database administrator (DBA) of your other system, give the downloaded templates 

to your DBA. Ask the DBA to: 

• 
Export the data from your other system, as specified in the import template spreadsheets. 

• 
Put the applicable data into each spreadsheet. 

• 
Save the spreadsheet as a comma-delimited file (CSV). 

If you do not have a DBA, or if your DBA does not have time to complete the whole task, you can 

complete the tasks. Refer to the following topics for guidance on creating importable data. 

---

Filling In an Import Template with Data 

Perform the following steps for each item that you want to import: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. The information in the template 

file can help you formulate extraction queries. 

2. 
Export the data from your other source. 

3. 
Copy the exported data into the template file for the same kind of object. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file to your system.  

Preparing Your CSV File for Import 

The Import data page is a quick way to import your information into the system. However, the 

way you prepare your CSV files directly affects the success or failure of importing your data. Learn 

the CSV import process to streamline the import process. 

This topic provides general information about preparing CSV files for import. Links to information 
about specific templates can be found in the Import data into the system, which lists all import 
topics. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file. 

Most imports start with getting the most recent template from the Import data page. When you 

get your templates from this list, you get templates that have been tailored to your specific 

company, including specific dimensions.

Next you add your data, using the correct formatting as explained in the template. After you’ve 

added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in mind. This helps 

eliminate anything that might make your import fail. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

Downloading a Template 

We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because: 

• 
Templates in the Import data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated by RealPage at any time, especially when a new version of 

RealPage Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work. 

To download an import template:

Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. The Import data page opens with a list of information that you can

3. 
Decide on the type of information to upload, and then click the Template link associated 

with that information. 

Other Templates

Contact your RealPage Support Representative for any templates that have been customized for 

your company. 

Adding Your Data 

After you download the appropriate template, add your data.

##### About CSV Templates
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 481*

Chapter 8: Importing Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

To add your data: 

1. 
Open the template that you downloaded from the Import data page. 

2. 
Enter your information. Use the header descriptions as a guide for how to enter information 

correctly. 

• 
Do not change the headers. 

The header titles in the header row correlate to fields in UI. Incorrect header titles will 

cause an import error. When you download a template, the correct headers are in the 

template. 

• 
Read the header descriptions. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains what type of 

information is accepted for each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, 

or with a value not accepted by the column, it will cause an error in your import. 

• 
Enter required information. 

Some data is required, while others are not. Read the description field to determine 

which information is required. If you do not enter the required information, your 

import will fail. 

3. 
After entering your data, save the file as a comma-separated value (CSV) file. When saving 

from Excel, select the comma delimited file type. The file will have the file extension .csv 

after you save it. 

About CSV Templates 

There are some things you should know about the CSV templates and how they behave before 

adding your data. 

Removing All Commas from Your CSV File 

RealPage recommends removing all commas from your CSV file. 

A CSV file is a Comma Separated Values file (also sometimes known as a comma delimited file). If 

there are commas in the data of your file (for example, if your numbers are formatted like 10,000 

or if you use commas between words in a field), your data will be shifted one column over 

because that is how the file is intended to work. This will either cause errors in the information or 

cause the whole import to fail. 

RealPage recommends you do not keep your actual data in a CSV file. Instead, use an Excel 
workbook to take advantage of the formatting options of Excel. When you’re ready, export your 
data as a CSV file for import into RealPage Accounting. In this way, your data is formatted 
correctly for import, but you also have Excel functionality in your workbook. 

---


<!-- Page 482 -->
Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Column Order 

You can change the order of the columns as you see fit, as long as the information in the header 

cell doesn’t change. 

Do not rename or otherwise change the headers in your templates. If you change the headers, 
your import will fail. 

However, some templates require information to be imported in a specific order. For example, 

transaction data should not be imported before information about the transactions has been 

imported. Header columns containing information about the entire import need to stay to the left 

of detail columns (columns that contain the details of an account, transaction, vendor, etc.). 

RealPage recommends reviewing the column order of the original template before moving 

columns around. 

Adding Additional Columns 

If you need to keep other related information in your template document, you can add your own 

columns for this information. If you add your own columns, use a # (hashtag) symbol before the 

name of any column you add. Examples: 

#BudgetNotes 

#ClientInfo 

If by chance you use a name already in use by the system, the # (hashtag) will make sure that the 

information in your columns is not imported by accident. 

You can also use the # (hashtag) to write notes to yourself in your template. If you place the # 

(hashtag) at the start of a row, the whole row of information is ignored during import. 

You can create rows of notes by starting the row with # in the first column. 

Hiding Columns for Easy Data Entry 

When editing your file in Excel, you can hide columns you won’t be using for data entry. 

Be sure to enter required information in your file. Hiding required columns and not entering 
required information will cause your import to fail. 

Data Must Conform to the Business Logic of RealPage 

For example, the Budget ID field on the Budget Information page allows a 20-character ID to be 

entered. It follows then that the Budget import template would have the same limitation: if you 

try to import a Budget ID with more than 20 characters in your CSV file, your import fails. 

How data should be formatted is found in the header description row, under the header row. 

You can also see a field-by-field description for your specific template in this help. 

---


<!-- Page 483 -->
Chapter 8: Importing Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Go to Importing Data, find the template you want to know more about, and click the 

corresponding link. 

Blank Fields Overwrite Existing Data 

A blank value in a cell is considered to be the desired value (a blank) for the field referenced by 

the column heading for the record being imported. 

In almost all cases, a blank field will overwrite existing data in RealPage to also be blank. 

Say you had the existing value 111 Elm St. as the address for a customer and you import a blank 

for this field. If you go to the normal user interface and examine the contents of that field, you will 

see that the original value 111 Elm St. is replaced by nothing, and the field is blank. 

This is not true, however, for these templates: 

• 
Update Vendor 1099 Transactions 

• 
Update Vendor 1099 Opening Balances 

If the value is blank in certain fields, the import does not overwrite the existing value. To remove 

the existing value in these few cases, enter the value NULL. These cases are clearly identified in 

their header descriptions. 

Budgets are an exception. Budgets can be appended with new dates, with new lines not 
previously budgeted, or they can be overwritten if same date/account combinations are used. 

Calculated Field Values 

If you used a formula to come to a value in a field, you can leave the result in place as long as you 

match the RealPage field value for decimals. 

Accounting Application Page Help 

In most cases, there is an exact match between the application pages (and the business logic with 

which they behave) and the data that you import. This includes the constraints on that data and 

any dependencies that may exist between the data in the import file and other data in the system, 

or other data that you also import. 

After you have added all of your data, you save the Excel spreadsheet as a CSV file. 

Debits and Credits Must Balance 

When importing a file that includes debits and credits, your debits and credits must balance. 

RealPage adheres to accepted accounting rules, which require debits and credits to balance. 

Likewise, if you require accounts to balance by location, then when you import location balances 

using a CSV template, the location debits and credits must also balance. 

---


<!-- Page 484 -->
Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Duplicating Records 

If an identical record already exists in the system, the import for that record typically fails because 

RealPage detects that the record exists and does not allow duplicates. 

Duplicates are not allowed in account numbers, departments, locations, employees, customers, 

and vendors. Although you can have duplicate transactions, the transaction summary name must 

be unique per application. 

Journal entries are an exception. The system does not check for duplicate journal entries, so 
when importing journal entries, be sure to check that they have a unique ID or name.

Line Numbers 

See the Line number examples page for more information on how to use lines numbers in your 

CSV imports. 

Special Characters 

UTF-8 is supported in imported files, so character accents and other special characters are 

imported correctly. 

RealPage recommends that you remove commas from all numbers and do not use commas in any 

text fields. 

CSV Data Exported from Non-Excel Software 

When exporting data from other applications, the other software might use a non-standard 

approach to quoting, which could cause problems when importing into the system. 

As noted above, RealPage recommends removing all commas from text fields in a CSV file. 

However, there could be times in which removing the commas is not the ideal solution. In this 

case, CSV files do allow quotes around a value that contains a comma, and the system accepts 

this in an import. For example: 

1,2,3, “All, with exceptions” 

There may also be instances when you need to include a quote mark inside a statement with a 

comma. In this case, you would use a second set of quote marks, as follows: 

1,2,3, “All, with “inventory” exceptions” 

---



##### Order of CSV Imports
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 485*



##### Importing a CSV File
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 485*

Chapter 8: Importing Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Order of CSV Imports 

In some cases, CSV imports must be performed in a specific order because of dependencies 

within the data. For example, if you have transactions that require locations, but you have not 

entered or imported the locations, the transaction import fails. 

It is always best to follow the order of the steps as they are presented in the Import data page 

when performing any type of import. Not all of the steps are required. For example, you may not 

use territories anywhere in your accounting data, therefore creating them is optional. 

In a few cases there are circular references. For example, an employee record can reference a 

department and vice versa. Problems that would otherwise result from such circular references 

have been eliminated for the purposes of importing by removing certain items. If you absolutely 

must have this data, you need to enter it manually. 

Importing a CSV File 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file into the system. 

To import your CSV file: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
Find the information type you want to import, and then click the corresponding Import link. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you want to import. 

5. 
If the CSV file includes dates that are not in mm/dd/yyyy format, select the date format that 

the data uses in the Date format field. 

The system attempts to import your file using the selected date format. If the system can’t 

import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to discover the date format used 

in your file and import the data using that date format. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

7. 
If your import box includes a Post to section, select one of the following: 

• 
Select Historical if your data is not active. 

• 
Select General Ledger to post imported invoices to the G/L. 

8. 
If the file that you’re importing is large, consider selecting the Process offline option to 

process the import offline. This will cause the import to run at a later time, when the system 

is less busy. If you prefer to import the data immediately and wait for the results, do not 

select the Process offline check box. 

---



##### Importing Offline
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 486*



##### Automating Imports
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 486*

Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

9. 
Type the email address to which import results and errors should be sent in the Email 

results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses, separated by a 

semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

RealPage highly recommends entering an email address. 

10. 
Click the Import button. After an import, the system informs you if the import was 

successful and how many records were imported. 

In a completely successful import, the confirmation page lets you verify that all of the 

records in your original file were successfully imported without having to manually verify 

them. 

Importing Offline 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much processing the 

system must do to the data. If you are in doubt, select the Process offline option on the import 

utility page. 

When the offline process is complete, the system sends an email to the address you entered in 

the Import Company Information box (where you imported your file). 

RealPage recommends selecting Process offline when importing CSV files and providing your 
email address. If your import fails, you will always be notified, and the failed records are sent to 
your email. 

Automating Imports 

You may be able to automate and schedule your imports using a third-party application, such as 

Workato. 

Contact your account representative to learn more about this option.

##### Importing A/R Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 487*

Chapter 8: Importing Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Importing A/R Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Accounts Receivable Invoices > Template/Import`


To import A/R invoices: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Accounts 

Receivable Invoices option. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the A/R invoices import template. You can find the file 

in your browser’s default download location.  

5. 
Open the template file in Excel.  

Filling the Template 

1. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
CUSTOMER_ID: Type the unique identifier of the customer associated with the invoice. 

This field is the customer dimension. 

• 
CREATED_DATE: Type the date of the invoice. 

• 
DUE_DATE: Type the date that the payment is due. 

• 
TOTAL_DUE: Type the total amount due. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number of the invoice item. The line number appears in the 

Entries list on the A/R invoice page. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type a G/L account number. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the invoice. 

• 
BASECURR: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code such as USD or EUR for the 

base currency. The currency and its format must be defined in the system. This field is 

required for shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies. Locations in 

line items must use the same base currency. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date for the exchange rate. This field is required unless 

you provide the exchange rate in the EXCHANGE_RATE column. 

These fields are required if the line is to be deferred: 

• 
REVREC_TEMPLATE: Type the revenue recognition template to use. 

DEFERREDREV_ACCOUNT: Type the account number. The account number must exist 

in the system.  

• 
REVREC_JOURNAL: Type the name of the revenue recognition journal. This journal 

must exist before you can use the journal name in an import. 

---


<!-- Page 488 -->
Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
REVREC_SCHEDULE_LINE_NO: Type the line number. Line numbers are the 

incrementing numbers on the left side of the transaction in the Entries list.

Importing Customer Records 

You can quickly update information for multiple customers at once by exporting customer data in 

CSV for Import format, editing the resulting spreadsheet, and then importing your changes.  

A CSV import works well for:  

• 
Updating information for multiple customers at once: Using a CSV import, you can update 

selected data for multiple customers. For example, you can export the Customers list with 

the Email Address field included, add or modify the email addresses in a spreadsheet 

application, and then import your changes.  

• 
Adding new customers to your existing Customers list: Using a CSV import, you quickly add 

new customers without having to create the customers one at a time. Any spreadsheet row 

that contains a unique  

Don’t overwrite existing data with blank data unless you intend to remove that data from 
your Customers list. For example, if you export the Email Address field and then clear the 
data in the Email Address column of your spreadsheet, existing customer email addresses 
will be deleted when you import the file.  

Using the import and export features on the Customers list, you can: 

• 
Export your Customers list in one of several standard formats (CSV, Excel, Word, PDF) so 

that you can print or use the information in another application. 

• 
Quickly update your Customers list by exporting selected data, making changes, and then 

importing your changes. 

Importing Customers 

You can import new customer information at the top level by uploading a CSV file. Follow these 

steps to import new customer information from an external source. 

1. 
Download a template from the Import Data page (on page 477) 

2. 
Fill the customer template with data 

3. 
Save the template file as a CSV file 

4. 
Import the CSV File (on page 485)

Downloading the Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Customers > Template`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of RealPage 

Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
In the Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Customers row.  

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

Filling In the Customer Template with Data 

You can update information for existing customers. For example, you might correct customer 

addresses or add email addresses for selected customers. You can also add new customers. If the 

Customer ID that you specify doesn’t already exist in the system, a new customer record will be 

created. 

You can include sets of fields for a Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact. The template contains fields for 

this information, but it is not required. 

The Bill-to contact fields have a B_ prefix and the Ship-to contact fields have an S_ prefix. 

If the Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact fields are not included, the primary contact information is 

used for the customer. This means that the COMPANY_NAME field, when used for the Bill-to 

contact, would be B_COMPANY_NAME, and the shipping contact would be S_COMPANY_NAME. 

To fill the customer template: 

1. 
Open the file in Excel.  

2. 
Fill the required columns in the customer template: 

• 
CUSTOMER_ID: Type a unique identifier for the customer. If customer sequence 

auto-numbering is enabled, the system completes the Customer ID if you do not 

supply one. (Company > Services: Subscriptions: A/R Preferences). 

• 
CUST_NAME: Type the name of the customer. 

---


<!-- Page 493 -->

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type the primary contact name. If the contact name already exists, 

you must create the customer manually in the system, or enter a new contact name in 

this file. 

• 
PRINTAS: Type the name of the company as you want it to appear on payments and 

notices. This field is used with the Customer ID field to create the suggested contact 

name, which is the unique contact ID used throughout the system that can’t be edited 

after creation. This is also the name that appears in all lists and drop-down lists. 

3. 
Optionally, add data into the rest of the columns. Refer to the Customers Data Structure (on 

page 614) for a full list of columns. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing Order of Precedence 

When importing customer records, child records must be imported after parent records. Child 

records that incorrectly reference a parent record can cause your import to fail. For example, if the 

parent record does not exist, or if the parent record references a child record as if it were a parent, 

your import can fail. 

If you include an ACCT_LABEL, the system creates an account label on-the-fly when you import 

your file. 

This means you can’t re-use the same ACCT_LABEL for another customer. 

If you include an ACCT_LABEL, you must also include: 

• 
a GL_ACCTNO that conforms to a primary/sub account specification in Company > 

Setup: Company Info. 

• 
the GL_ACCTNO must point to valid account. 

• 
DELIVERYOPTIONS can be set to online, only if the company subscribes to online 

delivery. 

Customer lists have optional sets of Contact fields for the Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact. The fields 

are identical to the required set of primary contact fields; except they have B- and S- prefixes. If 

either the Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact fields are not included, the primary contact information is 

used instead. 

The Don’t Include On Company’s Contact List and G/L Group fields found in the Customer 

Information page are not represented in the template.

##### Resolving Errors
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 496*



##### Import Error Notification
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 496*

Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Resolving Errors 

If any records contained errors and the import failed, then the system notifies you with a list of 

the errors and how to correct the problems in an email. 

Import Error Notification 

There are a number of reasons imported records fail, such as duplicated entries or invalid field 

content. RealPage provides information about the failed records in an attempt to help you fix the 

import error. 

Finding the Error Message 

The Import confirmation page indicates how many records failed. This page also contains a link 

to download a CSV file, which contains only the failed records. 

Records that are successfully imported are not returned in the CSV file. 

Click the link and download the CSV file. 

If you entered your email address into the Import Company Information box, an email is sent 

that contains the error messages for your attempted import. The email lists the error code, and 

then each unique instance of that error in the file you attempted to import. 

The error message email is sent to the email address associated with the user ID logged in at the 

time of the file upload; otherwise, the email address for the company contact is used. 

The import pages also allow another email address to be explicitly entered in the Email results to 

this address field. 

If you did not enter your email in the Import Company Information box, and you do not click the 
link in the Import confirmation page, there is no way to retrieve the CSV error report file for the 
import you just did. 

Best practice: Enter your email in the Import Company Information box at the beginning of every 
import. 

The reason you are sent a separate email with the error messages is because a record could fail 

for more than one reason. Displaying all of the text for each record in the CSV file could become 

quite cumbersome and hard to read. Furthermore, it is often the case that thousands of records 

are uploaded. If thousands of errors fail, the CSV file could become quite bloated. 

Read the Error Message Email 

The error messages for your failed upload file can be challenging to read. RealPage recommends 

the following strategy: 

• 
Start at the top of the email and look at each error message section. 

---


<!-- Page 497 -->
Chapter 8: Importing Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

• 
In each section, start reading from the bottom up. The error at the bottom of the section is 

the first error encountered during import. 

a) Start here. 

b) Read from the bottom up. 

c) In each section, the specific error is listed at the top. 

---


<!-- Page 498 -->
Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Start at the Top of the Email 

Error messages are presented in sections, and the sections are listed in the order that the errors 

are encountered in your file. 

Example: 

=================================================== 
Error BL01001973 
=================================================== 
BL01001973-1 Description: Duplicate account number.  
The account number ‘4150’ already exists. 
BL01001973-1 Correction: Enter unique account number. 
BL01001973-2 Description: Unable to create record Could not create  
GL Account record! 
=================================================== 

When you read the error messages such as the one above, start with the error number. 

The error codes, such as BL01001973 above, are internal codes. These internal codes can help 
RealPage locate the source of a systemic issue if one is identified. 

=================================================== 
Error BL03000019 
=================================================== 
BL03000019-1 Description: Invalid contact data entered. 
TRANSACTION TYPE is a required field and cannot be empty 
BL03000019-1 Correction: Some of the fields you have entered 
are invalid. Please correct them with proper values. 
=================================================== 

Read from the Bottom of the Error Message Up 

In the example, the error code is BL01001973-2. 

Description: Unable to create record Could not create G/L Account record! first. 

This identifies the first error that occurred during import. It’s not informative, however, so look at 

the next error message for more information. 

The next error message in the list (as read from the bottom up), BL01001973-1 Correction: 

Enter unique account number, identifies the reason the G/L account record couldn’t be 

created, but it’s not yet clear what to do to fix the problem. 

The final error message in the example above (as read from the bottom up) describes more fully 

the cause of the error and suggests a fix: find and delete the duplicate account number.

##### Handling Import Errors
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 502*

Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide

Handling Import Errors 

If you experience import errors, review the tips in About CSV Templates (on page 481) and review 

the common errors (on page 499).  

Import errors occur when you try to import information that does not match the requirements of 

the template. Each template has a set of required information that you must enter to successfully 

import the file, and formats to follow for certain kinds of information. Read the descriptions in the 

template to determine the most accurate way to enter your data.  

If individual transactions are in error, the rows in the transaction that are in error are saved in a 

CSV file for you along with an error code for each row. The system sends an email with 

information about specific errors (on page 496).

Adding an A/R Term 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > 
 Terms`


A/R terms can either be accessible to all entities or exclusive to a specific entity. We recommend 

that you create customer terms at the top level to be shared across all entities. Creating terms in 

an entity restricts them to that entity. If you do create terms in an entity, then use a naming 

convention that differentiates them at the top level. 

To add an A/R term: 

1. 
Type a Name for the term (for example, 2% 10 Net 30). The system displays the name on 

invoice and customer pages. 

2. 
In the Description field, type a note about the purpose and use of this term (for example, 

2% discount if paid 10 days from invoice, due on day 30). 

3. 
Set Status to Active. To change the status of an object to hide unused items, select Inactive. 

When an item is set to Inactive, the system retains the data but hides the inactive item on 

lists, drop-down lists, and so on. Examples of data you might want to hide or make inactive 

are employees who are no longer with your company or bank accounts you no longer use. If 

you want to permanently remove an item, you must delete it. 

Filling In the Due Section 

The Due date is a combination of the day(s) and what the day(s) references: 

1. 
To set terms that reference the number of days from the invoice date, such as Net 30, type 

the number of days in Day, and select from invoice/bill date from the drop-down list. 

2. 
To set a day on a month referenced from the invoice date, type the day of the month in 

Day, and select a month setting from the adjacent drop-down list. For instance, to set terms 

for the 15th of the month after the invoice date, type 15 in Day, and select of next month 

from invoice/bill date in the drop-down list. 

---


<!-- Page 506 -->
A/R and Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Filling In the Discount Section 

The Discount is a combination of the day(s), what the day(s) references, the dollar or percent 

discount, and the number of grace days. In addition, you can set how the system calculates 

discounts for transactions using this term. 

To set a discount that references the number of days from the invoice date, such as 2%-10: 

1. 
Type the number of days in Day. 

2. 
Select from invoice date from the drop-down list. 

3. 
Type the discount amount in Amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days before the discount is withdrawn.

In Day, type the day of the month.

Select a month setting from the drop-down list. 

3. 
Type the discount amount in Amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days before the discount is withdrawn. 

To set a discount based on a day on a month referenced from the invoice date: 

1. 
In the Day field, type the day of the month. 

2. 
Select a month setting from the drop-down list. 

3. 
Type the discount amount in Amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days before the discount is withdrawn. 

You can set how the system calculates discounts in transactions that use this term. You can 

calculate the discount based solely on: 

• 
The Line-items total, excluding added charges (such as taxes and shipping).

The Invoice total, including all charges.

discounts when you record a payment receipt.

Segments Overview 

Segments are custom classifications that help you organize, sort, and report on your company 

information in meaningful ways. Think of a segment as a tag with a set of values that you can 

associate with transactions and G/L entries. For example, you might add a custom segment to 

report on your expense types, employees, or special projects. 

When you enter a new transaction, you can assign a segment to that transaction and then tag it 

with one or more segment values. Segmenting transactions is optional; however, it can be useful 

for identifying transactions and analyzing data in your reports. 

You can define up to 15 segments for your company. An additional segment, called 

Intercompany segment, is available by default. Because it’s a system segment, it cannot be 

modified. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage segments. 

Application

Permissions 

Company 
Segments 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 584) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

Enable Segments 

Enable the segments (on page 513) function in the General Ledger application.

Configuring A/R Functionality 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality`


Use the Enable functionality section to enable or disable Accounts Receivable features. 

This topic describes how to: 

• 
Enable allocation in invoice entry. 

• 
Enable users to allocate charges to different accounts on a single line item of an invoice. 

• 
Turn off automatic payment suggestions. 

• 
Enable creating, editing, and deleting foreign currency invoices. 

• 
Enforce the rule that payment dates must be greater than their invoice dates. 

• 
Display tax and subtotals for invoices. 

• 
Enable inter-company bill back. 

To enable Accounts Receivable functions: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration option. 

4. 
Find the Enable functionality section. 

5. 
Select the Enable accounts receivable G/L account override in invoice and adjustment 

entry check box when you want to override the default G/L account as you create a 

transaction. 

To make use of this option, you also need to: 

• 
Configure one or more G/L accounts as override accounts. 

• 
Provide permissions for selected users to override the default G/L account in invoice 

and adjustment transaction, as well as for any invoice or adjustment transactions 

involving specific customers, as needed.

To tag an account, go to General Ledger, select the account, and designate it as either a 

Payables account or a Receivables account as appropriate. The system adds the account to 

the filtered list of override accounts that you can select from in specific pages, such as 

transaction pages and vendor and customer pages. 

Payables account: the system adds the account to the filtered list of A/P G/L accounts 

available as override accounts on A/P invoice, adjustment, and vendor pages. 

Receivables account: the system adds the account to the filtered list of A/R G/L accounts 

available as override accounts on A/R invoice, adjustment, and customer pages. 

You can enable override of the default A/R G/L account for: 

• 
An entire invoice or adjustment 

• 
One or more specific line-items in an invoice or adjustment 

• 
All transactions involving a specific customer 

6. 
Select the Enable account labels check box to provide restricted access to G/L accounts and 

a means of textually naming them.  

This setting determines whether Account labels will be required or not (On or Off). Account 

labels are a good way to restrict access to G/L accounts. If an Account label is not set up for 

a particular G/L account, that account can’t be accessed. Also, Account labels provide a 

plain-English equivalent for G/L account numbers, which can be helpful for users. When 

enabled, you can: 

• 
Associate an account number with an intuitive name that is easy to recognize and 

select from a drop-down list. 

• 
Create subtotal lines in invoices, such as for sales tax.  

• 
Categorize different products/expenses/services. 

• 
Restrict access to only those G/L accounts that do have labels. 

After you enable account labels, two additional options appear in this section: 

Display tax and subtotals fields for invoices: Select this option if you’re going to create an 
account label for use in tax subtotals. (US taxes only) 

Enable Advanced Tax schedules: This option is not supported. 

7. 
Select the Enable allocation in invoice entry check box to allow users to allocate charges to 

different accounts on a single line item of an invoice. 

This option can only be enabled here if you’ve enabled it in G/L configuration. 

8. 
Select the Enable the system to automatically apply discounts check box.

<!-- Page 515 -->
Chapter 10: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

When you record the receipt of a payment for an invoice with an associated term discount, 

the system automatically selects the Apply discount check box in the transaction and 

applies the term discount. 

Leave this option unselected if you want to manually apply the discount. 

9. 
Select the Turn off automatic payment suggestions check box to limit the system to using 

the payment amount you enter to populate the Amount Received fields on the Select 

Invoices for Payment page. 

By default, the system applies the payment to the invoices starting with the oldest invoice. 

• 
If the amount of the payment is sufficient to fully pay that invoice, the system 

automatically selects the Receive Full check box for that invoice, applies the remainder 

to the next invoice, and so on until the entire payment amount is used up. 

• 
If any amount is left over because the payment amount is greater than the total of the 

invoices, the system displays the overpayment amount in the Amount Overpaid field. 

If you usually overwrite the amounts proposed by the system, and no longer want the 
system to propose those amounts, select this check box to disable this feature. 

10. 
Select the Enable reclassification for invoices and adjustments check box to allow users 

with proper permissions to edit accounting information on both partially and fully paid 

invoices and adjustments. 

11. 
Select the Enable reversal of unpaid invoices check box to prevents the deletion of unpaid 

invoices. Instead, you must reverse unpaid invoices, which maintains an audit trail. 

Selecting Enable reversal of unpaid invoices changes the following pages: 

• 
Accounts Receivable: for Invoices, Delete becomes Reverse. 

• 
Permissions: for Invoices, Delete becomes a read-only selection. 

When this check box is enabled, you cannot delete invoices. 

12. 
Select the Enable creating, editing, and deleting foreign currency invoices check box. If 

your company uses multiple currencies, you can use multiple currencies in your invoice 

entry process. 

Depending on your configuration, this check box may also be named Enable creating 

foreign-currency advances, and enable creating, editing, and deleting foreign-currency 

invoices, and adjustments. 

Even after you enable multi-currency transactions in General ledger setup, you must 
enable multi-currency in each application. This gives you the option to configure your 
company so that users can make multi-currency transactions in one application but not 
another. For example, enable them in Accounts payable but not Accounts receivable. 

---


<!-- Page 516 -->
Configuration

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

13. 
Select the Payment dates must be greater than their invoice dates check box to enforce a 

rule that the payment date must be on or after the invoice date. 

14. 
Select the Display tax and subtotals for invoices check box to enable the system to display 

tax and subtotal fields on invoices. 

This feature is available only if you’ve enabled account labels in the Enable Functionality 

section. 

15. 
Skip the Use Advanced tax schedules check box. The Advanced Tax feature is not 

supported. 

16. 
Select the Enable inter-company bill back check box. This option enables the system to 

automatically create a bill on one entity’s books when an invoice is created in a second 

entity in multi-entity, single-currency companies.  

This feature is available only for multi-entity shared companies. 

17. 
Select the Enable bank account selection in A/R invoice check box to allow users to select a 

bank account when creating an A/R invoice. When paying the invoice, the system allows you 

to pay from the bank account that you select in the invoice. When paying the invoice, you 

can filter on the bank account so that you can select from invoices that were marked to be 

paid with that bank account.  

After you select this option, you cannot disable it. 

18. 
Select the Enforce entity/property currency and base currency check box when your 

company manages multiple currencies, and you want to restrict users to using only two 

currencies in transactions: their designated property’s currency and the entity’s base 

currency. 

19. 
Click the Save button.

Configuring A/R Accounting Settings 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Account Settings`


Use the Accounting settings section to define the default journals, accounts, and summary 

frequencies. 

• 
Journal: Records invoices, adjustments, and payment receipt transactions. 

• 
G/L accounts: Posts transactions, such as accounts receivable, penalties, and more. 

• 
Summary frequencies: Determines how often the system posts invoices, adjustments, 

manual deposits, and payment summaries to the G/L. 

• 
Open item/Balance forward: Sets the customer accounts to Open item (most common) or 

Balance forward. 

The selections in this section vary based on the accounting method selected in General 
Ledger. When you change the accounting method from cash or accrual to cash and accrual, 
the system automatically creates some journals that are related to the new accounting 
method. Changing your accounting method requires additional setup changes. For 
information, see Accounting methods—accrual, cash, or both. 

Be sure to contact your RealPage account manager. 

Filling In the Accounting Settings Section 

Select the default journals to use for the A/R subledger. The system uses these journals for 

automatically recording the following accounts receivable transactions: 

1. 
In the Payments drop-down list, select the journal to use for payment receipt transactions. 

2. 
In the Accrual basis reporting subsection, in the A/R invoices drop-down list, select the 

journal to use for A/R invoices. 

3. 
In the Adjustments drop-down list, select the journal to use for accrual adjustments. 

4. 
In the Cash basis reporting subsection, in the A/R invoices drop-down list, select the journal 

to use for A/R invoices. 

5. 
In the Adjustments drop-down list, select the journal to use for cash adjustments. 

Filling In the G/L Accounts Subsection 

In the G/L Accounts subsection, select the General Ledger accounts to use for posting the 

following accounts receivable transaction types: 

1. 
In the Account receivable drop-down list, select the account to use for receivables. 

In general, you configure G/L accounts at the top level. One exception is that you specify 
different default A/R accounts for each entity at the entity level. For more information, 
see Specifying different default accounts by property in the online help system. 

---


<!-- Page 518 -->

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

2. 
In the Discounts drop-down list, select the account to use for discounts. 

3. 
In the Penalties drop-down list, select the account to use for penalties and late fees. 

4. 
In the Overpayment drop-down list, select the account to use for overpayments. 

5. 
In the Customer advances drop-down list, select the account to use for advanced payments. 

This setting can be changed on a per-transaction basis. 

6. 
In the Multi-currency gain and loss drop-down list, when your company has enabled the 

multi-currency option, the system can handle currency conversions for multi-currency 

companies. 

For information about the gain/loss account, see Foreign currency revaluation. 

Some organizations track overpayments and customer advances in an account that is 
typically associated with the Cash Management application, such as a deposit liability 
account. If this is the case for your company, be sure to review your report setup to verify 
that your balance sheet will tie to customer aging. Specifically, you should make sure that 
the General Ledger accounts used to represent Accounts Receivable in your balance sheet 
reports include all of the accounts that you selected here, including those for 
overpayments and advances. 

Filling In the Summary Frequency Subsection 

In the Summary frequency subsection, select how often the system creates and processes 

automatic summaries of transactions and advances. 

1. 
In the A/R invoices drop-down list, select how often you want the system to create and 

process A/R invoices: 

• 
Daily: The system creates a daily summary and posts it to the G/L for each transaction 

day. Daily is recommended because it gives you the most granular reporting. 

• 
Monthly: The system creates a single summary at the end of each month, and no 

matter what the transaction date is within that period, it will always be posted as of the 

last day of that month. This frequency doesn’t provide the daily granular level of 

reporting. 

• 
One per invoice: The system creates and posts a summary for each invoice. 

Per-transaction summaries can increase system performance, particularly if your 

transactions result in a large number of journal entries with unique G/L account and 

dimension combinations. 

• 
User specified: The system only uses manually created summaries. It continues to use 

a manual summary until you select or create another. 

2. 
In the Adjustments drop-down list, select how often that you want the system to create and 

process A/R adjustments:

Configuring A/R Document Sequencing 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Document Sequencing`


In the RealPage Financial Suite, document sequences refer to the system’s automatic numbering 

feature used to assign unique identifiers to new records. This helps ensure consistency and avoids 

duplication. 

Automatic numbering, also known as document sequencing, is available only in select features in 

RealPage Accounting. These features use pre-defined numbering plans to assign sequential 

identifiers—typically when creating new records or transactions. 

If you prefer to number a transaction type manually, do not assign a document sequence for the 

transaction type. 

Before You Begin

section.

Document Numbering.

Overriding the G/L Account in A/R Transactions 

The configuration to override the G/L account for Accounts Receivable transactions takes place in 

the Accounts Receivable and General Ledger applications.  

You can override a default A/R G/L account for an invoice or adjustment. Specifically, you can 

override the default G/L account in these situations: 

• 
Override for an entire transaction 

• 
Override at the line-item level 

• 
Override for all transactions involving a specific tenant 

Currently, this feature applies to invoices and adjustments only. It doesn ’t apply to recurring 
invoices, manual deposits, quick invoice entry, or advances.

##### Defining Transaction Allocations
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 523*

Chapter 10: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Defining Transaction Allocations 

To use transaction allocations, you must first enable the feature in the desired application, then 

create an allocation template that determines how to allocate the amount. After completing this 

configuration, you can apply the allocation to a transaction’s line item. 

Enabling the Transaction Allocation Feature 

You can use transaction allocations in Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and the General 

Ledger. Before you can use transaction allocations in any application, you must enable the 

transaction allocation feature in each application’s Configuration page. Enable transaction 

allocations in the Configuration area in the application where you need to use them. This example 

shows where to enable transaction allocation in the Accounts Payable application. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality > Enable Allocation in`


Invoice Entry 

Creating the Allocation Template 

You create a template that defines how you want to allocate the transaction, and then apply the 

allocation template to the desired transaction.  

For example, you can create a transaction allocation template so that it allocates the cost of a 

single line item across multiple locations. Whenever you want to apply this allocation to a line 

item, you select the allocation in a transaction’s line item row. 

Applying the Allocation 

When you enter an A/R invoice, A/P invoice, or journal entry and apply a transaction allocation to 

any line, the system automatically splits the amount based on the transaction allocation template.  

For example, if a company distributes an expense such as janitorial services across five business 

units, the transaction allocation can be set up to reflect the percentages of occupancy per 

business unit. When you apply this transaction allocation to a line item, the system will 

automatically divide the amount across the business units according to the percentages saved in 

the transaction allocation template. 

To see how a transaction allocation is divided in a transaction, open the A/P invoice, A/R invoice, 

or journal entry, and then click the line in the Entries section, and then click Show details. The

Configuring Intercompany Bill Backs 

Inter-company bill back makes it easy for an entity to bill a second entity. Some configuration is 

required in order to make this feature work. During setup, you create a customer and vendor 

record for each entity and then associate the records with the entity. The bill back feature uses the 

customer and vendor records as proxies for the billing process.  

Configuration Workflow 

1. 
Enable the inter-company bill back feature. 

2. 
Grant bill back template permissions. 

3. 
Create inter-entity receivable and inter-entity payable accounts to use for inter-entity 

transactions if they don’t already exist. 

4. 
Create one vendor record and one customer record for each entity that you want to be able 

to use with the bill back feature. 

5. 
Associate the vendor record and customer record to its entity. 

6. 
Create bill back templates.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Accounts Receivable > Configure > 
Enable Functionality > Enable Inter-Company Bill Back`

2. 
Select Subscriptions. 

3. 
Find Accounts Receivable and then click Configure. The Configure Accounts Receivable 

page opens. 

4. 
In the Enable functionality section, select Enable inter-company bill back.

Granting permissions to bill back templates (on page 525)

Territories 


> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Territories`



> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Cash Management > All > Territories`


Territories are optionally included in Customer records and are used with Accounts receivable 

reports. They can be useful for filtering and categorizing data, assuming your company has 

multiple territories.  

Territories are similar to dimensions but aren’t actual dimensions, so they work differently than 

dimensions. They can be used with dimensions.  

Multi-entity companies 

For top-level multi-entity companies that use multiple base currencies, you must assign the 

territory to a specific entity, so the system knows which base currency to use for that territory. 

Entities are territories and–under certain circumstances–entities appear in lists. For example, you 

have the option to choose the entity as the parent territory and thus it appears in that list of 

locations.

#### List of Standard Accounts Receivable Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 532*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

List of Standard Accounts Receivable Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Reports`


The Accounts receivable application contains a number of standard reports that have been 

created for you. These reports involve amounts owed or paid by customers for goods and 

services. You can run, view, process, memorize, export, and customize A/R reports. Refer to Using 

Reports for information on creating, storing, and reusing reports. 

Customer Reports 

The Customer reports appear in the Accounts Receivable application’s menu in the Reports 

section, in the Customers group. 

• 
Customer aging report  

This report provides a snapshot of outstanding charges based on account label, G/L 

Account, or other selected parameters. It lists the customers who owe you money and either 

how many days it took them to pay you, or how many days past due their payments are. 

Use this report to determine how well you are collecting on your accounts receivable. This 

report is also available as a chart. 

• 
Customer listing report  

This report is a list of customers that includes details such as location and contact 

information, pricing details, payment methods, term, tax ID, and current customer balances.  

Registers and Reports 

These reports appear in the Accounts receivable application’s menu under the Reports column, 

in the Registers & Reports section. 

• 
A/R Ledger report 

The A/R Ledger report is a list of detailed customer accounts. Use this report to see if the 

balance in the A/R ledger agrees with that in the general ledger, and to see which 

customers have balances greater than zero. Details include the beginning balance for the 

selected period, current account balance, and the charges and payments for each customer. 

• 
Sales Register report 

The Sales Register report displays the invoices you sent to customers, account adjustments, 

payment details, and credit details. Each transaction includes the date, customer ID and 

name, invoice or adjustment number, due date, description (if any), amount, and amount 

paid. 

• 
Recurring Transaction Status report 

---


<!-- Page 533 -->
Chapter 11: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

This report presents information on the status of scheduled, completed, and failed 

transactions. The report includes transactions generated from the Accounts receivable and 

Accounts payable applications. 

• 
Recurring Transaction Forecast report 

This report provides insight into future billings based on recurring transaction schedules set 

up in the system. With this report, you can expand the number of forecasting periods, as 

well as select a forecasting frequency (monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, annually). 

Multi-currency enabled companies can choose to forecast on base currency or transaction 

currency. 

• 
Receipts Register report 

This report lists receipts from the customers that you select. Use this report to review all of 

the receipts that have been applied to invoice transactions.  

• 
Sales Tax report 

This report summarizes the taxes and labels them “Total Other Taxes.” 

• 
Deferred Revenue Forecast report 

This report illustrates how deferred income is recognized as revenue over time. Use this 

report to forecast revenue by time period, account, customer, and more. 

• 
Deferred Revenue Details report 

This report shows the details of customers and transactions for which you have deferred 

revenue. This report includes the transaction amount, transaction date, deferred amount, 

recognized amount, and amount paid. Use this report to see the transaction detail behind 

those deferred numbers and to tie back to the deferred balance on your G/L (like an audit 

report). 

• 
Deferred Revenue Revaluation report 

This report shows the adjustment of deferred revenue to reflect the business’s expected 

ability to fulfill the service obligations and generate revenue from prepaid amounts. 

Multicurrency must be enabled to access this report. 

• 
Intercompany Billing report 

This report lists the billing transactions between two entities. This report requires that you 

have configured the intercompany billing feature. Learn more about Configuring 

Intercompany Billing. 

• 
A/R Invoices Analysis report 

This report helps you analyze your sales from the perspective of revenue line items in the 

invoices. Use this report to review your invoices. This report is also available as a chart. See 

Invoices Analysis chart.

Recurring report 

This report shows a list of recurring invoices from your customers, along with details about

•

#### About Dimensions
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 542*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Dimensions 

A dimension is a category of data that you can organize and sort in meaningful ways. RealPage 

Accounting provides the following pre-defined dimensions: 

• 
Customer 

• 
Department 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Vendor 

In addition, RealPage Accounting enables you to define new dimensions to suit your needs. These 

user-defined dimensions enable you to organize and sort categories of data unique to your 

business. For example, if you are a software company with various product lines, you might create 

a user-defined dimension called Line of business. The values you could add are Direct customers, 

Channel partner, and OEM. 

Dimensions enable you to collect, sort, analyze, and report on data within one category, or 

between categories, so you can identify key factors such as: 

• 
Your most profitable or most costly customers. 

• 
The return on investment of a location or department. 

• 
Whether and to what degree a new product or product line is successful. 

• 
Which way a particular aspect of your business is trending. 

RealPage Accounting dimensions give you fine control over data definition and data hierarchy. 

With dimensions, you can customize financial reports around specific business activities, get 

greater visibility into how the business is doing, and make faster, more meaningful business 

decisions. 

Additional fees may apply for user-defined dimensions. Contact your RealPage account 

representative for more information. 

---

Limiting Members in Dimension Structures 

You can limit the output of a financial report to show only the top or bottom of a particular set of 

dimension data. For example, you can include only the top five customers by revenue. 

To include a top or bottom match on a financial report, you must create a dimension structure 

that contains the set of members from which you want to choose the top or bottom. On the 

checked report, you need to change the detail level for the dimension structure to show only the 

top or bottom matches based on a metric of your choice. 

Create a Dimension Structure With All Members 

As an example, if you plan to show the top five customers, you need a dimension structure that 

includes all customers. To build this type of structure, create a dimension structure that contains a 

group with “All customers.” 

Learn more about creating flat dimension structures and hierarchical dimension structures in the 

online help system or download the RealPage Accounting Reports User Guide. 

Use the Report Structure on Report Rows 

1. 
Create a new financial report. 

• 
Open the Reports menu. 

• 
In the Financial Reporting section, click 
 Add next to Financial Reports. 

The system opens the Financial report writer page. 

2. 
On the Report info tab, name the report and select Dimensions for the Report structure. 

3. 
On the Rows tab, add the dimension structure to the report rows. 

• 
Click the Select dimension structures button. 

The system opens the Define Report Structure - Add Dimension Structures box. 

• 
In the Section/Row type drop-down list, select the dimension type. For example, 

“Customers.” 

• 
In the Dimension structure drop-down list, select the dimension structure that 

includes all members. 

• 
Click the Include in this report button, and then click the OK button.

#### Attachments Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 546*

Attachments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Attachments Overview 

Attachments are bundles of one or more files that you associate with a transaction or record, such 

as a letter of credit, an invoice, or a photo. For example, if you have a contract signed by a 

customer, you can attach the contract to the customer record. You can attach as many files or 

combinations of file types as you need and bundle them into a single attachment record. 

To attach a document, you first need to create an electronic version of it. If it is a paper copy, scan 

the document, and then save it as one of the supported file types:  

• 
Word 

• 
PDF 

• 
Excel 

• 
Text 

• 
JPG 

• 
PNG 

Attaching Files to Transaction Records 

The Enable single scan upload setting in your user preferences changes the way that the system 

treats attachments. These differences are described below: 

When scanning is disabled: 

• 
You can select one attachment record to associate with a transaction, but the attachment 

record can contain multiple files as needed. 

• 
You can create folders for storing attachments from the transaction record. 

• 
You can access the attachment folders from the transaction record. 

When scanning is enabled: 

• 
You can add multiple attachments to a transaction record. 

• 
You can scan a document to attach it directly to the transaction record. 

• 
You cannot create or access attachment folders. 

For instructions on enabling the Enable single scan upload option, see Enabling the Scanning 

Feature.

In the Attach files section:

Open button. Alternatively, you can drag and drop files directly from your file explorer 

into the browser window. 

• 
If you have Commercial Property Management or Condo and Co-Op, and you 

purchased the portal add-on, then the Display on portal check box also appears. 

Select the check box for any attachment that you want the tenant or owner to be able 

to access on their portal.

Background Information 

• 
Names and IDs (on page 557): When you add a new record, it typically requires a unique 

name, identifier, or both. This section includes guidelines to help you create effective names 

and IDs. 

• 
Lists (on page 560): Most of the work that you do in the system takes place in lists. From 

lists, you add, view, edit, and delete records. Lists have several controls in common that let 

you filter, sort, and create views. Learn how to use lists effectively to get the most out of the 

system. 

• 
Audit trails (on page 581): Audit trails let you see who changed a record, when they 

changed it and in some case, see what was changed.  

• 
Terminology (on page 583): You can change the terminology that the system displays. For 

example, if you prefer to use the word “supplier” in place of the word “vendor, then you can 

change the term system-wide by accessing the Terminology option.

Roles and permissions (on page 584): Users must have permissions to access each type of 

information in the system. If you don’t see a menu option or cannot edit a type of record, it 

may be because you do not have permission to that type of information. Please contact 

your system administrator if you need access.

##### Best Practices for Creating Names and IDs
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 557*

Chapter 13: Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Best Practices for Creating Names and IDs 

Special Characters 

Most applications have best practices for names and IDs. In some cases, even if a name is allowed 

when you create a transaction or record, if that transaction or record interacts with another 

application—or even another area of the same application—the system might not be able to find 

and load it. 

Best practice: We recommend that you create a name or ID using only the following characters. 

Use 

• 
Letters 

• 
Numbers 

• 
A single space 

• 
A single dash 

• 
Underscores 

• 
Periods 

Don’t use 

• 
Special characters such as exclamation marks (!), at signs (@), equal signs (=), and any other 

character not specifically listed in the Use column. 

• 
Double spaces 

• 
Double dashes 

• 
Leading spaces 

• 
Trailing spaces 

You can use some special characters in names, but if you use only the ones in the Use column, you 
can be sure that the name or ID won’t cause problems elsewhere. 

When a name is rendered, double spaces often appear the same as single spaces, which can 

cause difficulty in name recognition. For example, if an application displays an error that an item 

with a double space doesn’t exist, but you know that it does, check the name in the appropriate 

list to make sure that no extra or hidden characters are part of the name or ID. 

Leading Zeros 

We recommend against using leading zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can cause 

errors when you import information into your company from Excel because Excel removes the 

leading zero. Use a character as a prefix to your ID. 

• 
Correct: C0001 

• 
Incorrect: 00C43 

---



##### Setting Default Line-Item Values
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 558*

Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Other Considerations 

When creating names and IDs, or configuring sequencing for applications, consider not only the 

impact of the naming scheme in different areas of the system but also the impact in outside 

applications such as importing and exporting files to Excel, Word, and CSV. Reports might sort 

differently than you expect if you use special characters or leading spaces. Some applications strip 

out leading zeros and spaces while others ignore them. 

Learn any limitations of third-party applications that you commonly use to help create your 

naming strategy. 

Setting Default Line-Item Values 

Setting default values is a time-saver when you need to fill in a long list of line items. 

To set a default value for a line-item field: 

1. 
In the Entries section of a transaction’s page, click the Show defaults link. 

The area expands to display all fields for which you can set defaults. The type of fields that 

appear here depend on your company setup. For example, if you’ve enabled standard 

dimensions, or created and deployed user-defined dimensions, multi-currency processing 

fields, or revenue-recognition fields, then you can set default values for them here. 

2. 
Click the drop-down arrow for any field that frequently uses the same value, and then select 

that value. 

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button above the first line item. 

The value that you selected appears on every line or in the line-item detail of every line, 

depending on where the field is located. 

You can override the default value by selecting a different value or typing over the text. 

4. 
Optionally, click the Hide defaults link to hide the defaults section after you have applied 

them to the list.

#### Managing Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 560*

Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Managing Lists 

Lists provide access to like records. After you create a record, you can access it from its list. Most 

lists allow you to add, edit, view, and delete the records in it. You can also export the list to an 

XML file or a PDF file. After exporting a list, you can import the list into an external application like 

Excel, and then print the list from that application. 

Some lists allow you to access related information. For example, from the customers list, you can 

also access the customers A/R ledger and view a breakdown of the total amount that the 

customer owes. 

Since the list page is where you perform most of your work, the system provides several features 

to let you filter and sort lists and create and manage custom views of your data. 

• 
Sorting (on page 561): Sort the list alphabetically by the data in the desired column. 

• 
Filtering (on page 562): Filter lists so that you see only the data that you need. 

• 
Views (on page 570): Create a custom view to determine which columns appear in your lists, 

and apply a filter so that the list appears just the way you want it. 

Lists and Links 

Each list is unique and can offer links to let you navigate into an associated record to see more 

detailed data. For example, some invoice lists have a Preview link that, when clicked, opens the 

invoice in PDF format in a browser window. Another type of list may have a link to the customer 

record or the vendor record. 

Many reports present figures as links that, when clicked, open the associated record. This example 

shows links in the Debit and Credit columns of a journal entry. When you click a link, the system 

navigates to more information, allowing you to delve into the details. 

---

*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 561*

Sorting Lists 

You can display a list by a column’s ascending or descending values by clicking the column name. 

An arrow to the right of the column name indicates the sort direction. The arrow points 
 up for 

ascending order and 
 down for descending order. Only one column can control the list’s sort 

order at a time. 

In this example, the system sorts the list by the data in the Entity ID column. The sort arrow 

appears on the column that the system is sorting on. 

To reverse the sort order, click the column name again. The sort order reverses, and the arrow 

flips direction to indicate that the sort is reversed. 

To sort on a different column, click the desired column name.
