##### Filtering Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 562*

Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Filtering Lists 

Using Column Filters 

Column filters are text boxes that appear at the top of each column. Filters let you find items in a 

list that match the text that you enter. 

To apply a column filter: 

• 
Type the text that you want to find in the column filter, and then press ENTER. 

The system searches for matches, and then displays the matches in the list. 

If a text box does not appear at the top of a column, the column is not searchable. 

Using the Wild Card Character 

• 
Use the % symbol as a wild card or placeholder. For example, typing “san%” in the City 

column’s filter would find both San Francisco and Santa Diego. 

• 
Placing the % in front of text tells the system to find these letters in the middle of text in a 

field. 

• 
Placing % at the end of a word tells the system to find the word and any letters that follow 

the word. 

• 
Use % to filter text columns only. The % symbol does not work on non-text columns such as 

date columns or amount columns. 

• 
For best success, anticipate differences and adapt your filter to account for them. 

To find records that contain a specific value: 

• 
Type the first part of the value. 

If you are looking for a contact in a city that starts with “San,” then you can filter the Contact 

list by typing “san” in the City filter field, then and pressing ENTER. The system searches for 

contacts with a city that begins with San, such as San Jose, San Francisco, and Santa Fe. 

---


<!-- Page 563 -->
Chapter 13: Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

• 
If you know only part of the text that you want to find, type “%” and then type the text that 

you have. 

For example, if you are looking for a contact with the letters “Will” in the name, but you do 

not have the full, correct name of the business, type “%will%” in the Contact name filter of 

the Contacts list, and then press ENTER. The system searches for matches, retrieving all 

contacts that contain the letters “will” in the Contact name field. 

Example 

Your company uses this standard format for naming invoice summaries: Invoices: Month Year. 

When you want to find all June summaries, type “%June” in the filter above the Summary column, 

and then press ENTER to apply the filter. Placing the % in front of June tells the system that the 

word “June” appears in the middle of the text string. Placing % at the end of the word “June” tells 

the system to find the word June and any word with letters that follow the word “June,” such as 

“Juneteenth.” 

Searches for Units 

You can search for a unit by entering any part of the unit ID. The system will find matches for any 

part of the unit ID string. For example, if the units in your property are configured with an 

alphanumeric pattern such as A-10, A-11, A12, B-20, B-21, B-22, then you can enter any part of 

the string, such as “22,” and the system will find B-22.  

The string does not have to start with the entered value to match. Typing “A” finds a list of units 

on the A floor as in our example or all units that have “A” in the unit ID.

Displaying One-Time Items 

Some quick-entry records are set for one-time use. For example, you may have a seasonal 

customer, such as a Halloween supply store, or customers who pay only once and are not likely to 

purchase again. 

Create the customer record so that you can record the cash receipt, but because you don’t need 

to see that customer in your customer list regularly, flag the customer as Exclude from the 

company contact list. One-time customers aren’t included in the list unless you specify them to be 

included. 

To include one-time items in the list, select the Include One-Time check box. The system displays 

the one-time items along with regular items and adds a One-Time column to show which items 

are one-time records. 

Example 

You may have a customer who purchases from you only once a year, and you do not want to see 

the customer’s name in the list all the time. You still need to create a Customer record so that you 

can record the cash receipt, but since you do not need to see the customer in your Customers list 

regularly, edit the Customer record, and select the One-Time Use check box.

Including Inactive Records in Search Results 

Almost every kind of record in the system has a Status field with choices of Active and Inactive. 

The Include Inactive check box appears at the top of many lists and allows the system to include 

the inactive records in search results. 

• 
Select the Include Inactive check box to include items set to a status of Inactive in the 

search. The system refreshes the list and adds a Status column to indicate which items are 

active and which are inactive. 

• 
Clear the Include Inactive check box to prevent inactive items from appearing in the list. 

A list can contain items that are inactive but still present because they link to transaction data. For 

example, you may have a vendor who no longer carries items you need to purchase. In the vendor 

record, you flag the vendor as Inactive. Inactive vendors aren’t included in the list unless you 

select Include Inactive. 

One-time use customers do not appear in the Company application’s Contacts list unless you 
select the Include one-time check box.

Include Private 

Customer records created prior to June 2020 could be created at the entity level. Records created 

at the entity level are private. Customer records that you create today can be created only at the 

top level. The Include Private check box controls whether entity level customer records appear in 

the Customers list. The Include Private check box is selected by default so that all records appear 

in the Customers list. 

• 
Clear the Include Private check box to display only public records (records that are set up at 

the top level).

where they were created. When the Include Private check box is selected, the list includes

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in RealPage Accounting do not have the CSV for import option. 

---

Audit Trails 

Each action you take can impact your financial statements, so both internal and external 

stakeholders need to know how things have changed and who made those changes. The system 

audit trail keeps track of the changes so that you know who made changes to a particular record 

and when they made the changes. The View audit trail command is available on most records. 

Viewing Audit Trails 

You can access the audit trail of a record. The method of accessing the audit trail varies based on 

the record type. 

Accessing the Audit Trail  

1. 
Open the record that you want to examine. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the View audit trail option.  

Instead of the More Actions button, some records have a View Audit Trail button. 

The Audit trail list opens with a list of changes that users have made.  

Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail 

You can export data from the audit trail to a file in one of three formats, Microsoft Excel, CSV, or 

PDF. 

1. 
Open the audit trail. 

2. 
Click the audit trail’s More actions button, and then select the format to which you want to 

export: 

• 
Export to CSV 

• 
Export to Excel 

• 
Export to PDF 

If the audit trail table is lengthy, you can change the size of the list. From the More actions 
drop-down list, select Table size, and then select the number of rows that you want to be 
able to view.

#### Roles and Permissions
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 584*

Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

---

##### Adding a G/L Account
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 586*

Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding a G/L Account 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > 
 Accounts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > All > 
 Accounts`


To add a G/L account: 

1. 
From the top level, open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, click the 
 Add button next to the Accounts menu option. 

The General Ledger accounts page opens. 

3. 
Enter the account number. After you save the account record, the account number cannot 

be edited. 

We recommend using dimensions (on page 542 ) instead of sub-accounts. This simplifies 
reporting when rolling up for reports.  

4. 
In the Title field, type a name for the account as you want it to appear as the heading on 

reports, for example, Assets.  

After you save the account record, you have the option to create additional titles for the 
account. This option is useful when your system has multiple entities that would benefit 
from custom titles, such as account titles in other languages or a variation of an account 
title that an entity ’s users are more familiar with. 

5. 
In the Category drop-down list, select the category of account that you are creating. 

Categories are permanently pre-assigned to account groups, which are used in financial 

reports and graphs that are supplied with the system. 

For example, you would assign the Petty Cash account to the category Cash and Cash 

Equivalents, which is assigned to the Cash and Cash Equivalents account group and appears 

on financial reports and graphs that contain this account group. If you do not want this 

account to be in your financials, then delete the text in this field so it is blank. 

The Category field is displayed only for companies that were created with a setup template 

or chose one later. If you need to assign categories to many accounts, the easiest way is to 

export your chart of accounts, make the changes in the file, and then upload the file. 

When Your System Was Set Up With the Services Template 
By default, the categories Manpower and Direct materials are assigned to account groups 
that are only used in the reports Project Profitability and Project Estimation Versus Actual. 
These two categories do not appear in balance sheet reports or income statements. If you 
assign an account to either of these two categories, and you want it to show up in your 
balance sheet, income statement, or other reports, you must manually assign these 
categories to the appropriate account groups.

6. 
In the Account type drop-down list, select either Balance sheet account or Income 

statement account. 

• 
Balance sheet accounts are snapshots of the current state of a company’s assets, 

liabilities, and equity at a specific time. 

• 
Income statement accounts (sometimes called profit and loss statements) are 

cumulative for the selected period. 

7. 
For Normal balance, select either Debit or Credit. 

When you create an account, you specify whether the normal balance, from an accounting 

standpoint, is a debit or credit. For example, expense accounts are normally debit accounts. 

Sales accounts are normally a credit. If you were to run a Trial Balance report, the normal 

balance of the accounts is what determines whether the account is a credit or debit. 

8. 
For the Period end closing type, select whether the account is a closing or non-closing 

account. For closing accounts, select an account in the Close into account drop-down list. 

• 
Instead of manually closing accounts at year-end, you can set them to be closing 

accounts and then specify the account in which to close that period. 

• 
Income statement accounts should be closing accounts; balance sheet accounts 

should be non-closing accounts. 

• 
For all income statement accounts, the close-into account will typically be Retained 

Earnings. The system then zeros closing-type accounts into retained earnings at 

year-end. 

9. 
In the G/L account alternative drop-down list, select a G/L account for the system to use as 

an alternative payables account. The account override must be enabled for this field to 

appear. 

10. 
The default status is Active. If you want to prevent this G/L account from appearing in lists, 

select Inactive in the Status drop-down list. (You can still list inactive accounts by clicking 

the Include inactive check box in lists.) 

You cannot make a G/L account inactive when the account is selected on the configuration 
page of an application or if the account is being used in a budget. 

11. 
Select the Disallow Direct Posting check box to prevent direct entry of journal entries to the 

subledger control account (for example, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, etc.). 

Use this control to ensure that the account balance for the subledger account is accurate 

and has the necessary subledger details supporting the figure, rather than a direct entry that 

would not be reflected in the subledger application area.

When a G/L account is marked as Disallow Direct Posting, the system allows OneSite 
transactions to be created for that G/L account (as these are system
-created entries) 
but still disallows manually created journal entries to post to the G/L account.  

12. 
Select the Require Unit check box to require the user to select a unit when using this 

account. 

13. 
Select the Require asset category/type during invoice entry check box if you want to 

require users to enter asset information whenever they select this G/L account when 

entering an A/P invoice. 

This option appears when the Enable asset in invoice entry check box is selected in

14.

when creating an elimination entity. 

Requiring Dimensions 

Dimensions drive visibility into the parts of your business that matter most. You can require users 

to select dimensions when selecting the G/L account. When you require a dimension for a G/L 

account, all transactions that post to that account must include the dimension or dimensions that 

you select here. If you require multiple dimensions, all dimensions must be included to post to the 

G/L account. 

Use the Require Dimensions section to select the dimensions that you want to require for this 

account. 

• 
To require dimensions for transaction entries assigned to this account, select the dimension 

check boxes to require. All selected dimensions will be required. Supported dimensions 

include:

Location

Customer

Employee

If This Account Overrides Other Accounts 

To flag this account as an override of the default A/P or A/R G/L account, select the type of G/L 

account that it can override. Although you can flag any account as an available override account, 

typically, you flag an A/R or A/P account. 

• 
Payables account: Adds the account to the filtered list of A/P G/L accounts available as 

override accounts for bill and adjustment transactions, and for transactions involving a 

specific vendor. 

• 
Receivables account: Adds the account to the filtered list of A/R G/L accounts available as 

override accounts for invoice and adjustment transactions, and for transactions involving a 

specific customer. 

As you enter transactions, you can select the same alternative G/L account for all line items, or 

select alternative accounts individually per line item. On the Vendor and Customer pages, you 

can select one alternative G/L account to use for balancing all transactions involving that vendor. 

Currently, this feature applies to A/P invoices, A/R invoices, and adjustments only. It doesn ’t 
apply to recurring A/P invoices or A/R invoices, manual payments, manual deposits, quick check 
entry, quick A/P invoice entry, quick A/R invoice entry, or advances. 

Including the Account in Chart Types 

You can simplify the accounting task by creating subsets of the chart of accounts. These subsets 

are called chart types. The Chart types option appears when your company has the chart type 

feature enabled.

account to each appropriate chart type.

Click the Chart types’ Select button. The multi-select box opens.

Select the chart type in which to include this account.

types.

##### Adding a Contact
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 591*

Chapter 13: Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Adding a Contact 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Contacts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > 
 Contact`


To create a contact quickly, you only need to assign it a unique Suggested contact name and a 

Print as name for documents. 

The Suggested contact name is the most important field in a contact record. It acts as a unique 

contact ID across the RealPage Financial Suite system, which means you can no longer edit the 

suggested contact name after you create the contact record. Furthermore, although you can 

change the printed name of a contact with the Print as field, the Suggested contact name is the 

name that appears in all lists and drop-down lists across RealPage Accounting. You can change 

the Suggested contact name of a contact in limited situations such as when a vendor’s name has 

changed. 

Additionally, when you create a new vendor, customer, employee, or user, a related contact is 

often created simultaneously based on specific fields in the record. See Creating a Contact from a 

Record to learn about which specific fields in each record create the related Suggested contact 

name. 

To create a more detailed contact record, fill in each tab on the Contact information page. 

Filling In Contact Information 

On the Contact information tab: 

1. 
Type the contact name. 

• 
This name isn’t necessarily the name that is used throughout your company because 

actual names aren’t always unique. For example, a name such as “Jose Hernandez” 

could be the same as a completely different contact in your company. 

• 
The system automatically suggests a unique Suggested contact name and Print as 

name based on the naming details you enter. 

2. 
Add the Primary email address, Primary phone number, and Company name for the 

contact.  

In the Property Management application, the system uses the primary email address that 
you enter here to fill in email addresses for emailing statements.  

3. 
Type a Suggested contact name if you want a different version than the one the system 

auto-populates. This name appears in lists and drop-down lists. 

After you save the contact, the Suggested contact name can’t be edited. 

---


<!-- Page 592 -->
Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

4. 
Enter the Print as name if you want a different version to appear on printed documents than 

the one the system auto-populates. 

Filling In Mailing Information 

On the Mailing information tab, add the mailing address for the contact. 

Filling In Additional Information 

On the Additional information tab, enter any secondary information you might have. This 

includes phone, URL, and taxable information. 

Marking a Contact to Be an Owner or Investor 

On the Reporting portal tab, select the This is an owner-Investor check box if you plan to include 

the contact as an owner or investor. This option enables the owners and investors to receive 

financial reports and other documents through the portal.  

Only contacts that are marked as an owner or investor will appear in the Contact drop-down list 
when you add a new Reporting Portal owner or investor record. Investor records are associated 
with the Investor Tracking application. Owner records, in this case, are associated with the 

Reporting portal application. They are not associated with the Owner records in the Condo and 

Co-op application and its Owner portal. 

Saving the Contact Record 

After providing the available information, click the Save button. 

To add another contact with the same information, click the Duplicate button. Everything is 

identical except for the Suggested contact name. Make any necessary changes, and then click the 

Save button.

##### Editing Customer Contact Information in a Transaction
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 593*

*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 593*

Editing Customer Contact Information in a Transaction 

If you notice that the customer contact information is incorrect on a transaction, or perhaps the 

transaction uses the wrong contact entirely, then you can edit or change the contact on the 

transaction’s page. 

If you notice the error during the creation of the transaction, change the contact in the 

transaction, but keep in mind that editing customer contact information only affects the current 

transaction being created and future transactions. 

If you already saved and posted the transaction, editing or changing a contact becomes more 

complicated. Depending on the type of transaction and the state of the transaction, you may have 

to reverse the transaction before you can make any changes to the transaction record, including 

changes to the associated contact record that apply to the existing transaction. 

See one of the following for more detailed information and step-by-step instructions. 

• 
Editing Contact Information from a Transaction During Creation (on page 593) 

• 
Editing Contact Information in an Existing Transaction (on page 594) 

• 
Changing a Contact in an Existing Transaction (on page 595) 

Editing Contact Information from a Transaction During Creation 

When you edit contact information used in a transaction, you only edit the information for that 

transaction and future transactions. If you want the same changes to apply to existing 

transactions, you must manually update the contact information in that record as well. 

To edit contact information during the creation of a transaction: 

1. 
In the new transaction record, click the drop-down arrow in the contact field and highlight 

the contact you want to edit, and then click View. 

2. 
In the Contact Information box, click Edit. 

3. 
Make any necessary changes to the contact record. The Suggested contact name is a 

unique ID used across the system by various records. It can’t be changed after creation. The 

Print as name is the text that appears on printed documents and transactions. 

4. 
Click Save. 

---



##### Editing Contact Information in an Existing Transaction
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 594*

Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Editing Contact Information in an Existing Transaction 

To edit the contact information used in an existing transaction, you may have to reverse the 

transaction and recreate it. Whether you can edit or reverse a transaction depends on the 

transaction type, the state of the transaction, and your permissions. 

You can only edit information in transactions that are still open. If the transaction is part of a 
closed period, you must open the books to make any changes. 

To edit contact information in an existing transaction: 

1. 
Go to the transaction and click Edit. If you can’t edit the transaction, you must first Reverse 

a transaction, and then Edit it. 

You can only edit transactions from where they were created. For instance, if you create a 
vendor invoice in Purchasing, you cannot edit the corresponding A/P invoice in Accounts 
Payable. Instead, you must edit the vendor invoice from the vendor invoice list in 
Purchasing. 

2. 
In the contact field you want to edit, click the drop-down arrow and highlight the contact, 

then click View. 

3. 
In the Contact Information window, click Edit. 

4. 
Make any necessary changes to the contact record. The Suggested contact name is a 

unique ID used across the system by various records. It can’t be changed after creation. The 

Print as name is the text that appears on printed documents and transactions. 

5. 
Click Save. 

---



##### Changing to a Different Contact in an Existing Transaction
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 595*

Chapter 13: Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Changing to a Different Contact in an Existing Transaction 

If you need to change a contact used in an existing transaction to a completely different one, you 

may have to reverse the transaction and recreate it. Whether you can edit or reverse a transaction 

depends on the transaction type, the state of the transaction, and your permissions. You can only 

edit information in transactions that are still open. If the transaction is part of a closed period, you 

must open the books to make any changes. See Open and close process workflow (on page 395) 

for more information. 

To change a contact used in an existing transaction: 

1. 
Find the desired transaction and click Edit. 

If you can’t edit the transaction, you must first Reverse the transaction, and then Edit it. 

2. 
In the contact field you want to change, click the drop-down arrow, and then click Find. 

3. 
In the Contact name column, type the name of the contact you want to use for this 

transaction. The system stores contacts by their unique Suggested contact name. Be sure to 

search by this name when selecting a new contact. 

4. 
Click Select next to the appropriate contact name. 

5. 
Save your changes.

Using the Multi-Select Box

Click the Select button to open the Multi-select box.

type.

 Add button. The item moves to the Selected items

 Delete button to remove an item.

 Rearrange

Click the 
 Delete button to remove an item.

Click the Add/Edit link to reopen the Multi-select box and change your selections.

##### How to Read Paths
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 605*

How to Read Paths 

If you have ever been puzzled over a path in the documentation, this topic describes what it all 

means. 

Application Menus and Tabs 

Most paths begin with the Applications menu. This menu is located in the upper-left corner next 

to the Home button. When you select an application, the name of the Applications menu 

changes to the application that you selected. 

Menus have two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab is available to all users, but the Setup tab is 

restricted to users with full or limited administrator privileges. 

The Company application has two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab contains setup options for 
global features and is available to all users with the appropriate permissions. The Setup tab is 
restricted to administrators only. 

---


<!-- Page 606 -->
Help and Support 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Simple Paths 

This is an example of a simple path: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry`


The first three parts in a path are standard; they translate to “Click the Applications menu (a), 

select the name of the application (b), and then select the menu tab (c).” 

The next steps in the path—the menu section (d) and the menu option (e)—direct you to a 

specific list or page in the application. 

a) Click the Applications menu.  

b) Select the application. 

c) Select the menu tab. 

d) Find the menu section or subsection, if any. 

e) Click the menu option.  

If you see the 
 icon in a path, then you can click the  icon in front of the menu option to add 
a new blank record. 

---


<!-- Page 607 -->
Chapter 14: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

Paths with Multiple Options 

Some paths offer multiple choices. The choices are separated with a “/” symbol.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable > Setup > Taxes > Authorities > 
View/Edit`


In this example, Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable means that the same option is available 

in two applications’ menus, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable. Likewise, View/Edit 

means that you can select either the View or the Edit link to get to the page that you need.

Customer Data Appendix 

This appendix contains information to help you import customer data.  

Customer Fields Required for Importing Customer Data 

The following example shows a complete set of fields required for uploading a customer list. 

The customer list may include optional fields for a BILL-TO contact and a SHIP -TO contact. If 
either the BILL-TO contact and/or SHIP -TO contact fields are not included, the primary contact 
information is used instead. The order of the fields or columns in your CSV file is not important. 
However, the column header must contain the field name exactly as it appears in the following 
field definitions. 

Basic customer fields - required 

CUSTOMER_ID 

CUST_NAME 

CUSTTYPE_NAME 

Contact information - required 

The following fields for the primary contact are required. If the bill-to (B- prefix) and/or ship-to (S- 

prefix) contact fields are not included in the upload, the primary contact information is used 

instead. 

CONTACT_NAME - required field 

COMPANY_NAME 

MRMS 

FIRST_NAME 

MI 

LAST_NAME 

PRINT_AS 

PHONE1 

PHONE2 

CELLPHONE

Customers Data Template 

1. 
Export the data from your other system, including as much of the data as is available. 

2. 
Mark any row you want the import to ignore with a # symbol. The system ignores any row 

starting with a # during import. 

Be sure to format the data to match the template precisely. This import can update existing 
customer records. (This is true only for the Customers import type.) 

Required fields show an asterisk (*) at the end.

### A/R Invoice Data Appendix
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 635*



#### A/R Invoice Data
*Source: `RP Accounting AR User Guide.pdf`, Page 635*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable User Guide 

A/R Invoice Data Appendix 

This appendix contains information to help you import A/R invoice data.  

A/R Invoice Data 

Best Practices 

• 
Export the data from your other system, including as much of the data as is available. 

• 
Mark any row you want the import to ignore with a # symbol. The system ignores any row 

starting with a # during import. 

• 
Be sure to format the data to match the template precisely. 

Your template’s columns may differ from this documentation, as your template is designed 
around your company’s business needs. Your template may also differ from the documentation if 
your company has chosen not to enable certain features. 

Required Fields 

Each column of the template represents a field in which you can import data. The required fields 

of the template must be filled in before you can import the data. 

• 
CUSTOMER_ID 

• 
CREATED_DATE  

• 
DUE_DATE 

• 
TOTAL_DUE 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE  

• 
LINE_NO  

• 
ACCT_NO  

• 
AMOUNT  

Required Fields if the Line Is to Be Deferred 

• 
REVREC_TEMPLATE 

• 
DEFERREDREV_ACCOUNT  

• 
REVREC_JOURNAL  

• 
REVREC_SCHEDULE_LINE_NO  

• 
REVENUE_ACCOUNT  

• 
REVREC_POSTINGDATE  

• 
REVREC_AMOUNT

Field Name: BASECURR  

• 
UI Field Name: Base Currency 

• 
Type: Character 

• 
Length: 3 

• 
Default Value: None  

• 
Valid Values: Any defined ISO three-letter ISO-4127 currency code such as USD or 

EUR. 

• 
Dependencies: Must reference a previously defined currency; locations in line items 

must use the same base currency. 

• 
Required: No, except for shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies. 

• 
Editable: No  

• 
Notes: Applies only to shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies. 

This field defines the transaction base currency. Verify that locations in line items use 

the same base currency.  

Field Name: CURRENCY  

• 
UI Field Name: Currency 

• 
Type: Character 

• 
Length: 3 

• 
Default Value: Base currency 

• 
Valid Values: Any defined ISO three-letter ISO-4127 currency code such as USD or 

EUR. Blank denotes base currency  

• 
Dependencies: Must reference a previously defined currency. 

• 
Required: No 

• 
Editable: Yes 

• 
Notes: Use only for multi-currency companies. This field defines the transaction 

currency. If no field is defined here, the base currency is used.  

Applies only if your company uses foreign currency transactions, and if the transaction 

is in a foreign currency. Otherwise, this field is optional, and the system uses base 

currency.

Field Name: AMOUNT  

• 
UI Field Name: Amount  

• 
Type: Number  

• 
Length: 38,2  

• 
Default Value: None  

• 
Valid Values: Should be non-zero with negatives designated by a leading dash. 

• 
Dependencies: None  

• 
Required: Yes  

• 
Editable: No  

• 
Notes: Amount refers to line items that make up a total payment.  

For example, if an invoice was $1000, and each line item in the invoice was $200, there 

would be one line with $1000 in the Total Due column, and then five separate lines 

with $200 in the Amount column.  

The total of the Amount column must match the total for the Total Due column if they 

are identified for the same invoice.

## Configuring Accounts Receivable
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 9*

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Configuring Accounts Receivable 

This book describes how to configure the Accounts Receivable application. 

The first chapter describes how to configure the Accounts Receivable application for general use. Refer to other 

chapters in the book to configure specific features, such as account labels, intercompany bill-backs, territories, 

overriding the G/L account in A/R transactions, and shipping methods features.

Accounts Receivable Configuration Workflow 

1. 
Select the Configuration option and enable the desired functions, including account labels, 

allocation during invoice entry, and automatic discount application. 

2. 
Restart the RealPage Accounting system to allow it to reset with the functionality you 

selected. 

3. 
Configure the rest of Accounts receivable: 

• 
Account labels 

• 
Account label tax groups 

• 
Customers 

• 
Customer groups 

• 
Customer types 

• 
Visibility (Select the companies that can see a customer’s details.) 

• 
Tax authorities 

• 
Tax schedules 

• 
Schedule maps 

• 
Territories 

• 
Territory groups 

• 
Terms 

• 
Shipping methods 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have limited or full Administrator privileges to configure the Accounts Receivable 

application.

### Configure Accounts Receivable Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 11*

Chapter 1: Configuring Accounts Receivable 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Configure Accounts Receivable Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Applications > Configure (Accounts 
Receivable)`


Use the Configure Accounts Receivable page to configure Accounts receivable functions. This 

page is composed of nine or ten sections, depending on the features that your company has 

chosen to enable.  

• 
Accounting settings: Use this section to select the journals, G/L accounts, summary 

frequencies, and customer account types to use. Refer to Configure A/R Accounting Settings 

(on page 12). 

• 
Thresholds: Use this section to select desired system responses to events. Refer to 

Configure A/R Thresholds (on page 16). 

• 
Enable functionality: Use this section to select optional functionality. Refer to Enable A/R 

Functionality (on page 18). 

• 
Intercompany billing setup: Use this section to configure intercompany billing, the billing of 

shared costs among several entities. Refer to Configure Intercompany Billing (on page 24). 

• 
Inter-company bill back setup: Use this section to set up automatic billing between two 

entities. This section appears only if the feature is enabled in the Company application. Refer 

to Configure Intercompany Bill Backs (on page 40). 

• 
Screen settings: Use this section to set up G/L posting date preferences. Refer to Configure 

A/R Screen Settings (on page 27). 

• 
Dimensions setup: Use this section to select the dimensions you want to use in the system. 

Refer to Configure A/R Dimensions (on page 28). 

• 
Document sequencing: Use this section to allow the system to number selected 

transactions automatically and to select the numbering sequence for each transaction type. 

Refer to Configure A/R Document Sequencing (on page 29). 

• 
Aging: Use this section to define aging periods. Refer to Configure A/R Aging (on page 31). 

• 
Formatting: Use this section to select the format of invoices, statements, and remittance 

slips, and to define your company’s Remit to address. Refer to Configure A/R Formatting 

(on page 32). 

• 
Payments: Use this section to select the credit cards that your company supports, the email 

address to use for credit cards, to select the default payment method, offline payment 

account, and the undeposited funds account. Refer to Configure Payments (on page 34). 

• 
Credits: Use this section to determine whether the system automatically applies credits to 

invoices.  

• 
PEX: Use this section to configure how and when PEX transactions are imported. Refer to 

Configuring PEX (on page 38).

#### Configuring A/R Accounting Settings
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 12*

Configuring Accounts Receivable 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Configuring A/R Accounting Settings 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Account Settings`


Use the Accounting settings section to define the default journals, accounts, and summary 

frequencies. 

• 
Journal: Records invoices, adjustments, and payment receipt transactions. 

• 
G/L accounts: Posts transactions, such as accounts receivable, penalties, and more. 

• 
Summary frequencies: Determines how often the system posts invoices, adjustments, 

manual deposits, and payment summaries to the G/L. 

• 
Open item/Balance forward: Sets the customer accounts to Open item (most common) or 

Balance forward. 

The selections in this section vary based on the accounting method selected in General 
Ledger. When you change the accounting method from cash or accrual to cash and accrual, 
the system automatically creates some journals that are related to the new accounting 
method. Changing your accounting method requires additional setup changes. For 
information, see Accounting methods—accrual, cash, or both. 

Be sure to contact your RealPage account manager. 

Filling In the Accounting Settings Section 

Select the default journals to use for the A/R subledger. The system uses these journals for 

automatically recording the following accounts receivable transactions: 

1. 
In the Payments drop-down list, select the journal to use for payment receipt transactions. 

2. 
In the Accrual basis reporting subsection, in the A/R invoices drop-down list, select the 

journal to use for A/R invoices. 

3. 
In the Adjustments drop-down list, select the journal to use for accrual adjustments. 

4. 
In the Cash basis reporting subsection, in the A/R invoices drop-down list, select the journal 

to use for A/R invoices. 

5. 
In the Adjustments drop-down list, select the journal to use for cash adjustments. 

Filling In the G/L Accounts Subsection 

In the G/L Accounts subsection, select the General Ledger accounts to use for posting the 

following accounts receivable transaction types: 

1. 
In the Account receivable drop-down list, select the account to use for receivables. 

In general, you configure G/L accounts at the top level. One exception is that you specify 
different default A/R accounts for each entity at the entity level. For more information, 
see Specifying different default accounts by property in the online help system. 

---


<!-- Page 13 -->
Chapter 1: Configuring Accounts Receivable 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

2. 
In the Discounts drop-down list, select the account to use for discounts. 

3. 
In the Penalties drop-down list, select the account to use for penalties and late fees. 

4. 
In the Overpayment drop-down list, select the account to use for overpayments. 

5. 
In the Customer advances drop-down list, select the account to use for advanced payments. 

This setting can be changed on a per-transaction basis. 

6. 
In the Multi-currency gain and loss drop-down list, when your company has enabled the 

multi-currency option, the system can handle currency conversions for multi-currency 

companies. 

For information about the gain/loss account, see Foreign currency revaluation. 

Some organizations track overpayments and customer advances in an account that is 
typically associated with the Cash Management application, such as a deposit liability 
account. If this is the case for your company, be sure to review your report setup to verify 
that your balance sheet will tie to customer aging. Specifically, you should make sure that 
the General Ledger accounts used to represent Accounts Receivable in your balance sheet 
reports include all of the accounts that you selected here, including those for 
overpayments and advances. 

Filling In the Summary Frequency Subsection 

In the Summary frequency subsection, select how often the system creates and processes 

automatic summaries of transactions and advances. 

1. 
In the A/R invoices drop-down list, select how often you want the system to create and 

process A/R invoices: 

• 
Daily: The system creates a daily summary and posts it to the G/L for each transaction 

day. Daily is recommended because it gives you the most granular reporting. 

• 
Monthly: The system creates a single summary at the end of each month, and no 

matter what the transaction date is within that period, it will always be posted as of the 

last day of that month. This frequency doesn’t provide the daily granular level of 

reporting. 

• 
One per invoice: The system creates and posts a summary for each invoice. 

Per-transaction summaries can increase system performance, particularly if your 

transactions result in a large number of journal entries with unique G/L account and 

dimension combinations. 

• 
User specified: The system only uses manually created summaries. It continues to use 

a manual summary until you select or create another. 

2. 
In the Adjustments drop-down list, select how often that you want the system to create and 

process A/R adjustments: 

---


<!-- Page 14 -->
Configuring Accounts Receivable 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
One per invoice adjustment: The system creates and posts a summary for each 

adjustment. Per-transaction summaries can increase system performance, particularly 

if your transactions result in a large number of journal entries with unique G/L account 

and dimension combinations. 

• 
Daily: The system creates a daily summary and posts it to the G/L for each transaction 

day. Daily is recommended because it gives you the most granular reporting. 

• 
Monthly: The system creates a single summary at the end of each month, and no 

matter what the transaction date is within that period, it will always be posted as of the 

last day of that month. This frequency doesn’t provide the daily granular level of 

reporting. 

• 
User specified. The system only uses manually created summaries. It continues to use 

a manual summary until you select or create another. 

3. 
In the Quick deposits drop-down list, select how often you want the system to create quick 

deposit summaries: 

• 
One per quick deposit: The system creates and posts a summary for each deposit. 

• 
Daily: The system creates a daily summary and posts it to the G/L for each transaction 

day. Daily is recommended because it gives you the most granular reporting. 

• 
Monthly: The system creates a single summary at the end of each month, and no 

matter what the transaction date is within that period, it will always be posted as of the 

last day of that month. This frequency doesn’t provide the daily granular level of 

reporting. 

• 
User specified. The system only uses manually created summaries. It continues to use

4. 
In the Payments drop-down list, select the frequency for creating and processing customer 

payments: 

• 
One per payment: Select this option to have the system create and post a summary 

for each payment. 

• 
Daily: Select this option to have the system post the summary every day. 

• 
Monthly: Select this option to have the system create a single summary at the end of 

each month, and no matter what the transaction date is within that period, it will 

always be posted as of the last day of that month. This frequency doesn’t provide the 

daily granular level of reporting. 

• 
User specified. The system only uses manually created summaries. It continues to use 

the manual summary until you select or create another. 

To enable separate summaries for each payment method for daily and monthly 
summaries, select the Per Payment Method check box.

#### Creating Automatic Summaries
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 15*

Chapter 1: Configuring Accounts Receivable 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Filling In the Open Item/Balance Forward Section 

For the Customer account type drop-down list, set the customer accounts to Open item (most 

common) or Balance forward. 

• 
Selecting Open item causes the system to apply customer payments against specific 

invoices. 

• 
Selecting Balance forward causes the system to apply customer payments against the total 

balance due. 

What’s Next? 

Optionally, select or enable features such as warning thresholds in posting transactions, 

dimensions that you want to track and report on, payment receipt requirements, and more. 

• 
Thresholds (on page 16) 

• 
Enable functionality (on page 18) 

• 
Dimensions (on page 28) 

• 
Payments (on page 34) 

Creating Automatic Summaries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration`


We recommend that you set up automatic summaries. The system offers four types of automatic 

summaries: 

• 
Invoices 

• 
Adjustments 

• 
Quick deposits 

• 
Payments 

The system posts summaries automatically to the G/L after the transactions in the summaries are 

saved. 

 You must be at the top level to use this feature. 

You must have administrator-level permissions to set up automatic summaries. 

RealPage standardizes the date format for all automatically created summaries on the 
internationally accepted format of YYYY -MM-DD24:MI:SS. Standardizing the date format in 
the summary title ensures that transactions are always grouped or matched to the appropriate 
summary, and eliminates the risk of posting errors due to a date format mismatch.  
The date that the system creates a summary is the date the General Ledger uses to post all 

---



#### Configuring A/R Thresholds
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 16*

Configuring Accounts Receivable 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

transactions in that summary. Therefore, it is important that you do not combine transactions 
from different time periods in the same summary.  

To create automatic summaries: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

3. 
In the Accounting settings section, locate the Summary frequency section. 

4. 
Select how often that you want the system to create summaries. 

5. 
Select the Per payment method check box if you want the system to run a separate 

payment summary for each method of payment. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

Configuring A/R Thresholds 

Use the Thresholds section to configure how you want the system to respond to three events:  

• 
When the G/L posting date is in the future 

• 
When the credit limit is exceeded 

• 
When the customer is on hold. 

To configure how you want the system to handle A/R events: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration option. 

4. 
Locate the Thresholds section.  

The system uses thresholds to allow you to choose how the system responds to three 

events: when the G/L posting date is in the future, when the credit limit is exceeded, and 

when the customer is on hold.  

---


<!-- Page 17 -->
Chapter 1: Configuring Accounts Receivable 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

5. 
Find the If future G/L posting date section, and then select how you want the system to 

respond when a user attempts to set a future period date as the general ledger posting date 

for the invoice. 

• 
Warn: Select this option to display a warning message, but allow the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Select this option to display a message 

requesting the user to select a date within the current period. 

• 
Do nothing: Select this option to allow the user to proceed with the transaction 

without any alert or action on the part of the system. 

Do nothing is the default. 

The subledgers share the same posting periods as the general ledger. 

6. 
Find the If credit limit is exceeded section, and then select how you want the system to 

respond when a user attempts to enter an invoice that exceeds the credit limit of a 

customer. 

• 
Warn: Select this option to display a warning message, but allow the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Select this option to display a message 

showing the total due for the customer and the set credit limit. The transaction can’t 

be created as entered. 

• 
Do nothing: Select this option to allow the user to proceed with the transaction 

without any alert or action on the part of the system. 

Warn is the default. 

7. 
Find the If customer is on hold section, and then select the desired system response to an 

attempt to enter an invoice from a customer with an On Hold status: 

• 
Warn: Select this option to display a warning message, but allow the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Select this option to display a message that 

the customer is currently on hold. The transaction can’t be created. 

• 
Do nothing: Select this option to allow the user to proceed with the transaction 

without any alert or action on the part of the system. 

Don’t allow transactions to be created is the default. 

8. 
Click the Save button.

#### Configuring A/R Functionality
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 18*

Configuring Accounts Receivable 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Configuring A/R Functionality 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality`


Use the Enable functionality section to enable or disable Accounts Receivable features. 

This topic describes how to: 

• 
Enable allocation in invoice entry. 

• 
Enable users to allocate charges to different accounts on a single line item of an invoice. 

• 
Turn off automatic payment suggestions. 

• 
Enable creating, editing, and deleting foreign currency invoices. 

• 
Enforce the rule that payment dates must be greater than their invoice dates. 

• 
Display tax and subtotals for invoices. 

• 
Enable inter-company bill back. 

To enable Accounts Receivable functions: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration option. 

4. 
Find the Enable functionality section. 

5. 
Select the Enable accounts receivable G/L account override in invoice and adjustment 

entry check box when you want to override the default G/L account as you create a 

transaction. 

To make use of this option, you also need to: 

• 
Configure one or more G/L accounts as override accounts. 

• 
Provide permissions for selected users to override the default G/L account in invoice 

and adjustment transaction, as well as for any invoice or adjustment transactions

Configuring A/R Document Sequencing 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Document Sequencing`


In the RealPage Financial Suite, document sequences refer to the system’s automatic numbering 

feature used to assign unique identifiers to new records. This helps ensure consistency and avoids 

duplication. 

Automatic numbering, also known as document sequencing, is available only in select features in 

RealPage Accounting. These features use pre-defined numbering plans to assign sequential 

identifiers—typically when creating new records or transactions. 

If you prefer to number a transaction type manually, do not assign a document sequence for the 

transaction type. 

Before You Begin 

You must create a new document numbering scheme before you see it as an option in this 

section. 

• 
Configure a document sequence for the desired record type in Company > All > Settings > 

Document Numbering. 

Setting Up Document Sequencing for A/R Transactions and Records 

Use the Document sequencing section to: 

• 
Set warnings. If you choose to enter any of the transaction IDs manually, you can set a 

warning whenever someone enters a duplicate ID. 

• 
Assign a document sequence for these select transactions and records: 

• 
A/R invoices 

• 
Recurring A/R invoices 

• 
A/R debit adjustments 

• 
A/R credit adjustments 

• 
Customer records 

• 
Require IDs on select types of transactions and records. 

• 
Invoices 

• 
Adjustments 

• 
Quick invoice entry 

• 
Recurring invoices 

• 
Manual deposits 

After a document sequence is configured and assigned, the system automatically assigns a 

sequential ID to each new transaction or record, ensuring a smooth and consistent flow of unique 

identifiers.

Auto Payment Suggestions 

If you usually overwrite the amounts proposed by the system and no longer want the system to 

propose those amounts, you can disable the automatic payment suggestions feature.  

When this feature is enabled, the system applies the payment to the invoices starting with the 

oldest invoice. If the amount of the payment is sufficient to fully pay that invoice, the system 

automatically selects the Receive Full check box for that invoice, and then applies the remainder 

to the next invoice, and so on until the entire payment amount is used. If any amount is left over 

because the payment amount is greater than the total of the invoices, the overpayment amount 

appears in the Amount Overpaid field.  

Simultaneously, the system also applies any available discounts. In doing so, the system subtracts 

them from the amount received and places that adjusted number in the Amount received field.  

For example, you receive a check from a customer for $200 against two invoices, each for $100. 

But the second invoice has a discount of $10. The system marks both invoices as Received Full. 

An amount of $100 is placed in the Amount received field for the first invoice, but only $90 

appears for the second because the system has subtracted the $10 discount. This leaves an 

overpayment of $10. If you wish, you may override the discount that the system applied by 

entering $100 into the Amount received field for that invoice.  

Turning Off Auto Payment Suggestions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality > 
Turn Off Automatic Payment Suggestions`



> **Navigation Path:** `You set preferences in the Configure Accounts Receivable page (Accounts Receivable > Setup`


tab > Configuration). If you usually overwrite the amounts proposed by the system, and no longer 

want the system to propose those amounts, select the Turn off automatic payment suggestions 

check box to disable this feature. 

When this feature is enabled, the system applies the payment to the invoices starting with the 

oldest invoice. If the amount of the payment is sufficient to fully pay that invoice, the system 

automatically selects the Receive Full check box for that invoice, and then applies the remainder 

to the next invoice, and so on until the entire payment amount is used. If any amount is left over 

because the payment amount is greater than the total of the invoices, the overpayment amount 

appears in the Amount Overpaid field.

Simultaneously, the system also applies any available discounts. In doing so, the system subtracts 

them from the amount received and places that adjusted number in the Amount Received field.  

Example 

You receive a check from a customer for $200 against two invoices, each for $100. The second 

invoice has a discount of $10. The system marks both invoices as Received Full. An amount of 

$100 is placed in the Amount Received field for the first invoice, but only $90 appears for the 

second because the system has subtracted the $10 discount. This leaves an overpayment of $10. If 

you wish, you can override the discount that the system applied by entering $100 into the 

Amount Received field for that invoice. 

To turn off automatic payment suggestions: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select Configuration. 

4. 
In the Enable functionality section, select the Turn off automatic payment suggestions 

check box. 

5. 
Click the Save button.

#### Configuring Intercompany Bill Backs
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 40*



#### Enabling the Intercompany Bill Back Feature
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 40*

Configuring Accounts Receivable 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Configuring Intercompany Bill Backs 

Inter-company bill back makes it easy for an entity to bill a second entity. Some configuration is 

required in order to make this feature work. During setup, you create a customer and vendor 

record for each entity and then associate the records with the entity. The bill back feature uses the 

customer and vendor records as proxies for the billing process.  

Configuration Workflow 

1. 
Enable the inter-company bill back feature. 

2. 
Grant bill back template permissions. 

3. 
Create inter-entity receivable and inter-entity payable accounts to use for inter-entity 

transactions if they don’t already exist. 

4. 
Create one vendor record and one customer record for each entity that you want to be able 

to use with the bill back feature. 

5. 
Associate the vendor record and customer record to its entity. 

6. 
Create bill back templates. 

Enabling the Intercompany Bill Back Feature 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Accounts Receivable > Configure > 
Enable Functionality > Enable Inter-Company Bill Back`


The first step for using inter-company bill back is to enable the feature. 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Subscriptions. 

3. 
Find Accounts Receivable and then click Configure. The Configure Accounts Receivable 

page opens. 

4. 
In the Enable functionality section, select Enable inter-company bill back. 

What’s Next? 

Granting permissions to bill back templates (on page 41) 

---

Select Users.

The Accounts receivable permissions page opens.

In the Activities/Lists section, find the Bill back templates permission and select the 

permissions that you want to grant. These permissions are available: List, View, Add, Edit, 

and Delete.

Enabling the intercompany bill back feature (on page 40 ). 

6. 
Click the Save button. After you save and exit the permission pages, the Bill Back Templates 

menu becomes available. 

For companies with role-based permissions 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab.

Select Roles. The Roles list opens. 

3. 
Locate the role that you want to grant permissions for bill back templates and click 

Subscriptions. The Roles subscriptions page opens with a list of applications that your 

company is subscribed to. 

4. 
Locate Accounts receivable, and then click Permissions. The Accounts receivable 

permissions page opens.

#### Creating Bill Back Templates
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 44*

Configuring Accounts Receivable 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide

Creating Bill Back Templates 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > 
 Bill Back Templates`


To create bill back templates: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the 
 Add button next to Bill back templates. 

The Bill Back Template Information page opens. Previously created templates are available 

for selection. You can add one or more line items, as many as you need. 

Filling In the General Information section 

This section applies to all the line items. 

1. 
Type the Template ID. 

Template IDs can be numbers, letters, or a combination and can include dashes and periods. 

The Template ID should be something that makes it clear what the template is used for. 

2. 
Enter a Description. 

While the ID is usually short, the description can fully describe the template purpose. You 

can overwrite the description later. 

3. 
Verify that the status is Active. 

Set the status to Inactive if you don ’t want the template to appear in the list. You can 
view inactive templates by clicking Show Inactive in the summary list. You can deactivate 
any template after any dependent transactions are complete. 

Filling In the Line Items Section 

1. 
Select the A/R invoice G/L account. 

2. 
Select the A/P invoice G/L account.  

When you choose this template for an invoice, the system uses the invoice G/L account 

number as the account number for the line item in the invoice. Similarly, if the system 

---


<!-- Page 45 -->
Chapter 1: Configuring Accounts Receivable 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

automatically creates an A/P invoice, then it uses the A/P invoice G/L account number in the 

corresponding line item.  

When using a template, ensure that your system has all of the General Ledger accounts 
that the template requires, and create them if it does not.  

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 

find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

3. 
Choose a Department.  

Whether you leave this blank or supply a department, the value here is included on the 

invoice. 

4. 
Choose a default Memo. 

This memo will appear on all invoices using this template. 

5. 
Repeat this step for each line item to be included on the bill back template. 

You have now completed the setup for inter-company bill back.

Invoices, Adjustments 

Frequency periods for creating and processing invoices:  

• 
Daily: The system creates a daily summary and posts it to the G/L for 

each transaction day. Daily is recommended because it gives you the 

most granular reporting.  

• 
Monthly: The system creates a single summary at the end of each 

month and no matter what the transaction date is within that period, 

it will always be posted as of the last day of that month. This 

frequency doesn’t provide the daily granular level of reporting.  

• 
One per invoice, One per invoice adjustment: The system creates and 

posts a summary for each invoice or adjustment. Per-transaction 

summaries can increase system performance, particularly if your 

transactions result in a large number of journal entries with unique 

G/L account and dimension combinations.  

• 
User Specified. The system only uses manually created summaries. It 

continues to use the manual summary until you select or create 

another.  

Quick deposits 

Frequency periods for creating and processing manual deposits:  

• 
Daily: The system creates a daily summary and posts it to the G/L for 

each transaction day. Daily is recommended because it gives you the 

most granular reporting.  

• 
Monthly: The system creates a single summary at the end of each 

month and no matter what the transaction date is within that period, 

it will always be posted as of the last day of that month. This 

frequency doesn’t provide the daily granular level of reporting.  

• 
One per quick deposit: The system creates and posts a summary for 

each deposit.  

• 
User Specified. The system only uses manually created summaries. It 

continues to use the manual summary until you select or create 

another.  

---

Payments  

Frequency periods for creating and processing customer payments:  

• 
Daily: The system posts the summary every day.  

• 
Monthly: The system creates a single summary at the end of each 

month and no matter what the transaction date is within that period, 

it will always be posted as of the last day of that month. This 

frequency doesn’t provide the daily granular level of reporting.  

• 
One per payment: The system creates and posts a summary for each 

payment.  

To enable separate summaries for each payment method for Daily and 

Monthly summaries, select Per payment method.  

Open item/balance forward 

Section 

Customer account type  

Sets the customer accounts to Open item (most common) or 

Balance forward.  

• 
Open Item: The system applies customer payments against 

specific invoices. 

• 
Balance forward: The system applies customer payments 

against the total balance due. 

Optionally, select or enable features, such as warning thresholds in posting transactions, 

dimensions that you want to track and report on, payment receipt requirements, and more.  

You can set thresholds for events and choose how the system responds if the event occurs. 

Thresholds Section 

If future G/L posting 

date 

The system response if a user attempts to set a future period date as the 

general ledger posting date for the invoice.  

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to 

proceed.  

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message 

requesting the user to select a date within the current period.  

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without 

any alert or action on the part of the system.  

• 
Do nothing is the default.  

The subledgers share the same posting periods as the general ledger.

Enable account labels Choose whether Account labels will be required or not (On or Off).  

Account labels are a good way to restrict access to G/L accounts. If an 

Account Label is not set up for a particular G/L account, that account 

can’t be accessed.  

Also, Account Labels provide a plain-English equivalent for G/L account 

numbers, which can be helpful for users. Provide restricted access to 

G/L accounts, as well as a means of textually naming them.  

Enable allocation in 

invoice entry  

Enables users to allocate charges to different accounts on a single line 

item of an invoice. This option can only be enabled here if you’ve 

enabled it in G/L configuration.  

Enable the system to 

automatically apply 

discounts  

When you record the receipt of a payment for an invoice with an 

associated term discount, the system automatically selects the Apply 

Discount check box in the transaction and applies the term discount.  

Leave this option unselected if you want to manually apply the 

discount.  

Turn off automatic 

payment suggestions  

Selecting this option limits the system to using the payment amount 

you enter to populate the Amount Received fields on the Select 

Invoices for Payment page.  

By default, the system applies the payment to the invoices starting with 

the oldest invoice.  

If the amount of the payment is sufficient to fully pay that invoice, the 

system automatically selects the Receive Full check box for that invoice, 

applies the remainder to the next invoice, and so on until the entire 

payment amount is used up.  

If any amount is left over because the payment amount is greater than 

the total of the invoices, the system displays the overpayment amount 

in the Amount Overpaid field.  

If you usually overwrite the amounts proposed by the system, and no 

longer want the system to propose those amounts, select this check 

box to disable this feature.

for invoices and

Setting Up Override Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Accounts`


Setting up override accounts is a two-step process. The first step flags an account as an override 

account for either Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable. The second step enables the 

override feature. 

To have this account act as an available override to the default A/P or A/R G/L account: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Accounts. 

3. 
Find the account for which you want to create an alternate account, and then click the Edit 

link. 

4. 
In the G/L account alternative drop-down list, select the type of account it can override: 

• 
Payables account: Adds the account to the filtered list of A/P G/L accounts available as 

override accounts for invoice and adjustment transactions, as well as transactions 

involving a specific vendor. 

• 
Receivables account: Adds the account to the filtered list of A/R G/L accounts 

available as override accounts for invoice and adjustment transactions, as well as 

transactions involving a specific customer. 

Currently, this feature applies to A/R invoices, A/P invoices, and adjustments only. It 
doesn’t apply to recurring invoices, manual checks, manual deposits, quick check 
entry, quick bill entry, quick invoice entry, or advances. 

To enable the override feature: 

1. 
Based on your selection in step 4, select either Accounts payable or Accounts receivable 

from the Applications menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab. 

3. 
Click Configuration. 

4. 
In the Enable functionality section, select the Enable Accounts (Receivable or Payable) G/L 

account override in invoice and adjustment entry check box. 

5. 
Click Save.

### Account Labels List
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 60*

Account Labels 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide

Account Labels List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Account Labels`


Use the Account Labels list to add new account labels, view and edit existing account label 

details, delete account labels and export the list of account labels. 

Account labels map to revenue and receivable accounts in the General Ledger (G/L). Multiple 

account labels can map to the same G/L account. 

Account labels help users select the correct general ledger account. When your system uses 

account labels, users don’t have to be familiar with an entity’s chart of accounts, which results in 

greater accuracy of financial transactions. Accuracy in labeling each transaction is critical in 

getting good information out of the system in the form of reports.  

The RealPage Accounting system has one set of account labels that the system uses for both 

RealPage Accounting and RealPage Commercial Property Management. 

a) Account number: This is the GL account number that maps to the label. 

b) Account title: This is the account title that joins to the account number when you use the 

account label in the system.

Adding Account Labels 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > 
 Account Labels`


When you add an account label, you are creating a name and mapping it to a General Ledger 

account number. Account labels appear in the Account labels drop-down lists throughout the 

system. 

To add an account label: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select

4.

5. 
In the Description field, type a description including the purpose and use of the label. 

Account labels play an important role in the system. 

You must use a descriptive name: 

• 
Account labels must be unique. 

• 
Account labels are case-sensitive. The system will see a match when searching for text 

only if the text matches it exactly, including the use of upper and lower case. 

Be aware that this can lead to the creation of duplicate account label names if the name has 

the same text, but the account label has upper/lower case differences. 

If you create an exact duplicate of an existing account label, the system displays an error 

message and discards the new label. 

6. 
In the Account number drop-down list, select the general ledger account number to which 

this label refers. You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L 

account’s record, or find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must 

be at the top level. 

7. 
In the Offset account drop-down list, select the general ledger account for the system to 

use when it needs to offset transactions in the main account for this account label. You can 

use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or find a G/L 

account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

8. 
Clear the Use for Property Management check box. For information on account labels used 

with RealPage Commercial Property Management, see Adding Property Management rent 

account labels in the RealPage Commercial Property Management User Guide. 

9. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active to allow this value to appear as a choice in 

Account label drop-down lists. Select Inactive to create the value and save activation for
