Exporting the Account Label List 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

To export the list of account labels: 

1. 
Select the Include inactive check box to include account labels with an Inactive status in the 

list, or clear the Include inactive check box so that only active account labels appear in the 

list. When selected, the Status column appears in the list.  

2. 
Select the Include private check box to list all account labels, regardless of where they were 

set up. When selected, the list includes the Entity column that contains the entity to which a 

private account label belongs. Clear the Include private check box to list only the account 

labels that are available to all entities. 

Private account labels belong to a specific entity.  

3. 
Click the Export button. 

4. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list: 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open.

### Intercompany Bill Backs
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 74*

Intercompany Bill-Backs 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Intercompany Bill Backs 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Bill Back Templates`


Inter-company bill back makes it easy for an entity to bill a second entity. Some configuration is 

required in order to make this feature work. During setup, you create a customer and vendor 

record for each entity and then associate the records with the entity. The bill back feature uses the 

customer and vendor records as proxies for the billing process.  

In this example, Entity A provides services to Entity B. In this way, Entity A is a vendor to Entity B. 

Entity B is a customer to Entity A. 

To bill for the service: 

1. 
Entity A uses the inter-company bill back feature by creating an invoice and selecting a bill 

back template.  

2. 
Entity A posts the invoice. 

3. 
The system creates an A/P invoice in Entity B’s Accounts payable subledger. 

4. 
Entity B pays the A/P invoice. 

Requirements 

This feature requires: 

• 
Multi-entity shared company 

• 
Create bill back invoices at the top level 

What is the difference between Intercompany bill-back and intercompany billing? 

The purpose of an inter-company bill back transaction is for one entity to bill another. It is a 

one-to-one transaction. When a bill back invoice is posted, the system creates a bill on the books 

of the second entity in Accounts payable. 

---


<!-- Page 75 -->
Chapter 3: Intercompany Bill-Backs 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

The purpose of intercompany billing is to distribute a shared cost among several entities. 

Intercompany billing is a one-to-many transaction. See Configuring Intercompany Billing (on 

page 24) for more information. 

Bill Back Configuration Workflow 

Inter-company bill back requires configuration changes and additional setup. 

1. 
Enable the bill back feature. 

2. 
Grant bill back template permissions. 

3. 
Create Inter-entity receivable and Inter-entity payable accounts to use for inter-entity 

transactions if you don’t have them already. 

4. 
Create a vendor record and a customer record for each entity. 

5. 
Associate the customer record and the vendor record with its entity. Do this for each entity. 

6. 
Create bill back templates. 

Associating Customer and Vendor Records 

You can have one bill back-associated customer and one bill back-associated vendor for each 

entity. The bill back customer and the bill back vendor are not mapped to each other, only to the 

entity. After association, if you create an invoice at the top level for the bill back customer, the 

customer information automatically appears on the invoice.  

Later, when you choose a bill back template for the bill back customer invoice, the system 

includes the information from that template on the invoice. The template bill back vendor serves 

as the billing entity.  

When inter-company bill back is enabled, creating the invoice automatically creates the bill in the 

Accounts Payable application of the customer-associated entity. 

If you create a vendor now but later associate it with a different entity, the vendor in the 

corresponding system-generated bill back creates the invoice for the newly associated entity. The 

vendor-entity association can be the top-level entity or another subordinate entity, as long as the 

invoice is created at the top level. 

Example 

Suppose you create a bill back customer named Paradise One and associate it with the Paradise 

Palms entity. You associate a vendor named Paradise Services to the Paradise Limited entity. 

Here’s what happens: 

• 
When you create an invoice and pick the Paradise Palms’ bill back customer (Paradise One), 

the customer information is included on the invoice. 

---


<!-- Page 76 -->
Intercompany Bill-Backs 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Now you select a bill back template that includes the bill back vendor that is associated with 

the Paradise Limited entity (Paradise Services). The information, including line items and 

G/L accounts for Paradise Services appears on the Paradise One invoice. 

• 
All line items in the bill back template appear on the invoice. 

• 
When the invoice is complete, the system creates a bill in Paradise One’s Accounts Payable 

subledger. 

Similarly, if you create or choose a new vendor (Paradise Properties) to associate with the Paradise 

Palms entity, here’s what happens. 

• 
If you create a new invoice, the system uses the updated vendor (Paradise Properties) 

information for the vendor information on the corresponding system-generated bill to bill 

back the invoice to the customer (Paradise One). 

• 
The previous vendor, Paradise Limited, is no longer associated with the customer and their 

information isn’t used. 

Bill Back Templates 

Bill back templates provide the information needed to automatically include the vendor 

information and invoice line, items and the corresponding items in the system-generated bill. You 

supply a mandatory invoice and bill G/L account for each line item, along with an optional 

department and memo. All line items in the template will appear on the bill. 

After you choose the bill back template when creating the invoice, the line items of that invoice 

are automatically populated with the revenue and expense account numbers, department, and 

memo. 

Create one template for each group of line items for which you invoice. You’ll still need to enter 

an amount for each line item on the invoice. While it is possible to use a template with line items 

that you’re not billing back, you then have to zero out the amount for the line item you don’t 

need to bill back. The line item still appears on the bill but as zeroed out.

Overriding the G/L Account in A/R Transactions 

This chapter describes how to configure G/L Account overrides. 

If you configure Accounts Receivable appropriately, you can override a default A/R G/L account for an invoice or 

adjustment. Specifically, you can select an alternative G/L account as an override as follows: 

• 
for an entire transaction 

• 
at the line-item level 

• 
for all transactions involving a specific customer 

Currently, this feature applies to invoices and adjustments only. It doesn’t apply to recurring invoices, manual 
deposits, quick invoice entry, or advances. 

As you enter an invoice or adjustment, you can select an alternative A/R account from a predefined list of 

accounts.

designate it as either a Payables account or a Receivables account as appropriate. The 
system adds the account to the filtered list of override accounts that you can select from 
in specific pages, such as transaction pages and vendor and customer pages.  

Payables account: the system adds the account to the filtered list of A/P G/L accounts 
available as override accounts in bill, adjustment, and vendor pages. 

Receivables account: the system adds the account to the filtered list of A/R G/L accounts 
available as override accounts in invoice, adjustment, and customer pages.

Click the Save button.

### Terms Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 94*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 94*

A/R Terms 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Terms Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > More > Terms`


A/R terms are the rules your company establishes for extending credit to customers. For instance, 

if you offer a customer Net 30 terms, you are allowing him or her to pay within 30 days without 

penalties. The system uses the terms information to recommend payment dates and, in some 

cases, such as 2 percent Net 10, the system can track discounts associated with A/R terms. 

When you enter an A/R transaction (such as an invoice), you can select the term you want to use. 

You can also associate terms that you’ve defined with specific customers. When you select a term 

from the Customer Information page for a particular customer, that term becomes the default for 

that customer. 

Multi-Entity, Multi-Currency Companies 

If your company is a multi-entity, multi-currency company, we recommend that you create 

custom terms at the top level to be shared across all the entities. However, you can create custom 

terms in an entity, so they are restricted to that entity. If you do create them in the entities, use a 

naming convention that differentiates them at the top level. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 323) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions.

### A/R Terms List
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 96*



#### Adding an A/R Term
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 96*

A/R Terms 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

A/R Terms List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Terms`


From the Terms list, you can: 

• 
Add a new term 

• 
Change an existing term’s details 

• 
View the term details 

• 
Delete the term  

• 
Export the list of terms 

Adding an A/R Term 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > 
 Terms`


A/R terms can either be accessible to all entities or exclusive to a specific entity. We recommend 

that you create customer terms at the top level to be shared across all entities. Creating terms in 

an entity restricts them to that entity. If you do create terms in an entity, then use a naming 

convention that differentiates them at the top level. 

To add an A/R term: 

1. 
Type a Name for the term (for example, 2% 10 Net 30). The system displays the name on 

invoice and customer pages. 

2. 
In the Description field, type a note about the purpose and use of this term (for example, 

2% discount if paid 10 days from invoice, due on day 30). 

3. 
Set Status to Active. To change the status of an object to hide unused items, select Inactive. 

When an item is set to Inactive, the system retains the data but hides the inactive item on 

lists, drop-down lists, and so on. Examples of data you might want to hide or make inactive 

are employees who are no longer with your company or bank accounts you no longer use. If 

you want to permanently remove an item, you must delete it. 

Filling In the Due Section 

The Due date is a combination of the day(s) and what the day(s) references: 

1. 
To set terms that reference the number of days from the invoice date, such as Net 30, type 

the number of days in Day, and select from invoice/bill date from the drop-down list. 

2. 
To set a day on a month referenced from the invoice date, type the day of the month in 

Day, and select a month setting from the adjacent drop-down list. For instance, to set terms 

for the 15th of the month after the invoice date, type 15 in Day, and select of next month 

from invoice/bill date in the drop-down list. 

---

Filling In the Discount Section 

The Discount is a combination of the day(s), what the day(s) references, the dollar or percent 

discount, and the number of grace days. In addition, you can set how the system calculates 

discounts for transactions using this term. 

To set a discount that references the number of days from the invoice date, such as 2%-10: 

1. 
Type the number of days in Day. 

2. 
Select from invoice date from the drop-down list. 

3. 
Type the discount amount in Amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days before the discount is withdrawn. 

To set a discount based on a day on a month referenced from the invoice date: 

1. 
In Day, type the day of the month. 

2. 
Select a month setting from the drop-down list. 

3. 
Type the discount amount in Amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days before the discount is withdrawn. 

To set a discount based on a day on a month referenced from the invoice date: 

1. 
In the Day field, type the day of the month. 

2. 
Select a month setting from the drop-down list. 

3. 
Type the discount amount in Amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days before the discount is withdrawn. 

You can set how the system calculates discounts in transactions that use this term. You can 

calculate the discount based solely on: 

• 
The Line-items total, excluding added charges (such as taxes and shipping). 

• 
The Invoice total, including all charges. 

In Configure Accounts Receivable, you can set up your company to automatically apply 
discounts when you record a payment receipt.

1.

Biweekly, Monthly, and so on. 

2.

4. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days after the due date that the penalty will 

take effect. For example, you can use the grace period to compensate for the delay caused 

when a check is mailed within the penalty period, but is delayed in the mail.

### About Sales Tax
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 104*

Taxes 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Sales Tax 

Depending on where you do business, you might need to collect and report on sales tax in 

Accounts Receivable. 

While there is no federal sales tax, most states in the United States, plus the District of Columbia, 

impose a sales tax on retail sales and some services, as well as use taxes on sales and services. 

There are approximately 8,000 state, county, and city jurisdictions in the US that charge a sales 

tax. Some states, such as Florida, Texas, and California, tax services in addition to tangible items. 

Businesses are required to collect sales taxes when: 

• 
The customer is in the same state, or 

• 
The business has nexus in the customer’s state 

The regular presence of a single sales person can be enough to create tax nexus requiring 
the collection of sales tax. 

Tax rates vary between states and also on what goods and services are taxable. For example, food 

is not taxed in some states. Clothing may have a lower tax than other items.  

In addition, most states allow counties, cities, and other local areas to levy a sales tax, too. So, 

businesses must keep records of sales in each city, county, and state in which they do business. 

---



### Calculating Tax
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 105*

Chapter 6: Taxes 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Calculating Tax 

The following is an overview of the setup and interaction required in Accounts Receivable for 

calculating tax: 

• 
Customers: Transaction for new customers are automatically flagged as taxable. 

• 
Account labels: Create labels to add subtotal tax lines in invoices. 

• 
Contact tax groups: Create groups of contacts to assign the way that Accounts Receivable 

transactions involving those customers, vendors, and their contacts are taxed. For example, 

you might have tax groups that represent different state, provincial, or local taxes. Suppose 

the Los Angeles sales tax is 8% but the San Francisco tax is only 7%. Create two tax groups, 

one for Los Angeles and another for San Francisco. You can then apply one tax schedule to 

all members in the San Francisco group, and another to the members of the Los Angeles 

group 

• 
A/R account label tax groups: Create groups to organize multiple account labels under one 

tax category. 

• 
Tax details: Describe the details of a specific type of tax to be applied to a line item. When 

the system calculates taxes, the tax schedule map applies the chosen tax details to any 

taxable line items. For example, you might specify two tax details (Los Gatos Local and 

California State) to define local and state tax. 

• 
Tax schedules: Create and use tax schedules to help you determine which tax schedule to 

apply to each line item. For example, you could create a schedule named Los Gatos - State 

& Local where two tax details (Los Gatos Local and California State) are assigned. When this 

schedule is referenced, both taxes are applied. 

• 
Tax schedule maps: Create and use tax schedule maps to determine which tax schedules to 

apply to which account labels and contact tax groups associated with those labels. In other 

words, if the item is taxable and the contact is in a certain city, the system automatically 

applies a particular tax schedule. 

---

Account Label Tax Groups 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Account Label Tax Groups`


Use the Account Label Tax Group list to add and manage account label tax groups. 

Account label tax groups are applicable only if you’re using value added tax (UK only). 

Account label tax groups organize account labels under one tax category. They are part of the 

glue in tax schedule maps, which associate tax schedules with one or more combinations of 

contact tax groups and account label tax groups (the amount of tax to apply to which customers 

for which account labels). 

After you’ve created at least one account label tax group, you can select the group for an account 

label on the Account Label Information page.

Tax authorities are agencies (for example, cities, states, provinces, federal, or HMRC, for example) 

for whom you are collecting sales and other taxes. If your organization uses VAT, the Tax 

authorities list shows all of the tax authorities in your system.  

You can create tax authorities, including hierarchies of tax authorities with parent-child 

relationships, and modify existing ones. Tax authorities are shared between Accounts Receivable 

and Accounts Payable and thus appear on the Setup menu of both applications.  

You use tax authorities by assigning a line item in a transaction to a tax authority when the item is 

taxable.

If your organization is using VAT taxes (UK only), the Tax details list shows all the tax details you 

have created to which items can be assigned.  

Use the Tax detail list to view the details of a specific type of tax to be applied to a line item. 

When the system calculates the taxes, the tax schedule map applies the chosen tax details to any 

taxable line items in invoices.  

You assign the tax detail in the tax schedule using the Tax schedules detail tab.

#### Adding Tax Details
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 118*

Taxes 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding Tax Details 

These are the most direct options for adding tax details. You may have additional options based 

on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Tax > 
 Details`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > 
 Details`


Not only can you specify the tax rate, but you can also specify a taxable range such that items 

with costs below a minimum are not taxed, and the tax stops when the cost of the item goes 

above the maximum.  

You can also specify an absolute minimum and/or maximum taxable amount. A minimum is that 

which must be paid when the calculated tax on an item is too low; the maximum tax overrides the 

calculated tax if that tax goes above the maximum taxable amount. In addition, you can also 

choose a tax authority (City of San Jose, for example) for whom you are collecting the taxes.  

To add tax details: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu.  

3. 
In the Tax section, click 
 Add next to Details. The Tax details information page opens. 

4. 
In the Detail ID field, type a name for the tax detail. After you save this name, it can’t be 

changed.  

5. 
In the Description field, type a description of the tax, such as Excise tax for Equipment. 

6. 
In the Minimum taxable amount field, If the item is not taxed until its cost passes a specific 

threshold, type that amount in the Minimum taxable amount box. 

7. 
In the Maximum taxable amount field, if the tax tops out at another limit, type that amount 

in the Maximum taxable amount box. For example, say items under $200 are not taxable. 

You enter $200 as the minimum. Taxes will not be added in any document using this tax 

detail for items under $200. However, for items over $200, the tax in the Percent field is 

added.  

8. 
In the Include in taxable amount drop-down list, click one of the following:  

• 
Full amount - include the cost from zero up to the maximum taxable amount.  

• 
Amount within range - include the amount between the minimum and maximum 

taxable amount.  

To save the record and open a new record page, click Save & new.  

9. 
In the Percent field, type the tax rate. For example, type 6 to apply a tax of 6%. 

---


<!-- Page 119 -->
Chapter 6: Taxes 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

10. 
In Minimum tax and Maximum tax fields, if an item has a fixed minimum or maximum tax 

regardless of amount, then enter those amounts.  

The Accounts Receivable application always uses account labels for tax computations. 

11. 
In the G/L Account drop-down list, select the general ledger account to which this tax is to 

be assigned. You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s 

record, or find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the 

top level. 

The Account label field displays only if tax schedules are enabled in the Accounts 
Receivable application. Both the Account label field and the G/L account field must 
reference the same general ledger account number. In other words, if you selected an 
account label already, choose the G/L account that is used by this account label. If you 
select the G/L account first, then select an account label that references that G/L 
account.  

12. 
In the Account label drop-down list, select the account label for the general ledger account 

you selected in the G/L account drop-down list. 

13. 
In the Tax authority drop-down list, select the tax authority to which this tax belongs.  

14. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active to add the new item to the Tax details 

drop-down list. Or select Inactive to prevent the new item from appearing in the list. To see 

the inactive tax details later, select the Show inactive check box in the list page.  

15. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

new. The system saves the record and opens a new blank record. 

---

Duplicating Records 

You can add a record by duplicating an existing one and then editing the duplicate.  

To duplicate an existing record: 

1. 
Open the record that you want to duplicate by clicking View or Edit.  

2. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system creates a new record that is identical to the original. 

3. 
Fill in the fields.  

4. 
The system sets the status to Active. You can leave the status set to Active or select Inactive 

to prevent the item from appearing in lists. 

5. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

New. The system saves the record and then opens a new blank record.

Tax Schedules

options based on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Tax > Schedules`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > Schedules`


A tax schedule record identifies the tax details that are applied when the schedule is referenced. 

For example, you could create a schedule named “Dallas - State & Local” where two tax details 

(“Dallas Local” and “Texas State”) are assigned. When the system references this schedule, it 

applies both taxes. 

Create and use tax schedules to help you determine which tax schedule to apply to each line item. 

Tax schedules are applicable only if you’re using VAT taxes (UK only). 

To find your tax schedules, go to the Accounts Receivable menu, and then click the Setup tab.  

• 
To edit or view your tax schedules, click Schedules.  

• 
To add a new tax schedule, click 
 Add.  

About Tax Schedules 

A tax schedule is where one or more tax details are assigned. For example, you could create a 

schedule named Los Gatos - State & Local where two tax details (Los Gatos Local and California 

State) are assigned. When this schedule is referenced, both taxes are applied. 

Viewing Your List of Tax Schedules 

These are the most direct options for viewing the tax schedules list. You may have additional 

options based on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Tax > Schedules`

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu.  

3. 
In the Tax section, select Schedules. The Tax schedules list opens.

### Tax Schedule Maps List
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 132*

Tax Schedule Maps List 

These are the most direct options for opening the Tax Schedule Maps list. You may have 

additional options based on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Tax > Schedule Maps`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > Schedule Maps`


A tax schedule map associates tax schedules with account labels (via account label tax groups) 

and customers (via contact tax groups). The tax schedule contains the tax detail records, which 

define the amount of tax to apply.  

When a user enters an invoice for a customer in a contact tax group and the user enters a line for 

an account label in an account label tax group, the tax schedule map tells the system which tax 

schedules to use for the subtotal tax account label. 

The Memo field displays the names of the tax detail records associated with the tax schedules 

assigned to the tax subtotal based on the tax schedule map.

Tax Schedule Map Overview 

A tax schedule map shows you which tax schedules apply to which account labels and contact tax 

groups associated with those labels. In other words, if the item is taxable and the contact is in a 

certain city, the system applies a particular tax schedule. 

Example 

When computer hardware is purchased (account label tax group) by a person in London (contact 

tax group), add both a sales tax and value-added tax (tax schedule with tax two details). 

When you create an invoice, the system evaluates all tax schedule maps against the line items in 

the invoice along with to whom the invoice is issued, and then knows which tax schedules to 

apply to each line item. 

The tax schedule map includes the account label tax group, contact tax group, and tax schedule. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with tax schedules and tax schedule maps.

### Territories
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 142*

Territories and Territory Groups 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Territories 


> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Territories`



> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Cash Management > All > Territories`


Territories are optionally included in Customer records and are used with Accounts receivable 

reports. They can be useful for filtering and categorizing data, assuming your company has 

multiple territories.  

Territories are similar to dimensions but aren’t actual dimensions, so they work differently than 

dimensions. They can be used with dimensions.  

Multi-entity companies 

For top-level multi-entity companies that use multiple base currencies, you must assign the 

territory to a specific entity, so the system knows which base currency to use for that territory. 

Entities are territories and–under certain circumstances–entities appear in lists. For example, you 

have the option to choose the entity as the parent territory and thus it appears in that list of 

locations.  

---



### Reports That Use Territories
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 143*

Chapter 7: Territories and Territory Groups 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Reports That Use Territories 

Not all Accounts receivable reports can be filtered by territory. Because only customers are 

assigned to territories, only reports that include customers can include territory filtering or 

categorization. The following standard A/R reports can include territories:  

• 
A/R Ledger  

• 
Customer aging graph/report  

• 
Customer list  

• 
Invoice analysis graph/report  

• 
Register, sales  

You can create custom reports that include a territories column using the Custom report writer, 

as long as the primary data source includes fields that use Customers, and the customers are 

assigned to territories.  

When using a custom report, you can output the data to a graph. For example, the following 

graph represents the number of customers who are assigned to each territory.  

Customer by Territory Graph (Stacked Column) 

Reports can be saved in another format, such as a Word or Excel document, as well.

Territories List

> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Cash Management > All > Territories`


Use the Territories list to see the territories in your company. You can sort and filter the territory 

list to see only the group of territories you want.  

From this list, you can add, edit, view, and delete territories. You can also export the list of 

territories. 

Creating a Hierarchical List of Territories 

You can create a hierarchy of territories to reflect how territories are organized within your 

company. The hierarchy is established by defining parent and child relationships between 

territories. For example, your West Coast Division contains several territories including California, 

Nevada, and Utah. In turn, California contains Northern California and Southern California.  

Adding Territories 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > 
 Territories`


To add a territory: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select 
 next to Territories. 

4. 
In the Territory ID field, type a unique identifier for the territory. After you save the territory 

record, you cannot change this field. 

5. 
In the Territory name field, type a name for the territory. 

6. 
In the Parent ID field, to create a territory hierarchy, select a parent territory. 

For example, the Denver Main Office is the parent territory. Durango, Colorado Springs, and 

Boulder are each a child territory. 

This field is required in the case of top-level, multi-entity companies that also use multiple 

base currencies. You must assign the territory to a specific entity, so the system knows 

which base currency applies to this territory. 

7. 
In the Manager drop-down list, select the name of the territory manager. 

The manager name is used for informational purposes only. 

8. 
In the Status field, assign a status (such as Active or Inactive) to this territory. The default 

status is Active. However, if you are no longer using the territory and do not want it to

Making a Territory Inactive 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Territories > Edit > Status`


If, for any reason, you no longer use a territory that’s been associated with customers, you can 

make that territory inactive so that you don’t see it on any future customers. You will continue to 

see an inactive territory in reports.  

To make a territory inactive:  

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select Territories. 

4. 
Locate the territory record you want to inactivate and click Edit. 

5. 
In the Status field, change the status to Inactive.  

6. 
Click the Save button. 

Deleting Territories 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Territories > Delete`


You delete territory records from the Territories list.  

You can delete a territory if it hasn’t been associated with a transaction or record. For example, if 

you create the territory New York and you have customers associated with the territory, you can 

no longer delete New York from the list of territories.  

To delete a territory record: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select Territories. 

4. 
Locate the territory record you want to delete and click the Delete link. 

5. 
Click OK to confirm that you want to delete the record.

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in RealPage Accounting do not have the CSV for import option.

#### How Merge Works
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 174*

Printed Document Templates 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

How Merge Works 

A standard customer document template is made up of two elements:  

• 
Static text  

• 
Placeholders for data 

The merge process combines the static text with data from the customer record. 

The example below is a template for a mailing label. In the example, “Mailing:” is the static text. 

Below “Mailing:” are placeholders for each piece of data in the customer’s billing address.  

When you are ready to print the customer’s mailing label, you select the template, filter the 

customers, and then print. As the system prints, it replaces <<BILLPRINTAS>> with the billing 

name that is stored in the customer’s record. The system replaces each placeholder with the 

appropriate bit of data to form the customer’s billing address.  

Customer A 

2201 Lakeside Blvd 

Richardson, TX 75252 

If the system does not find any data for a field, it leaves the placeholder blank.

Document Templates Workflow 

The workflow for document templates, from creation to delivery, is as follows: 

1. 
Download and install (on page 176) the Word Merge tool. 

2. 
Log in (on page 177) to the Word merge tool. 

3. 
Open a Word file (on page 180) for your template. 

4. 
If you are working with a blank document, add the static text to the Word document such as 

the title, and your business name and address. If you are working with an existing template, 

change the existing text to reflect your business needs. 

5. 
Use the RealPage Word Merge tool (on page 183) to add placeholders (merge fields) to 

your document template.  

6. 
Sync the document template (on page 204). 

7. 
Assign the template (on page 206) to a transaction or customer in RealPage Accounting. 

8. 
Test (on page 208) and troubleshoot (on page 209) the template as needed. 

9. 
Print or email the documents.

### Constructing a Statement Template
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 181*



#### Parts of the Statement
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 181*

Chapter 9: Printed Document Templates 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Constructing a Statement Template 

RealPage Accounting uses the Mail Merge feature of Microsoft Word to create customer 

statements for multiple recipients by merging the template with RealPage Accounting’s data.  

There are two key components to customizing your document templates: the formatting power of 

Word and the flexibility of merge fields from the system. Add selected merge fields to your 

document template to display data from the system specific to each customer, and then use 

Word to create tables, bold key information, and format your transactional information the way 

you want it. 

Parts of the Statement 

The customer statement is divided into two to three main areas. 

a) The lower section contains a list of charges and may include taxes and totals.  

b) The top section identifies the property, the customer, and the date. 

The footer is an optional third section (not shown below). Companies often include contact 

information and other helpful information in the footer of a statement. 

For a list of placeholders (merge fields) that you can include in customer statements, see 

Statement merge fields. 

When constructing the table section of the custom template, you must use placeholders that 
begin with <<PRENTRY_.  

---

*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 182*

Printed Document Templates 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Content Supported in a Document Template 

You can add the following types of content to a document template: 

• 
Static text 

• 
Merge fields 

• 
Images 

Static Text 

Static text is the actual text in the Word file. This text does not change each time you print or 

email your documents, but instead remains the same. Additionally, since the PDF of your 

document is created in the system, only specific fonts are available, which include: 

• 
Arial 

• 
Calibri Family 

• 
Courier New 

• 
Times New Roman 

• 
Tahoma 

• 
Cambria 

• 
Verdana 

• 
Trebuchet 

Merge Fields 

Merge fields are placeholders that get replaced with data from a particular field in the system at 

the time you create and send the statement. You can add both standard and custom fields to 

your document templates. See Statement Merge Fields for a list of available fields. Additional 

fields are available when you use the RealPage Merge tool (on page 176). 

Images 

You may want to include your company’s logo in the document template to meet your company’s 

branding guidelines. Document templates in RealPage Accounting support the following image 

file formats: 

• 
PNG 

• 
JPEG 

• 
GIF 

---



#### Using the Word Merge Tool to Insert Merge Fields
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 183*

Chapter 9: Printed Document Templates 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Using the Word Merge Tool to Insert Merge Fields 

To use the Word Merge tool: 

1. 
Open your document template in Word.  

You can open a new blank Word document or download an existing template using the 

Platform Services > Printed Document Templates > Template link.  

2. 
In Word, click the RealPage Word Merge Add-in option. If you do not see the option, see 

Downloading and Installing the Word Merge Tool (on page 176). The package that you 

download also contains some troubleshooting information in the Installation Guide. 

3. 
In the Login box, type your company name, user name, and password. 

4. 
Click the Insert Merge Fields option. The Merge Fields box opens. 

5. 
Select the desired functional area.  

The functional areas correspond with the Accounting applications Company, Accounts 

Receivable, Property Management, and Condo and Co-op.  

For the purpose of illustration, this example uses the Property Management application. 

6. 
In the Template field, select the template type. The options in the Template drop-down list 

vary depending on the application that you choose in step 5. These are the options that 

appear when you select Property Management in step 5. 

• 
Tenant Charge 

• 
Print/Email Statements 

• 
Correspondence 

For the purpose of this illustration, this example uses the Correspondence template. 

---


<!-- Page 184 -->
Printed Document Templates 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The Insert Merge Fields box fills up with fields that are related to your application and 

template selections. 

7. 
Place your cursor in the document template where you want to insert a field.  

8. 
In the Insert Merge field box, double-click the field that you want to add to the template. 

The system inserts the field into the Word document at the cursor location. 

9. 
Move your cursor to the next place in the document template where you want to insert a 

merge field.  

10. 
Repeat steps 8 and 9 until you have finished building your document template. 

11. 
When you are done customizing your document template, save it using a descriptive name 

so that you’ll be able to identify it easily in a list. For example, “NY_statement.doc.” 

Be sure to save your template as a Word 97 -2003 file after you finish customizing your 
document, or otherwise, you might encounter errors when printing and uploading your 
document. 

What’s Next? 

• 
Sync the document template (on page 204) with the system.

#### Using Merge Fields in Tables
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 185*

Chapter 9: Printed Document Templates 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Using Merge Fields in Tables 

When you want to insert merge fields into tables, you must add a tag to the beginning and 

ending of the table. You must also prefix each field. 

To use merge fields in tables: 

1. 
In the top left cell of a table, type “«TableStart:PRENTRY».” 

2. 
In the last column of the last row, type “«TableEnd:PRENTRY».” 

3. 
Add the desired merge fields into the table, and then add the prefix “PRENTRY_” to each 

merge field name. 

To use a table with tax data: 

1. 
In the top left data cell of a table (not in the heading row), type 

“«TableStart:PRENTRY_TAXENTRIES».”  

2. 
In the last column of the last row, type “«TableEnd:PRENTRY_TAXENTRIES».” 

3. 
Add the desired tax-related merge fields into the table, and then add the prefix 

“PRENTRY_TAXENTRIES_” to each merge field name.

#### Tips for Working in Word
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 203*

Chapter 9: Printed Document Templates 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Tips for Working in Word 

When working with your content in your Word document, we recommend the following 

guidelines: 

• 
Start small. Add and test information periodically while you create your document. For 

instance, add your company header first, then test it. After, add your table header, and then 

test that. Adding and testing information to your document template incrementally will help 

you identify any problems you may encounter. 

• 
Turn on paragraph markers in Word to see information grouped together. 

• 
Obtain any images you want to use at the correct size before you insert the images into 

Word. Do not use Word to resize images. 

• 
If you want the logo to appear on every page of your document, place the logo in the 

header of the document. 

• 
Use Word headers and footers for static text you want to display on every page. Consider 

using different headers for your first and last page, an option available in Header and Footer 

Tools. 

• 
Layout your content in separate tables. For example, use separate tables for company 

information, customer information, the transaction header, and transaction line item entries. 

• 
Turn on table grid lines for precise tables. 

---



#### Syncing a Document Template with RealPage Accounting
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 204*

Printed Document Templates 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Syncing a Document Template with RealPage Accounting 

After you have finished inserting merge fields into your document template, you must sync the 

document with RealPage Accounting. 

You can sync a new document template or one that you downloaded to make changes. 

To sync a template with RealPage Accounting: 

1. 
Click RealPage Word Merge Add-In. 

2. 
Click the Sync to Product option to update the template in the system. 

3. 
Type the name of the template. 

4. 
In the Functional area drop-down list, select the application that the template is associated 

with. 

5. 
In the Template drop-down list, select the template type that you used when you created 

the template. 

6. 
Click Save. The system saves the template. You can now use the template from the 

application that you selected in step 4.  

You can access these templates in the Platform Services (Customization Services) 
application using the Printed document templates menu option.

Adding and Uploading a Document Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > 
 Printed Doc 
Templates`


To add a new document template record and upload the template file: 

1.

Click the

The Printed document template information page opens.

Assigning a Document Template to a Transaction or Customer 

After you have created and uploaded your document template into the system, you must assign it 

to the desired transactions or customers.  

Overrides 

Document templates assigned to transactions override any default templates. Similarly, you can 

override top-level template assignments at the entity level. However, document templates 

assigned to specific customers override all other template assignments. 

Assigning a Document Template to Accounts Receivable Invoices or Statements 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Formatting > Printed 
Document Templates`


To assign a document template to an Accounts Receivable transaction: 

1. 
On the Configure Accounts Receivable page, find the Formatting section. 

2. 
In the Printed document templates sub-section, select the desired document template from 

the Invoice or Statement drop-down list. 

3. 
Click Save.

Assigning a Document Template to a Customer 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Customers > Edit > Additional Information 
> Printed Document Templates`


You can assign document templates to specific customers for Accounts Receivable invoices or 

statements. Document templates assigned to customers override the default template and the 

assigned transaction definition template whenever the applicable transaction type is printed for 

the customer. 

To assign a document template to a customer: 

1. 
In the Customers list, locate the desired customer, and then click the Edit link next to it. 

2. 
Click the Additional information tab. 

3. 
Find the Printed document templates section, and then select the desired custom document 

template from the applicable drop-down list. Each drop-down list only displays templates 

associated with the corresponding transaction type. 

4. 
Click Save.

Testing a Document Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > A/R Invoices > Print/Email > Print`


Before you send your documents to a customer using a custom document template, we 

recommend that you preview the template first to be sure the data displays appropriately and 

that the formatting of the document is correct. 

Use a test transaction or draft transaction to test a custom document template to avoid 
setting the Printed flag. 

To preview and test a custom document template: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu. 

2. 
Select A/R Invoices. 

3. 
In the applicable transaction list, click Print/Email next to the desired transaction. 

4. 
Click the Print option, and then click OK. The system prints the transaction to a PDF file. 

Depending on your configuration, the PDF file may open in your PDF reader or you may need 
to open your browser’s Downloads folder and open the PDF file from there. 

5. 
If you need to make changes to the custom document template in Microsoft Word, then 

re-upload the template to the appropriate custom document template record and repeat 

the test. 

If something went wrong with your custom document template, use the table (on page 
209 ) to troubleshoot your document template, apply the necessary changes, then 
re-upload the template.

Overview of Importing Data into RealPage Accounting 

The two most common imports into Accounts Receivable application are customer records and 

A/R invoice records. Consult the appendices for the data structure of customer and A/R invoice 

records.  

Regardless of the type of data that you are importing, the process contains the same basic steps: 

• 
Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page (on page 218). 

• 
Filling in the template with data that matches the template types (on page 219). 

• 
Save the file in CSV format. 

• 
Import the CSV file (on page 227). 

In addition, there are some nuances between handling invoice and customer data. For these, 

please refer to the individual import sections: 

• 
Importing accounts receivable invoices 

• 
Importing and exporting customer records (on page 232) 

This section includes best practices about the processing of imports. 

• 
Best practices for preparing data for import (on page 217) 

• 
Order of CSV imports (on page 226) 

• 
Importing Offline (on page 228) 

• 
Automating Imports (on page 228) 

This section also includes information that can help you resolve problems when importing: 

• 
Resolving errors (on page 235)

##### Best Practices for Preparing Data for Import
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 217*

Chapter 10: Importing Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 323) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

Best Practices for Preparing Data for Import 

Follow these best practices to prepare your data. 

• 
Download a template from the Import data page. 

Always use the latest template, especially following a product release. 

Use the correct template for the data object that you want to import. 

• 
Use the column descriptions as a guide to enter information. 

Do not change the titles in the header row. 

The header titles correlate to fields in the system. Incorrect header titles may cause an 

upload error. When you download a template from the Import data page, the correct 

headers are in the template. 

Read the header descriptions in the template. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains the type of 

information to include in each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, or with 

an incorrect accepted value, it may cause an error in your import. 

Enter required information. 

Read the description field to determine which information is required. If you do not enter 

the required information, your import may fail. 

• 
Save the data as a comma-separated value, or CSV, file. When saving from Excel, choose the 

comma delimited file (.csv) type. 

The file has the file extension .csv after you save it. 

• 
Leave the file open until your import is successful. Excel can sometimes reformat the file if 

you close it before the import is successful. 

---



##### Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 218*

Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of RealPage 

Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
Find the type of data that you want to import.  

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

A prompt opens at the bottom of the web page, asking if you want to Open, Save, or 

Cancel. 

• 
Open: Opens the file in Excel. 

• 
Save: Saves the file to your browser’s default download folder. 

• 
Save as: Saves the file under a new name and in a different location. 

• 
Save and Open: Saves the file to your local computer, and then opens the file in Excel. 

5. 
Click Save. 

Save the template to your computer, and then continue downloading templates as needed until 

you have downloaded all of the templates for data that you want to import. 

If you have a database administrator (DBA) of your other system, give the downloaded templates 

to your DBA. Ask the DBA to: 

• 
Export the data from your other system, as specified in the import template spreadsheets. 

• 
Put the applicable data into each spreadsheet. 

• 
Save the spreadsheet as a comma-delimited file (CSV). 

If you do not have a DBA, or if your DBA does not have time to complete the whole task, you can 

complete the tasks. Refer to the following topics for guidance on creating importable data. 

---



##### Filling In an Import Template with Data
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 219*



##### Preparing Your CSV File for Import
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 219*

Chapter 10: Importing Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Filling In an Import Template with Data 

Perform the following steps for each item that you want to import: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. The information in the template 

file can help you formulate extraction queries. 

2. 
Export the data from your other source. 

3. 
Copy the exported data into the template file for the same kind of object. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file to your system.  

Preparing Your CSV File for Import 

The Import data page is a quick way to import your information into the system. However, the 

way you prepare your CSV files directly affects the success or failure of importing your data. Learn 

the CSV import process to streamline the import process. 

This topic provides general information about preparing CSV files for import. Links to information 
about specific templates can be found in the Import data into the system, which lists all import 
topics. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file. 

Most imports start with getting the most recent template from the Import data page. When you 

get your templates from this list, you get templates that have been tailored to your specific 

company, including specific dimensions. 

Next you add your data, using the correct formatting as explained in the template. After you’ve 

added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in mind. This helps 

eliminate anything that might make your import fail.

Each template contains a set of pre-defined headers, such as BUDGET_ID, ACCT_NO, and soon. You enter your data into the blank cells below the header and header description rows without changing the headers. 
It is important to read the description for each of the column headers. Some columns are 
required and if left blank will cause your import to fail. 

The following illustration shows a portion of the template after the data has been added. The 

description row has been hidden for this example. 

To add your data: 

1. 
Open the template that you downloaded from the Import data page. 

2. 
Enter your information. Use the header descriptions as a guide for how to enter information 

correctly. 

• 
Do not change the headers. 

The header titles in the header row correlate to fields in UI. Incorrect header titles will 

cause an import error. When you download a template, the correct headers are in the 

template. 

• 
Read the header descriptions. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains what type of 

information is accepted for each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, 

or with a value not accepted by the column, it will cause an error in your import. 

• 
Enter required information. 

Some data is required, while others are not. Read the description field to determine 

which information is required. If you do not enter the required information, your 

import will fail. 

3. 
After entering your data, save the file as a comma-separated value (CSV) file. When saving 

from Excel, select the comma delimited file type. The file will have the file extension .csv 

after you save it.

##### About CSV Templates
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 223*

Chapter 10: Importing Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

About CSV Templates 

There are some things you should know about the CSV templates and how they behave before 

adding your data. 

Removing All Commas from Your CSV File 

RealPage recommends removing all commas from your CSV file. 

A CSV file is a Comma Separated Values file (also sometimes known as a comma delimited file). If 

there are commas in the data of your file (for example, if your numbers are formatted like 10,000 

or if you use commas between words in a field), your data will be shifted one column over 

because that is how the file is intended to work. This will either cause errors in the information or 

cause the whole import to fail. 

RealPage recommends you do not keep your actual data in a CSV file. Instead, use an Excel 
workbook to take advantage of the formatting options of Excel. When you’re ready, export your 
data as a CSV file for import into RealPage Accounting. In this way, your data is formatted 
correctly for import, but you also have Excel functionality in your workbook. 

Column Order 

You can change the order of the columns as you see fit, as long as the information in the header 

cell doesn’t change. 

Do not rename or otherwise change the headers in your templates. If you change the headers, 
your import will fail. 

However, some templates require information to be imported in a specific order. For example, 

transaction data should not be imported before information about the transactions has been 

imported. Header columns containing information about the entire import need to stay to the left 

of detail columns (columns that contain the details of an account, transaction, vendor, etc.). 

RealPage recommends reviewing the column order of the original template before moving 

columns around. 

Adding Additional Columns 

If you need to keep other related information in your template document, you can add your own 

columns for this information. If you add your own columns, use a # (hashtag) symbol before the 

name of any column you add. Examples: 

#BudgetNotes 

#ClientInfo 

If by chance you use a name already in use by the system, the # (hashtag) will make sure that the 

information in your columns is not imported by accident. 

---


<!-- Page 224 -->
Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

You can also use the # (hashtag) to write notes to yourself in your template. If you place the # 

(hashtag) at the start of a row, the whole row of information is ignored during import. 

You can create rows of notes by starting the row with # in the first column. 

Hiding Columns for Easy Data Entry 

When editing your file in Excel, you can hide columns you won’t be using for data entry. 

Be sure to enter required information in your file. Hiding required columns and not entering 
required information will cause your import to fail. 

Data Must Conform to the Business Logic of RealPage 

For example, the Budget ID field on the Budget Information page allows a 20-character ID to be 

entered. It follows then that the Budget import template would have the same limitation: if you 

try to import a Budget ID with more than 20 characters in your CSV file, your import fails. 

How data should be formatted is found in the header description row, under the header row. 

You can also see a field-by-field description for your specific template in this help. 

Go to Importing Data, find the template you want to know more about, and click the 

corresponding link. 

Blank Fields Overwrite Existing Data 

A blank value in a cell is considered to be the desired value (a blank) for the field referenced by 

the column heading for the record being imported. 

In almost all cases, a blank field will overwrite existing data in RealPage to also be blank. 

Say you had the existing value 111 Elm St. as the address for a customer and you import a blank 

for this field. If you go to the normal user interface and examine the contents of that field, you will 

see that the original value 111 Elm St. is replaced by nothing, and the field is blank. 

This is not true, however, for these templates: 

• 
Update Vendor 1099 Transactions 

• 
Update Vendor 1099 Opening Balances 

If the value is blank in certain fields, the import does not overwrite the existing value. To remove 

the existing value in these few cases, enter the value NULL. These cases are clearly identified in 

their header descriptions. 

Budgets are an exception. Budgets can be appended with new dates, with new lines not 
previously budgeted, or they can be overwritten if same date/account combinations are used. 

---


<!-- Page 225 -->
Chapter 10: Importing Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Calculated Field Values 

If you used a formula to come to a value in a field, you can leave the result in place as long as you 

match the RealPage field value for decimals. 

Accounting Application Page Help 

In most cases, there is an exact match between the application pages (and the business logic with 

which they behave) and the data that you import. This includes the constraints on that data and 

any dependencies that may exist between the data in the import file and other data in the system, 

or other data that you also import. 

After you have added all of your data, you save the Excel spreadsheet as a CSV file. 

Debits and Credits Must Balance 

When importing a file that includes debits and credits, your debits and credits must balance. 

RealPage adheres to accepted accounting rules, which require debits and credits to balance. 

Likewise, if you require accounts to balance by location, then when you import location balances 

using a CSV template, the location debits and credits must also balance. 

Duplicating Records 

If an identical record already exists in the system, the import for that record typically fails because 

RealPage detects that the record exists and does not allow duplicates. 

Duplicates are not allowed in account numbers, departments, locations, employees, customers, 

and vendors. Although you can have duplicate transactions, the transaction summary name must 

be unique per application. 

Journal entries are an exception. The system does not check for duplicate journal entries, so 
when importing journal entries, be sure to check that they have a unique ID or name.

Line Numbers 

See the Line number examples page for more information on how to use lines numbers in your 

CSV imports. 

Special Characters 

UTF-8 is supported in imported files, so character accents and other special characters are 

imported correctly. 

RealPage recommends that you remove commas from all numbers and do not use commas in any 

text fields. 

CSV Data Exported from Non-Excel Software 

When exporting data from other applications, the other software might use a non-standard 

approach to quoting, which could cause problems when importing into the system. 

---



##### Order of CSV Imports
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 226*

Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

As noted above, RealPage recommends removing all commas from text fields in a CSV file. 

However, there could be times in which removing the commas is not the ideal solution. In this 

case, CSV files do allow quotes around a value that contains a comma, and the system accepts 

this in an import. For example: 

1,2,3, “All, with exceptions” 

There may also be instances when you need to include a quote mark inside a statement with a 

comma. In this case, you would use a second set of quote marks, as follows: 

1,2,3, “All, with “inventory” exceptions” 

Order of CSV Imports 

In some cases, CSV imports must be performed in a specific order because of dependencies 

within the data. For example, if you have transactions that require locations, but you have not 

entered or imported the locations, the transaction import fails. 

It is always best to follow the order of the steps as they are presented in the Import data page 

when performing any type of import. Not all of the steps are required. For example, you may not 

use territories anywhere in your accounting data, therefore creating them is optional. 

In a few cases there are circular references. For example, an employee record can reference a 

department and vice versa. Problems that would otherwise result from such circular references 

have been eliminated for the purposes of importing by removing certain items. If you absolutely 

must have this data, you need to enter it manually.

Importing a CSV File 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file into the system. 

To import your CSV file: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
Find the information type you want to import, and then click the corresponding Import link. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you want to import. 

5. 
If the CSV file includes dates that are not in mm/dd/yyyy format, select the date format that 

the data uses in the Date format field. 

The system attempts to import your file using the selected date format. If the system can’t 

import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to discover the date format used 

in your file and import the data using that date format. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

7. 
If your import box includes a Post to section, select one of the following: 

• 
Select Historical if your data is not active. 

• 
Select General Ledger to post imported invoices to the G/L. 

8. 
If the file that you’re importing is large, consider selecting the Process offline option to 

process the import offline. This will cause the import to run at a later time, when the system 

is less busy. If you prefer to import the data immediately and wait for the results, do not 

select the Process offline check box. 

9. 
Type the email address to which import results and errors should be sent in the Email 

results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses, separated by a 

semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

RealPage highly recommends entering an email address. 

10. 
Click the Import button. After an import, the system informs you if the import was 

successful and how many records were imported. 

In a completely successful import, the confirmation page lets you verify that all of the 

records in your original file were successfully imported without having to manually verify 

them.

Importing Offline 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much processing the 

system must do to the data. If you are in doubt, select the Process offline option on the import 

utility page. 

When the offline process is complete, the system sends an email to the address you entered in 

the Import Company Information box (where you imported your file). 

RealPage recommends selecting Process offline when importing CSV files and providing your 
email address. If your import fails, you will always be notified, and the failed records are sent to 
your email.

Workato.

You can quickly update information for multiple customers at once by exporting customer data in 

CSV for Import format, editing the resulting spreadsheet, and then importing your changes.  

A CSV import works well for:  

• 
Updating information for multiple customers at once: Using a CSV import, you can update 

selected data for multiple customers. For example, you can export the Customers list with 

the Email Address field included, add or modify the email addresses in a spreadsheet 

application, and then import your changes.  

• 
Adding new customers to your existing Customers list: Using a CSV import, you quickly add 

new customers without having to create the customers one at a time. Any spreadsheet row 

that contains a unique  

Don’t overwrite existing data with blank data unless you intend to remove that data from 
your Customers list. For example, if you export the Email Address field and then clear the 
data in the Email Address column of your spreadsheet, existing customer email addresses 
will be deleted when you import the file.  

Using the import and export features on the Customers list, you can: 

• 
Export your Customers list in one of several standard formats (CSV, Excel, Word, PDF) so 

that you can print or use the information in another application. 

• 
Quickly update your Customers list by exporting selected data, making changes, and then 

importing your changes. 

Importing Customers 

You can import new customer information at the top level by uploading a CSV file. Follow these 

steps to import new customer information from an external source.

Filling In the Customer Template with Data 

You can update information for existing customers. For example, you might correct customer 

addresses or add email addresses for selected customers. You can also add new customers. If the 

Customer ID that you specify doesn’t already exist in the system, a new customer record will be 

created. 

You can include sets of fields for a Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact. The template contains fields for 

this information, but it is not required. 

The Bill-to contact fields have a B_ prefix and the Ship-to contact fields have an S_ prefix. 

If the Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact fields are not included, the primary contact information is 

used for the customer. This means that the COMPANY_NAME field, when used for the Bill-to 

contact, would be B_COMPANY_NAME, and the shipping contact would be S_COMPANY_NAME. 

To fill the customer template: 

1. 
Open the file in Excel.  

2. 
Fill the required columns in the customer template: 

• 
CUSTOMER_ID: Type a unique identifier for the customer. If customer sequence 

auto-numbering is enabled, the system completes the Customer ID if you do not 

supply one. (Company > Services: Subscriptions: A/R Preferences). 

• 
CUST_NAME: Type the name of the customer. 

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type the primary contact name. If the contact name already exists, 

you must create the customer manually in the system, or enter a new contact name in 

this file. 

• 
PRINTAS: Type the name of the company as you want it to appear on payments and 

notices. This field is used with the Customer ID field to create the suggested contact 

name, which is the unique contact ID used throughout the system that can’t be edited 

after creation. This is also the name that appears in all lists and drop-down lists.

Importing Order of Precedence 

When importing customer records, child records must be imported after parent records. Child 

records that incorrectly reference a parent record can cause your import to fail. For example, if the 

parent record does not exist, or if the parent record references a child record as if it were a parent, 

your import can fail. 

If you include an ACCT_LABEL, the system creates an account label on-the-fly when you import 

your file. 

This means you can’t re-use the same ACCT_LABEL for another customer. 

If you include an ACCT_LABEL, you must also include: 

• 
a GL_ACCTNO that conforms to a primary/sub account specification in Company > 

Setup: Company Info. 

• 
the GL_ACCTNO must point to valid account. 

• 
DELIVERYOPTIONS can be set to online, only if the company subscribes to online 

delivery. 

Customer lists have optional sets of Contact fields for the Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact. The fields 

are identical to the required set of primary contact fields; except they have B- and S- prefixes. If 

either the Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact fields are not included, the primary contact information is 

used instead. 

The Don’t Include On Company’s Contact List and G/L Group fields found in the Customer 

Information page are not represented in the template.

##### Import Error Notification

Import Error Notification 

There are a number of reasons imported records fail, such as duplicated entries or invalid field 

content. RealPage provides information about the failed records in an attempt to help you fix the 

import error. 

Finding the Error Message 

The Import confirmation page indicates how many records failed. This page also contains a link 

to download a CSV file, which contains only the failed records. 

Records that are successfully imported are not returned in the CSV file. 

Click the link and download the CSV file. 

If you entered your email address into the Import Company Information box, an email is sent 

that contains the error messages for your attempted import. The email lists the error code, and 

then each unique instance of that error in the file you attempted to import. 

The error message email is sent to the email address associated with the user ID logged in at the 

time of the file upload; otherwise, the email address for the company contact is used. 

The import pages also allow another email address to be explicitly entered in the Email results to 

this address field. 

If you did not enter your email in the Import Company Information box, and you do not click the 
link in the Import confirmation page, there is no way to retrieve the CSV error report file for the 
import you just did. 

Best practice: Enter your email in the Import Company Information box at the beginning of every 
import. 

The reason you are sent a separate email with the error messages is because a record could fail 

for more than one reason. Displaying all of the text for each record in the CSV file could become 

quite cumbersome and hard to read. Furthermore, it is often the case that thousands of records 

are uploaded. If thousands of errors fail, the CSV file could become quite bloated. 

Read the Error Message Email 

The error messages for your failed upload file can be challenging to read. RealPage recommends 

the following strategy: 

• 
Start at the top of the email and look at each error message section. 

---

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

• 
In each section, start reading from the bottom up. The error at the bottom of the section is 

the first error encountered during import. 

a) Start here. 

b) Read from the bottom up. 

c) In each section, the specific error is listed at the top.
