Start at the Top of the Email 

Error messages are presented in sections, and the sections are listed in the order that the errors 

are encountered in your file. 

Example: 

=================================================== 
Error BL01001973 
=================================================== 
BL01001973-1 Description: Duplicate account number.  
The account number ‘4150’ already exists. 
BL01001973-1 Correction: Enter unique account number. 
BL01001973-2 Description: Unable to create record Could not create  
GL Account record! 
=================================================== 

When you read the error messages such as the one above, start with the error number. 

The error codes, such as BL01001973 above, are internal codes. These internal codes can help 
RealPage locate the source of a systemic issue if one is identified. 

=================================================== 
Error BL03000019 
=================================================== 
BL03000019-1 Description: Invalid contact data entered. 
TRANSACTION TYPE is a required field and cannot be empty 
BL03000019-1 Correction: Some of the fields you have entered 
are invalid. Please correct them with proper values. 
=================================================== 

Read from the Bottom of the Error Message Up 

In the example, the error code is BL01001973-2. 

Description: Unable to create record Could not create G/L Account record! first. 

This identifies the first error that occurred during import. It’s not informative, however, so look at 

the next error message for more information. 

The next error message in the list (as read from the bottom up), BL01001973-1 Correction: 

Enter unique account number, identifies the reason the G/L account record couldn’t be 

created, but it’s not yet clear what to do to fix the problem. 

The final error message in the example above (as read from the bottom up) describes more fully 

the cause of the error and suggests a fix: find and delete the duplicate account number.

##### Handling Import Errors
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 242*

Importing Data 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide

Handling Import Errors 

If you experience import errors, review the tips in About CSV Templates (on page 223) and review 

the common errors (on page 239).  

Import errors occur when you try to import information that does not match the requirements of 

the template. Each template has a set of required information that you must enter to successfully 

import the file, and formats to follow for certain kinds of information. Read the descriptions in the 

template to determine the most accurate way to enter your data.  

If individual transactions are in error, the rows in the transaction that are in error are saved in a 

CSV file for you along with an error code for each row. The system sends an email with 

information about specific errors (on page 236).

Fill In the Defaults Section 

1. 
In the Payment method drop-down list, select the default payment method. The list 

includes all payment methods that your company has enabled.  

• 
Cash 

• 
Record transfer 

• 
Check 

•

2.

•

•

which you deposit payments. 

3.

Adding an A/R Term 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > 
 Terms`


A/R terms can either be accessible to all entities or exclusive to a specific entity. We recommend 

that you create customer terms at the top level to be shared across all entities. Creating terms in 

an entity restricts them to that entity. If you do create terms in an entity, then use a naming 

convention that differentiates them at the top level. 

To add an A/R term: 

1. 
Type a Name for the term (for example, 2% 10 Net 30). The system displays the name on 

invoice and customer pages. 

2. 
In the Description field, type a note about the purpose and use of this term (for example, 

2% discount if paid 10 days from invoice, due on day 30). 

3. 
Set Status to Active. To change the status of an object to hide unused items, select Inactive. 

When an item is set to Inactive, the system retains the data but hides the inactive item on 

lists, drop-down lists, and so on. Examples of data you might want to hide or make inactive 

are employees who are no longer with your company or bank accounts you no longer use. If 

you want to permanently remove an item, you must delete it. 

Filling In the Due Section 

The Due date is a combination of the day(s) and what the day(s) references: 

1. 
To set terms that reference the number of days from the invoice date, such as Net 30, type 

the number of days in Day, and select from invoice/bill date from the drop-down list. 

---


<!-- Page 246 -->
A/R and Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

2. 
To set a day on a month referenced from the invoice date, type the day of the month in 

Day, and select a month setting from the adjacent drop-down list. For instance, to set terms 

for the 15th of the month after the invoice date, type 15 in Day, and select of next month 

from invoice/bill date in the drop-down list. 

Filling In the Discount Section 

The Discount is a combination of the day(s), what the day(s) references, the dollar or percent 

discount, and the number of grace days. In addition, you can set how the system calculates 

discounts for transactions using this term. 

To set a discount that references the number of days from the invoice date, such as 2%-10: 

1. 
Type the number of days in Day. 

2. 
Select from invoice date from the drop-down list. 

3. 
Type the discount amount in Amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days before the discount is withdrawn. 

To set a discount based on a day on a month referenced from the invoice date: 

1. 
In Day, type the day of the month. 

2. 
Select a month setting from the drop-down list. 

3. 
Type the discount amount in Amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days before the discount is withdrawn. 

To set a discount based on a day on a month referenced from the invoice date: 

1. 
In the Day field, type the day of the month. 

2. 
Select a month setting from the drop-down list. 

3. 
Type the discount amount in Amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days before the discount is withdrawn. 

You can set how the system calculates discounts in transactions that use this term. You can 

calculate the discount based solely on: 

• 
The Line-items total, excluding added charges (such as taxes and shipping). 

• 
The Invoice total, including all charges.

In Configure Accounts Receivable, you can set up your company to automatically apply 
discounts when you record a payment receipt. 

Filling In the Penalty Section 

To set a penalty for paying after the due date, in the Penalty section set the following: 

1. 
In the Cycle field, set cycle to the time span in which the penalty accrues, such as Weekly, 

Biweekly, Monthly, and so on. 

2. 
In the Amount field, type the penalty amount. 

3. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

4. 
In the Grace days field, enter the number of days after the due date that the penalty will 

take effect. For example, you can use the grace period to compensate for the delay caused 

when a check is mailed within the penalty period, but is delayed in the mail. 

Penalties are not automatically applied. To apply a penalty, you must explicitly do so by 
pointing to Accounts Receivable > Apply Penalties. 

Adding Account Labels 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > 
 Account Labels`


When you add an account label, you are creating a name and mapping it to a General Ledger 

account number. Account labels appear in the Account labels drop-down lists throughout the 

system. 

To add an account label: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select 
 Add next to Account Labels. The A/R/PM account labels page opens. 

4. 
In the Account label drop-down list, type a unique name for the new account label. 

5. 
In the Description field, type a description including the purpose and use of the label. 

Account labels play an important role in the system. 

You must use a descriptive name: 

• 
Account labels must be unique. 

• 
Account labels are case-sensitive. The system will see a match when searching for text 

only if the text matches it exactly, including the use of upper and lower case. 

Be aware that this can lead to the creation of duplicate account label names if the name has 

the same text, but the account label has upper/lower case differences.

Segments Overview 

Segments are custom classifications that help you organize, sort, and report on your company 

information in meaningful ways. Think of a segment as a tag with a set of values that you can 

associate with transactions and G/L entries. For example, you might add a custom segment to 

report on your expense types, employees, or special projects. 

When you enter a new transaction, you can assign a segment to that transaction and then tag it 

with one or more segment values. Segmenting transactions is optional; however, it can be useful 

for identifying transactions and analyzing data in your reports. 

You can define up to 15 segments for your company. An additional segment, called 

Intercompany segment, is available by default. Because it’s a system segment, it cannot be 

modified. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage segments. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Segments 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 323) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

Enable Segments 

Enable the segments (on page 252) function in the General Ledger application. 

Enabling Segments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Configuration > Enable Segments`


To enable segments: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the Configuration option. The General Ledger setup page opens. 

3. 
In the Advanced G/L options section, select the Enable segments check box. 

4. 
Click the Save button.

##### Configuring A/R Functionality
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 253*

Chapter 12: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Configuring A/R Functionality 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality`


Use the Enable functionality section to enable or disable Accounts Receivable features. 

This topic describes how to: 

• 
Enable allocation in invoice entry. 

• 
Enable users to allocate charges to different accounts on a single line item of an invoice. 

• 
Turn off automatic payment suggestions. 

• 
Enable creating, editing, and deleting foreign currency invoices. 

• 
Enforce the rule that payment dates must be greater than their invoice dates. 

• 
Display tax and subtotals for invoices. 

• 
Enable inter-company bill back. 

To enable Accounts Receivable functions: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration option. 

4. 
Find the Enable functionality section. 

5. 
Select the Enable accounts receivable G/L account override in invoice and adjustment 

entry check box when you want to override the default G/L account as you create a 

transaction. 

To make use of this option, you also need to: 

• 
Configure one or more G/L accounts as override accounts. 

• 
Provide permissions for selected users to override the default G/L account in invoice 

and adjustment transaction, as well as for any invoice or adjustment transactions 

involving specific customers, as needed. 

To tag an account, go to General Ledger, select the account, and designate it as either a 

Payables account or a Receivables account as appropriate. The system adds the account to 

the filtered list of override accounts that you can select from in specific pages, such as 

transaction pages and vendor and customer pages. 

Payables account: the system adds the account to the filtered list of A/P G/L accounts 

available as override accounts on A/P invoice, adjustment, and vendor pages. 

Receivables account: the system adds the account to the filtered list of A/R G/L accounts 

available as override accounts on A/R invoice, adjustment, and customer pages. 

You can enable override of the default A/R G/L account for: 

---


<!-- Page 254 -->
Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
An entire invoice or adjustment 

• 
One or more specific line-items in an invoice or adjustment 

• 
All transactions involving a specific customer 

6. 
Select the Enable account labels check box to provide restricted access to G/L accounts and 

a means of textually naming them.  

This setting determines whether Account labels will be required or not (On or Off). Account 

labels are a good way to restrict access to G/L accounts. If an Account label is not set up for 

a particular G/L account, that account can’t be accessed. Also, Account labels provide a 

plain-English equivalent for G/L account numbers, which can be helpful for users. When 

enabled, you can: 

• 
Associate an account number with an intuitive name that is easy to recognize and 

select from a drop-down list. 

• 
Create subtotal lines in invoices, such as for sales tax.  

• 
Categorize different products/expenses/services. 

• 
Restrict access to only those G/L accounts that do have labels. 

After you enable account labels, two additional options appear in this section: 

Display tax and subtotals fields for invoices: Select this option if you’re going to create an 
account label for use in tax subtotals. (US taxes only) 

Enable Advanced Tax schedules: This option is not supported. 

7. 
Select the Enable allocation in invoice entry check box to allow users to allocate charges to 

different accounts on a single line item of an invoice. 

This option can only be enabled here if you
’ve enabled it in G/L configuration. 

8.

Configuring A/R Accounting Settings 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Account Settings`


Use the Accounting settings section to define the default journals, accounts, and summary 

frequencies. 

• 
Journal: Records invoices, adjustments, and payment receipt transactions. 

• 
G/L accounts: Posts transactions, such as accounts receivable, penalties, and more. 

• 
Summary frequencies: Determines how often the system posts invoices, adjustments, 

manual deposits, and payment summaries to the G/L. 

• 
Open item/Balance forward: Sets the customer accounts to Open item (most common) or 

Balance forward. 

The selections in this section vary based on the accounting method selected in General 
Ledger. When you change the accounting method from cash or accrual to cash and accrual, 
the system automatically creates some journals that are related to the new accounting 
method. Changing your accounting method requires additional setup changes. For 
information, see Accounting methods—accrual, cash, or both. 

Be sure to contact your RealPage account manager. 

Filling In the Accounting Settings Section 

Select the default journals to use for the A/R subledger. The system uses these journals for 

automatically recording the following accounts receivable transactions: 

1. 
In the Payments drop-down list, select the journal to use for payment receipt transactions. 

2. 
In the Accrual basis reporting subsection, in the A/R invoices drop-down list, select the 

journal to use for A/R invoices.

to use for A/R invoices. 

5. 
In the Adjustments drop-down list, select the journal to use for cash adjustments. 

Filling In the G/L Accounts Subsection 

In the G/L Accounts subsection, select the General Ledger accounts to use for posting the 

following accounts receivable transaction types: 

1. 
In the Account receivable drop-down list, select the account to use for receivables. 

In general, you configure G/L accounts at the top level. One exception is that you specify 
different default A/R accounts for each entity at the entity level. For more information, 
see Specifying different default accounts by property in the online help system.

This setting can be changed on a per-transaction basis.

Configuring A/R Document Sequencing 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Document Sequencing`


In the RealPage Financial Suite, document sequences refer to the system’s automatic numbering 

feature used to assign unique identifiers to new records. This helps ensure consistency and avoids 

duplication. 

Automatic numbering, also known as document sequencing, is available only in select features in 

RealPage Accounting. These features use pre-defined numbering plans to assign sequential 

identifiers—typically when creating new records or transactions. 

If you prefer to number a transaction type manually, do not assign a document sequence for the 

transaction type. 

Before You Begin 

You must create a new document numbering scheme before you see it as an option in this 

section. 

• 
Configure a document sequence for the desired record type in Company > All > Settings > 

Document Numbering. 

Setting Up Document Sequencing for A/R Transactions and Records 

Use the Document sequencing section to: 

• 
Set warnings. If you choose to enter any of the transaction IDs manually, you can set a 

warning whenever someone enters a duplicate ID. 

• 
Assign a document sequence for these select transactions and records: 

• 
A/R invoices 

• 
Recurring A/R invoices 

• 
A/R debit adjustments 

• 
A/R credit adjustments 

• 
Customer records 

• 
Require IDs on select types of transactions and records. 

• 
Invoices 

• 
Adjustments 

• 
Quick invoice entry 

• 
Recurring invoices 

• 
Manual deposits 

After a document sequence is configured and assigned, the system automatically assigns a 

sequential ID to each new transaction or record, ensuring a smooth and consistent flow of unique 

identifiers. 

---

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration option. The Configure Accounts Receivable page opens. 

4. 
Find the Document sequencing section. 

5. 
For each of the following, set the number sequence that you want the system to use for 

each new transaction. 

• 
A/R Invoices* 

• 
Recurring A/R invoices 

• 
A/R debit adjustments 

• 
A/R credit adjustments 

• 
Customers 

* In the case of invoices, using automatic numbered sequences is optional. 

6. 
In the If invoices or adjustments are assigned duplicate numbers section, select how you want 

the system to handle duplicate numbers. This setting applies to invoices and adjustments 

for the selected customer. 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message that the transaction 

number for this customer is a duplicate. The transaction can’t be created. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without any alert or action on 

the part of the system. 

7.

use document sequencing on.

A/R Invoices, adjustments, quick A/R invoice entry, and recurring A/R invoices only

Manual deposits

Overriding the G/L Account in A/R Transactions 

The configuration to override the G/L account for Accounts Receivable transactions takes place in 

the Accounts Receivable and General Ledger applications.  

You can override a default A/R G/L account for an invoice or adjustment. Specifically, you can 

override the default G/L account in these situations: 

• 
Override for an entire transaction 

• 
Override at the line-item level 

• 
Override for all transactions involving a specific tenant 

Currently, this feature applies to invoices and adjustments only. It doesn’t apply to recurring 
invoices, manual deposits, quick invoice entry, or advances. 

Defining Transaction Allocations 

To use transaction allocations, you must first enable the feature in the desired application, then 

create an allocation template that determines how to allocate the amount. After completing this 

configuration, you can apply the allocation to a transaction’s line item. 

Enabling the Transaction Allocation Feature 

You can use transaction allocations in Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and the General 

Ledger. Before you can use transaction allocations in any application, you must enable the 

transaction allocation feature in each application’s Configuration page. Enable transaction 

allocations in the Configuration area in the application where you need to use them. This example 

shows where to enable transaction allocation in the Accounts Payable application. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality > Enable Allocation in`


Invoice Entry 

Creating the Allocation Template 

You create a template that defines how you want to allocate the transaction, and then apply the 

allocation template to the desired transaction.

##### Configuring Intercompany Bill Backs
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 263*

Chapter 12: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

For example, you can create a transaction allocation template so that it allocates the cost of a 

single line item across multiple locations. Whenever you want to apply this allocation to a line 

item, you select the allocation in a transaction’s line item row. 

Applying the Allocation 

When you enter an A/R invoice, A/P invoice, or journal entry and apply a transaction allocation to 

any line, the system automatically splits the amount based on the transaction allocation template.  

For example, if a company distributes an expense such as janitorial services across five business 

units, the transaction allocation can be set up to reflect the percentages of occupancy per 

business unit. When you apply this transaction allocation to a line item, the system will 

automatically divide the amount across the business units according to the percentages saved in 

the transaction allocation template. 

To see how a transaction allocation is divided in a transaction, open the A/P invoice, A/R invoice, 

or journal entry, and then click the line in the Entries section, and then click Show details. The 

allocation is displayed in the Allocation Splits section of the Details page. You can further 

customize the allocation  

Configuring Intercompany Bill Backs 

Inter-company bill back makes it easy for an entity to bill a second entity. Some configuration is 

required in order to make this feature work. During setup, you create a customer and vendor 

record for each entity and then associate the records with the entity. The bill back feature uses the 

customer and vendor records as proxies for the billing process.  

Configuration Workflow 

1. 
Enable the inter-company bill back feature. 

2. 
Grant bill back template permissions. 

3. 
Create inter-entity receivable and inter-entity payable accounts to use for inter-entity 

transactions if they don’t already exist. 

4. 
Create one vendor record and one customer record for each entity that you want to be able 

to use with the bill back feature. 

5. 
Associate the vendor record and customer record to its entity. 

6. 
Create bill back templates.

#### Territories

Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide

Territories 


> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Territories`



> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Cash Management > All > Territories`


Territories are optionally included in Customer records and are used with Accounts receivable 

reports. They can be useful for filtering and categorizing data, assuming your company has 

multiple territories.  

Territories are similar to dimensions but aren’t actual dimensions, so they work differently than 

dimensions. They can be used with dimensions.  

Multi-entity companies 

For top-level multi-entity companies that use multiple base currencies, you must assign the 

territory to a specific entity, so the system knows which base currency to use for that territory. 

Entities are territories and–under certain circumstances–entities appear in lists. For example, you 

have the option to choose the entity as the parent territory and thus it appears in that list of 

locations.

#### List of Standard Accounts Receivable Reports

Reports

List of Standard Accounts Receivable Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Reports`


The Accounts receivable application contains a number of standard reports that have been 

created for you. These reports involve amounts owed or paid by customers for goods and 

services. You can run, view, process, memorize, export, and customize A/R reports. Refer to Using 

Reports for information on creating, storing, and reusing reports. 

Customer Reports 

The Customer reports appear in the Accounts Receivable application’s menu in the Reports 

section, in the Customers group. 

• 
Customer aging report  

This report provides a snapshot of outstanding charges based on account label, G/L 

Account, or other selected parameters. It lists the customers who owe you money and either 

how many days it took them to pay you, or how many days past due their payments are. 

Use this report to determine how well you are collecting on your accounts receivable. This 

report is also available as a chart. 

• 
Customer listing report  

This report is a list of customers that includes details such as location and contact 

information, pricing details, payment methods, term, tax ID, and current customer balances.  

Registers and Reports 

These reports appear in the Accounts receivable application’s menu under the Reports column, 

in the Registers & Reports section. 

• 
A/R Ledger report 

The A/R Ledger report is a list of detailed customer accounts. Use this report to see if the 

balance in the A/R ledger agrees with that in the general ledger, and to see which 

customers have balances greater than zero. Details include the beginning balance for the 

selected period, current account balance, and the charges and payments for each customer. 

• 
Sales Register report 

The Sales Register report displays the invoices you sent to customers, account adjustments, 

payment details, and credit details. Each transaction includes the date, customer ID and 

name, invoice or adjustment number, due date, description (if any), amount, and amount 

paid. 

• 
Recurring Transaction Status report 

---

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

This report presents information on the status of scheduled, completed, and failed 

transactions. The report includes transactions generated from the Accounts receivable and 

Accounts payable applications. 

• 
Recurring Transaction Forecast report 

This report provides insight into future billings based on recurring transaction schedules set 

up in the system. With this report, you can expand the number of forecasting periods, as 

well as select a forecasting frequency (monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, annually). 

Multi-currency enabled companies can choose to forecast on base currency or transaction 

currency. 

• 
Receipts Register report 

This report lists receipts from the customers that you select. Use this report to review all of 

the receipts that have been applied to invoice transactions.  

• 
Sales Tax report 

This report summarizes the taxes and labels them “Total Other Taxes.” 

• 
Deferred Revenue Forecast report 

This report illustrates how deferred income is recognized as revenue over time. Use this 

report to forecast revenue by time period, account, customer, and more. 

• 
Deferred Revenue Details report 

This report shows the details of customers and transactions for which you have deferred 

revenue. This report includes the transaction amount, transaction date, deferred amount, 

recognized amount, and amount paid. Use this report to see the transaction detail behind 

those deferred numbers and to tie back to the deferred balance on your G/L (like an audit 

report). 

• 
Deferred Revenue Revaluation report 

This report shows the adjustment of deferred revenue to reflect the business’s expected 

ability to fulfill the service obligations and generate revenue from prepaid amounts. 

Multicurrency must be enabled to access this report. 

• 
Intercompany Billing report 

This report lists the billing transactions between two entities. This report requires that you 

have configured the intercompany billing feature. Learn more about Configuring 

Intercompany Billing (on page 24). 

• 
A/R Invoices Analysis report 

This report helps you analyze your sales from the perspective of revenue line items in the 

invoices. Use this report to review your invoices. This report is also available as a chart. See 

Invoices Analysis chart.

##### Limiting Members in Dimension Structures
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 282*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide

About Dimensions 

A dimension is a category of data that you can organize and sort in meaningful ways. RealPage 

Accounting provides the following pre-defined dimensions: 

• 
Customer 

• 
Department 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Vendor 

In addition, RealPage Accounting enables you to define new dimensions to suit your needs. These 

user-defined dimensions enable you to organize and sort categories of data unique to your 

business. For example, if you are a software company with various product lines, you might create 

a user-defined dimension called Line of business. The values you could add are Direct customers, 

Channel partner, and OEM. 

Dimensions enable you to collect, sort, analyze, and report on data within one category, or 

between categories, so you can identify key factors such as: 

• 
Your most profitable or most costly customers. 

• 
The return on investment of a location or department. 

• 
Whether and to what degree a new product or product line is successful. 

• 
Which way a particular aspect of your business is trending. 

RealPage Accounting dimensions give you fine control over data definition and data hierarchy. 

With dimensions, you can customize financial reports around specific business activities, get 

greater visibility into how the business is doing, and make faster, more meaningful business 

decisions. 

Additional fees may apply for user-defined dimensions. Contact your RealPage account 

representative for more information. 

Limiting Members in Dimension Structures 

You can limit the output of a financial report to show only the top or bottom of a particular set of 

dimension data. For example, you can include only the top five customers by revenue. 

To include a top or bottom match on a financial report, you must create a dimension structure 

that contains the set of members from which you want to choose the top or bottom. On the 

checked report, you need to change the detail level for the dimension structure to show only the 

top or bottom matches based on a metric of your choice.

#### Attachments Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 286*

Attachments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Attachments Overview 

Attachments are bundles of one or more files that you associate with a transaction or record, such 

as a letter of credit, an invoice, or a photo. For example, if you have a contract signed by a 

customer, you can attach the contract to the customer record. You can attach as many files or 

combinations of file types as you need and bundle them into a single attachment record. 

To attach a document, you first need to create an electronic version of it. If it is a paper copy, scan 

the document, and then save it as one of the supported file types:  

• 
Word 

• 
PDF 

• 
Excel 

• 
Text 

• 
JPG 

• 
PNG 

Attaching Files to Transaction Records 

The Enable single scan upload setting in your user preferences changes the way that the system 

treats attachments. These differences are described below: 

When scanning is disabled: 

• 
You can select one attachment record to associate with a transaction, but the attachment 

record can contain multiple files as needed. 

• 
You can create folders for storing attachments from the transaction record. 

• 
You can access the attachment folders from the transaction record. 

When scanning is enabled: 

• 
You can add multiple attachments to a transaction record. 

• 
You can scan a document to attach it directly to the transaction record. 

• 
You cannot create or access attachment folders. 

For instructions on enabling the Enable single scan upload option, see Enabling the Scanning 

Feature.

##### Adding an Attachment to the System
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 288*

Attachments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide

Adding an Attachment to the System 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Storage > 
 Attachments`


You can create an attachment record in the Attachments list to upload one or more files into a 

single attachment and store it in RealPage Accounting. Any attachment records you create will be 

available in Attachment drop-down lists throughout RealPage Accounting; for example, when you 

are entering a new transaction or record and you want to attach supporting documents. 

To add an attachment, you need at least one attachment folder in which to store the attachment. 

Your company may have created an initial folder for you. If no folder currently exists, you can 

quickly create one while you are adding an attachment.  

To add a new attachment record in the system: 

1. 
In the Attachments list, click the Add button. 

The Select attachments page opens. 

2. 
Type a unique ID for the attachment record. If your company is configured to auto-number, 

then the system automatically displays an ID for the attachment. 

3. 
Type a Name that identifies your attachment. If you leave this field blank, the system 

automatically adds a Name for the attachment based on the first file that you upload. You 

can change this name as needed. 

Since an attachment record may contain more than one file, choose a name that describes 

all of the files in your attachment. For example, if you attached 20 scanned invoices to 

support 20 invoices, then you could name the attachment “Invoice Scans - 20 Files.” 

4. 
Select the Folder where you want to store your attachment in the system. If you have the 

appropriate Attachment permissions, you can create a folder:  

• 
Click the down arrow beside the Folder field, and then click Add. 

• 
Type a Name for the folder. 

5. 
Optionally, type a Description of the attachment. 

6. 
In the Attach files section: 

• 
Click the Choose files button, select the file(s) you want to attach, and then click the 

Open button. Alternatively, you can drag and drop files directly from your file explorer 

into the browser window. 

• 
If you have Commercial Property Management or Condo and Co-Op, and you 

purchased the portal add-on, then the Display on portal check box also appears. 

Select the check box for any attachment that you want the tenant or owner to be able 

to access on their portal. 

7. 
Attach additional files as needed.

 Delete icon next to the attachment file.

Deleting or Removing an Attachment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Storage > Attachments > Edit`


If you accidentally added the wrong attachment to a record, you can remove it from the system. 

Although you can delete some attachments from the Attachments list, you cannot delete an 

attachment that is currently attached to a record. Instead, go to the original record and delete the 

attachment there. 

Deleting an Attachment from the Attachments List 

To delete an attachment from the Attachments list: 

1. 
Select the Delete check box next to one or more attachment records. 

2. 
Click the Delete button. 

A confirmation box opens. 

3. 
Click OK to proceed. 

You cannot delete attachments that are already associated with a transaction or record. 

Removing an Attachment from a Transaction or Record 

To remove an attachment from a specific transaction or record: 

1. 
Edit the record with the attachment you want to delete. For example, to remove an 

attachment from an A/P invoice, go to the A/P invoices list, and then edit the appropriate 

A/P invoice. 

2. 
Find the attachment. This will be located in a different place depending on whether you’ve 

enabled scanning in your user preferences: 

• 
If scanning is enabled, find the Documents section, and then click the 
 Delete icon 

next to the attachment files you want to remove. 

• 
If scanning is not enabled, find the Attachment(s) field, and then clear the selected 

attachment. 

You can enable or disable scanning using the Enable single scan upload check box on the 

Preferences page. This setting is located in the Display section under Personalize 

interactive behavior. 

3. 
Click Save to save the transaction or record.

About This Chapter 

This chapter contains two kinds of information: helpful background information and common 

tasks. 

Background Information 

• 
Names and IDs (on page 297): When you add a new record, it typically requires a unique 

name, identifier, or both. This section includes guidelines to help you create effective names 

and IDs. 

• 
Lists (on page 300): Most of the work that you do in the system takes place in lists. From 

lists, you add, view, edit, and delete records. Lists have several controls in common that let 

you filter, sort, and create views. Learn how to use lists effectively to get the most out of the 

system. 

• 
Audit trails (on page 320): Audit trails let you see who changed a record, when they 

changed it and in some case, see what was changed.  

• 
Terminology (on page 322): You can change the terminology that the system displays. For 

example, if you prefer to use the word “supplier” in place of the word “vendor, then you can 

change the term system-wide by accessing the Terminology option. 

• 
Roles and permissions (on page 323): Users must have permissions to access each type of 

information in the system. If you don’t see a menu option or cannot edit a type of record, it 

may be because you do not have permission to that type of information. Please contact 

your system administrator if you need access.  

Common Tasks 

These are miscellaneous common tasks that you typically need as you configure Accounts 

Receivable’s features and functions. Please refer to the RealPage Financial Suite online help for

##### Best Practices for Creating Names and IDs
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 297*

Chapter 15: Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Best Practices for Creating Names and IDs 

Special Characters 

Most applications have best practices for names and IDs. In some cases, even if a name is allowed 

when you create a transaction or record, if that transaction or record interacts with another 

application—or even another area of the same application—the system might not be able to find 

and load it. 

Best practice: We recommend that you create a name or ID using only the following characters. 

Use 

• 
Letters 

• 
Numbers 

• 
A single space 

• 
A single dash 

• 
Underscores 

• 
Periods 

Don’t use 

• 
Special characters such as exclamation marks (!), at signs (@), equal signs (=), and any other 

character not specifically listed in the Use column. 

• 
Double spaces 

• 
Double dashes 

• 
Leading spaces 

• 
Trailing spaces 

You can use some special characters in names, but if you use only the ones in the Use column, you 
can be sure that the name or ID won’t cause problems elsewhere. 

When a name is rendered, double spaces often appear the same as single spaces, which can 

cause difficulty in name recognition. For example, if an application displays an error that an item 

with a double space doesn’t exist, but you know that it does, check the name in the appropriate 

list to make sure that no extra or hidden characters are part of the name or ID. 

Leading Zeros 

We recommend against using leading zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can cause 

errors when you import information into your company from Excel because Excel removes the 

leading zero. Use a character as a prefix to your ID. 

• 
Correct: C0001 

• 
Incorrect: 00C43 

---



##### Setting Default Line-Item Values
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 298*

Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide

Other Considerations 

When creating names and IDs, or configuring sequencing for applications, consider not only the 

impact of the naming scheme in different areas of the system but also the impact in outside 

applications such as importing and exporting files to Excel, Word, and CSV. Reports might sort 

differently than you expect if you use special characters or leading spaces. Some applications strip 

out leading zeros and spaces while others ignore them. 

Learn any limitations of third-party applications that you commonly use to help create your 

naming strategy. 

Setting Default Line-Item Values 

Setting default values is a time-saver when you need to fill in a long list of line items. 

To set a default value for a line-item field: 

1. 
In the Entries section of a transaction’s page, click the Show defaults link. 

The area expands to display all fields for which you can set defaults. The type of fields that 

appear here depend on your company setup. For example, if you’ve enabled standard 

dimensions, or created and deployed user-defined dimensions, multi-currency processing 

fields, or revenue-recognition fields, then you can set default values for them here. 

2. 
Click the drop-down arrow for any field that frequently uses the same value, and then select 

that value. 

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button above the first line item. 

The value that you selected appears on every line or in the line-item detail of every line, 

depending on where the field is located. 

You can override the default value by selecting a different value or typing over the text. 

4. 
Optionally, click the Hide defaults link to hide the defaults section after you have applied 

them to the list.

list. 

a) Select the location that you want the system to complete for you.

#### Managing Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 300*

Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Managing Lists 

Lists provide access to like records. After you create a record, you can access it from its list. Most 

lists allow you to add, edit, view, and delete the records in it. You can also export the list to an 

XML file or a PDF file. After exporting a list, you can import the list into an external application like 

Excel, and then print the list from that application. 

Some lists allow you to access related information. For example, from the customers list, you can 

also access the customers A/R ledger and view a breakdown of the total amount that the 

customer owes. 

Since the list page is where you perform most of your work, the system provides several features 

to let you filter and sort lists and create and manage custom views of your data. 

• 
Sorting (on page 301): Sort the list alphabetically by the data in the desired column. 

• 
Filtering (on page 302): Filter lists so that you see only the data that you need. 

• 
Views (on page 309): Create a custom view to determine which columns appear in your lists, 

and apply a filter so that the list appears just the way you want it. 

Lists and Links 

Each list is unique and can offer links to let you navigate into an associated record to see more 

detailed data. For example, some invoice lists have a Preview link that, when clicked, opens the 

invoice in PDF format in a browser window. Another type of list may have a link to the customer 

record or the vendor record. 

Many reports present figures as links that, when clicked, open the associated record. This example 

shows links in the Debit and Credit columns of a journal entry. When you click a link, the system 

navigates to more information, allowing you to delve into the details.

Sorting Lists

appears on the column that the system is sorting on. 

To reverse the sort order, click the column name again. The sort order reverses, and the arrow

To sort on a different column, click the desired column name.

##### Filtering Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 302*

Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Filtering Lists 

Using Column Filters 

Column filters are text boxes that appear at the top of each column. Filters let you find items in a 

list that match the text that you enter. 

To apply a column filter: 

• 
Type the text that you want to find in the column filter, and then press ENTER. 

The system searches for matches, and then displays the matches in the list. 

If a text box does not appear at the top of a column, the column is not searchable. 

Using the Wild Card Character 

• 
Use the % symbol as a wild card or placeholder. For example, typing “san%” in the City 

column’s filter would find both San Francisco and Santa Diego. 

• 
Placing the % in front of text tells the system to find these letters in the middle of text in a 

field. 

• 
Placing % at the end of a word tells the system to find the word and any letters that follow 

the word. 

• 
Use % to filter text columns only. The % symbol does not work on non-text columns such as 

date columns or amount columns. 

• 
For best success, anticipate differences and adapt your filter to account for them. 

To find records that contain a specific value: 

• 
Type the first part of the value. 

If you are looking for a contact in a city that starts with “San,” then you can filter the Contact 

list by typing “san” in the City filter field, then and pressing ENTER. The system searches for 

contacts with a city that begins with San, such as San Jose, San Francisco, and Santa Fe. 

---


<!-- Page 303 -->
Chapter 15: Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

• 
If you know only part of the text that you want to find, type “%” and then type the text that 

you have. 

For example, if you are looking for a contact with the letters “Will” in the name, but you do 

not have the full, correct name of the business, type “%will%” in the Contact name filter of 

the Contacts list, and then press ENTER. The system searches for matches, retrieving all 

contacts that contain the letters “will” in the Contact name field. 

Example 

Your company uses this standard format for naming invoice summaries: Invoices: Month Year. 

When you want to find all June summaries, type “%June” in the filter above the Summary column, 

and then press ENTER to apply the filter. Placing the % in front of June tells the system that the 

word “June” appears in the middle of the text string. Placing % at the end of the word “June” tells 

the system to find the word June and any word with letters that follow the word “June,” such as 

“Juneteenth.” 

Searches for Units 

You can search for a unit by entering any part of the unit ID. The system will find matches for any 

part of the unit ID string. For example, if the units in your property are configured with an 

alphanumeric pattern such as A-10, A-11, A12, B-20, B-21, B-22, then you can enter any part of 

the string, such as “22,” and the system will find B-22.  

The string does not have to start with the entered value to match. Typing “A” finds a list of units 

on the A floor as in our example or all units that have “A” in the unit ID. 

---


<!-- Page 304 -->
Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide

Displaying One-Time Items 

Some quick-entry records are set for one-time use. For example, you may have a seasonal 

customer, such as a Halloween supply store, or customers who pay only once and are not likely to 

purchase again. 

Create the customer record so that you can record the cash receipt, but because you don’t need 

to see that customer in your customer list regularly, flag the customer as Exclude from the 

company contact list. One-time customers aren’t included in the list unless you specify them to be 

included. 

To include one-time items in the list, select the Include One-Time check box. The system displays 

the one-time items along with regular items and adds a One-Time column to show which items 

are one-time records. 

Example 

You may have a customer who purchases from you only once a year, and you do not want to see 

the customer’s name in the list all the time. You still need to create a Customer record so that you 

can record the cash receipt, but since you do not need to see the customer in your Customers list 

regularly, edit the Customer record, and select the One-Time Use check box. 

Including Inactive Records in Search Results 

Almost every kind of record in the system has a Status field with choices of Active and Inactive. 

The Include Inactive check box appears at the top of many lists and allows the system to include 

the inactive records in search results. 

• 
Select the Include Inactive check box to include items set to a status of Inactive in the 

search. The system refreshes the list and adds a Status column to indicate which items are 

active and which are inactive. 

• 
Clear the Include Inactive check box to prevent inactive items from appearing in the list. 

A list can contain items that are inactive but still present because they link to transaction data. For 

example, you may have a vendor who no longer carries items you need to purchase. In the vendor 

record, you flag the vendor as Inactive. Inactive vendors aren’t included in the list unless you 

select Include Inactive. 

---


<!-- Page 305 -->
Chapter 15: Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

One-time use customers do not appear in the Company application’s Contacts list unless you 
select the Include one-time check box. 

Include Private 

Customer records created prior to June 2020 could be created at the entity level. Records created 

at the entity level are private. Customer records that you create today can be created only at the 

top level. The Include Private check box controls whether entity level customer records appear in 

the Customers list. The Include Private check box is selected by default so that all records appear 

in the Customers list. 

• 
Clear the Include Private check box to display only public records (records that are set up at 

the top level). 

• 
Select the Include Private check box to show all customer records in the list, regardless of 

where they were created. When the Include Private check box is selected, the list includes 

the Entity column, identifying the entity to which the private item belongs.

Display Hierarchy

check box appears above the list. 

• 
Select the Display Hierarchy check box to illustrate the relationships between the records. 

• 
Clear the check box to flatten the list so that no relationship information appears in the list. 

Learn more about hierarchical views. 

Advanced Filters 

Use advanced filters to apply standard operators to a list’s columns so that you can view only the 

records you want. You can do this using the simple column filter boxes, but advanced filters offer 

many more operators. Click the Advanced filters link to open the filtering box.

The Advanced filters section has three fields per filter row. 

a) Column name field: The first field is a drop-down list where you select the column that you 

want to filter. 

b) Operator field: The second field is where you select the operator that evaluates each record. 

In the example, the starts with operator evaluates whether the vendor name starts with the 

letters Ch. For a list of operators and what they do, see Operator definitions. 

c) Search field: The third field is where you type that foe which you want to search. 

d) Filter row: One row is called a filter row. You can add additional filter rows by clicking the 

Add filter link. To remove the last filter row, click the Delete last filter link. 

Filtering by Check Box Status 

In some lists, you can search for records by the status of a check box. To search for records with 

unselected check boxes, type “false.” To search for selected check boxes, type “true.” 

This example shows how to search for items that are not flagged as at risk or holdover. 

Clearing Filters 

Click the Clear all filters link to remove all filter conditions from the list. Clear the filters before 

beginning a new search, or when you want to restore all of the data to the list.

Optionally, if you want to change a column’s label, then you can type its new name in the 

text box. 

3. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

Step 3: Select Filters 

The third step is to set up any filters that you want to apply to the columns. 

1. 
In the Columns drop-down list, select the column to filter on. 

2. 
In the Operator drop-down list, select the comparison operator. 

3. 
In the Value field, type the value for the system to use for the comparison. 

For example, Columns equals  

4. 
Continue adding filters as needed. Click the Add filter link if you need more filter rows. You 

can also click the Delete last filter link to delete the bottom filter row. 

---

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

The more filters you add, the more granular the list view will be.

5. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

Step 4: Sort Results 

The fourth step is to set the default sort order for the data in each column. 

1. 
For each column, select whether to sort the data in ascending or descending order. If you 

do not want to sort the column, leave it as --None--. 

2. 
Drag and drop columns to determine their sort priority. The column at the top will have the 

highest priority and will be sorted first, followed by the second column, followed by the 

third column, and so on. 

3. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

Step 5: Save Advanced Options 

The fifth and final step is to deploy the view. 

1. 
In the Name field, type a meaningful name for the new custom view. 

2. 
Select the Deploy check box to make the view available to others. 

3. 
In the Description field, type the purpose of use of the view. 

4. 
When finished, click Save to save and deploy the custom view.

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in RealPage Accounting do not have the CSV for import option.

Audit Trails 

Each action you take can impact your financial statements, so both internal and external 

stakeholders need to know how things have changed and who made those changes. The system 

audit trail keeps track of the changes so that you know who made changes to a particular record 

and when they made the changes. The View audit trail command is available on most records. 

Viewing Audit Trails 

You can access the audit trail of a record. The method of accessing the audit trail varies based on 

the record type. 

Accessing the Audit Trail  

1. 
Open the record that you want to examine. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the View audit trail option.  

Instead of the More Actions button, some records have a View Audit Trail button. 

The Audit trail list opens with a list of changes that users have made.  

Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail 

You can export data from the audit trail to a file in one of three formats, Microsoft Excel, CSV, or 

PDF. 

1. 
Open the audit trail. 

2. 
Click the audit trail’s More actions button, and then select the format to which you want to 

export: 

• 
Export to CSV 

• 
Export to Excel 

• 
Export to PDF 

If the audit trail table is lengthy, you can change the size of the list. From the More actions 
drop-down list, select Table size, and then select the number of rows that you want to be 
able to view.

#### Roles and Permissions
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 323*

Chapter 15: Miscellaneous Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

---

Duplicating Records 

You can add a record by duplicating an existing one and then editing the duplicate.  

To duplicate an existing record: 

1. 
Open the record that you want to duplicate by clicking View or Edit.  

2. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system creates a new record that is identical to the original. 

3. 
Fill in the fields.  

4. 
The system sets the status to Active. You can leave the status set to Active or select Inactive 

to prevent the item from appearing in lists. 

5. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

New. The system saves the record and then opens a new blank record. 

Adding a G/L Account 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > 
 Accounts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > All > 
 Accounts`


To add a G/L account: 

1. 
From the top level, open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, click the 
 Add button next to the Accounts menu option. 

The General Ledger accounts page opens. 

3. 
Enter the account number. After you save the account record, the account number cannot 

be edited. 

We recommend using dimensions (on page 282 ) instead of sub-accounts. This simplifies 
reporting when rolling up for reports. 

4. 
In the Title field, type a name for the account as you want it to appear as the heading on 

reports, for example, Assets.  

After you save the account record, you have the option to create additional titles for the 
account. This option is useful when your system has multiple entities that would benefit 
from custom titles, such as account titles in other languages or a variation of an account 
title that an entity ’s users are more familiar with. 

5. 
In the Category drop-down list, select the category of account that you are creating. 

Categories are permanently pre-assigned to account groups, which are used in financial 

reports and graphs that are supplied with the system.

For example, you would assign the Petty Cash account to the category Cash and Cash 

Equivalents, which is assigned to the Cash and Cash Equivalents account group and appears 

on financial reports and graphs that contain this account group. If you do not want this 

account to be in your financials, then delete the text in this field so it is blank. 

The Category field is displayed only for companies that were created with a setup template 

or chose one later. If you need to assign categories to many accounts, the easiest way is to 

export your chart of accounts, make the changes in the file, and then upload the file. 

When Your System Was Set Up With the Services Template 
By default, the categories Manpower and Direct materials are assigned to account groups 
that are only used in the reports Project Profitability and Project Estimation Versus Actual. 
These two categories do not appear in balance sheet reports or income statements. If you 
assign an account to either of these two categories, and you want it to show up in your 
balance sheet, income statement, or other reports, you must manually assign these 
categories to the appropriate account groups. 

6. 
In the Account type drop-down list, select either Balance sheet account or Income 

statement account. 

• 
Balance sheet accounts are snapshots of the current state of a company’s assets, 

liabilities, and equity at a specific time. 

• 
Income statement accounts (sometimes called profit and loss statements) are 

cumulative for the selected period. 

7. 
For Normal balance, select either Debit or Credit. 

When you create an account, you specify whether the normal balance, from an accounting 

standpoint, is a debit or credit. For example, expense accounts are normally debit accounts. 

Sales accounts are normally a credit. If you were to run a Trial Balance report, the normal 

balance of the accounts is what determines whether the account is a credit or debit. 

8. 
For the Period end closing type, select whether the account is a closing or non-closing 

account. For closing accounts, select an account in the Close into account drop-down list. 

• 
Instead of manually closing accounts at year-end, you can set them to be closing 

accounts and then specify the account in which to close that period. 

• 
Income statement accounts should be closing accounts; balance sheet accounts 

should be non-closing accounts. 

• 
For all income statement accounts, the close-into account will typically be Retained 

Earnings. The system then zeros closing-type accounts into retained earnings at 

year-end. 

9. 
In the G/L account alternative drop-down list, select a G/L account for the system to use as 

an alternative payables account. The account override must be enabled for this field to 

appear.

10. 
The default status is Active. If you want to prevent this G/L account from appearing in lists, 

select Inactive in the Status drop-down list. (You can still list inactive accounts by clicking 

the Include inactive check box in lists.) 

You cannot make a G/L account inactive when the account is selected on the configuration 
page of an application or if the account is being used in a budget. 

11. 
Select the Disallow Direct Posting check box to prevent direct entry of journal entries to the 

subledger control account (for example, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, etc.). 

Use this control to ensure that the account balance for the subledger account is accurate 

and has the necessary subledger details supporting the figure, rather than a direct entry that 

would not be reflected in the subledger application area. 

When a G/L account is marked as Disallow Direct Posting, the system allows OneSite 
transactions to be created for that G/L account (as these are system
-created entries) 
but still disallows manually created journal entries to post to the G/L account.  

12. 
Select the Require Unit check box to require the user to select a unit when using this 

account. 

13. 
Select the Require asset category/type during invoice entry check box if you want to 

require users to enter asset information whenever they select this G/L account when 

entering an A/P invoice. 

This option appears when the Enable asset in invoice entry check box is selected in 
Accounts Payable settings. 

14. 
Select the Use for budgeting check box if you want to use this G/L account in budgets. 

15. 
Select the Allow as Elimination Account check box to allow this account to be selected 

when creating an elimination entity. 

Requiring Dimensions 

Dimensions drive visibility into the parts of your business that matter most. You can require users 

to select dimensions when selecting the G/L account. When you require a dimension for a G/L 

account, all transactions that post to that account must include the dimension or dimensions that 

you select here. If you require multiple dimensions, all dimensions must be included to post to the 

G/L account. 

Use the Require Dimensions section to select the dimensions that you want to require for this 

account. 

• 
To require dimensions for transaction entries assigned to this account, select the dimension 

check boxes to require. All selected dimensions will be required. Supported dimensions 

include: 

• 
Department

If This Account Overrides Other Accounts 

To flag this account as an override of the default A/P or A/R G/L account, select the type of G/L 

account that it can override. Although you can flag any account as an available override account, 

typically, you flag an A/R or A/P account. 

• 
Payables account: Adds the account to the filtered list of A/P G/L accounts available as 

override accounts for bill and adjustment transactions, and for transactions involving a 

specific vendor. 

• 
Receivables account: Adds the account to the filtered list of A/R G/L accounts available as 

override accounts for invoice and adjustment transactions, and for transactions involving a 

specific customer. 

As you enter transactions, you can select the same alternative G/L account for all line items, or 

select alternative accounts individually per line item. On the Vendor and Customer pages, you 

can select one alternative G/L account to use for balancing all transactions involving that vendor. 

Currently, this feature applies to A/P invoices, A/R invoices, and adjustments only. It doesn’t 
apply to recurring A/P invoices or A/R invoices, manual payments, manual deposits, quick check 
entry, quick A/P invoice entry, quick A/R invoice entry, or advances. 

Including the Account in Chart Types 

You can simplify the accounting task by creating subsets of the chart of accounts. These subsets 

are called chart types. The Chart types option appears when your company has the chart type 

feature enabled. 

If your company uses chart types, every time you create a new account, consider adding the 

account to each appropriate chart type.

1. 
Click the Chart types’ Select button. The multi-select box opens. 

2. 
Select the chart type in which to include this account.

##### Adding a Contact
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 329*

Adding a Contact 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Contacts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > 
 Contact`


To create a contact quickly, you only need to assign it a unique Suggested contact name and a 

Print as name for documents. 

The Suggested contact name is the most important field in a contact record. It acts as a unique 

contact ID across the RealPage Financial Suite system, which means you can no longer edit the 

suggested contact name after you create the contact record. Furthermore, although you can 

change the printed name of a contact with the Print as field, the Suggested contact name is the 

name that appears in all lists and drop-down lists across RealPage Accounting. You can change 

the Suggested contact name of a contact in limited situations such as when a vendor’s name has 

changed. 

Additionally, when you create a new vendor, customer, employee, or user, a related contact is 

often created simultaneously based on specific fields in the record. See Creating a Contact from a 

Record to learn about which specific fields in each record create the related Suggested contact 

name. 

To create a more detailed contact record, fill in each tab on the Contact information page. 

Filling In Contact Information 

On the Contact information tab: 

1. 
Type the contact name. 

• 
This name isn’t necessarily the name that is used throughout your company because 

actual names aren’t always unique. For example, a name such as “Jose Hernandez” 

could be the same as a completely different contact in your company. 

• 
The system automatically suggests a unique Suggested contact name and Print as 

name based on the naming details you enter. 

2. 
Add the Primary email address, Primary phone number, and Company name for the 

contact.  

In the Property Management application, the system uses the primary email address that 
you enter here to fill in email addresses for emailing statements.  

3. 
Type a Suggested contact name if you want a different version than the one the system 

auto-populates. This name appears in lists and drop-down lists. 

After you save the contact, the Suggested contact name can’t be edited. 

4. 
Enter the Print as name if you want a different version to appear on printed documents than 

the one the system auto-populates.

Filling In Mailing Information 

On the Mailing information tab, add the mailing address for the contact. 

Filling In Additional Information 

On the Additional information tab, enter any secondary information you might have. This 

includes phone, URL, and taxable information. 

Marking a Contact to Be an Owner or Investor 

On the Reporting portal tab, select the This is an owner-Investor check box if you plan to include 

the contact as an owner or investor. This option enables the owners and investors to receive 

financial reports and other documents through the portal.  

Only contacts that are marked as an owner or investor will appear in the Contact drop-down list 
when you add a new Reporting Portal owner or investor record. Investor records are associated 
with the Investor Tracking application. Owner records, in this case, are associated with the 

Reporting portal application. They are not associated with the Owner records in the Condo and 

Co-op application and its Owner portal. 

Saving the Contact Record 

After providing the available information, click the Save button. 

To add another contact with the same information, click the Duplicate button. Everything is 

identical except for the Suggested contact name. Make any necessary changes, and then click the 

Save button. 

Editing Customer Contact Information in a Transaction 

If you notice that the customer contact information is incorrect on a transaction, or perhaps the 

transaction uses the wrong contact entirely, then you can edit or change the contact on the 

transaction’s page. 

If you notice the error during the creation of the transaction, change the contact in the 

transaction, but keep in mind that editing customer contact information only affects the current 

transaction being created and future transactions. 

If you already saved and posted the transaction, editing or changing a contact becomes more 

complicated. Depending on the type of transaction and the state of the transaction, you may have 

to reverse the transaction before you can make any changes to the transaction record, including 

changes to the associated contact record that apply to the existing transaction. 

See one of the following for more detailed information and step-by-step instructions. 

• 
Editing Contact Information from a Transaction During Creation (on page 331) 

• 
Editing Contact Information in an Existing Transaction (on page 331) 

• 
Changing a Contact in an Existing Transaction (on page 332)

Editing Contact Information from a Transaction During Creation 

When you edit contact information used in a transaction, you only edit the information for that 

transaction and future transactions. If you want the same changes to apply to existing 

transactions, you must manually update the contact information in that record as well. 

To edit contact information during the creation of a transaction: 

1. 
In the new transaction record, click the drop-down arrow in the contact field and highlight 

the contact you want to edit, and then click View. 

2. 
In the Contact Information box, click Edit. 

3. 
Make any necessary changes to the contact record. The Suggested contact name is a 

unique ID used across the system by various records. It can’t be changed after creation. The 

Print as name is the text that appears on printed documents and transactions. 

4. 
Click Save. 

Editing Contact Information in an Existing Transaction 

To edit the contact information used in an existing transaction, you may have to reverse the 

transaction and recreate it. Whether you can edit or reverse a transaction depends on the 

transaction type, the state of the transaction, and your permissions. 

You can only edit information in transactions that are still open. If the transaction is part of a 
closed period, you must open the books to make any changes. 

To edit contact information in an existing transaction: 

1. 
Go to the transaction and click Edit. If you can’t edit the transaction, you must first Reverse 

a transaction, and then Edit it. 

You can only edit transactions from where they were created. For instance, if you create a 
vendor invoice in Purchasing, you cannot edit the corresponding A/P invoice in Accounts 
Payable. Instead, you must edit the vendor invoice from the vendor invoice list in 
Purchasing. 

2. 
In the contact field you want to edit, click the drop-down arrow and highlight the contact, 

then click View. 

3. 
In the Contact Information window, click Edit. 

4. 
Make any necessary changes to the contact record. The Suggested contact name is a 

unique ID used across the system by various records. It can’t be changed after creation. The 

Print as name is the text that appears on printed documents and transactions. 

5. 
Click Save.

depends on the transaction type, the state of the transaction, and your permissions. You can only 

edit information in transactions that are still open. If the transaction is part of a closed period, you 

must open the books to make any changes. See Open and close process workflow for more 

information. 

To change a contact used in an existing transaction: 

1. 
Find the desired transaction and click Edit. 

If you can’t edit the transaction, you must first Reverse the transaction, and then Edit it. 

2. 
In the contact field you want to change, click the drop-down arrow, and then click Find. 

3. 
In the Contact name column, type the name of the contact you want to use for this 

transaction. The system stores contacts by their unique Suggested contact name. Be sure to 

search by this name when selecting a new contact. 

4. 
Click Select next to the appropriate contact name. 

5. 
Save your changes.

*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 333*

Chapter 15: Miscellaneous Common Tasks

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

Using the Multi-Select Box 

Use the Multi-select box to select the items that you will act on in the next step. The goal is to 

find items in the Available items column that you want to act on and then move them into the 

Selected Items column. 

1. 
Click the Select button to open the Multi-select box. 

• 
To search for an item, type one or more letters in the Search items box. The system 

filters the items in the list to show only items that begin with the characters that you 

type.  

• 
To add an item, click the 
 Add button. The item moves to the Selected items 

column. 

• 
To add all items, select the Add all link. All items move from the Available items 

column into the Selected items column. 

• 
Click the 
 Delete button to remove an item. 

• 
To rearrange the list, drag an item to a new position in the list using the 
 Rearrange 

button. Repeat as necessary. 

2. 
When you have finished selecting items, click the Done button. The Selection box closes 

and is replaced by a smaller box that lists the items that you selected. The number of items 

appears in parentheses. The Select button changes to an Add/Edit link. 

In this box, you can: 

• 
Click the 
 Delete button to remove an item. 

• 
Click the Add/Edit link to reopen the Multi-select box and change your selections.
