Printing PDF Documents from Safari 

PDF reports appear in a new window. Make sure you allow pop-ups in your browser (the PDF 

appears in a pop-up). 

To set Safari to allow pop-ups: 

1. 
Open Safari. 

2. 
Select Preferences. 

3. 
Select Security. 

Additionally, make sure Safari is set to use the Adobe Reader to read PDFs. 

4. 
Locate Internet plug-ins and click Website settings. 

5. 
In the list of plug-ins, select Adobe Reader. 

6. 
Under When Visiting Other Websites, choose Allow Always from the drop-down list. 

7. 
Click Done. 

Printing PDF Documents from Firefox 

PDF reports appear in a box. Make sure you allow pop ups in your browser (the PDF appears in a 

box). 

To set Firefox to allow pop-ups, go to Options > Content. 

Additionally, make sure Firefox is set to use the Adobe Reader to read PDFs. For Firefox, be sure 

to check this setting every update since Firefox changes your default to the Firefox PDF viewer for 

every browser update: 

1. 
In Firefox, at the top of the page, click the menu bar. 

2. 
Click Options, and then click the Applications tab. 

3. 
For the Portable Document Format (PDF) option, select to Use Adobe Acrobat (in Firefox) 

or Use Adobe Reader (default). 

If Portable Document Format (PDF) isn’t listed, download Adobe Acrobat Reader from the 
Adobe website. 

4. 
Close the window.

#### How to Read Paths
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 341*

Chapter 16: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 

How to Read Paths 

If you have ever been puzzled over a path in the documentation, this topic describes what it all 

means. 

Application Menus and Tabs 

Most paths begin with the Applications menu. This menu is located in the upper-left corner next 

to the Home button. When you select an application, the name of the Applications menu 

changes to the application that you selected. 

Menus have two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab is available to all users, but the Setup tab is 

restricted to users with full or limited administrator privileges. 

The Company application has two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab contains setup options for 
global features and is available to all users with the appropriate permissions. The Setup tab is 
restricted to administrators only. 

Simple Paths 

This is an example of a simple path: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry`


The first three parts in a path are standard; they translate to “Click the Applications menu (a), 

select the name of the application (b), and then select the menu tab (c).” 

---


<!-- Page 342 -->
Help and Support 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The next steps in the path—the menu section (d) and the menu option (e)—direct you to a 

specific list or page in the application. 

a) Click the Applications menu.  

b) Select the application. 

c) Select the menu tab. 

d) Find the menu section or subsection, if any. 

e) Click the menu option.  

If you see the 
 icon in a path, then you can click the  icon in front of the menu option to add 
a new blank record. 

Paths with Multiple Options 

Some paths offer multiple choices. The choices are separated with a “/” symbol.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable > Setup > Taxes > Authorities > 
View/Edit`


In this example, Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable means that the same option is available 

in two applications’ menus, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable. Likewise, View/Edit 

means that you can select either the View or the Edit link to get to the page that you need.

## Introduction to Accounts Receivable Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 7*

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

Introduction to Accounts Receivable Reports 

This book describes how to work with Accounts Receivable reports. 

This chapter lists and describes the reports available in the Accounts Receivable application, how to set them up 

and run them, and what you can do with them.  

For additional A/R reporting, you can create a financial report and any of the following: 

• 
Select customers as a segment. 

• 
Expand any column by customers. 

• 
Filter by customers 

For information on A/R charts, see Accounts Receivable Charts (on page 171). 

In This Chapter 

List of Standard Accounts Receivable Reports ................................................................................ 8 

Report Workflow ...................................................................................................................................... 10 

C H A P T E R 1 

---



### List of Standard Accounts Receivable Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 8*

Introduction to Accounts Receivable Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

List of Standard Accounts Receivable Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Reports`


The Accounts receivable application contains a number of standard reports that have been 

created for you. These reports involve amounts owed or paid by customers for goods and 

services. You can run, view, process, memorize, export, and customize A/R reports. Refer to Using 

Reports (on page 125) for information on creating, storing, and reusing reports. 

Customer Reports 

The Customer reports appear in the Accounts Receivable application’s menu in the Reports 

section, in the Customers group. 

• 
Customer aging report (on page 13)  

This report provides a snapshot of outstanding charges based on account label, G/L 

Account, or other selected parameters. It lists the customers who owe you money and either 

how many days it took them to pay you, or how many days past due their payments are. 

Use this report to determine how well you are collecting on your accounts receivable. This 

report is also available as a chart (on page 179). 

• 
Customer listing report (on page 23)  

This report is a list of customers that includes details such as location and contact 

information, pricing details, payment methods, term, tax ID, and current customer balances.  

Registers and Reports 

These reports appear in the Accounts receivable application’s menu under the Reports column, 

in the Registers & Reports section. 

• 
A/R Ledger report (on page 34) 

The A/R Ledger report is a list of detailed customer accounts. Use this report to see if the 

balance in the A/R ledger agrees with that in the general ledger, and to see which 

customers have balances greater than zero. Details include the beginning balance for the 

selected period, current account balance, and the charges and payments for each customer. 

• 
Sales Register report (on page 42) 

The Sales Register report displays the invoices you sent to customers, account adjustments, 

payment details, and credit details. Each transaction includes the date, customer ID and 

name, invoice or adjustment number, due date, description (if any), amount, and amount 

paid. 

• 
Recurring Transaction Status report (on page 73) 

---


<!-- Page 9 -->
Chapter 1: Introduction to Accounts Receivable Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

This report presents information on the status of scheduled, completed, and failed 

transactions. The report includes transactions generated from the Accounts receivable and 

Accounts payable applications. 

• 
Recurring Transaction Forecast report (on page 78) 

This report provides insight into future billings based on recurring transaction schedules set 

up in the system. With this report, you can expand the number of forecasting periods, as 

well as select a forecasting frequency (monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, annually). 

Multi-currency enabled companies can choose to forecast on base currency or transaction 

currency. 

• 
Receipts Register report (on page 84) 

This report lists receipts from the customers that you select. Use this report to review all of 

the receipts that have been applied to invoice transactions.  

• 
Sales Tax report (on page 91) 

This report summarizes the taxes and labels them “Total Other Taxes.” 

• 
Deferred Revenue Forecast report (on page 49) 

This report illustrates how deferred income is recognized as revenue over time. Use this 

report to forecast revenue by time period, account, customer, and more. 

• 
Deferred Revenue Details report (on page 58) 

This report shows the details of customers and transactions for which you have deferred 

revenue. This report includes the transaction amount, transaction date, deferred amount, 

recognized amount, and amount paid. Use this report to see the transaction detail behind 

those deferred numbers and to tie back to the deferred balance on your G/L (like an audit 

report). 

• 
Deferred Revenue Revaluation report (on page 67) 

This report shows the adjustment of deferred revenue to reflect the business’s expected 

ability to fulfill the service obligations and generate revenue from prepaid amounts. 

Multicurrency must be enabled to access this report. 

• 
Intercompany Billing report (on page 97) 

This report lists the billing transactions between two entities. This report requires that you 

have configured the intercompany billing feature. Learn more about Configuring 

Intercompany Billing (on page 245). 

• 
A/R Invoices Analysis report (on page 103) 

This report helps you analyze your sales from the perspective of revenue line items in the 

invoices. Use this report to review your invoices. This report is also available as a chart. See 

Invoices Analysis chart (on page 194). 

---



#### Report Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 10*

Introduction to Accounts Receivable Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Recurring report (on page 111) 

This report shows a list of recurring invoices from your customers, along with details about 

the recurring payments, such as the frequency with which the invoice is paid, how many 

times the recurring invoice has been paid, the term, amount, and so on.  

• 
Reclassification report (on page 118)  

This report displays a list of documents with data that was reclassified from one account to 

another in the past month, and includes the names of those who reclassified them. 

Custom Views 

The Custom Views option appears at the bottom of the Reports column on the Accounts 

Receivable application menu when you have created at least one custom view for a list page that 

appears in the application. Click Custom views to open the submenu and select the desired 

custom view. Learn more about List Views (on page 221). 

Report Workflow 

Each report is different, but setting up any report offers several standard steps. Follow these steps 

to customize the report to get the results you want: 

1. 
Set up the time period that you want the report to cover. 

2. 
Set up filters to refine the report results. 

3. 
Choose the sort order and page orientation.  

4. 
Type a title, subtitle, and footer text for your report. 

5. 
Click View to run the report. 

After running the report, you can customize the settings to refine the results, memorize the report 

settings so that you can come back and run the same report later, export the report as an Excel or 

CSV file, process and store the report, and add the report to a dashboard. 

Consult each report for detailed steps that describe how to customize it.

Standard Reports 

Standard reports are reports that are typical to an application and have already been created for 

you.  

You can either run reports without customization or you can set up filters to narrow the results. 

Depending on the report, the report settings page offers several filter options. Many reports offer 

filters by customer, location, department, and level of detail. You can filter by reporting period or 

time period for the report coverage. Most reports have multiple options for formatting such as 

sorting, grouping, and orientation.

Customizing the Customer Aging Report 

To customize the Customer Aging report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu.  

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Customers section, select Customer aging, and then select 

Report. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report.  

1. 
In Aging periods, select the aging period to include in the report. 

2. 
In Report as of, select Today to report on customer aging as of today. You can also select 

Selected date, and then type a date or click 
 Calendar and then select a date. 

3. 
In the Based on section, select one of the options to determine whether the system uses the 

invoice date, due date, or G/L posting date. 

• 
Invoice date: Base the report date on the date the customer is invoiced. 

• 
Due date: Base the report on the billing due date. 

• 
G/L posting date: Base the report on the date the invoice is to be posted to the 

general ledger. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up report filter if needed. Using filters is optional. 

1. 
Use the From customer and To customer drop-down lists to select the beginning and 

ending customer in a range to include a range of customers in the report. 

In From customer, select the first customer in a range of customers to include in the report. 

The system fills in the To customer box with the same customer, setting it up in case you 

want to include just one customer in the report.

In To customer, select the last customer in a range of customers.

customer. 

2. 
In Customer type, if you want to limit the report to a certain customer type, select the type 

here. 

3. 
In Territory, if you want to limit the report to a certain territory, select the territory here. 

4. 
In Location, to limit the report to a specific location, select the location here. 

5. 
Select the Individual report check box to run a separate report for each selected location. 

6. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt you for a location when it is 

about to run the report. 

7. 
In Department, to limit the report to a specific department, select the department here. 

8. 
Select the Individual report check box to run a separate report for each selected 

department. 

9. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt you for a department when 

it is about to run the report. 

10.

This location: Include customer aging data for the selected location only.

•

• 
Due date: This column contains the date the payment is due. This column only appears in 

the detailed version of the report. 

• 
0-30: This column contains the amount overdue between 0 and 30 days after the invoice 

date.

## A/R Ledger Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 34*

Accounts Receivable Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

A/R Ledger Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > A/R 
Ledger`


The A/R Ledger report is a list of detailed customer accounts, including the current account 

balances for customers. This report shows the beginning balance for the period you have 

selected, along with the charges and payments for each customer. 

Use this report to see if the balance in the A/R ledger agrees with that in the general ledger and 

to see which customers have balances greater than zero. 

You can adjust the time period, customer, customer type, and payment summary to meet your 

reporting needs. Normally, this report shows only customers with balances greater than zero. 

However, you can choose to include zero-balance customers as well. In the report, you can click 

the customer name to drill down to the Customer information page. 

The people who typically need this report are accountants, controllers, and anyone who needs to 

see who owes money to whom.

A/R Ledger Report Columns 

The default A/R Ledger report consists of the following columns: 

• 
Customer: This column contains the name of the customer. When clicked, this link opens 

the customer’s record. 

• 
Date: This column contains the date of the invoice. When clicked, the system opens the 

associated invoice. 

• 
Document: This column contains the document ID, such as the invoice number. 

• 
Reference: This column contains a number such as an associated sales order or account 

number. 

• 
Memo: This column contains the ID associated with your customer (supplier) and the 

customer’s name. 

• 
Txn currency: This column contains the currency used in the transaction. 

• 
Txn amount: This column contains the amount exchanged in the transaction. 

• 
Charges: This column contains the debits posted to the customer’s account for the selected 

period. 

• 
Payments: This column contains the credits posted to the customer’s account for the 

selected period. 

• 
Balance: This column contains the total amount of your customer’s balance for the selected 

period (that is, the amount you owe the customer). 

• 
Total: This column contains the total amount of the customer’s balance for the selected 

period.

Sales Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Receivable > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Sales Register`


The Sales Register report displays the invoices you sent to customers in the specified time period, 

as well as any account adjustments that were entered. Each transaction that is listed shows the 

date, customer ID and name, invoice or adjustment number, due date, description (if any), 

amount, and amount paid. 

Using the report, you can:

View invoices and adjustments 

• 
See the payment details for invoices, including the payment method and date 

•

subtotals of invoice amounts by customer or location

corresponding transaction.

Registers Report Columns 

The Sales Register report consists of the following columns: 

• 
Date: This column contains the date on which you sent the invoice to the customer. 

• 
Customer: This column contains the ID associated with your customer followed by the 

customer’s name. 

• 
Inv #/ Adjustment #: This column contains the customer’s invoice number with your 

company. 

• 
Due date: This column contains the date on which the invoice was due. 

• 
Account label: This column contains the account label associated with the transaction. 

• 
Department: This column contains a description of the products or services the customer 

bought. 

• 
Location: This column contains the location involved in the transaction. 

• 
Descr: This column contains a description of the transaction. 

• 
Memo: This column contains an optional note about the transaction. 

• 
Curr: This column contains the transaction currency. 

• 
Txn amount: This column contains the amount of the invoice expressed in the transaction 

currency. 

• 
Base amount (currency): This column contains the amount of the invoice expressed in the 

currency of the location. The currency is specified in parentheses. 

• 
Amount paid (currency): This column contains the amount the customer paid your 

company. The currency is specified in parentheses. 

• 
Paid by/Paid to: This column contains the name of the customer that paid, and the name of 

the entity that was paid. 

• 
Method: This column contains the payment method that the customer used. 

• 
Pay date: This column contains the date the customer paid. 

• 
Bank account: This column contains the bank account where the payment was deposited.

## Deferred Revenue Forecast Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 49*



### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 49*

Chapter 2: Accounts Receivable Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

Deferred Revenue Forecast Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred 
Revenue Forecast`


The Deferred Revenue Forecast report illustrates how deferred income is recognized as revenue 

over time. Use this report to forecast revenue by time period, account, customer, and more.  

This report is typically used by Finance staff who need to do the following: 

• 
Budget and forecast revenue in-flows, based on prior projections. 

• 
Place revenue on hold or terminate it, or analyze revenue lost due to contract cancellations 

and terminations. 

• 
Determine how much revenue has yet to be recognized (on-hold forecasting). Running this 

report shows what the revenue would look like if the on-hold revenue were released. With 

that information, finance staff can look into the reasons why revenue is on hold. For 

instance, are there issues with collecting revenue or delivering products? Is the service team 

not turning things around as fast as it could? The report can make visible problems in excess 

deferred revenue. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option on the menu, ask your system administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run the Deferred Revenue Forecast report. 

Application 
Reports 
Permissions 

General ledger 
Deferred Revenue Forecast 
Run 

For more information about permissions and roles, see Roles and Permissions (on page 212). If 

you don’t have permissions to access or change any of the options above, then ask your system 

administrator for assistance.

### Customizing and Running the Deferred Revenue Forecast Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 50*

Accounts Receivable Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide

Customizing and Running the Deferred Revenue Forecast Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred 
Revenue Forecast`


To customize the Deferred Revenue Forecast report: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Registers & Reports section, select Deferred Revenue Forecast. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can either define the report coverage by date range or by as of date and number of periods, 

but not both. 

1. 
Type the starting date in the As of date field or click the 
 Calendar button, and then 

select the date from the calendar, and then type the number of periods to run the report. 

Use # of periods with the As of date and Forecast period fields as an alternate way to set 

the period of time you want the report to cover. For example, if you want a year of data and 

the Forecast period = Quarterly, enter 4 here; if the Forecast period = Monthly, enter 12 

here. 

The maximum number of periods allowed are: 

• 
60 for online reports 

• 
12 for PDF reports 

2. 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s coverage period. Set a specific 

Start date and End date.  

Leave the Start date blank to include all information from the earliest date you entered data 

into your company up to and including the End date. 

Leave the End date blank to include all information from the Start date up to today. The 

format must be: MM/DD/YYYY 

If you select a Start date and End date, don’t select an As of date. 

When entering a date, you can either type the dates or click the 
 Calendar button, and 

then select the date from the calendar.  

3. 
Select the Forecast period for which to run the report. 

Each column of the report will represent one period. Options are: 

• 
Monthly—displays as MMM-YY. For example, Jun-20. 

---


<!-- Page 51 -->
Chapter 2: Accounts Receivable Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

• 
Quarterly—displays as MMM-YY - MMM-YY. For example, Jan-20 - Mar-20. 

• 
Semi-annually—displays as MMM-YY - MMM-YY. For example, Jan-20 - Jun-20. 

• 
Annually—displays as Year-YYYY. For example, Year-2020. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Use this section to set up filters that refine your report results. 

1. 
Choose the transactions to include by selecting the check boxes: 

• 
Include not started schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for 

schedules that have not yet started. By default, the report will cover revenue details for 

schedules that have not yet started (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include in progress schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for 

schedules that are in progress. By default, the report will cover revenue details for 

schedules that are in progress (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include onhold schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for schedules 

that are on hold. By default, the report will cover revenue details for schedules that are 

on hold (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include partially terminated schedule: Select this check box to show revenue details 

for schedules that are partially terminated. By default, the report will cover transactions 

that have been partially terminated (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include terminated transactions: Select this check box to show the details of 

transactions that have been terminated. By default, the report will cover transactions 

that have been terminated (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include completed transactions: Select this check box to show the details of 

transactions that have been fully recognized. By default, the report will cover 

transactions that have been fully recognized (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include open period schedules: Select this check box to show project revenue that has 

not been scheduled or posted. This filter is associated with Percent completed or 

Milestone recognition methods. 

2. 
In the Report on section, select the desired option to run the report on: 

• 
Revenue account: Select this option to limit the report to transactions for a specific 

revenue account. 

• 
Deferred revenue account: Select this option to report deferred revenue accounts 

rather than revenue accounts.  

3. 
In the Revenue account drop-down box, select the revenue account to limit the report to 

one revenue account. By default, this box is blank, which means the report will cover 

transaction details for every revenue account. 

4. 
In the Deferred revenue account drop-down list, select the desired deferred revenue 

account to limit the report to one deferred revenue account. Use this filter if you chose

## Deferred Revenue Details
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 58*

Accounts Receivable Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Deferred Revenue Details 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred 
Revenue Details`


The Deferred Revenue Details report shows the details of customers and transactions for which 

you have deferred revenue. This report includes the transaction amount, transaction date, 

deferred amount, recognized amount, and amount paid. 

Use this report to see the transaction detail behind those deferred numbers and to tie back to the 

deferred balance on your G/L (like an audit report). 

This report is typically used by the following users: 

• 
Auditors who need to determine what constitutes the balance on the G/L 

• 
Finance staff 

Understanding this report 

The Deferred Revenue Details report is not, by default, a cumulative report; instead, it is a report 

for a specific period. 

For example, if the current month is March and you want to see revenue recognized as of March 

31, running this report shows you any transactions processed in March along with a breakdown of 

the revenue for the transactions that were deferred, recognized, and paid. However, if you want to 

see the cumulative results as of March 31, you need to backdate your report to include older 

transactions. Because you may have revenue schedules posting in the month of March for 

transactions dated six months ago, you must select a date range that includes the oldest 

schedule.  

To ensure that you accurately display the cumulative amount deferred, recognized, and paid, 

make sure the date range you enter includes all transactions processed from inception (that is, 

from the time your company went live in the RealPage Accounting application) to date.

To customize the Deferred Revenue Details report:

In the Reports column, in the Registers & Reports section, select Deferred Revenue Details. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can either define the report coverage by date range or by reporting period and as of date, 

but not both. 

To define the report’s scope by reporting period and as of date: 

1. 
Select the reporting period. 

2. 
Type the starting date in the As of date field or click the 
 Calendar button, and then 

select the date from the calendar. 

3.

of date at the time the user runs the report. 

To define the report’s scope by date range:

2. 
Enter a date into the Display Amount Deferred, Recognized and Paid As of This Date box 

to set a regular date—such as the first date of each month—on which the system will defer, 

recognize, or pay the amount. 

3. 
In the Based on section, select the date on which to base the report: 

• 
Transaction date 

• 
Posting date 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Use this section to set up filters that refine your report results. 

1. 
Choose the transactions to include by selecting the check boxes: 

• 
Include not started schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for 

schedules that have not yet started. By default, the report will cover revenue details for 

schedules that have not yet started (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include in progress schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for 

schedules that are in progress. By default, the report will cover revenue details for 

schedules that are in progress (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include onhold schedule: Select this check box to show revenue details for schedules 

that are on hold. By default, the report will cover revenue details for schedules that are 

on hold (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include partially terminated schedule: Select this check box to show revenue details 

for schedules that are partially terminated. By default, the report will cover transactions 

that have been partially terminated (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include terminated transactions: Select this check box to show the details of 

transactions that have been terminated. By default, the report will cover transactions 

that have been terminated (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include completed transactions: Select this check box to show the details of 

transactions that have been fully recognized. By default, the report will cover 

transactions that have been fully recognized (that is, the check box is checked).

transaction details for every revenue account.

account to limit the report to one deferred revenue account. Use this filter if you chose 

Deferred revenue account in step 2. By default, this box is blank, which means the report 

will cover transaction details for every deferred revenue account.

## Deferred Revenue Revaluation Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 67*



### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 67*

Chapter 2: Accounts Receivable Reports

Deferred Revenue Revaluation Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred 
Revenue Revaluation`


If your company uses multiple transaction currencies and revenue recognition, you can use the 

Deferred Revenue Revaluation report to revalue revenue recognition schedule entries. When the 

system created those entries, it used a specific exchange rate as of a certain date. You can change 

the exchange rate type and as of date, and calculate the currency gain/loss for every row of the 

revenue recognition schedule-entry table. 

You can filter the resulting data in several ways, such as by customer, customer type and 

transaction currency, and any enabled dimensions. You can generate a condensed summary 

report or a more detailed one that contains additional columns of information. You can group the 

information by customer/currency or location/currency. 

The Deferred Revenue Revaluation report is an informational source only. Revaluation reports 

don’t include information on inter-entity transactions. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run the Deferred Revenue Revaluation report. 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

General ledger 
Deferred Revenue Revaluation Report 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 212) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 212) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Multicurrency must be enabled to access this report. 

---



### Customizing and Running the Deferred Revenue Revaluation Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 68*

Accounts Receivable Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide

Customizing and Running the Deferred Revenue Revaluation Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred 
Revenue Revaluation`


To customize the Deferred Revenue Revaluation report: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu.  

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Registers & Reports section, select Deferred Revenue 

Revaluation. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

1. 
In the Revalue as of date field, type the date to use to calculate the exchange rate gains or 

losses as of a particular date. Type the Revaluation As Of Date in mm/dd/yyyy format, or 

click the 
 Calendar button, and then select the date from the calendar. 

2. 
To filter your data on a custom exchange rate type, select the custom type from the 

Revaluation Exchange Rate Types drop-down list. 

3. 
Select a customer in the From Customer drop-down list to limit the report to one customer.  

To limit the report to a set of customers, select the first customer to include in the From 

Customer drop-down list, and then, in the To Customer drop-down list, select the last 

customer to include. The report includes transactions for every customer in between. An 

unfiltered report includes every customer unless you limit the report to transactions with a 

specific customer or set of customers. 

4. 
Select a Customer type to limit the report to transactions for a specific customer type. The 

report includes transactions for every customer type unless you select a specific customer 

type. If your customers are grouped into subset types, such as Direct, Channel, and Partners, 

you can then filter the report for a specific subset, such as Direct. 

5. 
If you are a multi-currency company, you can filter transactions based on a specific currency. 

(This field does not display unless you work in a multi-currency environment.) To do this, 

use the Transaction currency drop-down list to select the currency you want the report to 

show. If you don’t select a currency, the report includes transactions in your base currency.

Recurring Transactions Status Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Registers & Reports > Recurring 
Transaction > Status`


The Recurring Transaction Status report presents information on the status of scheduled, 

completed, and failed transactions. The report includes transactions generated from the Accounts 

Receivable and Accounts Payable applications. From within the report, you can click links to view 

recurring templates as well as successfully generated documents. Links to failed transactions allow 

you to quickly re-generate invoices after resolving the cause of the failure.  

The report includes transactions generated from the Accounts receivable, Accounts payable, and 

Spend management applications. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Recurring Transaction Status Report Columns 

The Recurring Transaction Status report consists of the following columns: 

• 
Doc type: This column indicates the type of transaction of the report, such as A/R invoices.  

• 
Customer ID: This column contains the ID associated with the customer and the customer’s 

name. 

• 
Rec doc: Click this link to view the transaction’s record where you can make corrections as 

needed. 

• 
Frequency: This column indicates how often the invoice is paid (for example, weekly, 

monthly, etc.). 

• 
Date created: This column contains the date that the transaction was created. 

• 
Generated by: This column contains who generated the transaction. System-generated 

transactions indicate that the Scheduler generated the transaction. 

• 
Status: This column contains the status of the transaction (Success or Failed). 

• 
Doc date: This column contains the date that the doc 

• 
Result (view invoice): This column contains a View invoice link to the resulting transaction 

for a successful transaction or a View error link to the Scheduler log page for more 

information about a failed transaction.  

• 
Action: When a transaction fails, a Retry link appears. Click Retry to have the system run the 

recurring transaction again.

Recurring Transaction Forecast Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Registers & Reports > Recurring 
Transaction > Forecast`


The Recurring Transaction Forecast report provides insight into future billings. This report is based 

on recurring transaction schedules set up in the system. With this report, you can expand the 

number of forecasting periods, as well as select a forecasting frequency (monthly, quarterly, 

semi-annually, annually). Multi-currency enabled companies can choose to forecast on base 

currency or transaction currency.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Registers > Receipts`


The Receipts Register report lists your receipts and enables you to perform the following: 

• 
Navigate to the invoices to which the receipts were applied 

• 
Navigate to customer information 

• 
Reverse transactions 

• 
Locate payments that have not been fully applied, where the amount received is greater 

than the amount applied 

You can display the report in greater or lesser detail, and restrict it to those receipts that have not 

yet been deposited. 

Multi-entity shared users can reverse transactions when they are at the top level of the company 

or at the entity that created the transactions. Otherwise, the Reverse link is disabled.

Receipts Report Columns 

The Receipts Register report consists of the following columns: 

• 
Receipt date: The date you received the payment. 

• 
Customer: The customer who made the payment. Click to open the customer record. 

• 
G/L account/Account label: G/L account number or account label associated with the 

charge. 

• 
Payment method: Method used to make the payment. (EFT, Credit card) 

• 
Invoice number: Unique ID assigned to the invoice. Click to open the invoice. 

• 
Transaction number: Information about the payment. 

• 
Memo: An optional note about the charge. 

• 
Transaction date: Information about the payment. 

• 
Location: The location to which this payment was applied. 

• 
Department: The department to which this payment was applied. 

• 
Txn currency: For multi-currency, multi-entity companies only. The currency in which the 

transaction was paid. 

• 
Txn amount: For multi-currency, multi-entity companies only. The amount of the A/P 

invoice in the currency in which the transaction was paid (that is, the amount of the 

transaction in the vendor’s currency). 

• 
Txn amount applied: The amount paid by the customer in your base currency. 

• 
Amount (USD): The amount paid by the customer. 

• 
Amount applied: The amount of the payment that has already been applied to invoices. It 

might or might not equal the amount of payment. If you have not applied all of the 

payment, the number in this column is less than that in the Amount column. Consequently, 

one function of this report is to find any payments that have not been fully applied. 

• 
Deposited on: The date you deposited the payment. 

• 
Invoices: Click to drill down to view transaction details.  

• 
Total (currency): The total amount of all receipts. 

• 
Total amount applied: The total amount of all these payments that have been applied to 

invoices.

Sales Tax Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Registers & Reports > Sales Tax Report`


The Sales Tax Report details the amount of taxes you have collected for which tax authority, which 

allows you to attribute tax details to a tax authority. Taxes collected using simple tax (that is, 

without tax schedules and tax details) are summarized at the bottom of the report and labeled 

“Total Other Taxes.” 

You can choose the time period, and filter the report by item tax group, contact tax group, tax 

authority, and other criteria. For each tax authority, the report shows taxable, non-taxable and 

total sales, as well as the tax rate and amount of tax collected and payable as of date you specify. 

Benefit: This report is used by data entry clerks who need to look at an audit trail to make sure 

everything was entered correctly. 

Example

Sales Tax Report Columns 

The Sales Tax report consists of the following columns: 

• 
Total sales: The amount of the Accounts Receivable invoice that is not tax is the sale 

amount.  

• 
Adjustments: Shows adjustments due to discounts and similar calculations that reduce the 

taxable amount of the total sale. For example, assume that the total sale is equal to the line 

item amount on the invoice, which is $1,000. But you gave a 10% discount on that line item. 

The tax is calculated after the discount is applied. Consequently, the taxable sales amount is 

$1,000 - $100 (10% discount) or $900.  

• 
Taxable sales: If customer is taxable and the account label associated with the invoice line 

item is taxable, then the amount for that line is the taxable sale amount less any 

adjustments.  

• 
Non-taxable sales: If the account label does not have the Taxable check box selected, the 

amount for the corresponding line item in an invoice posts to non-taxable sales. If the 

customer is non-taxable, then all the line items of an invoice are non-taxable sales.  

• 
Tax rate (%): Shows the effective tax expressed as a percentage. 

• 
Tax collected: Amount paid to the Sales Tax Payable lines of the invoice.  

• 
Sales tax payable as of <date>: The sales tax payable amount when “Is Tax” is enabled for 

the account label.

Intercompany Billing Report Columns 

Consolidated Report 

The consolidated version of the Intercompany Billing report contains the following columns: 

• 
ICB ID: This column contains the system-assigned identifier of the intercompany billing 

transaction. 

• 
Billing entity: This column contains the name of the entity that generated the invoice. 

• 
Date: This column contains the date that the billing entity generated the invoice. 

• 
G/L Posting date: This column contains the date that the billing entity posted the invoice to 

the General ledger. 

• 
Bill amount: This column contains the total amount on the A/P invoice. 

• 
Receiving entities: This column contains the number of entities that received an A/P invoice. 

• 
Status: This column contains the status of the payment: Posted, Selected to pay, or Paid. 

Auto Process Invoice

Detailed Report 

The Intercompany Billing report consists of the following columns: 

• 
Intercompany billing number: This column contains the system-assigned identifier of the 

intercompany billing transaction. 

• 
A/P invoice number: This column contains the A/P invoice number. 

• 
Invoice number: This column contains the unique number of the invoice. This ID matches 

the ID of the A/P invoice. 

• 
Billing entity: This column contains the name of the entity that generated the invoice. 

• 
Date: This column contains the date that the billing entity generated the invoice. 

• 
G/L Posting date: This column contains the date that the billing entity posted the invoice to 

the General ledger. 

• 
Bill amount: This column contains the total amount on the A/P invoice. 

• 
Receiving entities: This column contains the number of entities that received an A/P invoice. 

• 
Status: This column contains the status of the payment: Posted, Selected to pay, or Paid.

Invoices Analysis Report Columns 

The A/R Invoices Analysis detailed report consists of the following columns: 

• 
Account label/Account: This column contains the account number or, if account labels are 

enabled, the account label associated with the invoice. 

• 
Date: This column contains the date on which the invoices were received by you from the 

customer. 

• 
Customer: This column contains the ID associated with your customer followed by 

customer’s name. 

• 
Invoice #: This column contains the customer’s billing account number with your company 

• 
Description: This column contains the type of items charged (for example, legal consulting, 

monthly A/P invoice, or telecommunications costs) 

• 
Department: This column contains the number and name of the department to which the 

A/P invoice is charged 

• 
Location: This column contains the physical location of the department 

• 
Txn currency: This column contains the currency in which the transaction was billed (for 

example, EUR or USD) 

• 
Txn amount: This column contains the amount of the A/P invoice in the specified currency. 

• 
Amount (currency): This column contains the amount of the bill in your base currency. (Used 

to automatically convert a foreign currency to your base currency.)  

• 
Date paid: This column contains the date that the customer paid. 

• 
Doc#: This column contains the reference number on the document. 

• 
Amount paid (currency): This column contains the amount paid, in the base currency.  

• 
Total paid (currency): This column contains the total amount paid, in the base currency.

## Recurring Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 111*



### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 111*

Chapter 2: Accounts Receivable Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

Recurring Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Registers & Reports > Recurring Report`


The A/R Recurring report shows a list of recurring invoices from your customers, along with details 

about the recurring payments, such as the frequency with which the invoice is paid, how many 

times the recurring invoice has been paid, the term, amount and so on. Within the report, you can 

drill down into customer information or the recurring invoice itself. 

You can adjust the time period, customer, customer type, and payment summary to meet your 

reporting needs. Normally, this report shows only customers with balances greater than zero. 

However, you can choose to include zero-balance customers as well. In the report, you can click 

the customer name to drill down to the Customer Information page. 

You can click any link to navigate into the details. 

Example 

This example shows the report with the Display payment details option selected. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to generate the Recurring Report: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Accounts receivable 
A/R Recurring Transaction Status 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 212) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 212) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

Running the A/R Recurring Report

To run the Recurring Report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Registers & Receipts section, select Recurring report. The A/R recurring report 

parameters page opens. 

3. 
Click the View button. A report showing all results for the default reporting period appears 

in your browser. 

Learn more about customizing the Recurring report (on page 113). 

Reports have two kinds of settings, persisting and non-persisting. 

Persisting settings retain any changes you make from session to session. When you return to this 

page to run this report again, each setting displays exactly as you set it before. For example, if you 

type “My Latest Report” into the Report title 1 field, the next time you run this report, the Report 

title 1 box displays My latest report. 

Persisting settings include: 

• 
Settings in the Format section 

• 
Settings in the Titles section 

• 
Check boxes in the Filters section 

Non-persisting settings do not retain your changes. Instead, every time you return to this page to 

run this report or chart, the settings are set to the system defaults. If you changed these settings 

the last time you ran this report, you will have to change them again. 

Non-persisting settings include: 

• 
Settings in the Time Period section 

• 
Drop-down lists in the Filters section

Next date: Select to base the transactions in the report on the date that the next transaction

Filling In the Filters Section 

Use the filters to focus the results of your report. In effect, filters enable you to isolate and 

assemble just the data you want. You can set any combination of filters. 

1. 
You can filter the list of customers by customer name or type. To show results for a specific 

customer or range of customers, use the From Customer and To Customer drop-down lists.

To show results for a specific customer type, click the Customer Type drop-down list, and

Multi-currency/Multi-entity Filters 

1. 
In Transaction currency, select the transaction currency to filter the report for a single 

currency. 

2.

province, or city in the Location box, or click the down arrow, and then click the location 

you want from the list that displays. 

You must enter or select a location if you want to run this report at the top level.  

• 
Select the Individual report check box to run a separate report for each location. 

• 
If you prefer to supply the location at runtime, select the Prompt on run check box. 

3. 
To filter the report by department within the company, type the name of the department in 

the Department box, or click the down arrow and then, from the list that displays, click the 

department you want. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to run a separate report for each department. 

• 
If you prefer to supply the department at runtime, select the Prompt on run check 

box. 

4. 
If you want the report to cover certain locations regardless of what you click in the Location 

box, use the Show For field. To do this, in the Show For field, click the down arrow and then 

click the locations you want the report to cover: If you want the report to include data for all 

locations regardless of the entity you’re currently using, click All Locations. 

• 
If you want the report to include data only for the entity you’re currently using, click 

This Location. 

• 
If you want the report to include data only for locations that are child locations of your 

current entity, click Child Locations. For example, if your current entity is California, 

and you have child locations for San Francisco and Los Angeles, use this option to 

have the report include data only for Los Angeles and California.

#### Recurring Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 116*

Accounts Receivable Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Recurring Report Columns 

The Recurring Report consists of the following columns: 

• 
Customer: ID associated with the customer and the customer’s name 

• 
Reference #: Customer’s order number or other reference number 

• 
Contract ID: ID associated with your customer, if any.  

• 
Frequency: How often the invoice is paid (for example, weekly, monthly, etc.) 

• 
Start date: Date on which the series of recurring invoices began 

• 
Document count: The number of documents generated by the recurring transaction. 

• 
Txn amount, Txn currency, Base amount (currency): These columns appear on the report 

only when multi-currency is enabled.  

• 
Txn amount is the total amount exchanged in the transaction, expressed in the 

currency used for the transaction. 

• 
Txn currency is the currency that was used in the transaction. 

• 
Base amount is the amount of the transaction, expressed in the Base currency. 

• 
Amount: Amount of the recurring payment (or billing transaction). This column appears 

when multi-currency is not enabled. 

• 
Next date: This column contains the date on which the next invoice will be sent  

• 
Term: This column contains the payment terms, such as Net 30. 

• 
Due date: This column contains the date on which the recurring payment is due. 

• 
Payment method: This column contains the payment method used in the transaction. 

• 
Pay in full: This column contains Yes when the customer paid the invoice in full. 

• 
Partial payment amount: This column contains a partial amount paid when the customer 

did not pay the full amount.

The Reclassification report displays a list of documents with data that was reclassified from one

Suppose your company has several users who have permission to change accounting data for 

invoices and/or adjustments that have already been partially or fully paid. Use this report to see a 

list of those transactions and who reclassified them.

Document number: This column contains the number assigned to the document. 

• 
Type: This column contains the type of transaction that was reclassified. 

• 
Document date: This column contains the date on which the document was created. 

• 
G/L posting date: This column contains the date on which the reclassification posted to the 

General ledger. 

• 
Reclassification date: This column contains the date on which the transaction was 

reclassified. 

• 
User: This column contains the ID of the person who reclassified the transaction.

### Memorized Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 126*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 126*

Using Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Memorized Reports 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Memorizing a report retains the report parameters so you don’t have to select them each time 

you want to run or display the report. When you memorize a report, you can assign it a unique 

name so you can add the report to dashboards or report groups or schedule it to run on a 

recurring basis. We recommend that you test run the report with the desired parameters to verify 

that the report output is correct before memorizing the report. 

Memorized Reports Locations 

Memorized reports appear in the Memorized reports list (on page 128) and in the Reports 

center. 

The Memorized reports list is accessible from most RealPage Financial Suite applications; 

however, it displays only the reports that were memorized in the application you access it from. 

For example, if you click the Memorized reports option in the Cash Management menu, then the 

list will include only reports memorized in Cash Management. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Memorizing a report requires that you have the permissions to do so. You must have permissions 

to access and run a report in order to memorize it. Permissions for users, groups, or roles are 

configured in the Company setup. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 212) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 212) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

Memorizing a Report or Chart 

To memorize a report or chart: 

1. 
Set up a report or chart with the filters and parameters that you want to save. 

2. 
Click the Memorize button. The Memorize report parameters box opens. 

3. 
In the Name field, type a name for the report or chart. 

4. 
Select the Public check box to make the report or chart available to other users in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to keep it private. Private reports and charts are 

visible only to the person who created them (owners), and administrators. 

5. 
Click OK.

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart

Schedule`


See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report (on page 136) page 

opens. 

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report (on page 136) page opens. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups, then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or more G/L account 

groups to filter the report by.

Storing Standard Reports and Charts 

You can process any report or chart on demand and have the system store it. The Process & store 

option is particularly useful when running large reports. It is also useful to maintain reporting 

history for a specific point in time. 

After setting up a report or chart, you have these options: 

• 
To run the report or chart and view it, click the View button. 

• 
To run the report or chart and store it, click the Process & store button. 

Choosing File Types to Store Reports and Charts 

When you store a report or chart, you can choose the report type. 

Report Type 
Delivery Options 

Financial Reports  
HTML, PDF, CSV, Excel

#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 153*

Chapter 3: Using Reports

My Stored Reports List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > (Application) > All > Reports > My Stored Reports`


Use the My stored reports list to: 

• 
View a list of reports that have been stored in the system. 

• 
Sort and filter the list to see only the reports you require. 

• 
Export the list of stored reports. 

Stored reports are ones that you have selected to be run at a later time, either by: 

• 
Scheduling reports: When you schedule a report to be run periodically (for example, on a 

weekly basis), you have the option to store the report in the system. 

• 
Processing and storing reports: While working with a particular report, you have the option 

to process it in the background and store it in the system. This option is particularly useful 

for reports containing amounts of data that are too large for the system to run in real time. 

Additionally, you can use this feature to automatically take periodic snapshots and keep 

them for future reference. 

The data in these reports is current as of the date on which you ran the report and does not 

reflect any changes since then. However, if you drill down through the report into other pages, 

you will be accessing the actual data. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to generate reports: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Any application 
Reports 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 212) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 212) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

 Print button to print the report.

Stopping a Scheduled Report

Schedule`


You can change when and how often a scheduled report is delivered. If you want to keep the 

scheduled report but stop its delivery, you can set the recurrence of the report to None. 

To stop a scheduled report from running again: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu.  

2. 
Select Reports center. 

3. 
Select the Scheduled tab. 

4. 
Click More actions next to the report, and then select Edit schedule. 

5. 
In the Schedule section, set the Recurrence option to None to keep the scheduled report 

but stop its delivery. 

Alternatively, in the Ending on drop-down list, select End date, and then set the End on 

date to the current date. 

Deleting a Stored Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > More > My Stored Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger/Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable/Cash 
Management/Forecasting & Planning > Reports > My Stored Reports`


Your reports are stored until you delete them. 

To delete a report: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select the application where you created the report.  

2. 
In the third column, select My stored reports. The list of stored reports opens.  

3. 
Click Delete for the report to remove. You’re prompted for confirmation.  

4. 
Click OK to delete the report.

Set the status of your report. The status of the report you created is Active by default.

To make the report inactive, click the drop-down menu next to status and choose Inactive.

added to both the application menu you selected and to the list of reports. From this list,

### Reasons Your A/R Subledger or Aging and G/L Might Not Balance
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 167*

Chapter 4: Troubleshooting A/R Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

Reasons Your A/R Subledger or Aging and G/L Might Not 
Balance 

This topic was designed to help you determine the cause of your aging report or subledger 

yielding unexpected results.  

This list describes possible reasons that your A/R subledger (or customer aging report) is failing to 

synchronize with the General Ledger and provides solutions for each reason. 

G/L beginning balance doesn’t equal your originally imported A/R balance 

Probable cause:  

Some transactions might not have been imported correctly. 

Solution: 

Determine if any invoices are missing from the originally imported invoices. Depending on 

what you find, take one of the following actions: 

If transactions were missing: Import the missing transactions as historical transactions. 

If transactions were not missing: Add a journal entry to make the G/L beginning balance 

match the amount of the originally imported invoices. 

Aging report is missing transactions 

There are two possible causes. 

Possible cause #1: 

Reversals done in the wrong period. Check your reversals to see if the transaction date 

matches the reversal date. If not, the transaction was probably reversed in an incorrect 

period. 

Solution: 

Make a journal entry to remove the reversal from the incorrect period. Then, make another 

journal entry to add the reversal to the correct period. 

OR 

Possible cause #2: 

Accounts Receivable is not configured correctly. 

Solution: 

Verify the configuration is correct, and correct it if needed. 

On the Configure accounts receivable page: 

---


<!-- Page 168 -->
Troubleshooting A/R Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Correct aging periods. For the first line of the Aging period range, leave the Minimum 

range blank and set the Maximum range to 0. 

• 
Make sure to the check box for Display reversals as historical transactions is selected. 

A/R Journal entries made in G/L don’t appear in A/R subledger 

Probable cause: 

This is expected behavior. Journal entries made directly to the Accounts Receivable G/L 

account don’t flow to the Accounts Receivable subledger. 

Solution: 

Manually reconcile and track direct journal entries to ensure the G/L ties to the A/R aging 

report. 

If you meant for journal entries to be there, outside of the system, deduct the values to 

ensure the balances match. If the journal entries are coded to the incorrect G/L accounts, 

edit the journal entries to fix the coding. 

---


<!-- Page 169 -->
Chapter 4: Troubleshooting A/R Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide

imported as historical and make a journal entry to

Run the A/R Subledger and Customer Aging reports 

based on the G/L posting date to tie the balances to the 

G/L. 

Payment was received

Use either of the two following procedures to tie the 

balances: 

Make journal entries to: 

• 
Clear the payment. 

•

Within the A/R application:

Example: You create an invoice on 12/1/2016 and 

erroneously recorded that payment was made on 

11/15/2016. When you make a journal entry to add the

Customer Aging Chart

 Graph 

The Customer Aging chart illustrates how many days customer invoices have aged before they 

were paid. Use any of several types of charts (bar, line, pie, etc.) to visually track how often 

customers paid their invoices by time period, account, customer, and more. Use this report when 

you want to see a visual representation of the Customer Aging report. 

Who typically needs this report?  

Finance managers who need to spot and correct problems in the management of receivables. 

You can display the chart as of today, or another date you enter, and can base the chart on the 

invoice date, due date, or G/L posting date. You can filter the list by a single customer or all 

customers. You can chart aging period totals or customer totals, or you can chart customer totals 

by your top customers.

Viewing a Monthly Chart 

When the chart’s customization page loads, click the View button. The chart displays, showing all 

results for the month to date. 

To refine the report, click the Customize button to return the customization page and follow the 

steps for customizing the chart. 

Reports have two kinds of settings, persisting and non-persisting. 

Persisting settings retain any changes you make from session to session. When you return to this 

page to run this report again, each setting displays exactly as you set it before. For example, if you 

type “My Latest Report” into the Report title 1 field, the next time you run this report, the Report 

title 1 box displays My latest report. 

Persisting settings include: 

• 
Settings in the Format section 

• 
Settings in the Titles section 

• 
Check boxes in the Filters section 

Non-persisting settings do not retain your changes. Instead, every time you return to this page to 

run this report or chart, the settings are set to the system defaults. If you changed these settings 

the last time you ran this report, you will have to change them again. 

Non-persisting settings include: 

• 
Settings in the Time Period section 

• 
Drop-down lists in the Filters section

*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 189*

Customizing and Running the Deferred Revenue Forecast Graph 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred

 Graph`


To customize the Deferred Revenue Forecast graph: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu.  

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Registers & Reports section, click the 
 Graph next to 

Deferred Revenue Forecast. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

1. 
Define the time period. You can either define the coverage by as of date and number of 

periods, or by date range, but not both. 

To define the time period by as of date: 

• 
Type the starting date in the As of date field or click the 
 Calendar button, and 

then select the date from the calendar. 

To define the time period by date range: 

• 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s coverage period. Set a 

specific Start date and End date.  

Leave the Start date blank to include all information from the earliest date you 

entered data into your company up to and including the End date. 

Leave the End date blank to include all information from the Start date up to today. 

The format must be: MM/DD/YYYY 

If you select a Start date and End date, don’t select an As of date. 

When entering a date, you can either type the dates or click the 
 Calendar button, 

and then select the date from the calendar.  

2. 
Select the Forecast period for which to run the report.  

Each column of the report will represent one period. Options are: 

• 
Monthly—displays as MMM-YY. For example, Jun-20. 

• 
Quarterly—displays as MMM-YY - MMM-YY. For example, Jan-20 - Mar-20. 

• 
Semi-annually—displays as MMM-YY - MMM-YY. For example, Jan-20 - Jun-20. 

• 
Annually—displays as Year-YYYY. For example, Year-2020. 

3. 
Set the length of time that you want the report to cover.  

---


<!-- Page 190 -->
Accounts Receivable Charts 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

In the # of Periods field, type the number of periods. For example, if you want a year of data 

and your Forecast Period is quarterly, type 4; if your Forecast Period is monthly, type 12. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Use this section to set up filters that refine your report results. 

1. 
Choose the transactions to include by selecting the check boxes: 

• 
Include not started schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for 

schedules that have not yet started. By default, the report will cover revenue details for 

schedules that have not yet started (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include in progress schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for 

schedules that are in progress. By default, the report will cover revenue details for 

schedules that are in progress (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include onhold schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for schedules 

that are on hold. By default, the report will cover revenue details for schedules that are 

on hold (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include partially terminated schedule: Select this check box to show revenue details 

for schedules that are partially terminated. By default, the report will cover transactions 

that have been partially terminated (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include terminated transactions: Select this check box to show the details of 

transactions that have been terminated. By default, the report will cover transactions 

that have been terminated (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include completed transactions: Select this check box to show the details of 

transactions that have been fully recognized. By default, the report will cover 

transactions that have been fully recognized (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include open period schedules: Select this check box to show project revenue that has 

not been scheduled or posted. This filter is associated with Percent completed or 

Milestone recognition methods. 

2. 
In the Report on section, select the desired option to run the report on: 

• 
Revenue account: Select this option to limit the report to transactions for a specific 

revenue account. 

• 
Deferred revenue account: Select this option to report deferred revenue accounts 

rather than revenue accounts.  

3. 
In the Revenue account drop-down list, select the revenue account to limit the report to 

one revenue account. By default, this box is blank, which means the report will cover 

transaction details for every revenue account. 

---


<!-- Page 191 -->

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

4. 
In the Deferred revenue account drop-down list, select the desired deferred revenue 

account to limit the report to one deferred revenue account. Use this filter if you chose 

Deferred revenue account in step 2. By default, this box is blank, which means the report 

will cover transaction details for every deferred revenue account. 

5. 
In the Revenue recognition template drop-down list, select the desired template to limit 

the report to it. 

6. 
Use the Customer From and Customer To drop-down lists to select the beginning and 

ending customer in a range to include a range of customers in the report. 

In Customer From, select the first customer in a range of customers to include in the report. 

The system fills in the Customer To box with the same customer, setting it up in case you

In Customer To, select the last customer in a range of customers.

## Invoices Analysis Chart
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 194*



### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 194*

Accounts Receivable Charts 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Invoices Analysis Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Registers & Reports > A/R Invoices Analysis 
> 
 Graph`


Use this chart when you want to see a visual representation of the Invoices Analysis report. The 

Invoices Analysis chart helps you analyze your sales from the perspective of revenue line items in 

the invoices by representing sales visually, using bar and line charts or pie charts. You can group 

line items across invoices and then perform your analysis.  

For example, use any of several types of charts (bar, line, pie, etc.) to visually track how much of a 

certain type of property your customers are leasing from you over a specific period of time and 

which customers leased that specific property. 

Before You Begin 

This report does not have a specific permission assigned to it, which means that anyone can run 

the report.

*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 195*

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

Viewing a Monthly Chart 

When the chart’s customization page loads, click the View button. The chart displays, showing all 

results for the month to date. 

To refine the report, click the Customize button to return the customization page and follow the 

steps for customizing the chart. 

Reports have two kinds of settings, persisting and non-persisting. 

Persisting settings retain any changes you make from session to session. When you return to this 

page to run this report again, each setting displays exactly as you set it before. For example, if you 

type “My Latest Report” into the Report title 1 field, the next time you run this report, the Report 

title 1 box displays My latest report. 

Persisting settings include: 

• 
Settings in the Format section 

• 
Settings in the Titles section 

• 
Check boxes in the Filters section 

Non-persisting settings do not retain your changes. Instead, every time you return to this page to 

run this report or chart, the settings are set to the system defaults. If you changed these settings 

the last time you ran this report, you will have to change them again. 

Non-persisting settings include: 

• 
Settings in the Time Period section 

• 
Drop-down lists in the Filters section
