Customizing Standard Reports and Charts 

The Customize button appears after you click the View button to run the report or create the 

chart. 

Click the Customize button to return to the report’s parameters page, where you can change the 

settings for dates, filters, format, and titles. 

Each report and chart have a unique set of parameters. Refer to the report or chart type for 

information about customizing that specific report. 

Memorizing Standard Reports and Charts Parameters 

To memorize a standard report’s or chart’s parameters: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, select the application, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select the report or chart that you want to customize and then memorize. The 

customization page opens. 

3. 
Customize the report or chart the way you want the system to run it in the future. 

4. 
Click the Memorize button. The Memorize report parameters box opens. 

5. 
In the Name field, fill in the name of the report or chart. 

6. 
In the Description field, type a description of the report or chart to remind you about its 

specific parameters. Make sure that your description distinguishes it from other memorized 

reports or charts. 

7. 
Select the Public check box to make the memorized parameters available to other system 

users. 

8. 
Click the OK button. The system adds the memorized parameters to the Memorized reports 

list. 

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Memorized > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

---


<!-- Page 204 -->

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report (on page 136) page 

opens. 

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report (on page 136) page opens. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups, then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or more G/L account 

groups to filter the report by. 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

If you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use.

Storing Standard Reports and Charts 

You can process any report or chart on demand and have the system store it. The Process & store 

option is particularly useful when running large reports. It is also useful to maintain reporting 

history for a specific point in time. 

After setting up a report or chart, you have these options: 

• 
To run the report or chart and view it, click the View button. 

• 
To run the report or chart and store it, click the Process & store button. 

Emailing Standard Reports and Charts 

Email 

To email a report or a chart: 

1. 
Click the Email button. The Email report box opens. 

2. 
In the To field, type the email address of the person to whom you want to send the report. 

To enter multiple addresses, separate each address with a comma (,) or semi-colon (;). 

3. 
Click the CC me check box if you want the system to send an email to your Inbox. 

4. 
In the Subject field, type the text that you want to appear in the subject line of the email 

message. 

5. 
In the Message field, type a message to the recipient. The system completes the signature 

line and fills the From field with your email address. 

6. 
Click OK. 

Adding a Memorized Standard Chart to a Dashboard 

Before You Begin 

Before you can add a chart to the dashboard, create a custom dashboard. For more information, 

see Adding a dashboard (on page 230). 

To add a chart to a dashboard: 

1. 
Create the chart that you want to add. 

2. 
From the created chart’s page, click the Add to dashboard button.  

3. 
In the Add to dashboard parameters box, select the dashboard to which you want to add 

the chart. 

4. 
In the Description field, type a description of the chart.  

---

and this report. Clear the Public check box if you do not want others to be able to view this 

chart on the dashboard.  

6. 
Click OK. The Memorized reports list opens. The system stores the chart in the Memorized 

reports list. 

What’s Next? 

• 
Edit (on page 203): Change the memorized chart’s name and any of its parameters. 

•

also deletes the schedule associated with it. If the chart never ran, the system does not store 

a chart in the My stored reports list.

Deleting a Memorized Report 

Deleting a memorized report removes the report from the list of memorized reports, and also 

removes the report from any dashboard on which it appears.  

To delete a memorized report: 

1. 
Open the menu of the application where you created the report. 

2. 
In the Reports section, select Memorized reports. 

3. 
Locate the report that you want to delete.

### Roles and Permissions
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 212*



#### Assigning Permissions for a New Feature
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 212*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

Assigning Permissions for a New Feature 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users > Subscriptions > Permissions`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions > Permissions`


When RealPage adds a new feature, it often comes with new permissions that you must enable 

before users can use the new feature. 

To add permissions for a new feature: 

• 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

---


<!-- Page 213 -->
Chapter 7: Common Tasks 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

If using Role-based permissions 

1. 
Select Roles. 

2. 
Find the role that you want to change. 

3. 
Click the Subscriptions link.  

4. 
Find the application that offers the new feature, and then select the Permissions link. The 

application’s permissions window opens. 

5. 
Find the new feature’s permission, and then enable the desired permissions. 

6. 
Click the Save button on the application’s permissions page. 

7. 
Click the Save button on the Roles subscriptions page. 

8. 
Click the Done button to close the list. 

If using User-based permissions 

1. 
Select Users. 

2. 
Locate the user who needs to be able to use the new feature.  

3. 
Select the Subscriptions link. 

4. 
Find the application that offers the new feature, and then select the Permissions link. The 

application’s permissions page opens. 

5. 
Find the new feature’s permission, and then enable the desired permissions.  

6. 
Click the Save button. 

7. 
Click the Save button on the User application subscriptions page. 

8. 
Click the Done button to close the list.

### Creating a Financial Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 214*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide

Creating a Financial Report 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

The Financial report writer provides options for controlling all aspects of your financial report, 

from building your rows and columns to setting precise formatting options. 

Adding a Financial Report 

To create a report using the Financial report writer: 

1. 
In the Financial reports list, click the Add button. The Financial report writer opens. 

2. 
Name your report. 

3. 
Select your basic report structure (Report info tab). 

4. 
Review the options in the Report structure section of the Report info tab, using the report 

samples as a guide. After you create a report, you can’t change the report structure. 

5. 
Select either Accounts or Dimensions, depending on what you’d like to see on your report 

rows. 

6. 
Build your account rows. 

Depending on the report structure you selected on the Report info tab, you’ll either build 

rows from account groups or dimension structures. For existing reports, the headings that 

you see along the left side of the tab reflect the account groups or dimension structures 

that have already been added to the report. 

       Type of rows  
        Description 

Accounts on rows (Rows 

tab) 

In this type of report, you select the account groups 

that you want to appear on the left side of your 

report. For example, a balance sheet report might 

include “Assets” and “Liabilities and Equity.” 

Dimensions on rows (Rows 

tab) 

In this type of report, you select the dimension 

structures that you want to appear on the left side 

of your report. For example, you might want to 

show rows for customers, or certain locations or 

departments. 

---


<!-- Page 215 -->
Chapter 7: Common Tasks 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

Setting Up Columns (Columns Tab) 

1. 
Choose the columns you want to include in the report. 

2. 
Decide what value you want to include in each column. For example, you might want to see 

the account names or dimension names on the left, followed by actual columns for different 

reporting periods. 

3. 
Column values can be based on calculations, such as summary calculations that operate on 

two or more columns (such as computing the average of a set of columns). For reports that 

feature account groups on rows, you can define more complex calculations on the 

Computations tab. 

4. 
Select the Account group purpose. This is displayed in the list and in the report. 

Filtering the Report (Filters Tab) 

You can set options such as the “as of date” and reporting method. You can also filter the report 

by dimension, such as filtering for a particular set of locations. 

In practice, many reports are designed to prompt the user for the “as of date” and other criteria 

when the report is run. That way you can create a single report and let the user choose the criteria 

when the report is run. 

Setting Up Headers and Footers (Format Tab) 

Set page header, footer, font, and other report format options. 

Row formatting options let you control the appearance and spacing of row headings and totals. 

Click the 
 Help buttons next to Row formatting and Total formatting in the Rows section to 

learn more. 

Filters

Setting Access Restrictions for the Report (Permissions Tab) 

Finish the report with any optional next steps, such as adding the report to a dashboard, making 

it a favorite, or scheduling it to run automatically (Next Steps). 

Multi-Entity Companies: Private Reports 

By default, financial reports are set to Public. 

This means that everyone can see them. If a report is private, only the users in the entity and with 

permissions can see the report. Top-level admins can also see private reports if they check 

Include Private in the list of reports. 

To make entity-level financial reports private by default, disable the Set default permissions to 

public setting at the top-level General Ledger configuration.

### Exporting from Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 223*

Chapter 7: Common Tasks 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

Exporting from Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

To export a list of records from the system: 

1. 
Select the Include inactive check box to include items with an Inactive status in the data 

export results or clear the Include inactive check box to exclude inactive items. 

2. 
Select the Include private check box to include items that are associated with an entity or 

clear the Include private check box to exclude these items. 

3. 
Click the Export button. 

4. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again.

Specifying Dates 

When you set a date format in your preferences, the system displays that format for all dates. 

If you enter a date using a format that is different from your preferred format, the system 

re-formats the date to your preferred format. For example, if you set your date format as 

MM/DD/YYYY, enter Dec 17, 2016, and then press TAB to move out of the field, then the system 

immediately displays the date as 12/17/2016. 

You can change your date format at any time. For example, if you want a particular date format to 

print a single report, change it in your settings, then print the report.

report is collapsed, click  Expand to show the full report.)  

14. 
Click the Save button.

Saving and Adding Your Report to a Menu 

The final step of the custom report wizard allows you to save your report and add your report to 

an application menu. This makes it available to other users who have access to that application.  

Saving and Deploying Your Report 

Name and save your report, and then deploy it to an application menu.  

On the final step of the Custom report writer (on page 161):  

1. 
Type a name in the required Name field.  

2. 
Select the Add to menu check box, and then select the application to which you want to 

add the report. The system adds the report to Custom reports submenu of the selected 

application. 

3. 
Enter a brief description of your report.  

4. 
Set the status of your report. The status of the report you created is Active by default.  

5. 
To make the report inactive, click the drop-down menu next to status and choose Inactive.  

6. 
Click the Save button at the top of the page to save your report. Your report is saved and 

added to both the application menu you selected and to the list of reports. From this list, 

you can view, edit, run, duplicate, or delete the report.

Scheduling and Sharing Your Report 

The advantage of custom reports is that you can schedule them to run at different times with the 

same settings and make them available in dashboards and report groups.  

To schedule and share your report:  

1. 
Memorize the report so it can be run again with the same settings. 

2. 
Share custom reports by adding them to your dashboard, so you’ll always have key 

performance indicators at your fingertips. See Adding a Report to a Dashboard (on page 

158).  

3. 
Add a memorized report to a report group. 

4. 
Schedule a memorized report. See Scheduling a Memorized Report or Graph (on page 130). 

5. 
Use the Process & store button to schedule a report. See Processing and Storing Reports 

(on page 143).

### Configuring A/R Document Sequencing
*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 243*

Chapter 7: Common Tasks 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 

Configuring A/R Document Sequencing 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Document Sequencing`


In the RealPage Financial Suite, document sequences refer to the system’s automatic numbering 

feature used to assign unique identifiers to new records. This helps ensure consistency and avoids 

duplication. 

Automatic numbering, also known as document sequencing, is available only in select features in 

RealPage Accounting. These features use pre-defined numbering plans to assign sequential 

identifiers—typically when creating new records or transactions. 

If you prefer to number a transaction type manually, do not assign a document sequence for the 

transaction type. 

Before You Begin 

You must create a new document numbering scheme before you see it as an option in this 

section. 

• 
Configure a document sequence for the desired record type in Company > All > Settings > 

Document Numbering. 

Setting Up Document Sequencing for A/R Transactions and Records 

Use the Document sequencing section to: 

• 
Set warnings. If you choose to enter any of the transaction IDs manually, you can set a 

warning whenever someone enters a duplicate ID. 

• 
Assign a document sequence for these select transactions and records: 

• 
A/R invoices 

• 
Recurring A/R invoices 

• 
A/R debit adjustments 

• 
A/R credit adjustments 

• 
Customer records 

• 
Require IDs on select types of transactions and records. 

• 
Invoices 

• 
Adjustments 

• 
Quick invoice entry 

• 
Recurring invoices 

• 
Manual deposits 

After a document sequence is configured and assigned, the system automatically assigns a 

sequential ID to each new transaction or record, ensuring a smooth and consistent flow of unique 

identifiers. 

---


<!-- Page 244 -->
Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Receivable Reports User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

To assign document sequences to transactions and records in A/R: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration option. The Configure Accounts Receivable page opens. 

4. 
Find the Document sequencing section. 

5. 
For each of the following, set the number sequence that you want the system to use for 

each new transaction. 

• 
A/R Invoices* 

• 
Recurring A/R invoices 

• 
A/R debit adjustments 

• 
A/R credit adjustments 

• 
Customers 

6. 
In the If invoices or adjustments are assigned duplicate numbers section, select how you want 

the system to handle duplicate numbers. This setting applies to invoices and adjustments 

for the selected customer. 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message that the transaction 

number for this customer is a duplicate. The transaction can’t be created. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without any alert or action on 

the part of the system. 

7. 
In the Numbers are required on section, select the records for which you want to require to 

use document sequencing on. 

• 
A/R Invoices, adjustments, quick A/R invoice entry, and recurring A/R invoices only 

• 
Manual deposits 

8. 
Click the Save button.

*Source: `RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 245*

Configuring Intercompany Billing 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Intercompany Billing 
Setup`


Use the Intercompany Billing section to enable the intercompany billing feature, select the 

document numbering scheme and the account to use for deposits. 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration option. The Configure accounts receivable page opens. 

4. 
Find the Intercompany billing setup section. 

5. 
Select the Enable Intercompany billing transactions (ICB) check box to enable the 

intercompany billing (ICB) feature. 

6. 
In the Sequence number drop-down list, select the document numbering scheme to use for 

ICB transactions. We recommend adding a document numbering scheme prefixed by ICB if 

one does not exist. For information, see Adding a Sequence ID (on page 246). 

7. 
Select the Auto process invoice on ICB payment check box. Select this option so that when 

the paying entity pays the A/P invoice, the beneficiary entity’s A/R invoice is automatically 

processed as paid.  

8. 
In the Undeposited Funds Account (ICB) list, select the account in which to deposit the 

intercompany billing payments. 

After applying payments to the intercompany billing invoices, the system uses this account 

for bank deposits. 

9. 
Select the Bank check box to have the system deposit funds into the default bank account 

rather than the Undeposited funds account. The default bank account is defined by entity. If 

an entity does not have a default bank account defined, then the system deposits ICB 

payments into the undeposited funds account.

About the Accounts Receivable Application

Use Accounts Receivable to create and manage customer
records; create A/R invoices, advances, and adjustments; and
receive customer payments.
Subscribe to the Accounts Receivable application on the
Subscriptions page in the Company application.
Configure the Accounts Receivable application on the Setup
tab with the Configuration command.
All procedures in this document start on the All tab of the
Accounts Receivable menu.

Adding a Customer

Customer is the customer paying the A/R invoice.

1. In Accounts Receivable, select 
 Add next to A/R Invoices.
2. Enter the A/R invoice information into each field on each tab:

▪
Customer
▪
Additional Information
▪
Contact List
▪
Restrictions (to limit which properties can see the Customer
record)

3. Click Save.

Adding a Payment to Bank Account

Enter a payment received by a customer.

1. In Accounts Receivable, select Receive a payment.
2. Select Bank account for the Account type.
3. Select which bank account to deposit money into.
4. Select the Bank G/L account.
5. Select the Customer that paid.
6. Type the Receipt date.
7. Type the Payment date.
8. Type the amount.
9. In the Available Invoices section, select the invoices to which to
apply the payments.
10. Click Save.

Receiving Payment to Undeposited Funds

Undeposited funds is the holding or suspense account that the
system uses to book a payment received but not deposited into
the bank. After depositing the funds, enter a deposit to relieve
the undeposited funds account.
Receive payment to undeposited funds account.

1. In Accounts Receivable, select Receive a payment.
2. Select Undeposited Funds Account.
3. Select the account to use for undeposited funds.

4. Select the Customer that paid.
5. Enter Receipt Date.
6. Enter the Payment date/Date on check.
7. Enter the Amount.
8. In the Available Invoices section, select the invoices to which to
apply the undeposited funds.
9. Click Save.

Recording a Deposit

Move money from the undeposited funds account to a cash
account.

1. In Accounts Receivable, select 
 Add next to Deposits.
2. Select the Bank Account where you want to deposit the funds.
3. Enter other required fields, and then click Continue.
The table shows the eligible undeposited amounts if any.
4. Select the undeposited funds to transfer into the bank.
5. Click Save.

Recording a Manual Deposit

Record a customer payment that isn't made against a specific
invoice.

1. In Accounts Receivable, select 
 Add next to Manual
deposits.
2. Add the header information.
3. Enter line items in the Entries section.
4. Click Save.

Adding an A/R Invoice

Enter information for customers that are invoiced.

1. In Accounts Receivable, select 
 Add next to A/R Invoices.
2. Fill in the header, term, and currency information.
3. Enter line items in the Entries section.
4. Click Post or Submit.

Adding a Recurring A/R Invoice

Schedule an A/R invoice to be generated.

1. In Accounts Receivable, select 
 Add next to Recurring A/R
Invoices.
2. Enter the A/R invoice information:

▪
Enter customer information.
▪
Enter transaction details.

3. In the Entries section, enter line items.
4. Select the Payment tab and fill in the details.
5. Select the Schedule tab and establish the schedule.

6. Click Save.

Adding an Adjustment

A debit memo adjustment decreases the balance due. A credit
memo adjustment increases the balance due.

1. In Accounts Receivable, select 
 Add next to Adjustments.
2. Enter the header information.
3. Enter line items in the Entries section.
4. Click the arrow on the Post & New button, and then select
Post.

Opening/Closing Subledger

Open the subledger to allow additional transactions. Close the
subledger so that no other Accounts Receivable transactions
can be booked.

1. In Accounts Receivable, select Open subledger or Close
subledger.
2. Select the Entity/Entity group.
3. In the To the start/end of period drop-down list, select the
period to open/close. You can also select Open/Close a single
summary to open or close a batch.
4. Click Open/Close.
